en: She argues that we need to close 75% of the planet’s coal-fired power plants, including all of South Africa’s, because they emit too much CO2.

zh: 戈尔的气候顾问，杰姆斯·汉森（James Hansen）认为，如果我们允许发展中国家“达到发达国家的水平，那么地球就完了。 ”
en: Al Gore’s climate adviser, James Hansen, argues that if we allow developing countries to “come up to the level of the developed world, then the planet is done for.”

zh: 是的，世界需要解决全球变暖问题（主要通过加大对绿色能源研究和发展的投资，促进廉价和低污染页岩气的开发 ） 。
en: Yes, the world needs to address global warming (mainly through higher investments in green research and development, and by promoting exploitation of cheap, less-polluting shale gas).

zh: 但全球变暖问题将在本世纪末导致大概价值占GDP1~5%的损失，而联合国预计那时发展中国家的收入已增长了1400~1800 % 。
en: But global warming will cause damage worth possibly 1-5% of GDP by the end of the century, when the UN expects developing-world incomes to have risen by 1,400-1,800%.

zh: 同时，随着全球GDP可能呈数量级增长的影响，贫困正在造成数百万人死亡。
en: Meanwhile, poverty is killing millions right now, with an impact on global GDP that is likely an order of magnitude higher.

zh: 并且，太多的人虽是出于好意，但不愿意承认取舍首先是要改善穷人的生活。
en: And too many people, however well-intentioned, are unwilling to acknowledge the tradeoffs needed to improve poor people’s lives.

zh: 全球乐观的现实主义
en: The Realism of Global Optimism

zh: 布拉格—看看报纸或者看看新闻，你会觉得世界无时无刻不再变坏。
en: PRAGUE – Read a newspaper or watch the evening news, and the world always seems to be getting worse.

zh: 镜头里，一个问题接着一个问题。
en: One problem after another is put under a spotlight.

zh: 死亡、毁坏、绝望，越多这样的消息，新闻越兴奋。
en: The more death, destruction, and despair, the better.

zh: 一本丹麦新闻学教科书说 ： “ 好故事通常都是坏消息。 ”
en: As one Danish journalism textbook puts it: “A good story is usually bad news.”

zh: 偶尔（只是偶尔）我们也可以遇到一些正能量的越变越好的故事。
en: Only occasionally do we get uplifting, things-are-getting-better stories.

zh: 这时我们就会有一种负罪感。
en: When we do, they feel like a guilty pleasure.

zh: 结果，我们通常觉得世界比实际上更糟 — — 尽管我们也认为我们的生活正在改善。
en: As a result, we often think that the world is in worse shape than it is – even if we think our own lives are improving.

zh: 举个例子。 1978年以来，美国消费者每年都会被调查当前财务状况比一年前更糟还是更好。
en: Consider this: Since 1978, American consumers have been asked whether their current financial situation is better or worse than it was a year earlier.

zh: 在过去25年中，平均有38%的人说情况更好了，有32%的人说情况更糟了。
en: Over the past 25 years, an average of 38% have said they are doing better, while 32% have said they are doing worse.

zh: 但是，在被问及美国经济总体状况时，平均有47%的人说情况更糟了，只有38%的人说情况更好了。
en: But, when asked the same question about the overall US economy, an average of 47% have said it is doing worse, compared to 38% who think it is doing better.

zh: 更多的人认为他们的生活在改善，而别人的生活在恶化，也许这就是新闻记者长久以来偏好坏消息的结果。
en: More people think their lives are improving, while others are doing worse, probably because of journalists’ persistent bias in favor of bad news.

zh: 这一现象并不局限于美国。
en: The phenomenon is not limited to the United States.

zh: 自1977年以来，盖洛普公司每年都会问世界各地的人认为明年是否回避过去的一年生活得更好。
en: Since 1977, Gallup International has asked people around the world whether they believe their lives will be better next year than they were the year before.

zh: 对于2014年，近50%的受访者说生活会变得更好，只有20%的人认为会变坏。
en: For 2014, almost 50% of those surveyed said that their lives will be better, with just 20% saying they will be worse off.

zh: 但是，再被问及世界经济，观点几乎是五五开，32%的人���为会变好，30%的人认为会变坏。
en: Yet, asked for their opinion of how the world economy will fare, the score is almost even, with 32% believing that it will be better, and 30% that it will be worse.

zh: 因此，有必要回过头查看并确认许多指标都表明世界正在改善。
en: So it is worth stepping back and recognizing that many indicators point to a world that is improving.

zh: 世界银行的新数据表明，极端贫困人口比例在过去30年中下降了一大半，从1981年占总人口的42%下降到2010年的17 % 。
en: New data from the World Bank show that the proportion of extremely poor people has more than halved over the last 30 years, from 42% of the global population in 1981 to 17% in 2010.

zh: 尽管12亿发展中世界的人们每天的生活费仍不到1.25美元 — — 这毫无疑问是必须得到解决的问题 — — 但极端贫困率从未如此之低。
en: While 1.2 billion people in the developing world still live on less than $1.25 per day – a problem that we certainly must address – the rate of extreme poverty has never been lower.

zh: 经济学家估算，在1820年，超过80%的人口生活在极端贫困中。
en: Economists estimate that in 1820, more than 80% of all people were extremely poor.

zh: 类似地，想想教育方面令人欣喜的改善。
en: Similarly, consider the amazing improvements in education.

zh: 如今，20%的世界人口仍在接受文盲的折磨，但比1900年的70 % （ 估计水平）已是天壤之别。
en: Illiteracy today still afflicts 20% of the world’s population, but that is down sharply from an estimated 70% in 1900.

zh: 在繁荣的西方，20世纪初就实现了识字率的快速上升。
en: In the prosperous West, rapid increases in literacy were achieved early in the twentieth century.

zh: 在发展中国家，类似的大规模（并仍在继续的）改善发生于1970—2000年，其中中国的成就最为显著。
en: In developing countries, similarly large (and continuing) gains were made from 1970 to 2000, with China recording the biggest improvement.

zh: 穷人教育的成本是巨大的。
en: The costs of poor education are substantial.

zh: 比如，1950年，巴基斯坦和韩国的教育和收入水平基本相当。
en: For example, Pakistan and South Korea started with about the same level of education and income in 1950.

zh: 如今，韩国人平均受教育年限为12年，而巴基斯坦不到六年。
en: Today, the average South Korean has 12 years of education, whereas the average Pakistani has fewer than six.

zh: 在此期间，韩国人均收入提高了23倍，而巴基斯坦只有三倍。
en: South Korea’s per capita income grew 23-fold over this period, compared to Pakistan’s three-fold growth.

zh: 经济学家在与哥本哈根共识（Copenhagen Consensus）的合作下试图评估文盲成本。
en: Together with the Copenhagen Consensus, economists have attempted to assess the cost of illiteracy.

zh: 据我们测算，如果1900年便已消灭了文盲，世界应该比实际情况多拥有2400亿美元（经通胀调整）的财富，相当于当时全球GDP的12 % 。
en: We estimate that if there had been no illiteracy in 1900, the world would have been $240 billion richer (in inflation-adjusted terms), equivalent to about 12% of global GDP at the time.

zh: 因此，可以说1900年时全球文盲问题让全世界付出了12%的GDP的代价。
en: So, the global illiteracy problem in 1900 can be said to have cost the world 12% of GDP.

zh: 如今，全球文盲造成的成本下降到GDP的7 % 。
en: Today, the cost of global illiteracy is down to 7% of GDP.

zh: 到2050年，文盲率将下降到12%左右，其成本将减少到只有GDP的3.8 % 。
en: By 2050, when illiteracy will reach about 12%, the cost will have dwindled to just 3.8% of GDP.

zh: 类似地，战争也会造成巨大的经济和人力成本。
en: Likewise, war carries a high economic and human cost.

zh: 但是，尽管如今我们可以以以前无法想象的速度和生动程度看到战争影像，但我们对冲突无处不在的感觉是错误的。
en: But, while the images of it that we see are more immediate and vivid than ever, our perception of ubiquitous conflict is wrong.

zh: 在20世纪，冲突夺走了1.4亿人的生命，其中两次世界大战就杀掉了7800—9000万人。
en: In the twentieth century, conflict killed 140 million people, including 78-90 million in the two world wars.

zh: 不太被公众了解的好消息（之所以如此，只是因为这是好消息）是未来军事开支会更高、不变或更低的情景都表明，二十世纪的高军事成本已经形成了类似于永久和平分裂的局面。
en: The good news, which is not often publicized (precisely because it is good), is that scenarios in which military spending is higher, the same, or lower in the future suggest that the high military costs of the twentieth century have been turned into what looks like a permanent peace dividend.

zh: 第一次世界大战造成的成本相当于全球GDP的20 % ， 二战则还要高出一倍。
en: World War I cost about 20% of global GDP, and WWII cost almost twice as much.

zh: 在考察冲突的成本时，哥本哈根共识经济学家估算的是全球军事开支的实际成本。
en: When examining the cost of conflict, the Copenhagen Consensus economists estimate the actual costs of global military expenditure.

zh: 如果我们还纳入战争中的生命损失，那么估计值还会提高50%左右。
en: If one also takes into account the lives lost in battle, the estimates increase by about 50%.

zh: 根据这些估计数字，二十世纪军事成本每年大约平均相当于GDP的5 % 。
en: According to these estimates, annual military costs in the twentieth century averaged about 5% of GDP.

zh: 但是，自朝鲜战争的顶峰（7 % ） 以来，全球成本一直在稳步下降，1980年大约为3.5 % ， 现在为1.7%左右。
en: Yet, since the Korean War peak of 7%, global costs have declined steadily, reaching 3.5% in 1980 and about 1.7% today.

zh: 即便是悲观的情景也表明，到2050年这一成本只会上升到1.8 % ； 而在乐观情境中，军事成本将进一步下降到GDP的1.6 % 。
en: Even a pessimistic outlook suggests an increase only to about 1.8% by 2050; under a more optimistic scenario, military costs could decline further, to 1.6% of GDP.

zh: 世界仍然充满各种问题，新闻媒体每天都在披露。
en: There are still plenty of problems in the world, as the news media point out every day.

zh: 我们需要将注意力集中在消除贫困、消灭文盲和推进和平上。
en: And we do need to focus on eliminating poverty, stamping out illiteracy, and promoting peace.

zh: 但我们也需要记住，总体而言世界比我们认为的更美好。
en: But we also need to remember that the world is a better place overall than we think.

zh: 达沃斯启示录
en: The Davos Apocalypse

zh: 劳德代尔堡 — — 在上个月召开的达沃斯世界经济论坛年会上，主要与会者呼吁迅速推广使用清洁能源以应对气候变化。
en: FORT LAUDERDALE – At the World Economic Forum’s annual meeting in Davos last month, leading participants called for a rapid shift to cleaner energy to tackle climate change.

zh: 全球权力精英一边飞到瑞士专属的滑雪胜地，一边呼吁其他人停用化石燃料让人感觉哪里不对劲。
en: There is something unsettling about the global power elite jetting into an exclusive Swiss ski resort and telling the rest of the world to stop using fossil fuels.

zh: 有关世界末日的夸大其词更让人心神不定。
en: The apocalyptic bombast is even more disturbing.

zh: 经合组织秘书长安赫尔·古里亚称“地球已经变暖到十分危险的地步 ， ” 我们必须立即行动才能“避免灾难的发生 ” ； 联合国气候负责人克里斯蒂娜·菲格雷斯认为全球变暖意味着“世界经济正处在危险之中 ” 。
en: According to Angel Gurría, Secretary-General of the OECD, “our planet is warming dangerously,” and we need to act now “to avoid catastrophe”; the United Nations climate chief, Christiana Figueres, maintains that global warming means that “the world economy is at risk.”

zh: 联合国前秘书长科菲·安南夺得最耸人听闻奖，他声称不制止全球变暖是在“拿地球的未来和生命本身做一场可怕的赌博。 ”
en: Former UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan takes the prize for the most extreme rhetoric, claiming that not curbing global warming is “a terrible gamble with the future of the planet and with life itself.”

zh: 但光靠信誓旦旦无法令人信服。
en: Yet, the rhetoric is unconvincing.

zh: 的确，全球变暖切实存在并与人类活动相关。
en: Yes, global warming is real and man-made.

zh: 但制造恐慌和提出不切实际的政策不会对解决问题有任何帮助
en: But creating panic and proposing unrealistic policies will not help in tackling the problem.

zh: 安南和古里亚不约而同地用去年11月的菲律宾台风海燕来证明气候变化造成的损失。
en: Both Annan and Gurría cited Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines last November as evidence of increased climate-change-related damage.

zh: 两人都全然不顾联合国政府间气候变化委员会（IPCC）发布的最新报告，该报告认为“当前数据未显示全球热带气旋频率与上世纪相比有明显趋势性变化 ” ， 并提出“不相信”过去（或未来）数十年中全球变暖会造成任何飓风变化。
en: Never mind that the latest report by the UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) found that “current datasets indicate no significant observed trends in global tropical cyclone frequency over the past century” and reported “low confidence” that any changes in hurricanes in recent (or future) decades had anything to do with global warming.

zh: 安南和古里亚忘了指出测量飓风总活动状况的全球气旋能量指数自20世纪70年代开始就徘徊在最低值。
en: Annan and Gurría also neglected to note that global Accumulated Cyclone Energy, an index for total hurricane activity, is hovering at the lowest values seen since the 1970’s.

zh: 事实上，菲律宾周边强飓风走势从1951年后一直处于下降状态。
en: Indeed, the trend for strong hurricanes around the Philippines has declined since 1951.

zh: 同样，古里亚称2012年猛烈袭击纽约市的飓风桑迪是在气候变化面前不作为的活生生的例子，飓风灾害每年为美国造成“相当于GDP 0.5%的财产损失 ” 。
en: Similarly, Gurría tells us that Hurricane Sandy, which slammed into New York City in 2012, is an example of inaction on climate change, costing the United States “the equivalent of 0.5% of its GDP” each year.

zh: 事实上，自20世纪有记录以来美国现在无强飓风登陆时长已创下历史记录，在此期间内包括飓风桑迪在内经调整的损失成本也略有降低。
en: In fact, the US currently is experiencing the longest absence of intense landfall hurricanes since records began in 1900, while the adjusted damage cost for the US during this period, including Hurricane Sandy, has fallen slightly.

zh: 菲格雷斯称“全球目前因极端天气和灾害造成的年度损失最高可达年度全球GDP的12 % 。
en: Figueres claims “that current annual losses worldwide due to extreme weather and disasters could be a staggering 12% of annual global GDP.”

zh: ”但她所引用的研究结果显示未来可能损失仅占GDP的1-12 % ， 而且这还不是全球数据，而仅限于8座精心挑选的易受气候变化影响的地区或者城市。
en: But the study she cites shows only a possible loss of 1-12% of GDP in the future, and this is estimated not globally but within just eight carefully selected, climate-vulnerable regions or cities.

zh: 相反，按照政府间气候变化专门委员会的研究成果 ， “ 气候变化并不决定经财富人口调整后经济灾害损失的长期趋势。 ”
en: By contrast, according to the IPCC, “long-term trends in economic disaster losses adjusted for wealth and population increases have not been attributed to climate change.”

zh: 相反，经业内审议的大部分经济证据表明截止到2050-2070年左右，因气温上升所造成的净全球经济影响可能是正面的。
en: On the contrary, the bulk of peer-reviewed economic evidence indicates that, up to around 2050-2070, the net global economic impact of rising temperatures is likely to be positive.

zh: 尽管全球变暖导致因酷热和水患造成的死亡人数增加，但寒冷造成的死亡人数减少和二氧化碳含量升高造成的农业高产将抵消前者所带来的损失。
en: Although global warming will create costs stemming from more heat-related deaths and water stress, they will be outweighed by the benefits from many fewer cold-related deaths and higher agricultural productivity from higher levels of CO2.

zh: 全球变暖是长期存在的问题。
en: Global warming is a long-term problem.

zh: 多数模型显示本世纪末全球变暖损失将占全球GDP的1-5 ％ 。
en: Most models indicate that the cost toward the end of the century will be 1-5% of world GDP.

zh: 上述损失绝非微不足道；但也没有“威胁到世界经济 ” 。
en: This is not a trivial loss; but nor does it put “the world economy at risk.”

zh: 相比之下，政府间气候变化专门委员会预计截止本世纪末，发展中国家的普通民众将比今天富裕1,400-1,800 % 。
en: For comparison, the IPCC expects that by the end of the century, the average person in the developing world will be 1,400-1,800% richer than today.

zh: 主要官员的这种错误说法助长了一厢情愿的浪费政策。
en: Such incorrect statements by leading officials reinforce wasteful policies based on wishful thinking.

zh: 菲格雷斯认为随着以中国为首的国家“减少煤炭使用 ” ， 推广气候政策成为越来越明显的势头。
en: Figueres sees “momentum growing toward” climate policies as countries like China “reduce coal use.”

zh: 国际能源机构统计显示现实生活中中国占2012至2014年全球煤炭消费增量的近60 % 。
en: In the real world, China accounts for almost 60% of the global increase in coal consumption from 2012 to 2014, according to the International Energy Agency.

zh: 虽然菲格雷斯称赞中国在2013年大幅增加了太阳能发电量，但中国对煤炭能源的依赖也增长了27倍。
en: While Figueres lauds China for dramatically increasing its solar-power capacity in 2013, the increase in China’s reliance on coal power was 27 times greater.

zh: 菲格雷斯不了解现实导致她不仅认为中国的气候变化对策是“正确的 ” ， 而且还臆测中国的成功因其“政治体制避免了美国等国家存在的立法障碍。
en: Figueres’s weak grasp on the facts has led her not only to conclude that China is “doing it right” on climate change, but also to speculate that China has succeeded because its “political system avoids some of the legislative hurdles seen in countries including the US.”

zh: ”换句话说，联合国首席气候官员似乎在暗示独裁政治制度更符合地球的需要。
en: In other words, the UN’s top climate official seems to be suggesting that an authoritarian political system is better for the planet.

zh: 现实情况是2012年全球推广风能和太阳能最多减排了2.75亿吨二氧化碳，却因此耗费了高达600亿美元的补贴。
en: The fact remains that global wind and solar power usage in 2012 cut, at most, 275 million tons of CO2, while soaking up $60 billion in subsidies.

zh: 由此生产的清洁电能可能价值100亿美元，因此减排每吨二氧化碳约耗费180美元成本。
en: With the electricity worth possibly $10 billion, the average cost of cutting a ton of CO2 is about $180.

zh: 经业内审议二氧化碳损失的最大估计值为5美元每吨，也就是说太阳能和风能发电每耗费1美元避免了约0.03美元的气候损失。
en: The biggest peer-reviewed estimate of the damage cost of CO2 is about $5 per ton. This means that solar and wind power avoid about $0.03 of climate damage for every dollar spent.

zh: 对比一下更明智的技术解决方案。
en: Compare this to smarter technological solutions.

zh: 从短期看，美国页岩能源革命已经用更便宜清洁的天然气取代了高污染煤炭。
en: In the short run, the US shale-energy revolution has replaced high-polluting coal with cheaper, cleaner natural gas.

zh: 此举减少了约3亿吨美国二氧化碳排放 — — 超过全世界所有风能及太阳能减排的总和 — — 同时还为美国人节省了能源开支1000亿美元。
en: This has cut about 300 million tons of US emissions – more than all the world’s solar and wind power combined – and at the same time has profited Americans by saving them $100 billion in energy costs.

zh: 长远看，当前绿色能源研发投资将使未来可再生能源价格低于化石燃料，从而创造出环境和经济的双赢选择。
en: In the long run, current investment in green research and development will help drive the price of future renewable energy below that of fossil fuels, enabling a choice that is both environmentally and economically sound.

zh: 同时，即便大幅减排二氧化碳也不会对今后50-100年的飓风灾害造成多大影响。
en: In the meantime, even dramatic cuts in CO2 emissions will have very little impact on hurricanes 50-100 years from now.

zh: 相反，让数十亿人摆脱贫困不仅从本质上是桩善举；同时也能使社会在应对全球变暖和其他原因所导致的极端天气时更加从容。
en: Lifting billions of people out of poverty, however, would not only be intrinsically good; it would also make societies much more resilient in the face of extreme weather, whether caused by global warming or not.

zh: 遗憾的是，我们在达沃斯看到全球气候辩论充斥着虚构和一厢情愿。
en: Unfortunately, as we saw at Davos, the global climate debate is polluted with myths and wishful thinking.

zh: 只有尽快改正，我们才能实现少花钱办好事的目标。
en: If we want to do more good at lower cost, we should start by cleaning it up.

zh: 贫困的环境
en: The Environment of Poverty

zh: 哥本哈根—尽管寿命预期有了提高、教育更加普及、贫困和饥饿率也有所下降，但世界在改善人民生活质量方面仍有很长的路要走。
en: COPENHAGEN – Despite gains in life expectancy, expanded access to education, and lower rates of poverty and hunger, the world has a long way to go to improve the quality of people’s lives.

zh: 近十亿人仍然食不果腹，12亿人生活在极端贫困中，26亿人无法获得清洁水 和卫生设施，近三十亿人在家中用有害燃料取暖。
en: Almost a billion people still go to bed hungry, 1.2 billion live in extreme poverty, 2.6 billion lack access to clean drinking water and sanitation, and almost three billion burn harmful materials inside their homes to keep warm.

zh: 每年都有一千万人死于疟疾、艾滋病和结核病等传染病以及肺炎和痢疾。
en: Each year, ten million people die from infectious diseases like malaria, HIV, and tuberculosis, along with pneumonia and diarrhea.

zh: 据估计，缺少水和卫生设施每年也至少造成300,000人死亡。
en: Lack of water and sanitation is estimated to cause at least 300,000 deaths each year.

zh: 营养不良至少要夺走140万儿童的生命。
en: Malnourishment claims at least 1.4 million children’s lives.

zh: 贫困是主要杀手之一。
en: Poverty is one of the main killers.

zh: 因为贫困，儿童无法获得合理的营养，只能生活在水不干净、卫生设施不足的社区。
en: It is why children do not receive proper nutrition and live in neighborhoods with unclean water and inadequate sanitation.

zh: 因为贫困，疟疾等完全可预防的疾病每年要杀死 600,000人；许多人太穷以至于买不起药品和防虫蚊帐，而政府在杀灭携带病菌的蚊子或遏制和治疗传染病暴发方面做得也太差。
en: And it is why an entirely preventable disease like malaria kills 600,000 people each year; many are too poor to buy drugs and bed nets, while governments are often too poor to eradicate the mosquitos that carry the disease or contain and treat outbreaks when they occurs.

zh: 但其中一些最致命的问题是环境问题。
en: But some of the most lethal problems are environmental.

zh: 根据世界卫生组织的数据，每年大约七百万人因为空气污染而死亡，其中大部分是因为在室内燃烧柴枝和粪便而致死。
en: According to the World Health Organization, about seven million deaths each year are caused by air pollution, with the majority a result of burning twigs and dung inside.

zh: 此前，含铅油漆和汽油据估计每年也要造成150,000多人死亡，而全球变暖造成的死亡人数为141,000人。
en: Previous generations’ use of lead in paints and gasoline is estimated to cause almost 700,000 deaths annually. Ground-level ozone pollution kills more than 150,000 people per year, while global warming causes another 141,000 deaths.

zh: 自然发生放射性氡（用作室内建筑材料）每年也要杀死大约100,000人。
en: Naturally occurring radioactive radon that builds up inside homes kills about 100,000 people every year.

zh: 在这里，贫困也起到了很大的作用。
en: Here, too, poverty plays a disproportionate role.

zh: 没有人会为了取乐每天在房子里点火；之所以如此是因为得不到取暖和烹饪所需要的电力。
en: No one lights a fire every night inside their house for fun; they do so because they lack the electricity needed to stay warm and to cook.

zh: 尽管室外空气污染部分原因在于不成熟的工业化，但这对穷人来说是一个临时性的权衡问题 — — 摆脱贫困、传染病和室内空气污染，从而能够更好地负担食品、医疗和教育成本。
en: While outdoor air pollution is partly caused by incipient industrialization, this represents a temporary tradeoff for the poor – escaping hunger, infectious disease, and indoor air pollution to be better able to afford food, health care, and education.

zh: 当国家足够富裕时，就能够负担更清洁的技术、开始实施环境立法以减少室外空气污染，墨西哥城和智利的圣地亚哥现在就是如此。
en: When countries become sufficiently rich, they can afford cleaner technology and begin to enact environmental legislation to reduce outdoor air pollution, as we now see in Mexico City and Santiago, Chile.

zh: 反贫困的最佳工具之一是贸易。
en: One of the best anti-poverty tools is trade.

zh: 过去三十年中，中国通过迅速融入全球经济的战略让6.8亿人走出了贫困。
en: China has lifted 680 million people out of poverty over the past three decades through a strategy of rapid integration into the global economy.

zh: 扩大整个发展中世界的自由贸易（特别是农业贸易）也许是这个十年��策者所能实施的最重要的减贫措施。
en: Extending free trade, especially for agriculture, throughout the developing world is likely the single most important anti-poverty measure that policymakers could implement this decade.

zh: 但另一个令人鼓舞之处是，在过去15年中，世界用于帮助穷人的钱正在增加，用实际值衡量，发展援助规模几乎翻倍。
en: But it is also encouraging that the world is spending more money to help the world’s poor, with development aid almost doubling in real terms over the past 15 years.

zh: 这扩大了帮助饱受疟疾、艾滋病、营养不良和疟疾的人群的资源。
en: This has boosted resources to help people suffering from malaria, HIV, malnutrition, and diarrhea.

zh: 此外，尽管数据方面存在一些不一致，但显然世界在环境方面的支出也在增加。
en: And, though the data are somewhat inconsistent, it is clear that the world is spending more on the environment.

zh: 环境项目援助占双边援助的比例从1980年的5%左右增加到今天的近30 % ， 相当于每年250美元。
en: Aid for environmental projects has increased from about 5% of measured bilateral aid in 1980 to almost 30% today, bringing the annual total to about $25 billion.

zh: 这听起来很不错。
en: That sounds great.

zh: 世界能够日益将援助集中于主要环境问题 — — 室内和室外空气污染以及铅和臭氧污染 — — 几乎所有与环境有关的死亡都是由这些问题造成的。
en: The world can increasingly focus aid on the main environmental problems – indoor and outdoor air pollution, along with lead and ozone pollution – that cause almost all environment-related deaths.

zh: 不幸的是，事实并非如此。
en: Unfortunately, that is not happening.

zh: 几乎所有环境援助 — — 根据经合组织的数据，总量达到了215亿美元左右 — — 都被用在了气候变化上。
en: Almost all environmental aid – about $21.5 billion, according to the OECD – is spent on climate change.

zh: 毫无疑问，全球变暖是我们应该巧妙应对的问题（尽管我们的历史记录并不令人鼓舞 ） 。
en: There is no doubt that global warming is a problem that we should tackle smartly (though our track record so far has not been encouraging).

zh: 但这样做需要廉价绿色能源（特别是在发达国家 ） ， 而不是将援助资金用于减少发展中国家的二氧化碳等温室气体的排放量。
en: But doing so requires cheap green energy, especially in the developed world, not spending aid money to reduce developing countries’ emissions of greenhouse gases like CO₂.

zh: 事实上，我们设置优先项的方式具有根本的不合理性。
en: Indeed, there is something fundamentally immoral about the way we set our priorities.

zh: 经合组织估计，世界花在减少温室气体排放上的发展资金总数至少在110亿美元。
en: The OECD estimates that the world spends at least $11 billion of total development money just to cut greenhouse-gas emissions.

zh: 其中很大一部分通过风电、水电和太阳能电等可再生电力实现。
en: A large part of this is through renewable power like wind, hydro, and solar.

zh: 比如，日本最近拨出3亿美元发展援助用于补贴印度的太阳能电和风电项目。
en: For example, Japan recently granted $300 million of its development aid to subsidize solar and wind power in India.

zh: 如果这110亿美元如同当前全球开支比例一样全部用于太阳能电和风电，全球二氧化碳排放量每年可以减少大约5,000万吨。
en: If all $11 billion were spent on solar and wind in the same proportion as current global spending, global CO₂ emissions would fall by about 50 million tons each year.

zh: 用标准气候模型计算，这对气温的降低效应可以忽略不计 — — 到2100年可降低0.00002℃ — — 相当于让截至本世纪末的全球变暖趋势停止七个多小时。
en: Run on a standard climate model, this would reduce temperatures so trivially – about 0.00002oC in the year 2100 – that it is the equivalent of postponing global warming by the end of the century by a bit more than seven hours.

zh: 当然，气候支持者也许会指出，太阳能板和风电涡轮机能为大约2,200万人提供电力 — — 尽管无法做到不间断供电。
en: Of course, climate campaigners might point out that the solar panels and wind turbines will give electricity – albeit intermittently – to about 22 million people.

zh: 但如果同样数量的钱用于燃气电气化，我们可以让近1亿人告别黑暗和贫困。
en: But if that same money were used for gas electrification, we could lift almost 100 million people out of darkness and poverty.

zh: 此外，这110亿美元可以用于解决更加紧迫的问题。
en: Moreover, that $11 billion could be used to address even more pressing issues.

zh: 哥本哈根共识中心（Copenhagen Consensus）的计算表明，如果这笔钱用于预防疟疾和结核病以及推广儿童免疫，每年可以挽救近三百万条生命。
en: Calculations from the Copenhagen Consensus show that it could save almost three million lives each year if directed toward preventing malaria and tuberculosis, and increasing childhood immunization.

zh: 这笔钱还可以用于增加农业生产率，在长期让2亿人告别饥饿，同时通过早期预警系统减轻自然灾害。
en: It could also be used to increase agricultural productivity, saving 200 million from starvation in the long run, while ameliorating natural disasters through early-warning systems.

zh: 此外还能有结余用于帮助发展中国家开发艾滋病疫苗、提供心脏病药物、推广乙肝疫苗，每年让3,100万儿童免于饥饿。
en: And there would be money left over to help develop an HIV vaccine, deliver drugs to treat heart attacks, provide a Hepatitis B vaccine to the developing world, and prevent 31 million children from starving each year.

zh: 让全球变暖停止7小时真的是更好的选择吗？
en: Is it really better to postpone global warming by seven hours?

zh: 即使我们在此后一百年继续将这笔钱用于阻止温室气体增加，截至世纪末，我们也只能让全球变暖进程停止不到一个月 — — 这一结果对地球上的任何人都无法形成实质影响。
en: Even if we continue spending $11 billion to avoid an increase in greenhouse gases for a hundred years, we would postpone global warming by less than one month by the end of the century – an achievement with no practical impact for anyone on the planet.

zh: 为何世界会有意地选择如此低效的帮助方针？
en: Why does the world consciously choose to help so ineffectively?

zh: 也许环境援助主要目的不是为了帮助世界，而是为了让我们感到好受些吧？
en: Could it be that environmental aid is not primarily about helping the world, but about making us feel better about ourselves?

zh: 浮华之风
en: Winds of Vanity

zh: 哥本哈根 — — 丹麦首都哥本哈根寄希望于到2025年成为世界首座二氧化碳中性城市。
en: COPENHAGEN – Copenhagen, Denmark’s capital, wants to be the world’s first CO2-neutral city by 2025.

zh: 但其他许多善意的城市和国家已经发现，削减碳排放远不像表面看上去那样简单，可能在相当程度上需要在账目上做手脚。
en: But, as many other well-meaning cities and countries have discovered, cutting CO2 significantly is more difficult than it seems, and may require quite a bit of creative accounting.

zh: 更令人惊讶的是，哥本哈根政治家们自信地宣称，现在减排二氧化碳终将使这座城市及其居民更加富裕，化石燃料价格上涨后今天昂贵的绿色能源投资终将带来回报。
en: More surprisingly, Copenhagen’s politicians have confidently declared that cutting CO2 now will ultimately make the city and its citizens wealthier, with today’s expensive green-energy investments more than paying off when fossil-fuel prices rise.

zh: 但刻意缩小选择范围怎样才能使未来更美好？
en: But how can deliberately limiting one’s options improve one’s prospects?

zh: 听上去这更像是环保人士的观点 — — 而这些人很有可能是错误的。
en: These sound more like the arguments of green campaigners – and they are most likely wrong.

zh: 哥本哈根实现零排放面临的首要挑战是找不到经济有效的能源替代某些碳排放燃料，特别是汽车燃料。
en: The first challenge that Copenhagen faces in reaching its zero-emissions goal is the lack of cost-effective alternatives for some sources of CO2, particularly automobiles.

zh: 丹麦的电动车补助已居世界首位，电动车可以免交180%的车辆登记税。
en: Denmark already provides the world’s largest subsidy to electric cars by exempting them from its marginal 180% car-registration tax.

zh: 保有量最大的电动车日产聆风（Leaf）的边际免税额已达85,000美元（合63,000欧元 ） 。
en: For the most popular electric car, the Nissan Leaf, this exemption is worth $85,000 (€63,000).

zh: 但丹麦270万辆机动车中电动车仍只有1，536辆。
en: Yet, just 1,536 of Denmark’s 2.7 million cars are electric.

zh: 此外还要解决风力发电的固有难题：保证城市在不刮风的时候也能正常运转。
en: There is also the challenge inherent in wind-generated electricity: ensuring that the city can continue to run when the wind is not blowing.

zh: 丹麦为此制定了发电战略，在必要时启动燃煤发电，而不计入净排放量。
en: To address this problem, Copenhagen has had to devise an electricity-generation strategy that enables it sometimes to run on coal-fired power when necessary, without creating net emissions.

zh: 哥本哈根市计划在大哥本哈根区及周边的浅水区建设100多座风电机组。
en: The city’s plan is to build more than 100 wind turbines within the greater Copenhagen area and in the shallow waters around it.

zh: 风电机组的总发电量为360兆瓦，并入电网后足以满足哥本哈根的电力需求 — — 剩余电量可用于抵消城市剩余的二氧化碳排放，包括哥本哈根市数百万辆非电动车。
en: With a combined output of 360 megawatts, which will feed electricity into the grid, these turbines will more than cover Copenhagen’s electricity needs – and the surplus can be used to offset the city’s remaining CO2 emissions, including from the city’s millions of non-electric cars.

zh: 因此只有当周边区域不追求二氧化碳零排放时哥本哈根市才能实现其目标。
en: Copenhagen’s success thus depends on the surrounding areas not aiming for CO2 neutrality.

zh: 归根结底，整个账面操作只有当别人仍在使用哥本哈根不可预测的风电矢志替代的化石燃料时才会有效。
en: After all, the whole accounting exercise works only if others are still using fossil fuels that Copenhagen’s unpredictable wind power can replace.

zh: 从这个意义上讲，正义的机会被哥本哈根霸占了。
en: In this sense, Copenhagen is hogging the chance to feel righteous.

zh: 只有煤、石油和天然气等传统能源价格在未来几年内上涨预期兑现，哥本哈根政治领袖许诺的这种碳中性政策才能“确保积极的总体经济状况并为哥本哈根人带来经济回报 ” 。
en: The city’s political leaders promise that this strategy for attaining carbon neutrality “provides an overall positive economic picture and will lead to economic benefits for Copenhageners” based on the expectation that prices for conventional energy sources like coal, oil, and gas will rise in the coming years.

zh: 但这种假设最常听到的理由 — — 人类正在快速消耗这些稀缺资源 — — 却因为创新近年来将石油、天然气及煤炭储量有效扩大至前所未有的水平而并不符合实际发生的状况。
en: But the often-heard justification for this assumption – that humanity is rapidly depleting these scarce resources – is inconsistent with real-world events, as innovation has effectively expanded oil, gas, and coal reserves to unprecedented levels in recent years.

zh: 我���仔细梳理一下哥本哈根唯一最大的节约来源风力发电计划。
en: Consider Copenhagen’s wind-turbine plan, the single largest expected source of savings.

zh: 风电项目的建设维护总成本约合9.19亿美元，就算加上高额的碳排放税也仅能节约1.42亿美元，这意味着该项目的价值所在 — — 节约2.61亿美元 — — 主要来自节省的10.4亿美元电费支出上。
en: The total cost of construction and maintenance is projected to be $919 million. Even assuming a very large carbon tax, this amounts to a rather paltry $142 million, meaning that the project’s value – $261 million in savings – stems largely from the $1.04 billion saved on electricity payments.

zh: 尽管听起来非常诱人，但这取决于到2030年化石燃料发电电价是否会大涨68 % 。
en: While that sounds impressive, it depends on a massive 68% increase in the price of fossil-fuel-produced electricity by 2030.

zh: 并不只有哥本哈根做出这样的假设；英国能源与气候变化部预测到2030年化石燃料发电电价会出现51%的涨幅。
en: And Copenhagen is not alone in making such assumptions; the United Kingdom’s Department of Energy & Climate Change estimates a 51% price increase by 2030.

zh: 这些预测很可能并不现实。
en: It is likely that these projections are unrealistic.

zh: 只需看看支撑绝大部分全球电力生产的煤和天然气的长期价格走势就知道了。
en: Look at the long-term price trends of coal and gas, which power the vast majority of global electricity production.

zh: 尽管最近略有上涨，但实际煤炭价格自20世纪50年代后一直处于下降趋势之中。
en: Despite a recent increase, real coal prices have been trending downward since the 1950s.

zh: 美国的页岩气革命在水力压裂法的推动下已经使天然气价格降到20世纪70年代石油危机天然气取得主导地位后的最低水平。
en: In the United States, the shale-gas revolution, facilitated by the development of hydraulic fracturing (“fracking”), has brought prices to their lowest levels since natural gas gained prominence after the oil crises of the 1970s.

zh: 未来十年随着更多国家着手开发页岩气储量，这种降价趋势极有可能将得以延续，并进一步降低发电价格。
en: With many more countries set to tap shale-gas reserves over the next decade, this downward trend will most likely continue, helping to lower the price of electricity generation further.

zh: 这也是极光能源研究所近期预测今后三十年电价显著下降的理由。
en: That is why Aurora Energy Research recently projected a significant decline in electricity prices for the next three decades.

zh: 水力压裂技术也使美国得以发掘其庞大的页岩油储量​​，使其成为领先沙特阿拉伯的世界第一大石油生产国。
en: Fracking technology has also enabled the US to tap its large shale-oil reserves, making it the world’s largest petroleum producer, ahead of Saudi Arabia.

zh: 花旗集团预测到2020年石油售价将降至仅75美元一桶，而经合组合国际预测部前负责人认为石油价格将逼近每桶50美元。
en: Citigroup estimates that, by 2020, oil will cost just $75 per barrel, and the former head of international forecasting at the OECD suggests that the number could be closer to $50.

zh: 现实对英国和哥本哈根的气候官僚非常不利，因为它降低了清洁能源的吸引力。
en: This is inconvenient for climate mandarins in the UK and Copenhagen alike, because it reduces clean energy’s allure.

zh: 即使以化石燃料为动力的电价保持不变，哥本哈根的风电机组也将成为净损失。
en: Even if fossil-fuel-powered electricity prices remain constant, Copenhagen’s wind turbines become a net drain.

zh: 如果极光研究所的预言最终实现，哥本哈根的风电项目将成为重大的失败，其成本超过节电总价50 % 。
en: If Aurora’s forecast proves correct, Copenhagen’s wind project would become a massive failure, costing 50% more than the saved electricity is worth.

zh: 民众不应容许政客自我感觉良好地将公共资金耗费在以遥远、不可靠的预测为基础的气候项目上，而应当鼓励领导人投资洁净能源研发。 此举的目的是使可再生能源便宜到足以超越化石燃料占领市场。
en: Instead of allowing politicians to spend public money on feel-good climate projects based on distant – and unreliable – predictions, citizens should encourage their leaders to invest those funds in clean-energy research and development, with the goal of making renewables inexpensive enough to overcome fossil fuels in the market.

zh: 像哥本哈根这类计划无论看起来多令人振奋，最终都不过是政绩工程，会使民众付出昂贵的代价。
en: Initiatives like Copenhagen’s, however wonderful they sound, are ultimately little more than costly vanity projects.

zh: 气候政策陷阱
en: The Climate-Policy Trap

zh: 罗马 — — 今天应对气候变化的政策成本远远高于它所产生的效益。
en: ROME – Today’s policies to combat climate change cost much more than the benefits they produce.

zh: 不幸的是，错误的政治选择往往令政策效益进一步恶化。
en: Unfortunately, bad political choices often make these policies even less cost-effective.

zh: 比方说欧盟的20-20政策，旨在实现2020年二氧化碳排放低于1990年20%的目标。
en: Consider the European Union’s 20-20 policy, which targets a 20% reduction in CO2 emissions below 1990 levels by 2020.

zh: 考量上述策略是否可行非常重要，不仅因为欧盟执行的是全世界涉及面最广、最雄心勃勃的气候政策，还因为其他气候政策也有着相似的缺陷。
en: It is important to examine this approach, not only because the EU is pursuing the world’s largest and most ambitious climate policy, but also because other climate policies suffer from similar shortcomings.

zh: 实现20%目标成本最低、效率最高的方法莫过于建立统一的欧盟碳市场，欧盟到2020年年均需耗费约960亿美元来实现这一目标。
en: The most cost-efficient way to achieve the 20% target would be to operate a single, EU-wide carbon-market, which would cost the EU about $96 billion annually by 2020.

zh: 但这一策略的全球效益却要低得多。
en: But the benefits to the entire world would be much lower.

zh: 事实上，欧盟气候政策唯一一次同行评估概述预测它每年可以避免约1000亿美元的气候损失。
en: Indeed, the only peer-reviewed overview of EU climate policy estimates that it can avoid climate-related damage of about $10 billion per year.

zh: 因此，每1美元投入，欧盟可以避免10美分的损失。
en: So, for every dollar spent, the EU stands to avoid about ten cents of damage.

zh: 这不是说气候变化不重要；只是说欧盟并未执行明智的气候政策。
en: This does not mean that climate change is not important; it means only that the EU’s climate policy is not smart.

zh: 纵观本世纪，理想中的欧盟政策将耗资7万多亿美元，但气温只能少升高0.05oC，此外还有区区9毫米的海平面下降。
en: Over the course of this century, the ideal EU policy would cost more than $7 trillion, yet it would reduce the temperature rise by just 0.05oC and lower sea levels by a trivial nine millimeters.

zh: 投入如此巨额资金后，造成的差异我们甚至都察觉不到。
en: After spending all that money, we would not even be able to tell the difference.

zh: 欧盟政策的倡导者往往辩解无论如何都应该执行这样的政策，因为全球变暖的风险也许比现在估计的严重得多。
en: Advocates of the EU’s policy often argue that we should pursue such policies nonetheless, because there is a risk that global warming will be much more severe than currently expected.

zh: 虽然这种说法原则上成立，但经济模型显示最好的政策对缓和危险也没有多大效果。
en: But, though this argument is valid in principle, economic models show that this risk has only a moderate effect on the best policy.

zh: 不仅如此，过去10-17年温度停止上升已经使结果不太可能比预期更差。
en: Moreover, the absence of any temperature rise over the past 10-17 years has made such worse-than-expected outcomes extremely unlikely.

zh: 错误的政治决策导致气候政策异乎寻常的糟糕才是真正的危险因素。
en: The real risk concerns the potential for bad political choices to make climate policies worse than necessary.

zh: 欧盟不只为实现碳排放目标建立了统一的碳市场。
en: The EU did not just implement a single carbon market in order to meet its target for CO2 emissions.

zh: 相反，欧盟一系列内部自相矛盾的政策让本来就不合理的安排付出更大的代价。
en: Instead, the EU made a bad deal a lot costlier through a host of partly contradictory policies.

zh: 比方说，欧盟要求到2020年风能及太阳能等可再生能源必须占能源供应的20 % ， 虽然这根本不是最廉价的减排方法。
en: For example, the EU demanded that renewables like wind and solar account for 20% of energy supplies by 2020, though this is by no means the cheapest way to cut emissions.

zh: 其实安装风力发电机组无法减排多余的二氧化碳，因为全欧盟的碳交易计划已经将总排放量规定死了。
en: In fact, putting up a wind turbine cuts no extra CO2, because total emissions are already capped under the EU-wide carbon-trading scheme.

zh: 其结果是当英国安装一台风力发电设备，葡萄牙和波兰烧煤就变得更便宜了。
en: It simply means that when Great Britain installs a wind turbine, it becomes cheaper to burn coal in Portugal or Poland.

zh: 鉴于如此愚蠢的政策并平均所有宏观经济模型，欧盟每年耗资2800亿美元挽回200亿美元损失的可能性更大。
en: Taking into account such poor policies and averaging all macroeconomic models, the EU is more likely to pay around $280 billion per year to avert $10 billion in damage.

zh: 换句话讲，欧盟气候政策的不合理设计增加了两倍成本，每耗资1美元只能防止3美分的气候损失。
en: In other words, the poor design of EU climate policies triples the cost and prevents only three cents of climate damage per dollar spent.

zh: 但这还不是最坏情况，因为这些模型仍然假设欧盟选择最廉价的可再生能源来满足其要求。
en: But it gets worse, because these models still assume that the EU picks the cheapest renewables to fulfill its requirements.

zh: 实际情况恰恰相反，多数欧盟国家为最昂贵的可再生能源提供更高的补贴。
en: Instead, most EU countries give higher subsidies to the most costly renewables.

zh: 比方说，在���国安装海岸风电机组减排一吨二氧化碳约耗资约35美元，每投入1美元能避免约14美分的气候损失。
en: For example, cutting a ton of CO2 with on-shore wind turbines in Germany probably costs about $35, avoiding about 14 cents of climate damage per dollar.

zh: 但海上风电机组减排一吨二氧化碳约耗资150美元，每投资1美元只避免了3美分的气候损失。
en: But offshore wind turbines cost about $150 per ton of CO2, avoiding just three cents of climate damage per dollar.

zh: 生物燃料的效率更差强人意，每减排一吨二氧化碳耗资超过300美元，1美元投入所起作用的略高于1美分。
en: Biofuels are even less efficient, costing more than $300 per ton of CO2 avoided, while doing just over one cent of good per dollar.

zh: 绝对高价的当数太阳能产品，每减排一吨二氧化碳耗资超过800美元，1美元投入所起的作用还不到1美分。
en: And solar takes the absolute prize, costing more than $800 per ton of CO2 to do less than a cent of good per dollar spent.

zh: 付出这种代价的还不止是欧洲。
en: These prices are not unique to Europe.

zh: 比方说中国要为由风能替代的每吨二氧化碳排放花费38美元，而美国则要为生物燃料替代的每吨二氧化碳排放耗资约600美元。
en: China pays $38 per ton of CO2 avoided with wind power, for example, while the US pays around $600 for cutting a ton of CO2 with biofuels.

zh: 此外，欧盟决心削减的部分内部排量不过是转移到其他地区。
en: Moreover, when the EU decides to cut its domestic emissions, part of the reduction simply migrates elsewhere.

zh: 如果欧盟生产某种产品因能源因素导致成本过大，这种产品很可能被转到其他能源便宜的地方生产，之后再进口回欧洲。
en: If making a product in the EU costs more because of higher energy costs, the product will likely be made somewhere else, where energy is cheaper, and then imported into the EU.

zh: 其实，最新研究结果显示38%的欧盟碳减排渗漏到了别处，这意味着欧洲的气候政策每耗费1美元避免的气候损失不是3美分，而是不到2美分。
en: In fact, new studies show that 38% of the EU carbon cuts leak elsewhere, meaning that European climate policy avoids not three cents of climate damage per dollar spent, but less than two.

zh: 从1990年到2008年，欧盟二氧化碳实现减排约2.7亿公吨。
en: From 1990 to 2008, the EU cut its emissions by about 270 million metric tons of CO2.

zh: 但事实证明单单来自中国一地进口增量的额外排放就几乎相当于欧盟的减排额。
en: But it turns out that the increase in imports from China alone implied an almost equal volume of extra emissions outside the EU.

zh: 因此从本质上看，欧盟只是将部分排放量向海外转移。
en: Essentially, the EU had simply shipped part of its emissions offshore.

zh: 最后，错误的气候政策所带来的负面影响还不仅局限在资金领域。
en: Finally, the negative effects of poor climate policies are not just financial.

zh: 现在光是欧盟就年耗资超过100亿美元、每1美元投资效益还不到1美分的生物燃料也在侵占粮食耕地。
en: Biofuels, for which the EU alone is now paying more than $10 billion annually to do less than one cent of good for every dollar spent, also take up fields that otherwise would have produced food.

zh: 这意味着粮食生产转移到别处，往往通过砍伐森林创造出的农业用地，从而释放出更多的二氧化碳并危及生物多样性。
en: That means that food production moves elsewhere, often to farmland created by cutting down forests, which releases more CO2 and damages biodiversity.

zh: 这种状况也推动食品价格上涨，迄今为止至少令3000万贫困人口陷入饥饿，到2020年预计还有4千到1亿3千万人会加入饥饿大军。
en: It also drives up food prices, which so far has pushed at least 30 million poor people into starvation, with another 40-130 million expected to be starving by 2020.

zh: 我们需要用更明智的策略应对气候变化。
en: We need a smarter approach to tackling climate change.

zh: 我们不能满足于以高得离谱的成本降低几吨二氧化碳排放，而要为降低绿色能源长期成本的研发创新项目进行投资。 只有这样才能让绿色能源实现普及。
en: Rather than relying on cutting a few tons of incredibly overpriced CO2 now, we need to invest in research and development aimed at innovating down the cost of green energy in the long run, so that everyone will switch.

zh: 目前来看，现行气候政策非常差劲 — — 而政客们一直想方设法让政策更糟糕。
en: For now, our current climate policies are poor – and our politicians consistently find ways to make them even poorer.

zh: 他们或许可以取悦农民和其他利益团体，但总体而言他们只是哄抬成本，并削减已经少得不能再少的效益。
en: They may please farmers and other interest groups, but overall they simply drive up costs and reduce already-minimal benefits.

zh: 更好的世界在这里
en: A Better World Is Here

zh: 哥本哈根—几百年来，悲观者和乐观者就世界的状态争论不休。
en: COPENHAGEN – For centuries, optimists and pessimists have argued over the state of the world.

zh: 悲观者认为更多的人意味着更少的食物，上升的资源需求意味着枯竭和战争，而近几十年来，扩张的产能意味着更多的污染和全球变暖。
en: Pessimists see a world where more people means less food, where rising demand for resources means depletion and war, and, in recent decades, where boosting production capacity means more pollution and global warming.

zh: 被当前一代悲观者奉为圭臬的《增长的极限》影响着当今环境运动。
en: One of the current generation of pessimists’ sacred texts, The Limits to Growth, influences the environmental movement to this day.

zh: 相反，乐观者兴高采烈地宣布所有东西 — — 人类健康、生活水平、环境质量，等等 — — 都在变得更好。
en: The optimists, by contrast, cheerfully claim that everything – human health, living standards, environmental quality, and so on – is getting better.

zh: 他们的反对者把他们看作“富饶派”经济学家，相信市场可以纠正一切问题。
en: Their opponents think of them as  “cornucopian” economists, placing their faith in the market to fix any and all problems.

zh: 但是，我们不应该有选择性地采纳符合衰败和进步的宏大叙事的事实和故事，而应该全方位地比较人类经验，研究世界是否真的在变好或变坏。
en: But, rather than picking facts and stories to fit some grand narrative of decline or progress, we should try to compare across all areas of human existence to see if the world really is doing better or worse.

zh: 我与21位世界顶尖经济学家一起正在做这个尝试，我们开发了一套150年来记分卡。
en: Together with 21 of the world’s top economists, I have tried to do just that, developing a scorecard spanning 150 years.

zh: 在十个领域中 — — 包括健康、教育、战争、性别、空气污染、气候变化和生物多样性 — — 经济学家回答同一个问题：自1900至2013年的每一年，这一问题的相对成本是多少？ 并且对2014—2050年的这一数字做出预测。
en: Across ten areas – including health, education, war, gender, air pollution, climate change, and biodiversity – the economists all answered the same question: What was the relative cost of this problem in every year since 1900, all the way to 2013, with predictions to 2050.

zh: 经济学家对从死亡、不健康和文盲到全球变暖引发的湿地破坏和台风伤害增加的一切做出经典经济估值，以此得出每一个问题的成本。
en: Using classic economic valuations of everything from lost lives, bad health, and illiteracy to wetlands destruction and increased hurricane damage from global warming, the economists show how much each problem costs.

zh: 为了评估问题的严重程度，该成本还与可用来纠正问题的资源总量相比较。
en: To estimate the magnitude of the problem, it is compared to the total resources available to fix it.

zh: 这让我们了解问题的规模 — — 占GDP的比重。
en: This gives us the problem’s size as a share of GDP.

zh: 自1900年以来的趋势颇有些出人意料。
en: And the trends since 1900 are sometimes surprising.

zh: 以性别不平等为例。
en: Consider gender inequality.

zh: 从根本上说，我们把近一半的世界人口排除在了生产之外。
en: Essentially, we were excluding almost half the world’s population from production.

zh: 1900年，全球劳动大军中只有15%是女性。
en: In 1900, only 15% of the global workforce was female.

zh: 女性劳动参与率低下有何损失？
en: What is the loss from lower female workforce participation?

zh: 即使考虑了一些女性必须承担不受薪的家务劳动以及女性教育成本的增加，其损失至少占1900年全球GDP的17 % 。
en: Even taking into account that someone has to do unpaid housework and the increased costs of female education, the loss was at least 17% of global GDP in 1900.

zh: 如今，女性参与率有所提高，工资差距有所降低，损失降到了7 % ， 到2050年预计将进一步降低到4 % 。
en: Today, with higher female participation and lower wage differentials, the loss is 7% – and projected to fall to 4% by 2050.

zh: 也许令人大吃一惊的是，积分牌预计在1900—2025年气候变化极有可能带来越来越多的净收益，每年可达GDP的1.5%左右。
en: It will probably come as a big surprise that climate change is expected to be mostly an increasing net benefit – rising to about 1.5% of GDP per year – in the period from 1900 to 2025.

zh: 这是因为全球变暖有利有弊；温和的变暖能给大家带来好处。
en: This is because global warming has mixed effects; for moderate warming, the benefits prevail.

zh: 一方面，由于二氧化碳是一种肥料，其水平的增加有利于农业，最大的积极效应也在于此，相当于GDP的0.8 % 。
en: On one hand, because CO2 works as a fertilizer, higher levels have been a boon for agriculture, which comprises the biggest positive impact, at 0.8% of GDP.

zh: 类似地，温和变暖减少了严寒造成的死亡，其数量超过因变暖导致的酷暑造成的死亡。
en: Likewise, moderate warming prevents more cold deaths than the number of extra heat deaths that it causes.

zh: 温和变暖还减少了取暖需求，节约的成本超过制冷成本的增加，这部分带来约GDP的0.4%的收益。
en: It also reduces demand for heating more than it increases the costs of cooling, implying a gain of about 0.4% of GDP.

zh: 另一方面，变暖增加了水压，大约造成GDP的0.2%的损失；对湿地等生态系统也有消极影响，成本大约为GDP的0.1 % 。
en: On the other hand, warming increases water stress, costing about 0.2% of GDP, and negatively affects ecosystems like wetlands, at a cost of about 0.1%.

zh: 但是，随着温度的升高，成本会增加而收益会降低，导致净收益的大降。
en: As temperatures rise, however, the costs will rise and the benefits will decline, leading to a dramatic reduction in net benefits.

zh: 2070年后，全球变暖将成为世界的净负担，这意味着必须在今后数十年中采取高成本效益的气候行动。
en: After the year 2070, global warming will become a net cost to the world, justifying cost-effective climate action now and in the decades to come.

zh: 但是，如若放长目光，记分牌还告诉我们，目前世界最大的环境问题是室内空气污染。
en: Yet, to put matters in perspective, the scorecard also shows us that the world’s biggest environmental problem by far is indoor air pollution.

zh: 如今，来自使用劣质燃料的烹饪和取暖的室内污染每年要杀死三百多万人，造成相当于全球GDP的3%的损失。
en: Today, indoor pollution from cooking and heating with bad fuels kills more than three million people annually, or the equivalent of a loss of 3% of global GDP.

zh: 但在1900年，该成本为GDP的19 % ， 并且预计在2050年降至GDP的1%��
en: But in 1900, the cost was 19% of GDP, and it is expected to drop to 1% of GDP by 2050.

zh: 全世界健康指标显示出一些最大的改善。
en: Health indicators worldwide have shown some of the largest improvements.

zh: 人类寿命预期在十八世纪末之前鲜有变化。
en: Human life expectancy barely changed before the late eighteenth century.

zh: 但自1900年以来，这方面的收益不可谓不巨：1900年全世界寿命预期为32岁，如今为69岁（2050年的预测值是76岁 ） 。
en: Yet it is difficult to overstate the magnitude of the gain since 1900: in that year, life expectancy worldwide was 32 years, compared to 69 now (and a projection of 76 years in 2050).

zh: 最大的因素是婴儿死亡率的下降。
en: The biggest factor was the fall in infant mortality.

zh: 比如，晚至1970年，能够接种麻疹、强直、百日咳、白喉和脊髓灰质炎疫苗的婴儿也只有5%左右。
en: For example, even as late as 1970, only around 5% of infants were vaccinated against measles, tetanus, whooping cough, diphtheria, and polio.

zh: 2000年，这一比例为85 % ， 每年能拯救约三百万生命，比20世纪世界和平所拯救的生命数量还要多。
en: By 2000, it was 85%, saving about three million lives annually – more, each year, than world peace would have saved in the twentieth century.

zh: 这一成功的功臣很多。
en: This success has many parents.

zh: 盖茨基金会和GAVI联盟已经出资25亿多美元用于疫苗事业，并承诺还将追加100亿美元。
en: The Gates Foundation and the GAVI Alliance have spent more than $2.5 billion and promised another $10 billion for vaccines.

zh: 扶轮社、世界卫生组织和其他许多组织的努力让脊髓灰质炎自1979年以来减少了99 % 。
en: Efforts by the Rotary Club, the World Health Organization, and many others have reduced polio by 99% worldwide since 1979.

zh: 从经济角度看，健康状况不良的成本在20世纪初达到了惊人的程度，相当于全球GDP的32 % 。
en: In economic terms, the cost of poor health at the outset of the twentieth century was an astounding 32% of global GDP.

zh: 如今这一比例已降至约11 % ， 预计到2050年还能在降低一半。
en: Today, it is down to about 11%, and by 2050 it will be half that.

zh: 乐观者也许并不完全正确（20世纪生物多样性损失每年大约相当于GDP的1 % ， 一些地区还要高 ） ， 但总体状况是明确的。
en: While the optimists are not entirely right (loss of biodiversity in the twentieth century probably cost about 1% of GDP per year, with some places losing much more), the overall picture is clear.

zh: 记分牌上的大部分项目都出现了相当于GDP的5—20%的改善幅度。
en: Most of the topics in the scorecard show improvements of 5-20% of GDP.

zh: 总体趋势更加明确。
en: And the overall trend is even clearer.

zh: 全球问题相对于可用于解决问题的资源大幅下降。
en: Global problems have declined dramatically relative to the resources available to tackle them.

zh: 当然，这不意味着没有其他问题。
en: Of course, this does not mean that there are no more problems.

zh: 尽管程度变小了很多，但健康、教育、营养不良、空气污染、性别不平等和贸易方面的问题仍然艰巨。
en: Although much smaller, problems in health, education, malnutrition, air pollution, gender inequality, and trade remain large.

zh: 但如今，现实主义者应该承认世界进步很大。
en: But realists should now embrace the view that the world is doing much better.

zh: 此外，记分牌告诉我们让2050年更加美好的主要挑战在哪里。
en: Moreover, the scorecard shows us where the substantial challenges remain for a better 2050.

zh: 我们的未来注意力不应该被最吓人的故事和声音最响的施压集团所左右，而应该根据关于我们在哪些方面做得最好的客观评估决定。
en: We should guide our future attention not on the basis of the scariest stories or loudest pressure groups, but on objective assessments of where we can do the most good.

zh: 全民教育的麻烦
en: The Trouble with Universal Education

zh: 哥本哈根—随着联合国千年发展目标（Millennium Development Goals）截止期的快速临近，世界正在抓紧为此后15年制定新的目标。
en: COPENHAGEN – With the deadline for the United Nations Millennium Development Goals fast approaching, the world is gearing up to establish a new set of goals for the next 15 years.

zh: 资源是有限的，决策者和国际组织必须扪心自问：用在哪里可以获得最好效果？
en: Given limited resources, policymakers and international organizations must ask themselves: Where can we do the most good?

zh: 在这15年中，2.5万亿美元用于发展援助的资金以及发展中国家的预算的大头应该用在健康、环境、粮食、水还是教育上？
en: Should a larger share of the $2.5 trillion that will be directed toward development aid over that period, and of developing-country budgets, be directed toward health, the environment, food, water, or education?

zh: 带着这些问题，哥本哈根共识（Copenhagen Consensus，我是负责人）请了一批世界顶尖经济学家评估了诸多不同目标的经济、社会和环境方面的成本效益。
en: With these questions in mind, the Copenhagen Consensus (which I direct) asked some of the world’s top economists to assess the economic, social, and environmental costs and benefits of many different targets.

zh: 全民教育也是评估目标之一。
en: Education for all was among the goals that were assessed.

zh: 教育的重要性是毋庸置疑的。
en: The importance of education is indisputable.

zh: 问题在于国际社会的普及教育承诺的信誉的让步；自1950年以来，国际社会至少在12项联合国宣言中做出过实现这一目标的承诺。
en: The problem is that the international community’s credibility in promising universal education has been compromised; it has pledged to achieve this goal in at least 12 UN-sponsored declarations since 1950.

zh: 比如，1961年联合国教科文组织承诺，到1980年非洲小学教育将“全民、义务、免费 ” 。
en: For example, UNESCO promised in 1961 that, by 1980, primary education in Africa would be “universal, compulsory, and free.”

zh: 但是，到1980年时，大约非洲小学适龄儿童仍然无学可上。
en: Yet, when the time came, about half of primary-school-aged children in Africa were still not attending school.

zh: 当目标日期度过时，这些目标会被重新制定，加上一个新的时间表，投入更多的资金，但关于资金如何使用的考虑很少。
en: When target dates pass, the goals are simply reformulated on a new timeline, and more money is thrown at the problem, with little consideration of how, exactly, it should be spent.

zh: 事实上，确保所有人都获得小学和初中教育的目标所需成本有可能超过全部全球教育援助预算。
en: And, in fact, the goal of ensuring primary and secondary education for all could well end up costing more than the entire global aid budget for education.

zh: 6,000万儿童仍然上不了学，因此国际社会不能简单地暂停2030年全民教育目标。
en: With 60 million children still out of school, the international community should not simply postpone the same universal-education target until 2030.

zh: 相反，国际社会应该放弃这一不现实的目标，转向可实现的高性价比定向方针。
en: Instead, it is time to abandon this unrealistic goal in favor of an achievable, targeted, and cost-effective approach.

zh: 经济学家乔治·萨卡洛普洛斯（George Psacharopoulos）在最新论文中建议，最紧迫的任务应该是效��最好的部分：早教，特别是学前教育。
en: As the economist George Psacharopoulos recommended in a recent paper, the highest priority should be what works best: early education, especially preschool.

zh: 关于早教可以提供更好的起点的最显而易见理由是人们在幼年时代吸收知识的能力最强。
en: The most obvious reasons why earlier education makes for a better starting point is that people are most receptive to knowledge when they are young.

zh: 此外，针对幼童的女性教育文化壁垒最低，儿童的劳动压力也最小。
en: Moreover, at younger ages, there are fewer cultural barriers to education for girls, and there is less pressure for children to contribute labor.

zh: 最后，学前教育比更高水平的学校教育成本更低。
en: Finally, preschool education is less expensive to deliver than higher-level schooling.

zh: 早期学习的长期效应不太明显，但更加深远。
en: The longer-term effects of early learning are less apparent but more profound.

zh: 尽管受过学前教育的学生在小学阶段的表现并不比未受学前教育的同学强，但成年后的收入确实更高。
en: Though students who attended preschool do not perform better than their peers in primary school, they do tend to earn more as adults.

zh: 这表明学前教育能够定性地提高儿童的社交技能或情商开发，使他们在随后的生活中拥有抓住更好经济机会方面的优势。
en: This suggests that preschool provides a qualitative boost to children’s social skills or emotional development that enables them to take better advantage of economic opportunity later in life.

zh: 当然，投资于扩张学前教育的准确回报很难估量。
en: Of course, the precise return on investment in expanded preschool education is difficult to discern.

zh: 但是，为了给发展目标（不管是否属于教育领域）排出优先级别，我们必须做一个评估。
en: But, in order to prioritize development targets – within and outside of the realm of education – estimates must be made.

zh: 首先，将教育成本 — — 如教师培训和薪酬、学校建设和维护，甚至童工的机会成本等 — — 加总，这个工作比较清楚。
en: First, there is the straightforward work of adding up the costs of education, such as teacher training and compensation, school construction and maintenance, and even the opportunity cost of child labor.

zh: 然后是比较模糊工作 — — 评估收益。 尽管收益难以量化，但也足以说明问题，以至于许多经济学家都支持早教。
en: Then there is the more ambiguous process of assessing the benefits, which, though difficult to quantify, are convincing enough that many economists champion early education.

zh: 基于可获得的最全面的数据，萨卡洛普洛斯认为最有效的目标应该是将不参加学前班的撒哈拉以南非洲儿童数量降低一半，这样做可以给每一美元投入带来33美元的社会和经济收益。
en: Based on the most extensive data available, Psacharopoulos determined that the most effective target would be to halve the proportion of children who are not attending preschool in Sub-Saharan Africa, which would yield social and economic benefits of $33 per dollar spent.

zh: 这一集中在单一的、挑战重重的地区的目标相当温和；但也相当现实并且可以实现 — — 而潜在回报相当巨大。
en: This goal, which focuses on a single challenge-plagued region, may seem modest; but it is also realistic and achievable – and the potential returns are massive.

zh: 目标雄心越大，影响会越小。
en: As targets become more ambitious, they lose their impact.

zh: 比如，追求在撒哈拉以南非洲完全普及小学教育会降低每一美元投入的社会和经济收益，但仍有7美元。
en: For example, the pursuit of universal primary education in Sub-Saharan Africa would yield a lower, but still significant, $7 of social and economic benefit for every dollar spent.

zh: 实现全球普及小学教育的成本要高得多，每一美元投入只能产生4美元收益。
en: And efforts to achieve universal primary education worldwide would cost far more, with each dollar spent bringing just $4 worth of benefits.

zh: 对于其他的重要目标，也必须做同样类型的比较，如改善教育质量 — — 这一目标的实现难度之高出乎意料，许多发达国家在经合组织国际评估中的差劲表现就是明证。
en: The same type of comparison must be made for other important goals, such as improving the quality of education – a surprisingly difficult objective to achieve, as many developed countries have learned from their poor performance in the OECD’s international assessment.

zh: 尽管用于（比如）缩小班级规模的资金几乎没有作用，但投资于制度变革 — — 如引入监控和评估系统、集中管理的考试制度、教师激励等 — — 可以为每一美元投入带来3—5美元收益。
en: While money allocated to, say, reducing class sizes has very little impact, investment in institutional changes – such as the introduction of monitoring and evaluation systems, centrally administered examinations, and incentives for teachers – could result in $3-5 of good per dollar spent.

zh: 至于职业培训，我们还没有找到评估标准。
en: As for vocational training, the jury is still out.

zh: 但它被认为比一般中学教育收益更差，这意味着它是次等投资选项。
en: But it has been identified as less profitable than general secondary education, making it an inferior investment option.

zh: 让人人上得起大学的努力问题更大。
en: Efforts to make university affordable for all are even more problematic.

zh: 由于较富家庭的孩子更可能获得高等教育，将有限的公共资源（包括税收收入）用于降低大学学费是劫贫济富。
en: Given that children from wealthier households are more likely to pursue higher education, directing limited public resources, including tax revenues, toward reducing its cost amounts to a subsidy for the wealthy, at the expense of the poor.

zh: 更好的办法是对富人家庭的孩子收学费，给穷人家庭的孩子奖学金。
en: A better approach would be to introduce tuition fees for the wealthy and scholarships for the poor.

zh: 实现稀缺资源作用最大化、改善世界最贫困人群的生活水平需要做出艰难的选择。
en: Maximizing the impact of scarce resources on the lives of the world’s poorest people demands tough choices.

zh: 在理想世界中，各层次齐全的全民优质教育是值得追求的目标。
en: In an ideal world, universal, high-quality education at all levels would be worth pursuing.

zh: 但是，健康和饮用水等基本需要也得满足，因此必须找出性价比最高的教育目标。
en: But, amid competing demands for basic necessities like health care and potable water, narrower, more cost-effective education targets are essential.

zh: 国际社会不应该追求与1950年一样的承诺，以高昂的代价轻微改善数十亿人的生活环境，而应该首先致力于改变撒哈拉以南非洲数百万儿童的生活。
en: Instead of aiming to improve billions of people’s circumstances slightly – at high cost – with the same promises that have been made since 1950, the international community should aim first to transform the lives of millions of children in Sub-Saharan Africa.

zh: 如果将这一方针应用于包括在国际社会的下一个发展日程中的所有目标，可以肯定2030年的世界将远比现在更加美好。
en: This approach, if applied to all of the goals included in the international community’s next development agenda, would ensure that the world of 2030 is a much better place.

zh: 可再生能源带来的贫穷
en: The Poverty of Renewables

zh: 迈阿密 — — 联合国秘书长潘基文曾说 ， “ 最先受到气候变化损害且受损最严重的是穷人。
en: MIAMI – According to UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon, “Climate change harms the poor first and worst.”

zh: ”他说的是事实，因为穷人最脆弱，也缺少资源去适应和调整。
en: This is true, because the poor are the most vulnerable and have the least resources with which to adapt.

zh: 但我们往往忘记了目前应对全球变暖的政策抬高了能源价格，而全世界的穷人因此受害最深。
en: But we often forget that current policies to address global warming make energy much more costly, and that this harms the world’s poor much more.

zh: 2012年有高达600亿美元的资金用来补贴风能和太阳能，也就是说全世界在能源消费领域比必要状况多花了600亿美金。
en: Solar and wind power was subsidized by $60 billion in 2012. This means that the world spent $60 billion more on energy than was needed.

zh: 而且因为这笔钱带来的总的气候利益只有区区14亿美元，另外586亿美元的补贴基本都成了沉落成本。
en: And, because the total climate benefit was a paltry $1.4 billion, the subsidies essentially wasted $58.6 billion.

zh: 还有190亿美元用于补贴生物燃料，而这笔钱所带来的气候利益几乎为零。
en: Biofuels were subsidized by another $19 billion, with essentially no climate benefit.

zh: 这些钱本来可以用来改善医疗条件、增聘师资、修建更好的道路或者是降低税收。
en: All of that money could have been used to improve health care, hire more teachers, build better roads, or lower taxes.

zh: 迫使所有人购买更贵、可靠性更差的能源推高了经济成本，也因此损伤了公益。
en: Forcing everyone to buy more expensive, less reliable energy pushes up costs throughout the economy, leaving less for other public goods.

zh: 宏观经济模型均值表明从2020年到本世纪末的每一年，欧盟气候政策的总成本将高达2090亿欧元（合2800亿美元 ） 。
en: The average of macroeconomic models indicates that the total cost of the EU’s climate policy will be €209 billion ($280 billion) per year from 2020 until the end of the century.

zh: 上述政策负担大部分落在全世界穷人的头上，因为富人可以轻而易举地购买涨价后的能源。
en: The burden of these policies falls overwhelmingly on the world’s poor, because the rich can easily pay more for their energy.

zh: 经济条件优越的环保主义者虽然用心是好的，但他们提出汽油价格应该翻番或者只允许使用高成本绿色能源的所谓骑士精神却常常令我目瞪口呆。
en: I am often taken aback by well-meaning and economically comfortable environmentalists who cavalierly suggest that gasoline prices should be doubled or electricity exclusively sourced from high-cost green sources.

zh: 这样的政策在生活富裕的新泽西州亨特顿县或许可以落实下去，据说那里的居民仅将收入的2%用来购买汽油。
en: That may go over well in affluent Hunterdon County, New Jersey, where residents reportedly spend just 2% of their income on gasoline.

zh: 但最贫困的30%美国民众却把税后收入的近17%都用来购买汽油。
en: But the poorest 30% of the US population spend almost 17% of their after-tax income on gasoline.

zh: 同样，环保主义者夸口说英国家庭自2005年后已经降低了近10%的电力消耗。
en: Similarly, environmentalists boast that households in the United Kingdom have reduced their electricity consumption by almost 10% since 2005.

zh: 但他们却忘了提到这是因为电价上涨50 % ， 而涨幅的绝大部分都是从1.8%增长到4.6%的可再生能源造成的。
en: But they neglect to mention that this reflects a 50% increase in electricity prices, mostly to pay for an increase in the share of renewables from 1.8% to 4.6%.

zh: 毫无疑问，穷人耗电的降幅远超过10 % ， 而富人耗电却根本没有减少。
en: The poor, no surprise, have reduced their consumption by much more than 10%, whereas the rich have not reduced theirs at all.

zh: 近五年一个英国家庭供暖费用上涨了63 % ， 而实际工资却在持续下降。
en: Over the past five years, heating a UK home has become 63% more expensive, while real wages have declined.

zh: 17%的英国家庭买不起能源 — — 换句话说他们被迫把10%的收入花在能源上；而且因为老年人经济能力普遍较差，约有四分之一的老年家庭陷入能源贫穷。
en: Some 17% of households are now energy poor – that is, they have to spend more than 10% of their income on energy; and, because elderly people are typically poorer, about a quarter of their households are energy poor.

zh: 领取退休金的贫困老人因为便宜而被迫焚烧旧书取暖，他们一天到晚待在有暖气的公交车上，有三分之一的人家里的暖气根本没烧。
en: Deprived pensioners burn old books to keep warm, because they are cheaper than coal, they ride on heated buses all day, and a third leave part of their homes cold.

zh: 今年德国的绿色补贴将耗资236亿美元，居民电价从2000年来上涨了80 % ， 导致690万家庭陷入能源贫困。
en: In Germany, where green subsidies will cost €23.6 billion this year, household electricity prices have increased by 80% since 2000, causing 6.9 million households to live in energy poverty.

zh: 巴伐利亚州经济宽裕的房主可以为低效率的太阳能电池板感觉良好，享受着由鲁尔区穷人最终支付的高额补贴，而这些穷人则因为自己买不起太阳能电池板，还要继续支付高昂的用电费用。
en: Wealthy homeowners in Bavaria can feel good about their inefficient solar panels, receiving lavish subsidies essentially paid by poor tenants in the Ruhr, who cannot afford their own solar panels but still have to pay higher electricity costs.

zh: 类似的例子不胜枚举。
en: The list goes on.

zh: 希腊对石油大举增税将取暖成本推高了48 % ， 越来越多的雅典人都去砍伐公园的树木，燃烧木柴造成的空气污染是烧油的三倍多。
en: In Greece, where tax hikes on oil have driven up heating costs by 48%, more and more Athenians are cutting down park trees, causing air pollution from wood burning to triple.

zh: 但气候政策令发展中国家付出更大的代价，那里的30亿民众无法得到充足的廉价能源，于是永远无法摆脱贫困状况。
en: But climate policies carry an even larger cost in the developing world, where three billion people lack access to cheap and plentiful energy, perpetuating their poverty.

zh: 他们靠燃烧树枝和牛粪来做饭取暖，由此造成的室内空气污染每年导致350万人死亡 — — 这才是世界范围内最迫在眉睫的环境问题。
en: They cook and keep warm by burning twigs and dung, producing indoor air pollution that causes 3.5 million deaths per year – by far the world’s biggest environmental problem.

zh: 用电可以解决这个问题，这样可以让家庭成员能在晚上看书、购买冰箱防止食物变质，或者用电脑和全世界沟通。
en: Access to electricity could solve that problem, while allowing families to read at night, own a refrigerator to keep food from spoiling, or use a computer to connect with the world.

zh: 这样企业也可以更有竞争力，从而创造就业机会和带动经济增长。
en: It would also allow businesses to produce more competitively, creating jobs and economic growth.

zh: 以南非和巴基斯坦为例，那里发电量不足导致企业频繁停电，同时也对就业机会产生了很大影响。
en: Consider Pakistan and South Africa, where a dearth of generating capacity means recurrent blackouts that wreak havoc on businesses and cost jobs.

zh: 但这两个国家为新建燃煤电厂的筹资却遭到了用心良苦的西方民众和政府的普遍抵制。
en: Yet the funding of new coal-fired power plants in both countries has been widely opposed by well-meaning Westerners and governments.

zh: 相反，他们提议用可再生能源来解决能源短缺问题。
en: Instead, they suggest renewables as the solution.

zh: 但此举充满了虚伪的味道。
en: But this is hypocritical.

zh: 富裕国家利用耗资巨大的太阳能和风能仅占能源总量的1.2 % ， 而且我们永远也不可能接受只在刮风的时候才有电用。
en: The rich world gets just 1.2% of its energy from hugely expensive solar and wind technologies, and we would never accept having power only when the wind was blowing.

zh: 今后两年德国将兴建十座新燃煤电厂以保障照明之用。
en: Over the next two years, Germany will build ten new coal-fired power plants to keep the lights on.

zh: 1971年，中国能源总量的40%来自可再生能源。
en: In 1971, 40% of China’s energy came from renewables.

zh: 其后，中国全靠高污染的煤炭让6.8亿人摆脱贫困，并实现了爆炸式的经济增长。
en: Since then, it has powered its explosive economic growth almost exclusively with highly polluting coal, lifting 680 million people out of poverty.

zh: 今天，中国使用的太阳能和风能仅占其能源总量的0.23 % 。
en: Today, China gets a trifling 0.23% of its energy from wind and solar.

zh: 相比之下，非洲能源总量却有50%来自可再生能源 — — 而且仍未能摆脱贫困。
en: By contrast, Africa gets 50% of its energy today from renewables – and remains poor.

zh: 全球发展中心一份新的分析报告量化了我们对全世界穷人的漠不关心。
en: A new analysis from the Center for Global Development quantifies our disregard of the world’s poor.

zh: 投资于可再生能源，我们需要约500美元才能帮一个人摆脱贫困。
en: Investing in renewables, we can pull one person out of poverty for about $500.

zh: 但用燃气发电，同样的投资可以帮四个人脱贫。
en: But, using gas electrification, we could pull more than four people out of poverty for the same amount.

zh: 我们以气候问题为重相当于在明知后果的情况下故意让超过四分之三的民众无法摆脱黑暗和贫穷。
en: By focusing on our climate concerns, we deliberately choose to leave more than three out of four people in darkness and poverty.

zh: 有效解决全球变暖需要长期创新，让所有人都用得起绿色能源。
en: Addressing global warming effectively requires long-term innovation that makes green energy affordable to all.

zh: 在此之前，以损害穷人利益为代价浪费巨额财富根本不可能解决问题。
en: Until then, wasting enormous sums of money at the expense of the world’s poor is no solution at all.

zh: 全球变暖的颠倒说法
en: Global Warming’s Upside-Down Narrative

zh: 纽约 — — 世界各地的政界人士在讲述全球变暖的故事时，把全球变暖描绘成人类最严峻的挑战。
en: NEW YORK – When politicians around the world tell the story of global warming, they cast it as humanity’s greatest challenge.

zh: 不过他们承诺能以较低成本加以应对，同时从无数其他方面改善世界各地的局面。
en: But they also promise that it is a challenge that they can meet at low cost, while improving the world in countless other ways.

zh: 我们现在知道这纯属无稽之谈。
en: We now know that is nonsense.

zh: 从美国国务卿克里到联合国秘书长潘基文这样的重量级政界人士均称气候变化是“我们这代人最严峻的挑战 ” 。
en: Political heavyweights from US Secretary of State John Kerry to UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon call climate change “the greatest challenge of our generation.”

zh: 克里称如果解决不了这一问题，人类将会付出灾难性的代价。
en: If we fail to address it, Kerry says, the costs will be “catastrophic.”

zh: 事实上，从2006年由英国政府委托撰写的所谓斯特恩报告出炉后，这已经成为政要们的标准说法。
en: Indeed, this has been the standard assertion of politicians since the so-called Stern Review commissioned by the British government in 2006.

zh: 斯特恩报告尽人皆知的断言全球变暖引发的损失将占GDP的5-20 % ， 并称这是“与大规模战争和二十世纪上半叶经济衰退规模类似”的重大破坏。
en: That report famously valued the damage caused by global warming at 5-20% of GDP – a major disruption “on a scale similar to those associated with the great wars and the economic depression of the first half of the twentieth century.”

zh: 我们被告知解决气候变化问题可以大幅降低所付出的代价。
en: Tackling climate change, we are told, would carry a much lower cost.

zh: 欧盟委员会主席承诺虽然欧盟气候政策“并非毫无成本 ” ， 但只占GDP的0.5 % 。
en: The president of the European Commission promised that while the European Union’s climate policies are “not cost-free,” they would amount to just 0.5% of GDP.

zh: 事实上，各路政要重申了斯特恩报告的观点，即可以通过仅占全球GDP1%的成本成功控制全球变暖。
en: Indeed, politicians of all stripes have reiterated the Stern Review’s finding that global warming can be curtailed by policies costing just 1% of world GDP.

zh: 此外，据说气候政策的作用还体现在其他很多方面。
en: Climate policies, moreover, are said to help in many other ways.

zh: 美国总统奥巴马承诺应对全球变暖的政策将创造出500万个新的绿色就业机会。
en: US President Barack Obama promised that policies to combat global warming would create five million new green jobs.

zh: 欧盟则称绿色能源将有助于“改善欧盟在能源供应领域的安全。 ”
en: The EU claimed that green energy would help “improve the EU’s security of energy supply.”

zh: 联合国政府间气候变化委员会（IPCC）最新报告完成后，我们知道这种说法错得多么荒诞。
en: With the completion of the latest report by the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), we can now see that this narrative is mostly wrong.

zh: 首期IPCC报告显示气候问题确实存在 — — 温室气体、特别是二氧化碳的排放导致气温升高，最终会危及到这个世界。
en: The first installment of the IPCC report showed that there is indeed a climate problem – emissions of greenhouse gases, especially CO₂, lead to higher temperatures, which will eventually become a net problem for the world.

zh: 这一结果已经广为人知了。
en: This result was highly publicized.

zh: 但报告同时显示过去15年中全球变暖速度已经大幅减慢或者完全停止。
en: But the report also showed that global warming has dramatically slowed or entirely stopped in the last decade and a half.

zh: 几乎所有气候模型的测算数据都过于炎热，也就是夸大了全球变暖的实际问题。
en: Almost all climate models are running far too hot, meaning that the real challenge of global warming has been exaggerated.

zh: 德国和其他几个国家的政府呼吁删除全球变暖速度减缓的证据。
en: Germany and other governments called for the reference to the slowdown to be deleted.

zh: 第二期IPCC报告显示我们预计将在2055-2080年前后看到的气温升高会带来占GDP0.2-2%的净成本 — — 相当于不到一年的经济衰退。
en: The second IPCC installment showed that the temperature rise that we are expected to see sometime around 2055-2080 will create a net cost of 0.2-2% of GDP – the equivalent of less than one year of recession.

zh: 因此，虽然IPCC明确提出全球变暖会带来问题，但其带来的成本显然远低于二十世纪的两次世界大战和经济大衰退。
en: So, while the IPCC clearly establishes that global warming is a problem, the cost is obviously much less than that of the twentieth century’s two world wars and the Great Depression.

zh: 不出所料，此次政要们再次力求删掉这项发现。
en: Again, not surprisingly, politicians tried to have this finding deleted.

zh: 英国官员认为这项经过同行审议的估算实际“毫无意义 ” ， 并且纠集比利时、挪威、日本和美国想要将这部分内容删除重写。
en: British officials found the peer-reviewed estimate “completely meaningless,” and, along with Belgium, Norway, Japan, and the US, wanted it rewritten or stricken.

zh: 一位学者推测联合国驳斥此前政要们的夸大其辞可能让他们感到“有些下不来台 ” 。
en: One academic speculated that governments possibly felt “a little embarrassed” that their previous exaggerated claims would be undercut by the UN.

zh: 第三期IPCC报告显示强硬的气候政策也比之前所说的更加昂贵 — — 2030年将占GDP的4 % ， 2050年6 % ， 2100年11 % 。
en: The third installment of the IPCC report showed that strong climate policies would be more expensive than claimed as well – costing upwards of 4% of GDP in 2030, 6% in 2050, and 11% by 2100.

zh: 而真正的成本可能还会更高，因为以上数据都假定政策处置恰当且立即生效，同时还神奇地采用了关键技术。
en: And the real cost will likely be much higher, because these numbers assume smart policies, instantly enacted, with key technologies magically available.

zh: 政要们再次试图删除或修改上述高成本的发现。
en: Again, politicians tried to delete or change references to these high costs.

zh: 英国官员解释道他们希望降低相关的成本估算，因为它们“会助长怀疑需要采取行动者的气焰。 ”
en: British officials explained that they wanted such cost estimates cut because they “would give a boost to those who doubt action is needed.”

zh: 绿色就业完全依赖巨额补贴，会导致其他领域损失相近的就业数。
en: Green jobs have been created only with heavy subsidies, costing a similar number of jobs elsewhere.

zh: 事实上，耗资超过1100万美元才能在美国额外创造出一份绿色就业。
en: Indeed, each extra job created cost more than $11 million in the US.

zh: 乌克兰危机爆发后可再生能源改善能源安全的肤浅说法可信度大幅降低；欧洲现在知道只有大量而稳定的能源供应关系才值得考虑。
en: And facile claims that renewable sources can boost energy security look a lot less convincing after the crisis in Ukraine; Europe now understands that only large and stable energy supplies matter.

zh: 气候变化曾被描绘成一场损失高达全球GDP20%的巨型灾难，虽然勇气可嘉的政要们称能用1%的GDP解决这一问题。
en: Climate change has been portrayed as a huge catastrophe costing as much as 20% of world GDP, though brave politicians could counter it at a cost of just 1% of GDP.

zh: 但现实情况却恰好相反：我们现在知道损失成本或许是全球GDP的2 % ， 而气候政策最终却可能耗资超过GDP的11 % 。
en: The reality is just the opposite: We now know that the damage cost will be perhaps 2% of world GDP, whereas climate policies can end up costing more than 11% of GDP.

zh: 让这个故事更为神奇的是所有这些事实专家们其实早就知道。
en: What makes this story all the more amazing is that experts have known almost all of these facts for a long time.

zh: 斯特恩报告是从未经过同行审议的官僚体制的产物。
en: The Stern Review was produced by bureaucrats and never subjected to peer review.

zh: 经济学家们知道损失成本其实经过大幅篡改，预测数据其实仅仅是学术文献中的剔除值。
en: Economists knew that the damage costs had been extensively massaged, and that the estimates were outliers compared to the academic literature.

zh: 政策成本低得不可思议其实是忽略了多数不利因素的人为产物，再次与学术文献形成了鲜明的对比。
en: The unfathomably low projections for policy costs were artifacts of ignoring most liabilities, again contradicting the academic literature.

zh: 事情演变到今天这种状况渴望头条新闻让人喘不过气来的媒体要与政要共同承担责任。
en: The media, eager for breathless headlines, share the blame with politicians for this state of affairs.

zh: 斯特恩报告发布后，据称一家英国报纸曾经报导 ： “ 要么即刻采取行动，要么听任我们熟悉的世界永久失去。
en: Following the release of the Stern Review, one British newspaper reportedly wrote: “Act now or the world we know will be lost forever.”

zh: ”准确报道虽然不那么性感，但远比危言耸听更加翔实。
en: Being accurate is less sexy, but much more informative.

zh: 我们生活的世界有六分之一的人死于本来可以轻松治愈的传染性疾病；八分之一的人死于空气污染，主要原因是很多人用牛粪和树枝为燃料在室内做饭；数十亿人生活在赤贫当中，既缺少电能又食不果腹。
en: We live in a world where one in six deaths are caused by easily curable infectious diseases; one in eight deaths stem from air pollution, mostly from cooking indoors with dung and twigs; and billions of people live in abject poverty, with no electricity and little food.

zh: 我们永远不该接受这样的观点，认为我们这代人在全球范围内最严峻的挑战是将气温升高降低零点几度。
en: We ought never to have entertained the notion that the world’s greatest challenge could be to reduce temperature rises in our generation by a fraction of a degree.

zh: 我们应该停止为警告将会发生灾难并推动糟糕政策的政要们击节叫好。
en: The solution is to stop applauding politicians who warn of catastrophe and promote poor policies.

zh: 与其补贴很难产生实际效益的低效的太阳能及风能发电，还不如投资于长期的绿色创新项目。
en: Instead of subsidizing inefficient solar and wind power with little benefit, we need to invest in long-term green innovation.

zh: 还有其他很多问题需要我们给予更多的关注。
en: And we need to give more attention to all of the other problems.

zh: 这或许不像危言耸听那么有趣，却会带来更好的实际效果。
en: This is perhaps less entertaining, but it will do much more good.

zh: 暴力经济学
en: The Economics of Violence

zh: 哥本哈根 — — 什么是世界上最大的暴力来源？
en: COPENHAGEN – What is the biggest source of violence in our world?

zh: 因为叙利亚、乌克兰和其他国家的暴力冲突经常见诸报端，很多人可能会说战争。
en: With the brutal conflicts in Syria, Ukraine, and elsewhere constantly in the news, many people would probably say war.

zh: 但这原来大错特错。
en: But that turns out to be spectacularly wrong.

zh: 如果想找到解决这些全球问题的经济有效的办法，第一步就是要先确定暴力的来源。
en: Getting it right matters if we are to find cost-effective solutions to this and other global problems.

zh: 显然，每个人都愿意制止战争和暴力，就像我们想要消除贫困、饥饿和全球变暖，并为所有人提供教育资源。
en: Obviously, everyone would like to stop wars and violence, just as we would like to end poverty, hunger, and global warming, while providing education to all.

zh: 但资源的有限性制约着国际社会。
en: But, given limited resources, the international community can only do so much.

zh: 我们必须分出轻重缓急，对成本效益进行经济分析可以做到这一点。
en: We have to prioritize, which is what an economic analysis of costs and benefits can do.

zh: 国际社会正在制定今后15年新的发展目标，而《哥本哈根共识》已要求一些世界知名经济学家评估他们眼中最明智的目标。
en: The international community is working on new development goals for the next 15 years, and the Copenhagen Consensus has asked some of the world’s leading economists to give their assessment of the smartest targets they can choose.

zh: 用本可以用于减少饥饿的资源来减少暴力是否值得？
en: Is reducing violence a goal worthy of resources that would otherwise be spent on, say, reducing hunger?

zh: 如果答案是肯定的，那么需要针对的暴力形式有哪些？
en: And, if so, which forms of violence should be targeted?

zh: 斯坦福大学詹姆斯·费伦和牛津大学非洲经济研究中心安柯·霍芙勒的研究结果显示杀人、尤其是针对妇女和儿童的社会暴力远比内战更具破坏性。
en: A study by James Fearon of Stanford University and Anke Hoeffler of Oxford University’s Center for the Study of African Economies argues that societal violence – homicides and especially violence against women and children – is a much bigger problem than civil wars.

zh: 人际暴力与内战的死亡比率高达9：1，而且每牺牲两名战士就有一名儿童死亡。
en: Nine people are killed in interpersonal violence for every battlefield death in a civil war, and one child is killed for every two combatants who die.

zh: 2008年全球发生凶杀案共计418,000起，太多国家有记录的谋杀率达到100，000分之10以上。 世卫组织将其视为一种传染病。
en: In 2008, there were 418,000 homicides around the world, with far too many countries recording a murder rate of more than 10 per 100,000, which the World Health Organization regards as an epidemic.

zh: 美国一起凶杀案给个人和社会造成的损失高达910万美元。
en: A single homicide in America costs the individual and society $9.1 million.

zh: 如果按照全球国民收入计算，仅此一项暴力犯罪就让全球GDP付出1.7%的代价。
en: If we scale this by national income across the world, this single category of violent crime costs 1.7% of global GDP.

zh: 当然，这并非全球经济的直接损失，而是衡量影响的一种方法。
en: Of course, this is not a direct financial loss to the global economy, but a way of expressing the impact.

zh: 如果谋杀得以消除，各国社会得到的好处可以用1.7%的GDP来衡量。
en: If murders could be eliminated, societies around the world would be better off in ways that can be valued at 1.7% of GDP.

zh: 与此相比内战成本要低得多，大致相当于全球GDP的0.2 % 。
en: Compare this to the much lower cost of civil wars, which are equivalent to about 0.2% of global GDP.

zh: 但这仍远逊于妇女所受的家庭暴力这一最大的暴力来源。
en: But this is still much less than the biggest source of violence of all: violence against women in the home.

zh: 《科学》杂志发表研究显示，撒哈拉以南非洲女性总人口的28%反应去年曾遭受过伴侣或家人的家庭暴力。
en: Based on studies published in Science, 28% of all women in Sub-Saharan Africa reported experiencing violence in the past year at the hands of their partners or family.

zh: 其中包括妇女遭到殴打、在年龄很小的时候被迫结婚、性侵 、 “ 荣誉”犯罪和女性生殖器阉割。
en: This includes women subjected to beatings, forced marriage at an early age, sexual assault, “honor” crimes, and female genital mutilation.

zh: 保守统计显示仅伴侣施暴一项的社会福利成本就高达4.4万亿美元，占全球GDP的5.2%左右。
en: A conservative estimate puts the welfare cost of intimate partner violence alone at $4.4 trillion, or 5.2% of global GDP.

zh: 虐童是第二大暴力来源，80%的虐童案作案者都是父母。
en: The second-largest source of violence is the abuse of children, 80% of which is inflicted by parents.

zh: 虐童的定义依文化的不同而不同；但约有15%的儿童每月都遭到联合国所谓的严厉体罚。
en: The definition of what constitutes child abuse varies by culture; but about 15% of children suffer each month from what the UN calls severe physical punishment.

zh: 体罚内容包括掌掴面部、头部、耳朵，而且其中有四分之一的儿童遭到某种器械的反复殴打。
en: This includes being slapped on the face, head, or ears, and a quarter of these children are beaten with some kind of implement repeatedly and as hard as possible.

zh: 每月都有2.9亿儿童忍受这样的痛苦。
en: Every month, some 290 million children endure such suffering.

zh: 虐童相关的社会福利成本为3.6万亿美元，约合全球GDP的4.2 % 。
en: The welfare cost is $3.6 trillion, or 4.2% of global GDP.

zh: 只有很少一部分国际援助基金目前被用于减少社会暴力和改善刑事司法系统。
en: A tiny fraction of international aid funding currently goes toward reducing societal violence and improving criminal justice systems.

zh: 社会和个人付出的巨大代价要求我们采取行动。
en: The enormous cost borne by society and individuals seems to cry out for action.

zh: 不幸的是，依然鲜有硬性证据显示资源分配的最佳去处。
en: Unfortunately, there is still little hard evidence about where resources should best be focused.

zh: 我们只能说减少暴力的资金可能有更好的用途。
en: All we can say is that the money spent to reduce violence might be better targeted.

zh: 有相当数量的援助流向“脆弱国家”用以结束或预防内战，但只有0.27%的国际援助流向包括“预防犯罪”的项目。
en: Considerable amounts of aid are directed toward “fragile states” to help stop or prevent civil war, but only 0.27% of international aid goes to projects with a “crime prevention” component.

zh: 其他计划可能带来某种间接的好处，但显然还有极大的空间有待提高。
en: Other programs may help in indirect ways, but there obviously is much room for improvement.

zh: 显而易见，某些解决方法很有效果。
en: Some solutions, it is clear, do work very well.

zh: 加强社会服务可以减少儿童暴力案件。
en: Stronger social services can reduce violence against children.

zh: 华盛顿州研究显示由训练有素的工作人员家访可以减少虐童案件，改善儿童的身心健康和生活质量，降低儿童福利和诉讼成本。
en: Studies in Washington State show that home visits from trained staff can reduce child abuse, improve children’s quality of life and physical and mental health, and reduce child-welfare and litigation costs.

zh: 该项目上每投入1美元可以产出14美元效益，这项政策因此成本效益很高。
en: A dollar spent on this program produces benefits of $14, making it a highly cost-effective policy.

zh: 很多情况下需要改变社会态度。
en: In many cases, changes in social attitudes are needed.

zh: 为减少针对妇女和女童的暴力，乌干达一个名为SASA ! （ 斯瓦西里语“现在！
en: To reduce violence against women and girls, one program in Uganda, called SASA!

zh: ” ） 的项目宣传伴侣暴力不可接受的理念，并协助实现了降低伴侣暴力比例一半的目标。
en: (Kiswahili for “Now!”) promotes the view that partner violence is unacceptable, and has helped to halve the rate of it.

zh: 这当然是个梦幻般的结果，虽然没有人实际分析过它的成本效益有多高。
en: This is a fantastic outcome, of course, though there has been no analysis of how cost-effective it is.

zh: 还有国家采取有效行动的其他实例。
en: There are other examples of countries taking effective action.

zh: 1993年，波哥大每100,000人发生80起谋杀。
en: In 1993, Bogota suffered 80 murders per 100,000 people.

zh: 通过采取综合性举措 — — 包括限制卖酒时间、回收公共空间和改善警察及司法系统 — — 2004年谋杀率下降到每100,000人21起谋杀。
