en: LONDON – Economic reality is beginning to catch up with the false hopes of many Britons.

zh: 一年前，英国以微弱多数投票退出欧盟，当时的英国人流行媒体承诺，相信支持脱欧阵营的政客的承诺。 他们说，英国脱欧不会降低英国人的生活水平。
en: One year ago, when a slim majority voted for the United Kingdom’s withdrawal from the European Union, they believed the promises of the popular press, and of the politicians who backed the Leave campaign, that Brexit would not reduce their living standards.

zh: 事实上，在此后的一年里，他们通过增加家庭债务维持了英国的生活水平。
en: Indeed, in the year since, they have managed to maintain those standards by running up household debt.

zh: 这管用了一段时间，因为家庭消费的增加刺激了经济。
en: This worked for a while, because the increase in household consumption stimulated the economy.

zh: 但英国经济的真相时刻马上就要来了。
en: But the moment of truth for the UK economy is fast approaching.

zh: 英格兰银行最新发布的数据显示，英国工资增长跟不上通货膨胀，因此，真实收入已经开始下降。
en: As the latest figures published by the Bank of England show, wage growth in Britain is not keeping up with inflation, so real incomes have begun to fall.

zh: 如果这一趋势在未来几个月中保持下去，家庭很快就会认识到他们的生活水平正在下降，从而必须调整支出习惯。
en: As this trend continues in the coming months, households will soon realize that their living standards are falling, and they will have to adjust their spending habits.

zh: 更糟糕的是，他们还将认识到自己举债过多，必须降低杠杆，这将进一步降低支撑经济的家庭消费。
en: To make matters worse, they will also realize that they have become over-indebted and will have to deleverage, thus further reducing the household consumption that has sustained the economy.

zh: 此外，英格兰银行和普通家庭犯了同样的错误：它低估了通货膨胀的影响，现在，它将面临顺周期升息的压力。
en: Moreover, the BoE has made the same mistake as the average household: it underestimated the impact of inflation and will now be catching up by raising interest rates in a pro-cyclical manner.

zh: 利息的升高将让家庭更加难以偿还债务。
en: These higher rates will make household debt even harder to pay off.

zh: 英国正在快速接近所有不可持续的经济趋势所共有的引爆点。
en: The British are fast approaching the tipping point that characterizes all unsustainable economic trends.

zh: 我将这个引爆点称为“反身性 ” ， 它是原因和结果开始互相影响的那个点。
en: I refer to such a tipping point as “reflexivity” – when both cause and effect shape each other.

zh: 经济现实被政治现实所强化。
en: Economic reality is reinforced by political reality.

zh: 事实上，英国脱欧是一个双输方案，英国和欧盟都得不偿失。
en: The fact is that Brexit is a lose-lose proposition, harmful both to Britain and the EU.

zh: 英国脱欧公投不可能推翻，但人民可能改变想法。
en: The Brexit referendum cannot be undone, but people can change their minds.

zh: 显然，这正是现在正在发生的。
en: Apparently, this is happening.

zh: 首相梅试图通过举行提前大选来加强她在谈判中的地位，但结果适得其反：她失去了议会多数地位，造成了一个悬浮议会（没有一个政党能够单独赢得多数 ） 。
en: Prime Minister Theresa May’s attempt to strengthen her negotiating position by holding a snap election badly misfired: she lost her parliamentary majority and created a hung parliament (no single party has a majority).

zh: 梅之败的主要原因在于她犯了一个致命的错误：要求年长者自己想办法承担他们的社保支出的大头，这个办法往往就是依靠他们住了一辈子得房子。
en: The primary cause of May’s defeat was her fatal misstep in proposing that elderly people pay for a substantial portion of their social care out of their own resources, usually the value of the homes that they have lived in all of their lives.

zh: 这就是众所周知的“老年痴呆税 ” ， 极大地冒犯了梅的保守党的核心票仓 — — 年长者。
en: This “dementia tax,” as it became widely known, deeply offended the core constituency, the elderly, of May’s Conservative Party.

zh: 许多人要么拒绝投票，要么转投其他政党。
en: Many either did not vote, or supported other parties.

zh: 年轻人参与率的提高也是梅惨遭失败的重要原因。
en: The increased participation of young people was also an important contributing factor in May’s defeat.

zh: 他们中很多人投了反对党工党，不是因为他们想加入工会或者他们支持工党党首杰里米·科尔宾（Jeremy Corbyn，不过他在选战期间的表现出人意料地令人印象深刻 ） 。
en: Many of them voted for Labour in protest, not because they wanted to join a trade union or because they support Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn (although he gave an unexpectedly impressive performance throughout the campaign).

zh: 英国年轻人对单一市场的态度与梅和“硬”脱欧支持者截然相反。
en: The attitude of Britain’s young people to the single market is diametrically opposed to that of May and supporters of a “hard” Brexit.

zh: 年轻人渴望找到高薪工作，管它是在英国还是在欧洲别的地方。
en: Young people are eager to find well-paying jobs, whether in Britain or elsewhere in Europe.

zh: 从这个角度讲，他们的利益与伦敦金融城的利益是一致的，而伦敦金融城颇提供了一些高薪工作。
en: In that respect, their interests correspond with the interests of the City of London, where some of those jobs are to be found.

zh: 如果梅想要保持权力，就必须改变英国脱欧谈判的方针。
en: If May wants to remain in power, she must change her approach to the Brexit negotiations.

zh: 有迹象表明她正准备这么做。
en: And there are signs that she is prepared to do so.

zh: 带着妥协的精神进入将于6月19日开始的脱欧谈判，梅可以与欧盟就日程问题形成谅解，并同意在足够长的时间内继续作为单一市场的一员解决所有需要解决的法律问题。
en: By approaching the negotiations that will start on June 19 in a conciliatory spirit, May could reach an understanding with the EU on the agenda and agree to continue as a member of the single market for a period long enough to carry out all the legal work that will be needed.

zh: 这对于欧盟来说可以大松一口气，因为欧盟不必因为英国的缺席而面临可能的预算巨洞。
en: This would be a great relief to the EU, because it would postpone the evil day when Britain’s absence would create an enormous hole in the EU’s budget.

zh: 这将是一个双赢安排。
en: That would be a win-win arrangement.

zh: 只有走这条路，梅能够寄希望于说服议会通过脱欧谈判完成、英国脱离欧盟后需要就位的所有法律。
en: Only by taking this path can May hope to persuade Parliament to pass all the laws that need to be in place once the Brexit talks are completed and Britain withdraws from the Union.

zh: 她可能需要放弃与奥尔斯特的民主联盟党（Democratic Unionist Party）的错误结盟，更加团结一致地与想要软化英国脱欧立场的苏格兰保守党站在一起。
en: She may have to abandon her ill-considered alliance with the Democratic Unionist Party in Ulster and side more emphatically with the Tories of Scotland, who are keen on a softer version of Brexit.

zh: 梅还需要补偿保守党在伦敦所辖自治市肯星顿（Kensington）所犯的错误 — — 上周肯星顿格伦菲尔大楼（Grenfell Tower）发生大火，至少30人丧生，并且人数可能还会继续上升。
en: May will also need to atone for the sins of the Tories in the London borough of Kensington with regard to last week’s Grenfell Tower fire, in which at least 30 people, and perhaps many more, lost their lives.

zh: 如果梅采取了这样的姿态，就可以继续领导少数派政府，因为没有人想要取代她。
en: If May embraces such a platform, she could then carry on leading a minority government, because nobody else would want to take her place.

zh: 英国脱欧仍将至少需要五年才能完成，在此期间，还会发生新的选举。
en: Brexit would still take at least five years to complete, during which time new elections would take place.

zh: 如果一切顺利，英国和欧盟或许在还没有完成离婚之前就想复合了。
en: If all went well, the two parties might want to remarry even before they have divorced.

zh: 英国的万劫不复之路
en: Britain’s Road to Perdition

zh: 伦敦—英国完全退欧已经从选项表中剔除。
en: LONDON – Full English Brexit is off the menu.

zh: 在彻底脱离欧盟之前，英国政府现在想要一个“过渡期 ” ， 在此期间，英国将保留欧元区成员的商业权利，同时继续缴纳欧元预算，遵守欧盟监管和司法裁决，允许人员自由流动。
en: Before leaving the European Union altogether, the British government now wants an “interim period,” in which the United Kingdom would retain the commercial rights of EU membership, while still contributing to the EU budget, observing EU regulations and legal judgments, and allowing the free movement of people.

zh: 过渡期将在2019年3月 — — 英国退欧过程的官方期限 — — 后继续维持至少两年，也就是说，在2021年之前，英国都将是实质上的欧盟成员国，但没有任何投票权。
en: This period would last for at least two years after March 2019 – the official deadline for the Brexit process – meaning that until 2021, Britain would essentially be an EU member state without any voting rights.

zh: 与此同时，英国首相梅的政府 — — 它承诺要保持与欧洲的“深刻而特殊”的关系 — — 将试图谈判一个新的与欧盟的“基于条约的协定 ” 。
en: In the meantime, British Prime Minister Theresa May’s government, having promised to maintain a “deep and special” relationship with Europe, would try to negotiate a new “treaty-based arrangement” with the EU.

zh: 但英国在这么短的时间内达成新条约的机会十分渺茫。
en: But Britain will have a vanishingly small chance of concluding a new treaty in so short a time.

zh: 事实上，到了2021年，英国将仍然在向“悬崖边缘”运动，即完全脱离欧洲，不再准备替代安排抵御冲击。
en: Indeed, come 2021, the UK will still be hurtling toward a “cliff edge”: a full break from Europe, with no alternative arrangement in place to cushion the blow.

zh: 从政治上讲，这样的择时将给梅政府带来比现在更大的风险，因为下一次选举必须在2022年6月前举行。
en: Politically, that timing would pose even greater risks for May’s government than it faces today, since the next general election must be held by June 2022.

zh: 因此，英国可能会试图将过渡期延长到2022年以后。
en: So the UK may try to extend the transition period beyond 2022.

zh: 而过去的经验告诉我们，期限一旦被延长了一次，就会无休无止地一次次延长下去。
en: And as past experience tells us, once an extension is granted, it may never end.

zh: 英国似乎正在走向我三个月前列出的情景。
en: The UK seems to be approaching the scenario I outlined three months ago.

zh: 梅在6月提前举行的大选的重大决定让她的反对派有机会要求英国去谈判一个类似于挪威作为欧洲经济区（EEA）成员的过渡性安排。
en: May’s fateful decision to hold an early election in June has allowed her opponents to demand that the UK negotiate a transitional arrangement similar to what Norway has as a member of the European Economic Area.

zh: EEA始创于1994年，是为了几个准备加入欧盟的国家而制定的临时性框架。
en: The EEA was originally created in 1994 as a temporary framework for various countries preparing to join the EU.

zh: 但由于挪威选民在11个月后的欧盟成员公投中拒绝加入欧盟，EEA也一直持续到24年后的今天。
en: But because Norwegian voters rejected a referendum on EU membership 11 months later, the EEA has now lasted for 24 years.

zh: 没人能够预料24年后会发生什么。
en: Nobody can predict what will happen in 24 years.

zh: 但对英国来说，好消息是欧盟可能已经开始慢慢向双轨结构转变。
en: But the good news for Britain is that the EU may already be moving slowly toward a two-track structure.

zh: 要想实现繁荣，欧元区需要建立一个政治联盟。
en: To prosper, the eurozone will need to establish a political union.

zh: 这将让丹麦、波兰和瑞典等非欧元国家形成一个欧元区外的经济合作外环。
en: This will leave non-euro countries such as Denmark, Poland, and Sweden forming an outer ring of economic cooperation outside the eurozone.

zh: 这些国家将拥有单一市场成员地位，但不参与货币或政治联盟。
en: These countries would have membership in the single market, but not in the monetary or political union.

zh: 双轨欧洲与今天的“双速”模式截然不同。
en: A two-track Europe would be very different from the “two-speed” model that applies to Europe today.

zh: 在双速模式中，每个国家理论上都在朝“日益紧密”的联盟前进，只不过速度有所不同。
en: In the latter, every country is theoretically heading toward “ever-closer union,” just at different rates.

zh: 相反，在双轨情景中，英国可以心安理得地重新加入外轨，和挪威，也许还有瑞典一起。
en: In a two-track scenario, by contrast, Britain could comfortably re-join the outer track along with Norway and, perhaps, Switzerland.

zh: 现在来看坏消息。
en: Now for the bad news.

zh: 英国过渡安排可能对于欧盟各国政府和英国选民来说都是不可接受的。
en: A transition arrangement for the UK may be unacceptable to both EU governments and British voters.

zh: 欧盟的坚定的联邦主义者希望英国尽快退出，因为长期以来英国一直为其他抵制深化融合的国家 — — 如丹麦、波兰和瑞典 — — 提供掩护。
en: Committed federalists in the EU want Britain out as quickly as possible, because Britain has long given cover for others – such as Denmark, Poland, and Sweden – to resist deeper integration.

zh: 狂热联邦派憎恨双轨欧洲的概念。
en: Federalist zealots hate the idea of a two-track Europe.

zh: 他们希望迫使所有欧盟成员国在下一个十年中接受欧元，并永远地牢牢锁定在全方位的政治和财政联盟中。
en: They want to force all EU member states to adopt the euro within the next decade, and to embed themselves permanently into a full-scale political and fiscal union.

zh: 他们正确地相信，将英国踢出局，能够更加容易地实现这一目标。
en: And they rightly believe that achieving this goal will be easier with Britain out of the picture.

zh: 但过渡期对英国来说也不是万灵丹。
en: But a transition period is no panacea for the UK either.

zh: 随着曾经将英国作为欧洲业务枢纽的跨国企业开始将一些业务活动迁移到其他国家，英国人已经开始领略英国退欧的经济成本。
en: Britons have already started to get a glimpse of the economic costs of Brexit, as international businesses that once used Britain as a hub for their European operations have started to relocate some of their activities.

zh: 由于英国政府一直心存有严格时间限制的过渡期的幻想，这一过程还会进一步加速。
en: As the UK government tries to maintain the fiction of a strictly time-limited transition, this process will accelerate further.

zh: 此外，欧盟将利用过渡期改变自己的监管规则，使创造就业和大量税收收入的企业将不得不迁往欧盟领土。
en: Moreover, the EU will use the transition period to change its own regulations, so that businesses generating employment and large tax revenues will have to move onto EU territory.

zh: 比如，欧洲银行局（European Banking Authority）和欧洲药品局（European Medicines Agency）已经开始迁出伦敦，这意味着许多与受监管程度较高的活动（如金融和药物研究）有关的法律、管理和游说工作，也必须外迁。
en: For example, the European Banking Authority and the European Medicines Agency are already relocating from London, meaning the many legal, managerial, and lobbying jobs connected to highly regulated activities such as finance and pharmaceutical research will have to relocate, too.

zh: 因此，过渡期将用监管双击打击位于英国的跨国企业：它们将同时受到英国和欧盟官僚的管理。
en: A transition period would thus hit international businesses based in Britain with a regulatory double-whammy: they would be subject to the whims of UK and EU bureaucracies at the same time.

zh: 更糟糕的是，长过渡期的憧憬可能延长公众观点的变化，导致无法及时地扭转退欧。
en: Making matters worse, the promise of a long transition could delay the shift in public opinion needed to reverse Brexit before it is too late.

zh: 2019年3月以后，英国将正式退出欧盟，而欧盟的经济增长已经开始赶超英国。
en: After March 28, 2019, the UK will be officially out of the EU, where economic growth has already started to overtake that of Britain.

zh: 如果英国想要再次加入欧盟，将不得不接受比现在恶劣得多的条件。
en: If it ever wants to be readmitted, it will have to settle for far less attractive terms than what it enjoys today.

zh: 英国不但无法获得预算回款或社会监管方面的特殊待遇；还有可能被迫加入欧元区。
en: Not only would it no longer receive budget rebates or special treatment on social regulations; it might even be forced to join the euro.

zh: 即使是投票“留欧”的英国选民，也有可能无法接受如此令人蒙羞的条件。
en: Even the 48% of British voters who voted “Remain” might reject such humiliating terms.

zh: 因此，英国将进退两难 — — 就像挪威一样，但它没有挪威的石油财富和社会凝聚力。
en: Britain would thus be stuck in limbo – like Norway, but without the oil wealth or social cohesion.

zh: 工党贸易发言人正确地指出，基于“挪威模式”的准永久性过渡期，将让英国沦为“附庸国 ” 。
en: As the Labour Party’s trade spokesman has aptly put it, a semi-permanent transition period based on the “Norway model” would turn Britain into a “vassal state.”

zh: 它将为欧盟预算提供巨款，并遵守欧盟法律，但它无权置喙这些钱怎么用，或这些法律如何制定。
en: It would still pay large sums into the EU budget and adhere to EU laws, but it would have no say over how that money is spent or how those laws are made.

zh: 在未来几个月中，英国公众可能会开始想见这一耻辱性结局。
en: In the months ahead, the British public may start to foresee this humiliating endgame.

zh: 挪威模式满足不了英国年长群体，满足不了地方仇欧派，也满足不了想要保留他们出生以来就视为理所当然的欧盟公民权利的年轻城市选民。
en: The Norway model will satisfy neither Britain’s elderly, provincial Europhobes, nor the young, urban voters who want to preserve the rights of EU citizenship that they have taken for granted all their lives.

zh: 前进如此暗淡，英国选民可能会在领导人完成退欧过程之前，就改变对退欧的想法。
en: With this depressing prospect setting in, British voters could change their minds about Brexit before their leaders go through with it.

zh: 但要发生这一大转变，英国必须经历一场足够大的政治或经济危机，让公众观点摆脱致命的自负。
en: But for such a Damascene conversion to happen, the country would have to experience a political or economic crisis large enough to shake public opinion out of its fatalistic complacency.

zh: 目前，英国人一直在效仿他们所喜爱的国家口号“保持冷静，坚持不懈 ” 。
en: As things stand, Britons have been emulating that beloved national slogan, “Keep calm and carry on.”

zh: 在英国的情况可能好转之前，或许先要大大恶化。
en: Before things can get better for Britain, they will probably have to get much worse.

zh: 爱尔兰问题重现
en: The Return of the Irish Question

zh: 伦敦—大约整20年前，在经历了几个月的微妙而艰难的谈判后，北爱尔兰两大主要政治阵营的领导人 — — 一边是天主教民族主义者和共和党人，另一边是新教统一派 — — 签署了受难日协定（Good Friday Agreement ） ， 结束了30多年的暴力和流血。
en: LONDON – Almost exactly 20 years ago, after months of delicate and difficult negotiation, leaders of Northern Ireland’s two main political camps – Catholic nationalists and republicans on one side; Protestant unionists on the other – signed the Good Friday Agreement, ending more than 30 years of violence and bloodshed.

zh: 如今，这一协定 — — 以及它所促成的互相尊重和和谐关系 — — 正遭到威胁。
en: Now, that agreement – and the mutually respectful and harmonious relationship that it enabled – is under threat.

zh: 受难日协定由英国首相和爱尔兰总理 — — 当时分别是布莱尔和埃亨 — — 在美国参议员乔治·米切尔（George Mitchell）的斡旋下达成。
en: The Good Friday Agreement was brokered by the prime ministers of the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland – Tony Blair and Bertie Ahern, respectively – with the help of United States Senator George Mitchell.

zh: （布莱尔的前任梅杰也做了大量铺垫工作。
en: (A great deal of spadework had also been done by Blair’s predecessor, John Major.)

zh: ）协定基于一项动议，即，如果所有各方都同意北爱尔兰宪法地位只有通过自由民主选择才可改变，则人民可以自行选择效忠身份：英国人、爱尔兰人，或双重身份。
en: It was based on the proposition that, as long as everyone agreed that changes to Northern Ireland’s constitutional status could come only as a result of free democratic choice, people could assert their loyalty to their preferred identity: British, Irish, or even both.

zh: 为了支持和平，协定在北爱尔兰建立了一个分权政府，冲突双方各有代表。
en: To support peace, the agreement created a power-sharing government in Northern Ireland, with representatives from both sides of the conflict.

zh: 协定还成立了一个北爱尔兰治安独立委员会，由我担任主席，负责改革警察服务。
en: It also established the Independent Commission on Policing for Northern Ireland, which I chaired, to reform the police service.

zh: 我们的努力让警察安排能够令所有群体都感到可以接受，因而有助于减少对警察的抨击，同时也让天主教警察招募人数大幅增加。
en: Our efforts helped to reduce attacks on the police by making them acceptable to all groups, and led to a substantial increase in the recruitment of Catholics, among other things.

zh: 协定签署后，英国和爱尔兰的欧盟成员国地位使得过渡进行的非常顺利。
en: Once the agreement was signed, the status of both Britain and Ireland as European Union members made the transition incomparably easier.

zh: 就这样，两者之间的边境变成了不过是地图上的一条线：没有栅栏，没有通关站，也没有隔离标志显示从一国迈入了另一国。
en: Just like that, the border between them was little more than a line on the map: there were no barriers, customs posts, or other divisive symbols to show where one country ended and the other began.

zh: 贸易和人可以自由在两国之间转移。
en: Trade and people could move freely between them.

zh: 事实上，它们作为欧洲伙伴的地位 — — 始自1973年爱尔兰成为欧共体成员 — — 长期以来一直强化着英国和爱尔兰之间的关系。
en: In fact, their status as European partners – ever since Ireland became a member of the European Communities in 1973 – has long reinforced the ties binding the UK and Ireland.

zh: 平心而论，两者之间的暴力史 — — 包括征服、殖民、反抗和饥荒 — — 使得恨意根深蒂固。
en: To be sure, their violent history – which has included conquest, colonization, rebellion, and famine – has left deep-seated animosity.

zh: 但是，作为欧洲伙伴国，更不用说同属欧洲西海岸群岛的邻居关系，它们之间的联系也是难解难分。
en: Yet, as European partners, not to mention neighbors in an archipelago off the west coast of Europe, they are inextricably connected.

zh: 英格兰、威尔士和苏格兰有五百多万人至少有一位爱尔兰祖辈。
en: More than five million people in England, Wales, and Scotland have at least one Irish grandparent.

zh: 在网前追溯一代，这一数字还会增加。
en: Go back a generation further, and the number rises higher.

zh: 在过去二十年里，英国和爱尔兰收获了互相尊重和和平关系的硕果。
en: Over the last two decades, the UK and Ireland have enjoyed the fruits of a mutually respectful and peaceful relationship.

zh: 对我们大部分英国人来说，爱尔兰显然有很多地方值得敬仰：它的经济增长，它在文学和音乐方面的复兴，还有它对全世界各地移民的吸引力（目前移民占全国人口的17 % ） 。
en: There is certainly much for us British to admire in Ireland today: its economic growth, its cultural renaissance in literature and music, its appeal to immigrants from around the world, who now comprise 17% of the country’s population.

zh: 爱尔兰早已非常成熟，抛弃了狭隘教义，成为一个现代而慷慨的国家。
en: With extraordinary maturity, Ireland has left behind narrow clericalism, and become a modern and generous state.

zh: 但如今，严峻的挑战正在浮现。
en: Yet serious challenges are now emerging.

zh: 在北爱尔兰，分权政府已经解体，英国政府也无法强力帮助重建有建设性的合作。
en: In Northern Ireland, the power-sharing government has broken down, and the UK government is not in a strong position to help restore constructive collaboration.

zh: 在去年灾难性的提前选举后，为了确保下议院有效多数，英国首相梅的保守党与北爱尔兰民主统一党（Democratic Unionist Party，源自更加极端的统一传统）做了一笔交易。
en: In order to secure a working majority in the House of Commons after last year’s disastrous snap election, British Prime Minister Theresa May’s Conservatives made a deal with Northern Ireland’s Democratic Unionist Party, which has its roots in the more extreme unionist traditions.

zh: 其结果是英国政府无法再像一位不偏不倚的调停者那样行动。
en: As a result, the UK government seems unable to act as an even-handed mediator.

zh: 尚未完结的英国退欧谈判让局面进一步复杂化，似乎没人知道这会给北爱尔兰和爱尔兰共和国造成什么后果 — — 它们将被英国和欧盟的边境隔开。
en: The ongoing Brexit negotiations are complicating matters further, as nobody seems to know how to deal with the consequences for Northern Ireland and the Irish Republic, which will be divided by the UK’s border with the EU.

zh: 许多政客说希望形成一条无摩擦的边境，但梅和她的一些同事已在讨论要同时退出单一市场和关税联盟，即英国将位于有共同监管促进贸易的免关税区之外。
en: While many politicians say they want a frictionless border, May and some of her colleagues have discussed leaving both the single market and the customs union, thereby putting the UK outside the tariff-free zone in which trade is facilitated by shared regulations.

zh: 他们主张，北爱尔兰应该有和英国其他部分一样的贸易规则。
en: Northern Ireland, they assert, will have to have the same trade rules as the rest of the UK.

zh: 这带来了两种可能：要么形成一个适用于整个不列颠群岛的无摩擦的贸易机制；要么在爱尔兰形成一条硬边境。
en: This leaves two possibilities: either a frictionless trade regime that operates throughout the British Isles, or a hard border across Ireland.

zh: 毕竟，其他欧盟国家不会允许只有英格兰、苏格兰和威尔士退出单一市场和关税联盟，而北爱尔兰仍留在其中。
en: After all, other EU countries are not going to allow only England, Scotland, and Wales to leave the single market and customs union, while leaving Northern Ireland in.

zh: 这将使规避监管易如反掌，比如原产地规则非欧盟国家只要将出口货物经爱尔兰转运至英国即可，反之亦然。
en: That would make it far too easy to avoid regulations, such as rules of origin, with a non-EU country exporting goods to Ireland for onward shipment to the UK, or vice versa.

zh: 类似的问题在欧盟内部人员自由流动方面也存在 — — 英国不想受改规则约束。
en: Similar problems arise with regard to the free movement of people within the EU – a rule to which the UK does not want to be subject.

zh: 所有这些挑战都不令人惊讶。
en: None of these challenges should come as a surprise.

zh: 警示信号早就已经浮现；只是英国政府完全视而不见。
en: The warnings were issued a long time ago; the British government simply ignored them.

zh: 潜在解决方案仍是一个谜，但当局迟早需要面对问题。
en: Potential solutions remain a mystery, but the authorities will have to confront the question sooner or later.

zh: 显然，不存在容易的技术解决方案。
en: There is certainly no easy technological solution.

zh: 任何检查制度都免不了要包含一些实体控制。
en: Any system of checks will inevitably involve some sort of physical control.

zh: 负责实施检查的海关官员难免会成为分离的象征，甚至成为一种挑衅，引起共和派极端分子的暴力行为，过去就曾发生过这样的事情。
en: The customs officers tasked with implementing those checks will inevitably become symbols of division, and potentially even a provocation to violence by republican extremists, as happened in the past.

zh: 所需要的动作只是发动一次袭击，迫使政府提高安全级别，加深分裂、刺激暴力。
en: All it would take would be one attack to impel the government to boost security, deepening divisions and spurring more violence.

zh: 在爱尔兰重新引入硬边境将是灾难性的，因为它会削弱受难日协定。
en: The reintroduction of a hard border in Ireland would be devastating, as it could undermine the Good Friday Agreement.

zh: 单元爱尔兰领导人能让英国政客深刻认识到这一点，为不会威胁到爱尔兰好不容易赢得的和平与繁荣的方案铺平道路。
en: One hopes that Irish leaders can impress this upon politicians in the UK, opening the way for a solution that doesn’t threaten Ireland’s hard-won peace and prosperity.

zh: 英国退欧与爱尔兰问题
en: Brexit vs. the Irish Question

zh: 伦敦—英国退欧日 — — 2019年3月29日，皇家海军不列颠海盗号（HMS Buccaneer Britannia）将起航巡航“英国势力圈 ” 。
en: LONDON – On Brexit day – March 29, 2019 – the HMS Buccaneer Britannia will set sail in search of the riches of the “Anglosphere.”

zh: 但有一个问题：某些人忘了升起牢牢固定在爱尔兰的舰锚。
en: But there is a hitch: Someone has forgotten to raise the anchor, which remains planted firmly in Ireland.

zh: 这并不奇怪。
en: This isn’t surprising.

zh: 我所了解的所有疑欧派保守党政客，没有一位提到过北爱尔兰，更不用说位于其南部的那个主权国家了。
en: Of all the Euroskeptic Conservative politicians I know, not one has ever mentioned Northern Ireland, let alone the sovereign country to the south of it.

zh: 退欧派脑子里只有要求从超越国家的布鲁塞尔“超国家”手中夺回议会主权和自由。
en: The only thing on the Brexiteers’ minds is the quest for parliamentary sovereignty and liberation from the supranational “superstate” in Brussels.

zh: 这一盲目的观点可能纯粹反映了无知。
en: This blinkered view may simply reflect ignorance.

zh: 即使是像现任北爱尔兰政务大臣卡伦·布拉德利（Karen Bradley）这样的前“留欧派 ” ， 最近也坦承 “ [ … … ]当我开始担任这个职位时，我对于一些北爱尔兰根深蒂固的问题都不甚了解。
en: Even an erstwhile “Remainer” like Karen Bradley, the current Secretary of State for Northern Ireland, recently confessed that, “[…] when I started this job, I didn’t understand some of the deep-seated and deep-rooted issues that there are in Northern Ireland.”

zh: ”换句话说，直到最近，她对于十九和二十世纪英国历史的核心问题之一还漠不关心。
en: In other words, until very recently, she has been incurious about one of the central issues of nineteenth- and twentieth-century British history.

zh: 处于同一状态的保守党政客如果了解一下已经导致了3,600多起暴力死亡的“爱尔兰问题 ” ， 将大有裨益。
en: Conservative politicians who find themselves in such a position would do well to know that conflicts over the “Irish question” have resulted in more than 3,600 violent deaths.

zh: 如果他们了解历届保守党首相 — — 从希斯到撒切尔夫人再到梅杰 — — 都没能解决这个问题、直到1998年受难日协定才解决了这个问题，也会颇有助益。
en: They might also benefit from knowing that successive Conservative prime ministers, from Edward Heath to Margaret Thatcher to John Major, struggled and failed to resolve the issue before it was put to rest by the 1998 Good Friday Agreement.

zh: 除了撤军，受难日协定通过让北爱尔兰和爱尔兰共和国之间的贸易，在欧盟关税同盟的庇护下实现平稳化，让相互敌对的体制能够共存。
en: In addition to military decommissioning, the Good Friday Agreement brought together antagonistic communities by mandating smooth trade between Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland, under the aegis of the EU customs union.

zh: 55.8%的北爱尔兰选民在2016年公投中支持“留欧 ” ， 这一事实便部分来自这一了不起的成就。
en: The fact that 55.8% of Northern Irish voters backed “Remain” in the 2016 referendum partly reflects this astonishing achievement.

zh: 稍有远见的人都应该知道，北爱尔兰地位将成为英国退欧谈判的核心难题。
en: Anyone with an ounce of foresight should have known that the status of Northern Ireland would become a stubborn conundrum at the center of the Brexit negotiations.

zh: 事实上，这个问题是如此棘手，以至于信奉阴谋论的退欧派现在开始怀疑欧盟谈判员利用它来拖延和妨碍不列颠海盗号的光荣起航。
en: In fact, the problem is so intractable that conspiracy-minded Brexiteers now suspect EU negotiators of using it to delay or stymie Buccaneer Britannia’s glorious departure.

zh: 讽刺的是，欧盟中有许多人也认为有阴谋。
en: Ironically, many in the EU also think that a plot is afoot.

zh: 欧盟向来认为，在讨论英国-欧盟的未来关系之前，双方必须先落实有法律约束力的分手协议。
en: The EU has long insisted that a legally binding divorce settlement must be concluded before there can be any discussion of future UK-EU relations.

zh: 但如今，英国被怀疑用爱尔兰问题暗示要在正式退欧协定中纳入详细的未来关系“政治宣言 ” 。
en: But now Britain is suspected of exploiting the Irish question to insinuate a detailed “political declaration” about future relations into the formal exit agreement.

zh: 关键的问题是，如果没有更全面的英国-欧盟未来关系协议，所谓的爱尔兰障碍（Irish backstop ） — —将阻止在北爱尔兰和爱尔兰共和国之间建立硬边界。
en: The key problem is the so-called Irish backstop, which would prevent the establishment of a hard border between Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland in the absence of a wider deal on the future of UK-EU relations.

zh: 2017年12月，所有各方一致同意，这一障碍对于根据受难日协定维持和平来说是必不可少的。
en: In December 2017, all parties concurred that such a backstop was necessary to preserve the peace under the Good Friday Agreement.

zh: 但如何将这一点写入有法律约束力的协定，则众说纷纭。
en: But there has been disagreement over the translation of this into legally binding language.

zh: 如果无法达成协定 ， “ 北爱尔兰领土将是欧盟关税区的一部分。 ”
en: Failing an agreement, “the territory of Northern Ireland would be part of the customs territory of the European Union.”

zh: 英国政府坚持，它能够解决边界问题，方法是保持与欧盟关税规则紧密一致，并部署目前尚未开发出来的关税监控技术 — — 也就是说，英国将依靠魔法来解决边界问题。
en: For its part, the UK government insisted that it can address the border issue by remaining in close alignment with EU customs rules and deploying customs-monitoring technologies that have yet to be invented – which is to say, by magic.

zh: 但爱尔兰政府坚持要敲定爱尔兰障碍的细节，并要写入有法律约束力的退盟条约。
en: Yet the Irish government has insisted that every detail of the backstop be nailed down and included in the legally binding withdrawal treaty.

zh: 但这一先行协定马上给梅带来了一个问题。 梅能否在议会下院保持多数取决于十位来自北爱尔兰的民主联盟党（Democratic Unionist）议员。
en: But this preliminary agreement immediately posed a problem for May, whose majority in the House of Commons depends on ten Democratic Unionist MPs from Northern Ireland.

zh: 此外，由于她所在政党和内阁因为想要的退欧方式的不同而产生了裂痕，爱尔兰共和国和欧盟其他国家正在目睹英国自我伤害的大戏。
en: And, because her own party and the cabinet are divided on the kind of Brexit they want, the Irish Republic and the rest of the EU are in the position of spectators to a colossal act of national self-harm.

zh: 如果北爱尔兰要留在欧盟关税和监管联盟中，就必须在爱尔兰海划出一条边界。
en: If the province were to remain in the EU’s customs and regulatory orbit, there would have to be a border in the Irish Sea.

zh: 这不但将破坏英国内部关税联盟的运转，还会妨碍大不列颠和北爱尔兰联合王国的宪政一体性。
en: That would jeopardize not just the workings of the UK’s internal customs union, but also the constitutional integrity of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

zh: 更糟糕的是，搪塞的用词导致苏格兰民族主义者“我们也要”的回应，他们正确地指出，如果北爱尔兰留欧派多数能获得特殊安排，那么同样支持留欧的苏格兰也应该获得类似的协议。
en: Worse, the fudging language invited a “we, too” riposte from Scottish nationalists, who rightly argued that if special arrangements were going to be made for Northern Ireland’s Remain majority, then the Scots, who also voted to remain, should be offered a similar deal.

zh: 否则，他们将要求再来一次2014年苏格兰独立公投。
en: Failing that, they would demand a rerun of the 2014 Scottish independence referendum.

zh: 但这一次，苏格兰民族主义者不用担心统一党所提出的独立就等于事实退出欧盟的说法了。
en: This time, however, Scottish nationalists would not have to worry about the Unionist argument that independence implies a de facto withdrawal from the EU.

zh: 欧盟拒绝了英国提出的在退欧后暂时留在关税联盟中的方案，因为这意味着英国既享受到自由贸易的好处，又可以不允许欧盟公民的自由流动。
en: The EU rejected British offers to remaintemporarily in the customs union after Brexit, because that would allow the UK to enjoy the benefits of tariff-free trade without having to permit the free movement of EU citizens.

zh: 在这一情形中，欧盟再一次怀疑英国用北爱尔兰当作特洛伊木马，获得不公平的优势，而英国退欧派则指责梅屈服于布鲁塞尔的勒索犯。
en: On this occasion, the EU once again suspected the UK of using Northern Ireland as a Trojan horse to gain an unfair advantage, and the Brexiteers accused May of capitulating to the extortionist gangsters in Brussels.

zh: 梅的“退欧大臣”大卫·戴维斯（David Davies）立即辞职，随后，时任外交大臣鲍里斯·约翰逊（Boris Johnson）也辞去了职务（他需要考虑自己取代梅的希望 ） 。
en: May’s “Brexit secretary,” David Davis, immediately resigned, and he was soon followed out the door by then-Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson (who needed a moment to consider his own prospects of replacing May).

zh: 此后，谈判员一直在探寻超现实的“障碍的障碍 ” （ backstop to the backstop ） ， 以防第一道障碍从“全天候”变成“有时限 ” （ 用他们的致命术语来说 ） 。
en: Negotiators have since been exploring the surreal idea of a “backstop to the backstop” in the event that the first backstop ends up being “time-limited” instead of “all-weather,” to use their deadly jargon.

zh: 现在，强调点转向了如何让整个英国留在关税联盟，附带条件是“某一天”它可以退出。
en: Emphasis has now shifted to how the entire UK can remain in the customs union, with the proviso that “one day” it might be able to escape.

zh: 但基本点并未改变：主要由英格兰人组成的退欧派，并没有认真考虑爱尔兰问题，甚至没有考虑与偶们决裂可能让英国回到黑暗时代的可能。
en: But the basic point remains: Predominantly English Brexiteers have given no serious thought to the Irish question, nor even to the likelihood that crashing out of the EU might take the UK back to the dark ages.

zh: 他们中有许多人宁可失去北爱尔兰和苏格兰，也不愿放弃退欧。
en: Many of them would rather lose Northern Ireland and Scotland than forgo Brexit.

zh: 相反，他们一直在忙于构建一个有无限可能的幻想世界，这个世界的基础，是以1940年德雷克爵士（Sir Francis Drake ） 、 罗利爵士（Sir Walter Raleigh ） 、 英属印度和保持“独行”为特色的国家神话。
en: Instead, they have been busy constructing a fanciful world of limitless possibility, based on a national mythology featuring Sir Francis Drake, Sir Walter Raleigh, the British Raj, and standing “alone” in 1940.

zh: 在心理上，其中一些人似乎是在复兴一场与我们最紧密的邻居和贸易伙伴之间的想象的战争。
en: Psychologically, some of them seem to be reliving an imaginary war with our closest neighbors and trading partners.

zh: 大部分明智之士生活在当下。
en: Most sensible people live in the present.

zh: 不管从哪个方向上看，从特朗普的贸易战到俄罗斯和摩尔多瓦准备阻止英国在退欧后进入世界贸易组织，现实不可避免地要与退欧派的英国重要性幻想发生正面碰撞。
en: And wherever one looks, from Trump’s trade wars to Russia and Moldova vowing to block Britain’s post-Brexit accession to the World Trade Organization, reality is ineluctably crushing Brexiteers’ fantasies of English importance.

zh: 英国退欧的衰亡
en: The Decline and Fall of Brexit

zh: 伦敦—一开始，英国首相梅有一个计划 ： “ 英国退欧就意味着英国退欧。
en: LONDON – In the beginning, British Prime Minister Theresa May had a plan: “Brexit means Brexit.”

zh: ”其中的思想是让英国迅速退出欧盟，让选民们无法认识到自己在欧盟公决选战中被出卖，因此也就不会惩罚欺骗他们的保守党。
en: The idea was to withdraw the United Kingdom from the European Union so fast that voters would not realize they had been sold a bill of goods during the EU referendum campaign and should therefore not punish the Conservative Party for having lied to them.

zh: 其计划是假装与欧盟谈判的所有协议都是“量身定制 ” ， 是退欧的“最佳选择 ” ， 英国能够在退出欧盟的同时，不受限制地进入欧洲市场。
en: The plan was to pretend that whatever deal was negotiated with the EU would be a “bespoke” and “best possible” Brexit, allowing Britain to quit the bloc while retaining unfettered access to the European market.

zh: 用严格的党派政治术语讲，这个计划在去年6月的提前选举前有效，而在选举中，梅失去了议会多数。
en: In strictly partisan political terms, the plan made sense right up until the snap election last June, when May lost her parliamentary majority.

zh: 平心而论，最近在面对下议院的亲欧派保守党时，梅取得了胜利。
en: To be sure, May recently scored a victory when she faced down Tory Europhiles in the House of Commons.

zh: 自去年6月以来，英国政坛一直围绕着一个谜团在转：如何避免英国制造业大部毁于一旦 — — 它们需要依赖及时的欧洲供应链 — — 而不需要接受“挪威模式 ” — —遵守欧盟规则但对这些规则完全没有说话的份。
en: But it hardly matters. Since last June, British politics has been spinning around the same conundrum: how to avoid the sudden destruction of much of British manufacturing – which depends on European just-in-time supply chains – without also accepting the “Norway model” of obeying EU rules without having any say in making them.

zh: 为了帮助梅政府避免英国制造业陷入灾难，欧盟委员会仁慈地同意在2019年3月29日英国正式退盟后给它21个月的“落实期 ” 。
en: To help the May government stave off disaster for British manufacturing, the European Commission has graciously agreed to a 21-month “implementation period” that will follow the UK’s official exit on March 29, 2019.

zh: 其思想是这段时期应该被用于敲定未来关系的大部分细节。
en: The idea was that this period should be used to settle most of the details of the future relationship.

zh: 但梅坚持所谓的红线 — — 包括拒绝欧洲法院（ECJ）的司法管辖权 — — 这导致她已将这一机会白白浪费。
en: Yet May has already squandered the opportunity by continuing to insist on so-called red lines, which include rejection of the jurisdiction of the European Court of Justice (ECJ).

zh: 梅试图移植欧盟单一市场内部无摩擦贸易的好处，但她的红线让欧盟委员会无法接受。
en: While May is trying to replicate the benefits of frictionless trade within the European single market, her red lines make this impossible for the Commission to accept.

zh: 结果，英国退欧谈判陷入了僵局，及时达成“英国退欧日”最终协议也变得几乎不可能。
en: As a result, the Brexit negotiations have gone nowhere, and reaching a final agreement in time for “Brexit day” has become virtually impossible.

zh: 此外，即使“落实期”将“经济退欧”日期延后到了2021年，英国制造业也没有足够时间重新组织，从而在引入欧盟外部常规边境控制后生存下来。
en: Moreover, even with the “implementation period” delaying “economic Brexit” until 2021, there simply is not enough time to restructure British manufacturing so that it can survive the introduction of the normal border controls that operate outside the EU.

zh: 梅政府中预见到灾难的亲欧派提出了“泽西模式 ” （ Jersey model ） ， 英国制造业继续留在欧盟关税联盟、自由市场和共同增值税区，同时去掉劳动力和服务的自由流动。
en: Foreseeing disaster, pro-Europeans in May’s government have proposed a “Jersey model,” whereby British manufacturing alone would remain in the EU customs union, single market, and common value-added-tax area, while free movement of labor and services would be curtailed.

zh: 但欧盟不会考虑这一方案，它坚持“四大自由 ” （ 商品、资本、服务和劳动力的自由流动）不可分割。
en: But this is a non-starter for the EU, which insists on the inseparability of the “four freedoms” (free movement of goods, capital, services, and labor).

zh: 爱尔兰边境这一棘手问题也无法在梅的红线框架内得到解决。
en: Nor can the vexing question of the Irish border be resolved within the confines of May’s red lines.

zh: 12月，梅同意不在北爱尔兰和爱尔兰之间设置实体或经济边境。
en: In December, May agreed that there would be no physical or economic border between Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland, which will remain an EU member state.

zh: 但她也向奥尔斯特新教徒（Ulster Protestants）做出让步，北爱尔兰和英国主岛之间不会有边境。
en: But she has also conceded to the Ulster Protestants that there will be no border between Northern Ireland and mainland Britain.

zh: 这两个承诺不可调和，因为这将导致英吉利海峡上出现一条硬边境。
en: These two promises cannot be reconciled, given that there is to be a hard border on the English Channel.

zh: 因此，梅唯一的出路是接受四大自由（这要求同时也接受欧洲法院的司法管辖）以避免与欧洲大陆之间的硬边境。
en: May’s only way out, then, is to avoid a hard border with continental Europe by accepting the four freedoms (which also requires accepting ECJ jurisdiction).

zh: 不管欧盟委员会或梅政府有没有认识到，他们的目标之间矛盾重重。
en: Whether or not the Commission or the May government yet realizes it, the contradiction between their goals is absolute.

zh: 英国想要欧盟放弃其立盟原则，以换取400亿欧元和爱尔兰没有硬边境。
en: The British want the EU to abandon its founding principles in exchange for €40 billion ($46 billion) and no hard border in Ireland.

zh: 但英国已经承诺了这些让步，因此欧盟没有理由去听取它的特殊要求。
en: But, given that the UK has already committed to those concessions, the EU has no reason to listen to its special pleading.

zh: 如果梅政府食言其在12月所做出的承诺，就将面临“没有协议的英国退欧 ” 。
en: Were the May government to renege on the commitments it made in December, it would confront a “no-deal Brexit.”

zh: 英国将被驱逐出欧盟，英国经济的许多行业将受到灭顶之灾。
en: The UK would crash out of the EU, and many sectors of the British economy would be decimated.

zh: 仍然有三个可能的结果，两个比较简单，一个比较复杂。
en: Three possible outcomes remain, two simple and one complicated.

zh: 在第一种情形中，英国放弃“红线 ” ， 接受“挪威+模式 ” ， 不但留在单一市场中，也留在关税联盟中。
en: In the first scenario, Britain would abandon its “red lines” and adopt a “Norway-plus model,” remaining not just in the single market, but also in the customs union.

zh: 在第二种情形中，英国英国接受爱尔兰海上的经济边境，保持主岛的红线，与欧盟达成自由贸易协定。
en: In the second scenario, the UK would accept an economic border in the Irish Sea and maintain its red lines for mainland Britain, by entering into a free-trade agreement with the EU.

zh: 矛盾的是，欧盟委员会和英国强硬退欧派都有可能接受这一主岛的结果，除非后者拒绝接受主岛和北爱尔兰之间的边境。
en: Paradoxically, both the European Commission and hardline Brexiteers could agree on this outcome for mainland Britain, except that the latter refuse to accept a border between the mainland and Northern Ireland.

zh: 更大的问题是这些“简单”方案都不可能在秋季截止期之前被梅同意。
en: The larger problem is that neither of these “simple” solutions will be agreed by May before the fall deadline.

zh: 第二个结果将是英国制造业的灾难，除非过渡期延长许多年，给企业时间重组业务。
en: And the second outcome would spell disaster for British manufacturing, unless the transition period was extended by many years to give businesses time to restructure their operations.

zh: 因此，唯一的出路是政治危机。
en: The only way out, then, is through a political crisis.

zh: 这场危机很可能发生在欧洲内部，起因将是主要成员国或美国总统特朗普试图削弱欧盟。
en: Such a crisis may well occur within Europe, as a result of conflicts between major member states or US President Donald Trump’s attempts to undermine the EU.

zh: 但欧洲危机无法成为梅为全体英国确保“泽西模式”的及时雨。
en: But a European crisis would not come in time for May to secure a “Jersey model” for the UK as a whole.

zh: 更有可能的情况是，在此之前，英国本身就将因为公众日益认识到没有协议的退欧所带来的巨大的经济和社会成本而发生危机。
en: It is far more likely that before then, Britain itself will experience a crisis as the public grows increasingly aware of the massive economic and social costs of a looming no-deal Brexit.

zh: 一旦危机爆发，英国的红线消失，可能的结果将不可胜计。
en: Once the crisis erupts and British red lines begin to dissolve, any number of possible outcomes could follow.

zh: 过渡期可能被延长到（比如）2025年，随后建立自由贸易协定和爱尔兰海经济边境。
en: The transition period could be extended to, say, 2025, to be followed by a free-trade agreement and an economic border in the Irish Sea.

zh: 或者英国退欧本身可能延长多年，以“挪威+”模式为终极目标。
en: Or Brexit itself could be delayed for a number of years, with the “Norway plus” model serving as the ultimate goal.

zh: 这两种情形都有可能导致第二次公投，将退欧完全推翻。
en: Then again, either scenario might lead to a second referendum and a reversal of Brexit altogether.

zh: 无论如何，显然英国方现在所构想的退欧绝无可能实现。
en: In any event, it is clear that Brexit, as the British side currently conceives it, is simply impossible.

zh: 如果它发生的话，也不会是梅目前所建议的。
en: If it happens at all, it will not look like anything May has proposed so far.

zh: 金钱如何扫清英国退欧谈判障碍
en: How Money Could Unblock the Brexit Talks

zh: 伦敦—和许多离婚过程一样，英国与欧盟的谈判也陷入了只有通过妥协才能打破的僵局。
en: LONDON – Like many divorce proceedings, Britain’s negotiations with the European Union have reached an impasse that can be broken only by compromise.

zh: 解决办法是双方都承认无法在2019年3月英国退欧大限前的短暂的时间里形成永久性新关系。
en: The solution is for both sides to admit that a permanent new relationship cannot be agreed in the short time remaining until the Brexit deadline in March 2019.

zh: 因此，谈判不应该着眼于让英国在那时离开欧盟，而应该转向英国首相梅在上个月正式要求的临时性“过渡 ” ， 这也是如今英国商界领袖和公众形成强烈抑制并要求的。
en: So, instead of letting the United Kingdom crash out of the EU then, the talks should now shift to the temporary “transition” that Prime Minister Theresa May officially requested last month – and which a strong consensus among Britain’s business leaders and public now demands.

zh: 最重要的是，谈判者应该立即将重点放在有序过渡所要求的英国预算贡献上。
en: Above all, the negotiators should focus immediately on the British budget contributions that will be required to make an orderly transition possible.

zh: 形成双赢过渡协定需要双方都做出一些妥协。
en: An agreement on a mutually beneficial transition would require some compromises from both sides.

zh: 但不论是英国还是欧盟，都不需要放弃任何根本性原则。
en: But neither Britain nor the EU would have to abandon any fundamental principles.

zh: 对欧洲来说，将谈判焦点转向临时性协定 — — 也许可以以欧盟与挪威的关系作为样板 — — 只不过是略微失去点颜面：欧盟领导人不得不承认他们最初安排的英国退欧谈判顺序必须重新调整。
en: For Europe, shifting the focus of negotiations to a temporary agreement, probably modeled on the EU’s relationship with Norway, would involve only a small loss of face: EU leaders would have to concede that the sequencing they originally proposed for the Brexit talks had to be rejigged.

zh: 不再是首先进行金融结算，然后谈判贸易关系，相反，必须认识到金融和贸易是相互依存关系 — — 因此要同时讨论。
en: Instead of agreeing on a financial settlement first, and then moving on to trade relations, finance and trade would have to be acknowledged as interdependent – and thus be discussed simultaneously.

zh: 对英国来说，谈判焦点从永久性协定转向有序过渡的条件能够将现在阻止退欧进程的预算问题转变为清除谈判障碍的关键。
en: For Britain, a change of focus from permanent arrangements to the conditions for an orderly transition could transform the budgetary issues now preventing progress into a key that could unlock the talks.

zh: 在上个月于佛罗伦萨所做的讲话中，梅提出在英国退欧大限之后设定至少两年的过渡期，在此期间，英国每年贡献大约10亿欧元的预算，并保持劳动力自由流动和执行所有欧盟规则。
en: In a speech delivered in Florence last month, May offered to make EU budget contributions of roughly €10 billion ($11.8 billion) annually for a transition period of at least two years after the Brexit deadline, as well as to maintain free movement of labor and enforce all EU rules.

zh: 梅希望她的承诺能够赢得欧洲领导人 — — 特别是最大的预算贡献者德国，以及主要预算受益者波兰和葡萄牙。
en: May hoped that her promise would win over European leaders – especially the biggest contributor, Germany, and the big net recipients, such as Poland and Portugal.

zh: 但她的建议并没有引起多大关注，也许这是因为欧盟领导人并不太担心英国在2019年和2020年退欧所造成的金融漏洞，而是更关心2021—2026年的下一个预算周期。
en: But her offer failed to impress, probably because EU leaders are less worried about the financial hole created by Brexit in 2019 and 2020 than they are about the next budget cycle, from 2021 to 2026.

zh: 提出英国应该在下一个十年的大部分时间里继续缴纳预算看上去完全不现实，因为梅所在的保守党中的疑欧派强烈反对一切向欧盟的支付项。
en: To suggest that Britain should pay budget contributions well into the next decade may seem completely unrealistic, given the vehement opposition to all EU payments from Euroskeptics in May’s Conservative Party.

zh: 但是，更仔细的观察可以发现，长期缴纳预算对梅来说有两个大优点。
en: But, on closer inspection, making a long-term budget offer could have two big advantages for May.

zh: 首先，过渡性预算贡献可以包装为商业支付，以支持英国能从中受益的欧洲计划，而不是欧盟现在所要求的、听起来像是惩罚性质的五六十亿欧元的“离婚费 ” 。
en: First, transitional budget contributions could be presented as commercial payments to support European programs from which Britain benefits, instead of the punitive-sounding “divorce settlement” of €50-60 billion currently demanded by the EU.

zh: 如果英国过渡性支付在五六年中一直保持在当前水平（10亿欧元）左右 — — 这是谈判永久性贸易关系的现实要求 — — 其总和也将达到这一规模。
en: If Britain’s transitional payments continued near the current level of €10 billion for the five or six years realistically required to negotiate a permanent trading relationship, they would add up to the same amount.

zh: 其次，英国提出缴纳预算是实现梅所谓的她的终极目标 — — 与欧盟的“深刻而特殊的关系”的强大工具。
en: Second, a British budget offer would be a powerful tool to create the “deep and special partnership” with Europe that May claims is her ultimate goal.

zh: 直到上个月，梅一直避免提出这一方案，担心这样会引起党内强硬疑欧派的抵触。
en: Until last month, May avoided defining this phrase, for fear of antagonizing her party’s hardline Europhobes.

zh: 但在佛罗伦萨讲话中，梅承诺英国企业能获得与接近当前水平的欧洲市场准入。
en: But in her Florence speech, May promised British businesses something close to the current level of access to EU markets.

zh: 她还认可了任何欧洲市场准入特权都需要英国贡献欧盟预算，就像挪威和瑞士一样。
en: She also recognized that any privileged access to EU markets would require budget contributions, as in the case of Norway and Switzerland.

zh: 言下之意显而易见：要想获得接近当前水平的欧盟市场准入，就要贡献接近胆管水平的欧盟预算。
en: The implication was clear: something close to the current level of access to EU markets would demand something close to the current level of budget contributions.

zh: 而如果梅的“深刻而特殊的关系”要想成为英国-欧盟关系的永久性特征，预算贡献也必须是永久性的。
en: And if May’s “deep and special partnership” is to be a permanent feature of British-EU relations, the budgetary contributions will have to be permanent, too.

zh: 但万一没对于“深刻而特殊的关系”其实并不是认真的呢？
en: But what if May is not really serious about that “deep and special partnership”?

zh: 万一她的真正目标是通过与欧盟“决裂”满足保守党强硬派呢？
en: What if her true objective is to satisfy Conservative hardliners by bringing about a “clean break”  with the EU?

zh: 即便如此，英国仍需要支付预算多年，如果它想实现有序的、不会引起破坏的退欧的话。
en: Even then, Britain will need to continue paying budget contributions for many years, if it wants an orderly and non-disruptive Brexit.

zh: 不妨认为英国的终极目标是建立全新的全球贸易关系，而不是特殊的欧盟贸易特权。
en: Let’s assume that Britain’s ultimate aim is to create completely new global trading relationships, without any special EU trading privileges.

zh: 这些新贸易协议需要多年时间谈判，在它们完成之间，英国企业急需避免两大迫在眉睫的破坏：一个将发生在2019年3月英国不再具有欧盟成员资格时，另一个发生在新全球协定完成并生效时（可能在未来的任何时候 ） 。
en: These new trade deals will take many years to negotiate, and until their completion, British businesses are desperate to avoid two costly disruptions: one when EU membership ends in March 2019, and another at whatever future date the new global trade agreements are finalized and come into effect.

zh: 避免这一双重破坏是梅提出在2019—2021年间设立一个“静止”过渡期的全部目的。
en: Avoiding such a double disruption is the whole point of May’s proposal for a “standstill” transition period from 2019 to 2021.

zh: 但实现这一目标需要英国的欧盟安排一直保持静止，直到新全球协定准备就绪。
en: But achieving that objective will require the standstill in Britain’s EU arrangements to continue until new global agreements are ready to implement.

zh: 这意味着英国的预算贡献也必须一直保持到新全球协定完成。
en: This implies that Britain’s budget contributions must also continue until new global agreements are finalized.

zh: 与几十个国家进行的复杂谈判在短短两年的英国退欧期之内完成，这样的概率微乎其微。
en: The probability that complex negotiations with dozens of countries can be completed within just two years of Brexit is vanishingly small.

zh: 因此，即使英国政客和选民真的想要完全与欧洲撕破脸面的硬退欧，英国企业也需要保留特殊的欧盟贸易安排 — — 至少在2021年之后再延续几年，相应地，英国也需要继续缴纳欧盟预算。
en: So, even if British politicians and voters really want a hard Brexit involving total rupture with Europe, UK businesses will need to preserve their special EU trading arrangements, along with the associated budget contributions, for at least several years beyond 2021.

zh: 最后的结果是，无论英国希望哪种退欧，有序撤退都需要在其在退欧之后继续为欧盟支付预算。
en: The upshot is that, regardless of what type of Brexit the UK wants, any orderly withdrawal will require continued post-Brexit budget payments to the EU.

zh: 唯一的问题是这一支付是持久的 — — 如果梅真的想要“深刻而特殊的关系的话 ” ， 还是只延续到在硬退欧后进行新贸易谈判所需要的5—7年。
en: The only question is whether these payments turn out to be permanent, as they would if May really wants a “deep and special partnership,” or continue only for the 5-7 years required to negotiate new trade agreements after a hard Brexit.

zh: 无论如何，梅应该认识到，支付欧盟预算是退欧后多年之内都无法避免的。
en: Either way, May should recognize that EU budget payments will be inevitable for many years after Brexit.

zh: 此外，她还应该将这一认识转变为有吸引力的长期金融方案，以扫清退欧谈判的障碍。
en: More than that, she should turn this recognition into an impressive long-term financial offer to unblock the Brexit talks.

zh: 退欧的君子协定
en: A Brexit Gentlemen’s Agreement

zh: 布鲁塞尔—在最新的退欧讲话中，英国首相梅拒绝接受英国留在欧盟关税联盟中的方案，理由是英国需要自己的贸易政策。
en: BRUSSELS – In her latest speech on Brexit, British Prime Minister Theresa May rejected the prospect of the United Kingdom remaining in the European Union’s customs union, on the grounds that the UK wants its own trade policy.

zh: 这不符合英国和欧盟的最佳利益。
en: This is not in the best interest of either the UK or the EU.

zh: 诚然，挪威和瑞士都是高度融入欧盟市场但和欧盟保持关税隔离的国家。
en: It is true that Norway and Switzerland, both of which are highly integrated into the EU market, have customs borders with the bloc.

zh: 这些国家需要独立的商业政策为国内农业部门提供比欧盟更大的保护，因为多山的地形，两国农业部门无法实现高效。
en: These countries need an independent commercial policy to provide greater protection than the EU offers to their domestic agricultural sectors, which in both cases can never be efficient, owing to mountainous terrain.

zh: 但传统上英国对其农业的保护力度要小得多，在退欧后更可能采取和欧盟非常相近的商业政策。
en: Yet the UK has traditionally been much less protective of its agriculture, and is thus likely after Brexit to pursue a commercial policy that is very similar to that of the EU, anyway.

zh: 因此，很难看出英国可以从国家贸易政策中获得什么好处 — — 特别是在特朗普所领导的美国正在采取毫不顾及小贸易伙伴的政策（如对进口钢铁和铝征收关税）的情况下。
en: It is therefore difficult to see what the UK would gain from pursuing a national trade policy – especially at a time when the United States, under President Donald Trump, is pursuing policies (such as imposing tariffs on imported steel and aluminum) that show little regard for its smaller trade partners.

zh: 事实上，英国退欧后关税联盟的最主要障碍是政治。
en: The truth is that the main impediment to a post-Brexit customs union is political.

zh: 支持留在关税联盟的工党领导人杰里米·科尔宾（Jeremy Corbyn）强调，像英国这样的重要性和影响力巨大的国家，不可让人觉得跟着对它完全没有影响力的欧盟的决定亦步亦趋。
en: As Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, who supports remaining in the customs union, has emphasized, a country with the heft and influence of the UK cannot be viewed as merely following EU decisions, over which it has no influence.

zh: 但这个问题是可以解决的 — — 或者说，是可以巧妙处理的。
en: Yet this problem can be solved – or, rather, finessed.

zh: 英国参与欧盟决定的要求应该真诚以对，让来自英国的专家加入决定贸易政策的委员会。
en: The UK’s demand to weigh in on EU decisions can and should be accommodated, with experts from the UK included in the committees that decide trade policy.

zh: 这些专家不会拥有投票权，但可以影响决策。
en: Those experts would have no voting rights, but they would be able to shape decision-making.

zh: 欧盟已经和冰岛、挪威和瑞士在申根区问题上有了类似的协议。
en: The EU already has similar arrangements with Iceland, Norway, and Switzerland regarding matters relating to the Schengen Area.

zh: 当然，正式决策权力是另一个问题。
en: Formal decision-making power is of course another matter.

zh: 欧盟的法律结构不可能允许非成员国参与到有约束力的决策制定中。
en: The EU’s legal structure cannot allow a non-member state to participate in binding decisions.

zh: 这就需要君子协定，欧盟承诺在制定贸易政策中考虑英国的利益。
en: This calls for something of a gentlemen’s agreement, with the EU pledging to take UK interests into account when making trade-policy decisions.

zh: 如果英国留在现有欧盟关税联盟中 — — 过渡期预计将会如此 — — 而不是与欧盟谈判新的关税协定，那么这个君子协定也可以扩展到欧盟与第三方国家签署的新贸易协定。
en: If the UK remains in the existing EU customs union – as is foreseen for the transition period – rather than negotiating a new customs agreement with the EU, that gentleman’s agreement would also extend to new trade agreements that the EU concludes with third countries.

zh: 毕竟，这样的协定将明确适用于欧盟的关税区全体 — — 根据世界贸易组织规则的意义准确的条款。
en: After all, such agreements would apply explicitly to the EU’s entire customs territory – a term with a precise meaning under WTO rules.

zh: 因此，一切其中所包含的市场准入收益都会自动适用于英国。
en: So, whatever market-access benefits they include would automatically apply to the UK.

zh: 欧盟还应该摆出善意姿态，支持英国在现有欧盟自由贸易协定所授予的市场准入事宜上的“便宜行事 ” ， 从而避免每项协议都重新谈判的必要。
en: As a gesture of goodwill, the EU should also support the UK’s efforts to “grandfather” its market access resulting from existing EU free-trade agreements and thereby avoid the need to renegotiate each and every deal.

zh: 法律上的论点是欧盟关税区没有发生改变，因此现有欧盟贸易协定必须继续适用于英国。
en: The legal argument would be that the EU customs territory has not changed, so existing EU trade agreements must continue to apply to the UK.

zh: 但这一论点可能受到反驳，让英国出口商突然面临关税和其他贸易壁垒。
en: But this argument could be contested, leaving UK exporters suddenly confronting tariffs and other trade barriers.

zh: 欧盟委员会官员可能不会考虑这个问题，因为这是英国的问题。
en: European Commission officials could dismiss that as the UK’s problem.

zh: 但这样的反应和2017年4月欧洲理事会指引的精神背道而驰。 欧洲理事会要求与英国“就针对第三国贸易伙伴的共同方针问题”展开“建设性对话 ” 。
en: But such a response would run counter to the spirit of the European Council guidelines of April 2017, which call for “a constructive dialogue” with the UK “on a possible common approach toward third-country partners.”

zh: 这一建设性方针应该包括让过渡期内摩擦最小化的举措 — — 如支持贸易协定的便宜行事。
en: Such a constructive approach would include steps – like supporting the grandfathering of trade agreements – that minimize friction during the transition period.

zh: 留在欧盟关税联盟中将让英国的地位大大强于（比如）土耳其，尽管土耳其已经完成了与欧盟建立关税联盟的谈判，但它并不是欧盟关税区真正的一部分。
en: Remaining in the EU’s customs union would leave the UK in a much stronger position than, say, Turkey, which, despite having concluded an agreement to create a customs union with the EU, is not actually part of the bloc’s customs territory.

zh: 因此，第三方并不会自动给予土耳其出口商欧盟水平的市场准入。
en: As a result, third parties do not automatically have to grant Turkish exporters EU-level access to their markets.

zh: 相反，土耳其必须试图说服已经与欧盟达成协议的第三国给予其这一待遇。
en: Instead, Turkey must try to persuade third countries with which the EU has concluded trade deals to do so.

zh: 通常，土耳其能获得成功。
en: Turkey has usually succeeded.

zh: 但其进入谈判时处境总是弱势而尴尬，因为根据要求，对于它的每一份与欧盟的协定，都要授予第三国与欧盟所做出的同样的让步，而第三国没有法律或政治上的义务予以回报。
en: But it enters such negotiations in a weak and somewhat awkward position, because it is required, per its agreement with the EU, to grant to the third country all of the concessions the EU has made, whereas the third country has no legal or political obligation to reciprocate.

zh: 对欧盟来说，同意在未来贸易谈判中考虑英国利益不应该被视为让步，因为这符合欧盟自身的长期利益。
en: For the EU, agreeing to take the UK’s interests into account in future trade negotiations should not be viewed as a concession, because it is in the EU’s own long-term interest.

zh: 毕竟，如果欧盟能够提供欧盟和英国市场的事实准入 — — 总和比只有欧盟市场的情况大20 % — —其谈判实力将大幅增强。
en: After all, if the EU can offer de facto access to the EU and UK markets – which, together, are 20% larger than the EU market alone – its negotiating power is significantly strengthened.

zh: 在这个例子中，让英国留在欧盟关税联盟中有助于保持欧盟在全球贸易中的地位。
en: In this sense, keeping the UK in the EU customs union would help to preserve the EU’s global standing in trade.

zh: 尽管许多欧盟官员，特别是欧盟委员会委员，有自己的小算盘 — — 让英国留在关税联盟中，但忽视它的利益 — — 但这显然不是一个选项。
en: And while many in the EU, especially the European Commission, would like to have their cake and eat it – keeping the UK in the customs union, while ignoring its interests – that is simply not an option.

zh: 欧盟的选项包括，要么眼看英国退出关税联盟，要么做出政治承诺考虑英国利益，从而让它留在关税联盟。
en: The alternatives available for the EU is either to see the UK to leave its customs union, or to keep the UK in, by making a political commitment to take British interests into account.

zh: 从长期角度，后一个选项更可取。
en: From a long-term perspective, the latter is preferable.

zh: 最后，留在欧盟关税联盟中意味着有可能避免英国退欧后与爱尔兰共和国重新形成硬边境。
en: Finally, remaining in the EU customs union would make it possible to avoid reestablishing a hard border between the UK and the Republic of Ireland after Brexit.

zh: 尽管梅已经同意，任何协议都应该包括避免出现硬边境的条款，但对于如何实际实现这一目标，她只给出了模糊的建议。
en: Though May has agreed that avoiding a hard border should be part of any deal, she has offered only vague suggestions concerning how that could actually be achieved.

zh: 英国退欧是，未来也将一直是双输方案。
en: Brexit is, and will remain, a lose-lose proposition.

zh: 如果退欧观点占据上风，就没有赢家。
en: Neither side can claim victory if its point of view prevails.

zh: 但双方的损失可以降低。
en: But the losses on both sides can be reduced.

zh: 在这方面，让英国留在欧盟关税联盟中 — — 通过保证它扮演非正式但重要的角色 — — 是谈判员的最好的意愿。
en: To that end, keeping the UK in the EU customs union – by guaranteeing it an active, albeit informal role – is negotiators’ best bet.

zh: 为何欧盟必须对英国保持大度
en: Why the EU Must Be Generous to Britain

zh: 慕尼黑—英国首相梅确认了这一点。
en: MUNICH – British Prime Minister Theresa May has confirmed it.

zh: 英国将无可置疑地脱离欧盟，谈判新贸易协定。
en: The United Kingdom will, without a doubt, leave the European Union and negotiate new trade agreements.

zh: 问题是欧盟会接受怎样的协定。
en: The question is what kind of agreement the EU will accept.

zh: 梅清楚地挑明，英国不想要类似于瑞士或挪威的安排，因为这样的安排要求英国让出一定的移民政策控制权。
en: Britain, May has made clear, doesn’t want an arrangement like that of Switzerland or Norway, because that would require it to cede some control over its immigration policy.

zh: 英国领导人指责欧洲法院的判决以既得利益为基础，因此，将司法管辖权让渡给它也绝不是一个选项。
en: Submitting to the jurisdiction of the European Court of Justice, which UK leaders accuse of delivering judgments based on vested interests, is not an option, either.

zh: 但欧盟不准备让英国想怎样就怎样，至少不能让英国不付出点代价。
en: But the EU is not ready simply to allow the UK to drop whatever it doesn’t like, at least not without paying a price.

zh: 欧盟领导人坚持要求英国不能在不允许人员自由流动的情况下与欧洲单一市场自由贸易。
en: The EU’s leaders insist that the UK cannot have free trade with the single market without allowing free movement of people.

zh: 这一顽固立场部分来自这样的担忧：如果英国获得了不对称协议，其他欧盟国家也会照样画葫芦。
en: This stubbornness arises partly from the fear that, if the UK secured such a lopsided deal, other EU countries would attempt to do the same.

zh: 但希望惩罚英国 — — 哪怕只是为了震慑其他成员国脱欧 — — 也肯定是一个因素。
en: But the desire to punish the British, if only to deter other member states from bolting, is surely also a contributing factor.

zh: 这一方针大错特错。
en: This approach is all wrong.

zh: 毫无疑问，英国退欧令人遗憾，但真相是与欧盟的自由贸易不一定非要伴随人员自由流动。
en: While it is undoubtedly regrettable that the UK is leaving, the truth is that free trade with the EU does not have to be accompanied by free movement of people.

zh: 纯粹贸易理论认为，来自自由贸易的经济效应和福利收益与来自劳动力的自由流动的经济效应和福利收益之间是替代关系，前者不会因为后者而得到强化。
en: As pure trade theory shows, the economic effects and welfare gains resulting from free trade are substituted, not enhanced, by those of free movement of labor.

zh: 如果无法移民，各国就更有可能出现工资结构的差异 — — 从而带来价格结构的差异。
en: If migration is not possible, different wage structures are more likely to arise among countries – bringing different price structures with them.

zh: 这些差异增加了来自贸易的收益；事实上，利用这些差异就是贸易的全部意义。
en: These differences increase gains from trade; indeed, exploiting such differences is the entire point of trade.

zh: 如果欧盟拒绝与英国保持自由贸易，欧盟公民蒙受的损失与英国公民一样大。
en: If the EU refuses to sustain free trade with the UK, its citizens will suffer as much as the British.

zh: 其他欧盟国家可能照搬英国的榜样，这样的观点也颇可质疑。
en: The argument that other EU countries would be likely to follow the UK’s lead is dubious.

zh: 政治共同体有两种类型。
en: There are two types of political community.

zh: 一种符合帕累托最优标准：由于共同体做出一致决定 — — 或至少遵守保护少数全体的规则 — — 因此能够实施让一些或所有成员都获益、同时不会让任何人受损的措施。
en: One fulfills the criterion of Pareto optimality: because the community makes decisions unanimously – or, at least, adhering to rules that protect minorities – it implements measures that provide advantages to some or all members and create disadvantages for none.

zh: 这一方针意味着各国不会为了争夺更大蛋糕的份额而牺牲其他国家。
en: That approach means that countries are not fighting for a bigger piece of the pie at the expense of others.

zh: 相反，他们自愿共同致力于确保让蛋糕越做越大，从而所有人都可以分到体面的一大块。
en: Instead, they work together voluntarily to ensure that the pie keeps growing, and that everyone gets a decent slice.

zh: 另一种类型的共同体的首要特征是在各国之间进行资源再分配，第二个特征是多数决策。
en: The other type of community is characterized by, first, the redistribution of resources among countries and, second, by majority decision-making.

zh: 这种共同体会产生赢家和输家，因为多数群体可以强迫推行它的偏好，即使其成员所获得收益大大小于少数群体所蒙受的损失。
en: Here, there are winners and losers, because the majority can force through its preferences, even if the gains its members reap are dwarfed by the losses incurred by the minority.

zh: 结果，蛋糕通常越变越小，一些国家将感到十分不爽。
en: As a result, the pie often becomes smaller, and some countries end up very unhappy.

zh: 第二种类型具有内在不稳定性，因为输家会选择退出。
en: This second type is inherently unstable, because the losers tend to opt out.

zh: 唯一让它们不退出的办法是让退出变得更加不具有吸引力 — — 比如进行惩罚。
en: The only way to keep them in is to make leaving even less appealing – say, by punishing them.

zh: 通过将英国树立为“榜样 ” ， 欧盟传递的信息是它是一个某些成员注定要输的联盟。
en: By seeking to make an example of the UK, the EU is sending the message that it is a union in which some members are bound to lose.

zh: 这正是美国新总统特朗普大力宣传的故事，他宣布支持英国人，并预计更多的国家将效仿英国。
en: This is the narrative being promoted by America’s new president, Donald Trump, who has declared his support for the British and his expectation that more countries will follow suit.

zh: 要避免这样的结果，欧盟必须改革自身，从一个多数统治的再分配联盟转变为一致性统治的最优和自愿的联盟 — — 即符合帕累托原则的联盟。
en: To avoid such an outcome, the EU must transform itself from a redistributive union ruled by the majority to an optimal and voluntary union ruled by unanimity – one that conforms to the Pareto principle.

zh: 第一步应该是放弃在自主收税权之上设立一个共同的欧盟财政部的计划。
en: The first step should be to scrap the plan to install a common EU finance minister at the head of an authority with autonomous taxation powers.

zh: 第二步是向英国提供一个双赢的自由贸易协定。
en: The next is to offer the UK a mutually beneficial free-trade agreement.

zh: 如果欧盟不改变方针，就有可能演变为一个非一致性的共同体，只能让部分成员满意，而其他成员渴望退出。
en: If the EU does not shift its approach, it risks becoming a non-consensual community in which only some members are happy – and others want out.

zh: 尽管惩罚和其他强制措施或能一时留住摇摆成员国，但欧盟也将因此容易动摇，其成员国也容易被利用。
en: While penalties and other coercive measures may be able to keep wavering member states in for a while, this approach would leave the EU susceptible to instability and its members vulnerable to exploitation.

zh: 欧洲可能最终走上苏联的命运。
en: Europe could end up suffering the fate of the Soviet Union.

zh: 当成员感觉“被坑”时，任何关系都无法兴旺。
en: No relationship can flourish if its members feel trapped.

zh: 联盟也不例外。
en: A union is no different.

zh: 看上去有些反直觉，但保持欧盟团结的唯一之道是慷慨大度地让英国离开。
en: As counter-intuitive as it may seem, the only way to keep the EU together is to let Britain go, on generous terms.

zh: 英国退欧的全面失败
en: The Appalling Failure of Brexit

zh: 伦敦—自英国以微弱多数投票支持退出欧盟以来，已经过去了近两年。
en: LONDON – It has been nearly two years since the United Kingdom narrowly voted in favor of leaving the European Union.

zh: 随着退欧进程的展开 — — 按照正式安排，应该在明年3月完成 — — 英国-欧盟关系的未来性质这一根本性问题仍然没有得到回答。
en: As the march toward Brexit – formally set for the end of next March – proceeds, fundamental questions about the nature of the future UK-EU relationship remain unanswered.

zh: 相反，每一次布鲁塞尔谈判需要做出艰难的决定时，英国的部长们就会虚与委蛇，或干脆避而不谈。
en: Instead, every time a tough decision must be made in the negotiations in Brussels, British ministers kick the can down the road, or even into the long grass.

zh: 这有些令人惊奇。
en: This is somewhat surprising.

zh: 显然，那些谋划多年要让英国退出欧盟的政客和报纸编辑们，根本没有想过他们的诡计得逞后会发生什么。
en: Apparently, none of the politicians and newspaper editors who plotted for years to get the UK out of the EU thought much about what would happen if their machinations succeeded.

zh: 他们甚至连英国应该采取“软”退欧还是“硬”退欧都没有形成一致意见。 软退欧意味着英国仍会与欧洲市场保持紧密联系；硬退欧则是不顾对经济的影响一刀两断。
en: They have been unable to agree even on whether the UK should pursue a “soft” Brexit, with the UK remaining closely connected to European markets, or a “hard” Brexit that severs ties without regard for the economic impact.

zh: 一些狂热的退欧分子声称，退出欧盟易如反掌。
en: Some ardent Brexiteers claimed that leaving the EU would be as easy as falling off a log.

zh: 我们的欧洲伙伴，他们说，需要我们远甚于我们需要他们：德国渴望卖给我们骑车，意大利渴望卖给我们普洛赛克葡萄酒，法国渴望卖给我们卡芒贝尔（Camembert）奶酪。
en: Our European partners, they suggested, need us much more than we need them: Germany is desperate to sell us cars, Italy to sell us Prosecco, the French to sell us Camembert.

zh: 大错特错。
en: They could not have been more wrong.

zh: 事实上，是英国严重依靠向欧洲出售商品和服务（占英国出口的大约一半 ） ， 而不是相反。
en: In truth, the UK depends far more on selling to Europe, which accounts for about half of British exports, than Europe does on selling to the UK.

zh: 即使有明确现实的战略，分配给英国退欧谈判的两年时间 — — 从2017年3月英国援引里斯本条约第50条开始 — — 也不足以覆盖需要关注的众多问题。
en: Even with a clear and realistic strategy, the two-year time period allotted for negotiating the UK’s departure – which began in March 2017, when the UK invoked Article 50 of the Treaty of Lisbon – would hardly be sufficient to cover the plethora of issues that demand attention.

zh: 英国在还没有制定好战略的情况下就开始了谈判，让这一过程对所有人都变得更加艰难。
en: By launching that process without such a strategy, the UK government made the process much more difficult for everyone.

zh: 除了逼迫英国谈判员参与几乎不可能的谈判，首相梅还自缚手脚，做出了旨在满足她的强硬右派保守党的承诺。
en: Beyond forcing British negotiators into a near-impossible timetable, Prime Minister Theresa May has tied their hands by making promises aimed at satisfying her Conservative Party’s hard-right Brexiteers.

zh: 这些承诺中包括取消欧洲人的自由流动，尽管一些英国人怨声载道的移民有一大半来自欧洲之外。
en: These include a pledge to end the free movement of people from Europe, even though well over half of the immigration that some Britons decry comes from outside the EU.

zh: 这些承诺还包括退出欧盟单一市场和关税联盟。
en: It also includes a promise to leave the EU’s single market and customs union.

zh: 到目前为止，对谈判负主责的英国部长们 — — 一群以教条主义和个人野心，而非胜任能力著称的人 — — 成功确保了一个关键领域的一致意见：2019年3月的截止期后将开始为期两年的过渡期。
en: The UK ministers mainly responsible for the talks – a group better known for their dogmatism and personal ambition than their competence – have so far managed to secure agreement in one key area: following the March 2019 deadline, a two-year transition period will begin.

zh: 但即使是这一共识也并非铁板一块，因为它取决于谈判员首先是否能在另一个问题上达成共识：英国退出关税联盟后如何处理爱尔兰共和国和北爱尔兰之间的边界。
en: But even that agreement is not set in stone, as it depends on whether negotiators can first agree on what to do about the border between the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland once the UK leaves the customs union.

zh: 你可以留在没有边界的关税同盟中，也可以留在有边界的关税同盟外。
en: You can be in a customs union without a border, or outside a customs union with a border.

zh: 全世界还没有这一点不成立的例子。
en: There is no example anywhere in the world where this is not true.

zh: 但在爱尔兰岛上重新划定边界会引起严重问题，不仅影响跨境贸易，还会影响安全和20年前给北爱尔兰带来和平的受难日协定的未来。
en: Yet reintroducing a border on the island of Ireland raises serious problems, affecting not just cross-border trade, but also security and the future of the Good Friday Agreement that brought peace to Northern Ireland 20 years ago.

zh: 眉头紧皱的官员们焚膏继晷地试图找出办法跳出这一循环。
en: With furrowed brows, officials burn the midnight oil trying to devise a way to square this circle.

zh: 但政治学的几何定律令他们无功而返。
en: But the laws of political geometry have torpedoed their efforts.

zh: 退出关税联盟的好处与巨大的风险完全不对称。
en: The benefits of leaving the customs union do not come close to outweighing the risks.

zh: 退欧派说，自由制定与世界其他国家和地区的贸易协议最终能让英国受益。
en: Brexiteers claim that the UK would ultimately benefit from being free to make its own trade deals with the rest of the world.

zh: 但认为英国单干能比它作为世界最富裕的单一市场的一份子更好，这简直是痴心妄想。
en: But to believe that the UK can do better on its own than it can as part of the world’s richest single market is nothing short of delusional.

zh: 英国在试图达成新贸易协议时，本质上都是在复制欧盟（不管是现有的还是正在谈判中的）与墨西哥、中国、韩国、越南、新加坡和日本等国家的协议。
en: As the UK attempts to strike new trade deals, it will be trying essentially to replicate the EU’s agreements, both existing and under negotiation, with countries like Mexico, China, South Korea, Vietnam, Singapore, and Japan.

zh: 这不仅要耗费大量时间，并且英国也不可能得到与欧盟一样的有利条件。
en: Not only will that take a lot of time; the UK is unlikely to secure terms as favorable as the EU has.

zh: 毕竟，众所周知在贸易谈判中，大合作方总是比小合作方更好。
en: After all, it is well known that, in trade negotiations, the bigger partner tends to do better than the smaller one.

zh: 而英国的地位将因为原产地规则等技术性问题进一步削弱。
en: And the UK’s position will be weakened further by technical issues like rules of origin.

zh: 目前，即便产品的零部件在欧洲其他地方生产，英国也能受益（取决于商定的限度 ） 。
en: At present, the country benefits even when parts of a product are manufactured elsewhere in Europe, up to an agreed limit.

zh: 失去这一弹性将给汽车和其他制造商造成严重的问题。
en: The loss of that flexibility will pose a major problem to car manufacturers, among others.

zh: 到目前为止，英国退欧过程并没有带来明显的好处。
en: So far, the march toward Brexit has brought no obvious gains.

zh: 相反，据英格兰银行数据，英国平均真实家庭收入比退欧公投前预测低了900英镑。
en: On the contrary, according to the Bank of England, average real household income in the UK is £900 ($1,200) below pre-referendum forecasts.

zh: 促使相对微弱多数选民选择退欧的丰厚承诺根本没有实现；其中绝大部分永远都不会实现。
en: The lofty promises that drove a relatively slim majority of voters to choose Brexit in 2016 are nowhere near being fulfilled; in most cases, they never will be.

zh: 随着英国退欧残酷现实逐渐显现，英国内阁成员和退欧派领袖开始面面相觑，互相指责，争相撇清自己：法官、公务员、议员 — — 甚至是那些投票支持留在欧盟的人。
en: As the stark reality of Brexit sinks in, members of Britain’s cabinet and leading Brexiteers have increasingly turned on one another and attempted to cast blame on everyone but themselves: judges, civil servants, parliamentarians – even those who voted to remain in the EU.

zh: 他们说，英国必须砥砺前行，因为这是“人民的意愿 ” （ 尽管选民认为他们支持的东西恰恰仍然被遮遮掩掩 ） 。
en: They declare that Britain must plunge ahead, because that was “the will of the people” (though exactly what voters believed they were voting for remains opaque).

zh: 与此同时，他们为即将到来的灾难准备好了借口。
en: Meanwhile, they prepare their excuses for the impending debacle.

zh: 列宁有一句名问 ： “ 准备怎么办？
en: As Lenin famously asked, “What is to be done?”

zh: ”很难说。
en: It is hard to say.

zh: 我们也许只需要期待最好的事情，同时为最坏的情况做好准备，认识到我们的孩子们很有可能要替我们收拾残局。
en: We may simply have to hope for the best, while preparing for the worst, recognizing that our children may well be the ones who have to pick up the pieces.

zh: 但愿，果真如此的话，他们会比今天的领导人把英国治理得更好。
en: One hopes that, if that does turn out to be the case, they do a better job governing the UK than today’s leaders.

zh: 英国的关键时刻
en: Britain’s Moment of Truth

zh: 发自布鲁塞尔 — — 英国投票脱离欧盟的举措令该国在欧洲所扮演的角色日益弱化。
en: BRUSSELS – Britain’s vote to leave the European Union has put the country’s role in Europe in limbo.

zh: 时间每流逝一天，英国与欧盟之间的僵局就恶化一点，使未来增加更多的不确定性。
en: Every day that passes deepens the impasse between the United Kingdom and the EU and makes the future more uncertain.

zh: 欧盟领导人希望尽快依照《里斯本条约》的第50条（成员国退出条款）开始走流程，也敦促英国方面从速照此办理。
en: The EU leadership would like to move the process along and has called on the UK to immediately take steps to do so, as outlined in Article 50, the member-withdrawal provision of the Treaty of Lisbon.

zh: 英国这边则是一片混乱，首要解决的是在首相卡梅伦宣布辞职后选择一个新的领导者。
en: The UK side is in disarray and first must choose a new leader now that Prime Minister David Cameron has announced his resignation.

zh: 不过英国政界大部分人都已经坦然接受了脱欧公投的结果，当务之急就是以最能维护英国国家利益的方式来实现选民这这一意愿。
en: But most British politicians have come to accept the outcome of the “Brexit” referendum, and that the will of the voters must now be carried out in a manner that best upholds Britain’s national interests.

zh: 由于欧盟内部市场一直是英国的重中之重，其中一个得到跨党派支持并进行了广泛讨论的选项就是采取所谓“挪威模式 ” ： 成为欧洲经济区协定（European Economic Area）的成员国。
en: Because the EU’s internal market has always been a key priority for the UK, one widely discussed option, which has cross-party support, is the so-called the “Norway model”: membership in the European Economic Area (EEA).

zh: 根据欧洲经济区协定的安排，挪威（以及冰岛）拥有全部且不受阻碍地进入欧洲单一市场的权限，其中包括金融服务。
en: Under the EEA arrangement, Norway (along with Iceland) has full, unfettered access to the EU’s single market, including for financial services.

zh: 但进入欧盟内部市场同时也需要欧洲经济区成员国接受来自欧盟侧的自由流入，不仅包括商品，服务和资本，还包括劳动者。
en: But access to the internal market also requires EEA members to accept full freedom of movement not only for goods, services, and capital, but also for workers.

zh: 那么挪威选项比欧盟成员国资格更好？
en: Would the Norway option be better for Britain than full EU membership?

zh: 一个简单的逻辑推演可以帮助我们理解：试想四十年前法国否决了英国的欧盟成员国资格，而英国转而加入欧洲经济区。
en: A simple thought experiment might help: go back four decades and assume that France had vetoed UK membership in the EU, and that the UK had joined the EEA instead.

zh: 那么在这种情况下，脱欧公投就变成了决定英国是否应留在欧洲经济区内。
en: Under this scenario, the Brexit referendum would have been on whether the UK should remain in the EEA.

zh: 假设也会有一场“脱区”运动，其论据又能有何不同？
en: Would the arguments offered by this hypothetical “Leave” campaign have been any different?

zh: 真实的脱欧运动将论点集中在三个议题上：英国对欧盟的预算贡献，自由流动的劳动者，以及国家主权。
en: The real Leave campaign’s arguments focused on three issues: the UK’s contributions to the EU budget, free movement for workers, and national sovereignty.

zh: 现在让我们轮流来检视这几点：
en: Let’s consider them in turn.

zh: 脱欧运动主张说与其作为一个成员国向欧盟贡献预算，不如把这笔钱更合理地花在本国身上。
en: The Leave campaign argued that the money the UK contributes to the EU budget as a member state could be better spent at home.

zh: 然而同样的论点也适用欧洲经济区成员。
en: This same argument would apply against EEA membership.

zh: 事实上相对其国民收入来说，英国对欧盟的财政贡献其实比经济区下的挪威还小。
en: In fact, the UK’s financial contribution to the EU is actually smaller, relative to its national income, than Norway’s under the EEA.

zh: 脱欧运动还声称，劳动力的自由流动还加剧了传闻中的恐怖主义威胁，令英国本土工人的失业率走高。
en: The Leave campaign also claimed that free movement of labor heightens the supposed dangers of terrorism and higher unemployment for British workers.

zh: 但在欧盟关于劳动力流动的规定也同样适用于挪威和所有欧洲经济区国家。
en: But the provisions governing labor mobility in the EU apply to Norway and all EEA countries as well.

zh: 如果说迁徙自由是离开欧盟的关键原因，那么挪威模式也同样是无法接受的。
en: To the extent that freedom of movement was the key reason for leaving the EU, the Norway model would be equally unacceptable.

zh: 这给我们引出了脱欧运动的第三个论据和核心主题 ： “ 重夺对英国经济的控制权 ” 。
en: This brings us to the Leave campaign’s third argument and central theme: “getting back control” of the rules and regulations governing Britain’s economy.

zh: 然而这个目标对欧洲经济区成员国资格的破坏性可比欧盟要大。
en: This objective would be an even stronger argument against EEA membership than it was against EU membership.

zh: 根据经济区协议，英国仍然得服从布鲁塞尔总部制定的相关规则，但在制定这些规则时的发言权要比作为欧盟成员国更少。
en: Under the EEA, the UK would still have to abide by the rules and regulations set in Brussels, but it would have far less say in their creation than it does as an EU member.

zh: 事实上，在欧盟内部，英国在金融服务业规则的制定上享有相当大的影响力，而该行业正是其经济中最重要的产业。
en: In fact, within the EU, Britain had considerable influence over financial services, the most important industry in its economy.

zh: “重夺控制权”的矛头同时也直指位于卢森堡的欧洲法院，按照欧盟公约规定，其判决的效力超过各国本国法院。
en: “Getting back control” was also directed against the EU Court of Justice in Luxembourg, whose judgments, by convention, have precedence over judgments by national courts.

zh: 但欧洲经济区也有自己的法院，其判决同时也对欧洲经济区成员国具有约束力。
en: But the EEA also has its own court, whose judgments are binding on EEA member states.

zh: 总而言之，一切反对加入欧盟的论点也适用于欧洲经济区成员国资格，而且往往更具说服力。
en: In short, all the arguments against EU membership also apply, often with even more force, against EEA membership.

zh: 不过，一些国家依然会选择此选项。
en: Still, some countries do choose this option.

zh: 挪威一直倾向于留在欧洲经济区，并已经不止一次地大比数公投否决加入欧盟的动议。
en: The Norwegians have consistently preferred to remain in the EEA, and have voted more than once, by large majorities, against joining the EU.

zh: 丹麦也是个类似的例子，1992年丹麦人投票否决了根据《马斯特里赫特条约》的欧元区成员国身份。
en: Denmark has been a similar case since 1992, when Danish voters rejected eurozone membership under the Maastricht Treaty.

zh: 如今丹麦克朗与欧元的联系是如此紧密，导致丹麦央行实际上已经丧失了自身的独立性。
en: Now, the Danish krone is so tightly linked to the euro that Denmark’s central bank has effectively lost its independence.

zh: 如果当年能加入欧元区，丹麦起码还能获得一点上谈判桌讨价还价的权利。
en: By joining the euro, Denmark would at least have gained a seat at the table.

zh: 瑞士的全民公决甚至都否决了加入欧洲经济区；但是为了能更好地与欧盟做生意，瑞士政府后来不得不接受大部分欧洲经济区规则，无论如何，包括人员的自由流动以及对欧盟预算的贡献。
en: The Swiss rejected even EEA membership in a referendum; however, to do business with the EU on the level it wanted, the Swiss government later had to accept most of the EEA rules anyway, including the free movement of people and contributions to the EU budget.

zh: 正如这些真实的例子所表明的那样，没有任何一个想从���洲进程中受益的国家能鱼与熊掌兼得。
en: As these real-world examples show, no country that wants to benefit from the European project has been able to have its cake and eat it.

zh: 开放边界和经济一体化需要共同规则。
en: Open borders and economic integration require common rules.

zh: 在这块拥有超过30个中小规模国家和5亿人口的大陆上是无法通行好几套左右逢源的“意大利面碗”式协定的。
en: A “spaghetti bowl” of different à la carte arrangements would not work for a continent of more than 30 small and medium-size countries and more than 500 million people.

zh: 而欧盟则提供这一套共同规则，通过共同的机构，让每一个国家 — — 即使是最小的 — — 都能有发言权。
en: The EU provides this set of common rules, buttressed by common institutions that give every country, even the smallest, a say.

zh: 这就是欧洲的主权平衡手段：每个国家都保留正式的主权，但如果实现经济繁荣，就必须接受共同的规范和法规令欧洲实现高度的跨境劳动分工。
en: This is the balancing act of sovereignty in Europe: Each state remains formally sovereign, but if it wants to prosper economically, it must accept the common norms and regulations that enable Europe’s intensive cross-border division of labor.

zh: 当然，欧洲不仅仅是一个自由贸易区；也是共同社会和文化生活的集散地。
en: Of course, Europe is more than just a free-trade area; it is also a hub of shared social and cultural life.

zh: 这就是为什么迁徙自由是如此的吸引人，而不仅仅从经济角度来看。
en: This is why freedom of movement is so appealing, not only from an economic point of view.

zh: 一些规模较小的国家已经放弃了自身在影响欧洲未来方面所扮演的角色。
en: Some smaller countries have abdicated their role in influencing Europe’s future.

zh: 但奇怪的是连英国这么一个拥有悠久全球领导地位的国家会突然放弃了自己。
en: But it is surprising to see a country with such a long history of global leadership as Britain suddenly withdrawing into itself.

zh: 那么放弃了在塑造欧洲未来的历史任务的英国，会否真正满足于永远靠边站呢？
en: Having abandoned its historical role in shaping Europe’s future, will the UK really be content to remain on the sidelines?

zh: 英国悲剧一幕
en: A British Tragedy in One Act

zh: 牛津 — — 对那些宣传离开欧盟、背弃21世纪英国未来的人而言，星期四的夜晚据说非常值得回味。
en: OXFORD – Thursday night is said to have been momentous for those who campaigned to leave the European Union and turn Britain’s back on the twenty-first century.

zh: 至少在这一点上，我同意他们的看法。
en: On that, at least, I can agree.

zh: 西塞罗说 ： “ 那一天是多么悲惨和不幸 ” 。
en: As Cicero wrote: “O wretched and unhappy was that day.”

zh: 脱欧决定将影响今后10年英国国民的生活。
en: The decision to leave the EU will dominate British national life for the next decade, if not longer.

zh: 短期和长期经济冲击的准确规模有待探讨，但很难想象在哪种情况下英国不会变得更加无足轻重和贫穷。
en: One can argue about the precise scale of the economic shock – short- and long-term – but it is difficult to imagine any circumstances in which the United Kingdom does not become poorer and less significant in the world.

zh: 很多被鼓励为所谓“独立”而投票的民众将发现他们不仅没有重获自由，反而因此失去了工作。
en: Many of those who were encouraged to vote allegedly for their “independence” will find that, far from gaining freedom, they have lost their job.

zh: 那么，究竟是什么原因导致了这样的结果？
en: So, why did it happen?

zh: 首先，公投荒谬地简化了原本复杂的事务。
en: First, a referendum reduces complexity to absurd simplicity.

zh: 英国欧盟成员资格所代表的国际合作和共同主权被诋毁为一系列虚假的声明和承诺。
en: The tangle of international cooperation and shared sovereignty represented by Britain’s membership of the EU was traduced into a series of mendacious claims and promises.

zh: 英国民众被告知脱欧不必付出任何经济代价，那些受益于欧洲的行业也不必为此承担损失。
en: The British people were told there would be no economic price to pay for leaving, and no losses for all those sectors of its society that have benefited from Europe.

zh: 选民得到的承诺是与（英国最大的市场）欧洲签订有利的贸易协议、降低移民人数，并节约资金用于国家卫生体系和其他稀缺的公共产品及服务。
en: Voters were promised an advantageous trade deal with Europe (Britain’s biggest market), lower immigration, and more money for the National Health Service and other cherished public goods and services.

zh: 最重要的是，据说英国将就此恢复“魔力 ” ， 恢复曾风暴般席卷全球的创造性的生机勃勃。
en: Above all, Britain, it was said, would regain its “mojo,” the creative vitality needed to take the world by storm.

zh: 随着谎言被一一戳穿，最可怕的将是“脱欧”支持者的失望情绪日益高涨。
en: One of the horrors that lie ahead will be the growing disappointment of “Leave” supporters as all of these lies are exposed.

zh: 选民们被告知他们将“夺回自己的国家 ” 。
en: The voters were told that they would “get their country back.”

zh: 我不相信他们会喜欢最后的结果。
en: I do not believe they will like what it turns out to be.

zh: 这场灾难的第二个原因是英国两大政党的分裂。
