en: But it would be a mistake to accept the Conservative narrative as the last word.

zh: 从根本上，这是宣传手段，没有什么支持，倒是有破坏性的实践效果。
en: It is basically a tissue of propaganda, with little support in theory and destructive effects in practice.

zh: 如果换了一个政府，这也许不重要。
en: This might not matter so much had there been a change of government.

zh: 但奥斯本又回到了财政大臣的位子上，承诺在未来五年采取更严格的削减开支。
en: But Osborne is back as Chancellor, promising even tougher cuts over the next five years.

zh: 而拜德国所赐，财政紧缩也依然是欧元区主宰观念。
en: And fiscal austerity is still the reigning doctrine in the eurozone, thanks to Germany.

zh: 因此，伤害还会继续。
en: So the damage is set to continue.

zh: 如果没有令人信服的反驳，我们也许不得不目睹受害者到底能承受多少痛苦。
en: In the absence of a compelling counter-narrative, we may be fated to find out just how much pain the victims can withstand.

zh: 站不住脚的英国理由
en: The Eclipse of British Reason

zh: 柏林— 当拉力过大时，链条会从最薄弱的一环断起。
en: BERLIN – When placed under too much strain, chains tend to break at the weakest link.

zh: 这形象地说明了欧盟的状况。
en: Figuratively speaking, the same applies to the European Union.

zh: 因此，全世界都会非常自然地认为，如果欧盟开始分裂，最初一定从危机深重的南欧（其中又以希腊首当其冲）开始。
en: So the entire world quite naturally assumed that any process of EU disintegration would start primarily in the crisis-ridden European south (Greece, first and foremost).

zh: 但是，正如英国首相卡梅伦最近所指出的，欧洲之链的断环极有可能不出现在最弱的一环，而出现在最不理智的一环。
en: But, as British Prime Minister David Cameron has now demonstrated, the European chain is most likely to break not at its weakest link, but at its most irrational.

zh: 英国 — — 实用主义和现实主义的发轫地，一个有着惊人镇定和适应性的国家，一个在成功对抗纳粹德国、捍卫欧洲自由之后放弃帝国地位的国家 — — 如今正在迷失方向。
en: The United Kingdom – the homeland of pragmatism and realism, a country of unflappable principles and unmatched adaptability that stoically gave up its empire after successfully defending Europe’s freedom against Nazi Germany – has now lost its way.

zh: 更准确滴说，它是被保守党意识形态幻象 — — 欧盟权力可以也应该回归英国主权 — — 带错了路。
en: More precisely, it has been led astray by the Conservative Party’s ideological fantasy that certain EU powers can and should be returned to British sovereignty.

zh: 英国的国家利益并未改变，欧盟的根本性变化也并不对英国国家利益构成威胁。
en: The UK’s national interests have not changed, and no fundamental shifts within the EU have worked against those interests.

zh: 改变的是英国的国内政治：首相太弱，镇不住下议院约100人的反欧洲议员（称之为“茶话会 ” （ High Tea Party ） ） ，而保守党政府还担心英国独立党的崛起，这会导致保守党失去右翼选票，让工党在大选中占先。
en: What has changed is Britain’s domestic politics: a prime minister too weak to control his roughly 100 anti-European backbenchers (call them the “High Tea Party”) in the House of Commons, and a Conservative establishment wary of the UK Independence Party’s rise, which could cost the Tories enough votes on the right to give Labour an electoral advantage.

zh: 卡梅伦说，他不愿看到英国离开欧盟。
en: Cameron claims that he does not want the UK to leave the EU.

zh: 但他的战略 — — “重议”欧盟成员国资格，然后就新协议举行英国全民公投 — — 是两大幻觉的产物。 其一是他可以确保产生积极结果，其二是欧盟可以也愿意给出他想要的让步。
en: But his strategy – “renegotiation” of EU membership, followed by a British referendum on the new agreement – is the product of two illusions: first, that he can ensure a positive outcome, and, second, that the EU is able and willing to give him the concessions that he wants.

zh: 事实上，有充分的理由认为，整个过程会按自己的逻辑发展，可能出现意料之外的英国退出欧盟的结果。
en: In fact, there is good reason to believe that such a course would take on a dynamic of its own, possibly leading to an unintended British exit from the EU.

zh: 这将是欧盟的一次严重退步；对英国来说，历史表明这一结果将是名副其实的灾难。
en: That would be a severe setback for the EU; for the British, blundering through history, it would be a veritable disaster.

zh: 毫无疑问，脱离欧盟的英国也能生存，但生存质量如何就难说了。
en: While Britain surely would survive outside the EU, the quality of its existence is another matter.

zh: 退出欧盟会严重损害英国的经济利益，既失去了单一市场，也丢掉了伦敦的金融中心地位。
en: By exiting the EU, the UK would severely damage its economic interests, losing both the single market and London’s role as a financial center.

zh: 退出欧盟也会危害英国的地缘政治利益，不仅包括其在欧洲的利益（讽刺的是，这方面它倒是支持欧盟扩张的 ） ， 也包括其在全世界的利益，其在全球事务中的地位以及其与美国的特殊关系（美国明确表示更希望看到欧洲英国 ） 。
en: An exit would also harm Britain’s geopolitical interests, both in Europe (where, ironically, it favors EU enlargement) and, worldwide, in its global standing and special relationship with the United States (which has made clear its preference for a European UK).

zh: 不幸的是，卡梅伦的欧洲政治表现记录实在无法激起人们对他获得不同结果的信心。
en: Unfortunately, Cameron’s track record in European politics does not inspire confidence in his ability to manage a different outcome.

zh: 2009年，他下令保守党MEP退出欧洲人民党（European People’s Party，泛欧洲的中右翼政治势力集团 ） ， 此举剥夺了保守党在欧洲议会的一切影响力，而保守党现在已与派系主义者和反启蒙主义者处在同一阵营中。
en: When, in 2009, he ordered the Conservative MEPs to withdraw from the European People’s Party, the Europe-wide grouping of center-right political forces, he merely deprived the Tories – now consigned to sit with the sectarians and obscurantists – of any influence in the European Parliament.

zh: 他削弱了英国在欧盟的地位，最终加重了党内对欧元的疑虑
en: By weakening the UK’s position within the EU, he ended up strengthening the Euro-skeptics within his party.

zh: 但是，尽管卡梅伦应该知道惨痛的教训，却仍抛弃了理智的思路。
en: But, while Cameron should know from grim experience what is looming, it seems that he has abandoned rational considerations.

zh: 事实上，认为欧盟会重议英国的成员资格条件 — — 这意味着德国不会反对 — — 简直是白日做梦。
en: Indeed, the belief that the EU would renegotiate Britain’s membership terms – which assumes, further, that Germany would not object – borders on magical thinking.

zh: 如此先河将被其他成员国所援引，从而意味着欧盟的末日。
en: Such a precedent would be applicable to the other member states, which would mean the end of the EU.

zh: 尽管英国德高望重，但为了继续其成员资格而解散欧盟实在太过荒谬。
en: With all due respect to the UK, dismantling the EU as the price of its continued membership is an absurd idea.

zh: 卡梅伦应该认识到，他的战略是不可能实现的（即使他担心对条约修饰性的修改无助于他在国内的处境 ） 。
en: Cameron should recognize that his strategy cannot be allowed (even if he fears that a few cosmetic corrections to the treaty won’t help him at home).

zh: 与此同时，如果保守党想将此作为重议众多欧洲条约的第一步，那么他们将有可能失去解决一个关键问题 — — 改革欧元区和非欧元区欧盟成员国关系 — — 的机会。
en: In the meantime, the Tories risk losing their way on a crucial issue – reform of the relationship between the eurozone and non-euro EU members – if they try to use it as leverage to renegotiate the various European treaties.

zh: 英国知道，欧元的生存需要更紧密的政治一体化，也知道作为金融中心的伦敦之于英国就像核工业之于法国、汽车工业之于德国，若是欧元崩溃，将受到严重损害。
en: Britain knows that the euro’s survival requires much closer political integration, and also that London’s role as a financial center – as important for the UK as the nuclear industry is for France and the auto industry is for Germany – would be greatly damaged if the euro should fail.

zh: 尽管没人会期待英国在不久的将来加入欧元区，但欧盟内部的政治领导力需要明智地考量一国本身的核心利益和其他成员国的核心利益，不能把目光集中在威胁上。
en: Although no one should expect the British to join the euro any time soon, political leadership within the EU requires the acumen to take account of the central interests of one’s own country and those of the other member states without indulging in threats.

zh: 但是，这又要求充分理解这些利益，并愿意在互惠基础上合作，而这在欧洲大家庭中应是理所当然之事。
en: This, however, requires an adequate understanding of those interests and a willingness to cooperate on the basis of mutual trust, which should be a given within the European family.

zh: 说辞，特别是来自大国领导人的说辞，可能有用，可能不切题，也可能有害。
en: Speeches, particularly when delivered by leaders of great nations, can be useful, irrelevant, or dangerous.

zh: 卡梅伦酝酿已久的关于欧洲的讲话被一再打断。
en: Cameron’s long-planned speech on Europe was postponed time and again.

zh: 也许他应该将这作为反思其立场的信号。
en: Perhaps he should have taken that as a sign that he should rethink his position.

zh: 他还可以这样做，再不做就晚了。
en: He still can, before it is too late.

zh: 最佳起点是重读一下丘吉尔1946年在苏黎世的著名演讲。
en: The best starting point would be a re-reading of Winston Churchill’s famous speech in Zurich in 1946.

zh: “我们必须建设一个欧罗巴合众国 ， ” 英国20世纪最伟大首相如是说。
en: “We must build a kind of United States of Europe,” urged Britain’s greatest twentieth-century statesman.

zh: 如今，这仍然是我们 — — 也是英国 — — 的任务。
en: That remains our task – and Britain’s – to this day.

zh: 英国如何改变退欧思维
en: How Britain Could Change Its Mind About Brexit

zh: 伦敦—2018年会成为英国改变脱离欧盟思维的一年吗？
en: LONDON – Will 2018 be the year when the United Kingdom changes its mind about leaving the European Union?

zh: 传统智慧说，停止退欧是不可能的。
en: Conventional wisdom says that stopping Brexit is impossible.

zh: 但传统智慧对特朗普怎么说？
en: But what did conventional wisdom say about Donald Trump?

zh: 马克龙呢？
en: Or Emmanuel Macron?

zh: 或者，一开始的退欧公投呢？
en: Or, for that matter, the original Brexit referendum?

zh: 在革命年代，事件可以从不可能跨越未必能，直接变成不可免。
en: In revolutionary times, events can go from impossible to inevitable without ever passing through improbable.

zh: 英国退欧就是一起这样的事件，它的逆转则有可能是另一起这样的事件。
en: Brexit was such an event, and its reversal could be another.

zh: 问问尼格尔·法拉奇（Nigel Farage ） 。 他是英国独立党（UK Independence Party）前领导人，他突然说，2016年6月的英国退欧公投可以推翻。
en: Just ask Nigel Farage, the former UK Independence Party leader, who has suddenly said that the June 2016 Brexit referendum could be overturned.

zh: “留欧阵营遥遥领先 ， ” 法拉奇在这个周末警告他的强硬退欧派同志们。
en: “The Remain side are making all the running,” Farage warned his fellow hardline Leavers this weekend.

zh: “他们在议会中是大多数，除非我们自己也组织起来，否则我们将失去英国退欧这一历史性胜利。 ”
en: “They have a majority in parliament, and unless we get ourselves organized we could lose the historic victory that was Brexit.”

zh: 投票给英国退欧和特朗普，这样的现象在今天常常被描述为是不平等和全球化等深刻社会经济因素的不可避免的结果。
en: The votes for Brexit and Trump are often described today as an ineluctable result of deep socioeconomic factors like inequality or globalization.

zh: 从某些角度讲，这一描述是对的。
en: In some ways, this description is right.

zh: 2008年经济危机后，发生某些形式的政治剧变是意料中事，我多年来一直这样认为。
en: Political upheavals of some kind were to be expected after the 2008 economic crisis, as I have argued for years.

zh: 但具体发生的剧变，完全不是不可避免的。
en: But there was nothing inevitable about the specific upheavals that happened.

zh: 和特朗普一样，英国退欧是选民行为出现小波动的偶然结果。
en: Brexit, like Trump, was a contingent outcome of small perturbations in voter behavior.

zh: 只要1.8%的英国人投出不同的票，英国退欧现在早已是一个被忘却的笑话。
en: If just 1.8% of Britons voted differently, Brexit would now be a forgotten joke-word.

zh: 如果希拉里·克林顿（Hillary Clinton）所多赢的三百万张选票能够在各州之间分布得略有不同 ， “ 特朗普总统”现在也将和2016年1月时一样可笑。
en: If Hillary Clinton’s popular majority of three million votes was distributed slightly differently among the states, the phrase “President Trump” would be as laughable today as it was in January 2016.

zh: 要想在新的一年里阻止英国退欧，需要发生四个类似的略微的行为变化。
en: To stop Brexit in the year ahead, four similarly modest shifts in behavior need to happen.

zh: 公共观点必须略微更加反对退欧决定。 目前，认为它“事后看来是个错误”的人要比不那么认为的人多4 % 。
en: Public opinion must shift slightly further against the Brexit decision, which is already viewed as “wrong in hindsight” by a 4% point margin.

zh: 私下里反对英国退欧的政客必须公开说出来。
en: Politicians who privately detest Brexit must speak out publicly.

zh: 理性反对政府政策必须再次被认为是民主的标志，而不是叛国行为。
en: Reasoned opposition to government policies must be recognized again as a hallmark of democracy, not an act of treason.

zh: 英国退欧不可避免的观点必须消除干净。
en: And the sense that Brexit is inevitable must be dispelled.

zh: 这些要求是相辅相成的关系。
en: These requirements are interdependent.

zh: 只有当政客感到公共观点有所改变时，才会公开发声；但公共观点只有在可信的政治领导下，才会发生改变。
en: Politicians will speak out only if they sense public opinion shifting; but public opinion will shift only with credible political leadership.

zh: 如果所有的反对都被打上反民主的标签，那么政客就会三缄其口。
en: Politicians are cowed into silence if all opposition is branded as anti-democratic.

zh: 而如果英国退欧看起来不可避免的话，为什么选民还要重新思考这个问题?
en: And if Brexit appears inevitable, why should voters bother to think again?

zh: 民意调查和焦点小组表明，不可避免感是逆转退欧决定的最重要的障碍。
en: The sense of inevitability, opinion polls and focus groups show, is the most important obstacle to a reversal.

zh: 大约30%的英国选民坚决反对欧盟，他们永远都是脱离欧盟的支持者，不管这回带来多大的经济代价，正如特朗普的“票仓”永远都会支持“他们的”总统，不管他的行为如何。
en: About 30% of British voters oppose the EU so passionately that they will always back leaving, regardless of the economic costs, just as Trump’s “base” will always support “their” president regardless of how he behaves.

zh: 但只要这些死硬疑欧派无法赢得对欧洲不太在乎，当将公投视为抗议投票的20%选民，他们就无法赢得多数。
en: But these diehard Euroskeptics would never have won a majority without some 20% of voters who cared little about Europe, but treated the referendum as a protest vote.

zh: 如今，这些立场并不太坚定的选民中有很多惊愕于退欧让人们的注意力从他们真正的怨恨对象 — — 医疗、不平等性、低工资、住房和其他问题 — — 上转移开去。
en: Many of these low-conviction voters are now dismayed that Brexit has distracted attention from their real grievances about health, inequality, low wages, housing, and other issues.

zh: 但正是出于这一原因，他们想要不可避免的退欧尽快发生，以使国家可以回到常规轨道上来。
en: Yet, for this very reason, they want the inevitable departure from Europe to happen as quickly as possible so that the country can get back to business as usual.

zh: 现在，假设这些选民看是相信，英国退欧远非不可避免，倒有可能永远不会发生。
en: Now suppose these voters began to believe that Brexit, far from being inevitable, might never happen.

zh: 他们会要求政客“停止在欧洲问题上喋喋不休 ” ， 开始解决人民真正的担忧。
en: They would demand that politicians “should stop banging on about Europe” and start dealing with the people’s real concerns.

zh: 不可避免感可能因为最近在保守党政府和工党反对派内部政治局面的改变而消失。
en: The sense of inevitability could be dispelled by recent shifts in the internal politics of both the Conservative government and the Labour opposition.

zh: 工党已经开始认识到，其唯一的重掌权力之路便是反对英国退欧。
en: Labour has begun to realize that its only possible route back to power is by opposing Brexit.

zh: 2017年选举结果的详细分析表明明，工党出人意料的胜利几乎完全可以归因于出于希望“搅黄”英国退欧动机的富裕年轻选民。
en: Detailed analysis of the 2017 election returns has shown that Labour’s unexpected gains were due almost entirely to affluent young voters whose motivation was the hope of derailing Brexit.

zh: 如果不是这些反对退欧的选民，首相梅可能将赢得被广泛预测的一边倒的大胜。
en: Had it not been for these anti-Brexit voters, Prime Minister Theresa May would have won the widely predicted landslide.

zh: 如果工党党魁杰里米·科尔宾（Jeremy Corbyn）现在成为“英国退欧侍女 ” — —布莱尔令人印象深刻的用词 — — 不进行有效的反对，那么这些新选民会感到遭到了背叛，工党也将分裂为马克思主义者和中间派，其赢得大选的希望将付之东流。
en: If Jeremy Corbyn, the Labour leader, now becomes “the handmaiden of Brexit,” in Tony Blair’s memorable phrase, by shying away from effective opposition, these new voters will feel betrayed, the party will split between the Marxists and centrists, and its hopes of ever winning a general election will be dashed.

zh: 另一方面，如果工党决定要挑战英国退欧，公共观点将迅速转变。
en: If, on the other hand, Labour decided to fight Brexit, public opinion would rapidly shift.

zh: 反对退欧将开始被认为是民主政治的自然结果。
en: Opposition to Brexit would start to be treated as a natural feature of democratic politics.

zh: 工党将开始从政府的谈判失误中受益。
en: Labour would start to benefit from the government’s negotiating blunders.

zh: 英国退欧的不可避免感也将消失。
en: And the sense of Brexit’s inevitability would vanish.

zh: 这反过来将给予亲欧保守党以勇气。
en: That, in turn, would give courage to pro-European Conservatives.

zh: 如果因为工党不高举反对大旗而导致政府无论如何都会胜出，那么保守党议员就不可能反对本党领导层。
en: Tory MPs are unlikely to vote against their party leadership if the absence of Labour opposition allows the government to win anyway.

zh: 但如果工党的一致反对创造了阻止退欧的真正的可能性，那么将国家利益置于当派忠诚之前的保守党议员就会因为勇气而被歌颂，而不会因为愚蠢而被取笑。
en: If, however, concerted opposition from Labour created a genuine possibility of stopping Brexit, Tory MPs who put national interest ahead of party loyalty would find themselves praised for their mettle, not ridiculed for folly.

zh: 他们甚至会觉得，如果本党与欧洲形成妥协，自己的职业生涯也会就此添彩。
en: They might even calculate that their own careers would prosper if their party reconciled itself to Europe.

zh: 这一系列连锁事件似乎正在启动。
en: This chain of events now seems to be starting.

zh: 12月，梅输掉了第一场重要的退欧战役，工党议员联合12位保守党叛徒通过了一份修正案，要求一切与欧盟谈成的协议都需要国会法案批准。
en: In December, May lost her first important Brexit battle, when Labour MPs united with 12 Tory rebels to pass an amendment requiring a specific Act of Parliament to approve whatever deal is negotiated with the EU.

zh: 这意味着任何引起严重反对的退欧计划 — — 不管是来自强硬民族主义者还是来自亲欧保守党 — — 都可以用来触发新的公投。
en: This means that any Brexit plan that arouses serious opposition, either from hardline nationalists or from pro-European Tories, could be used to trigger a new referendum.

zh: 随着这一突破，第一波明确以阻止退欧为目标，而不仅仅是以通过“软”分手协议来降低伤害为目标的严肃的跨党派行动将在本月晚些时候发动。
en: Following this breakthrough, the first serious cross-party campaign explicitly aiming to stop Brexit, and not merely to mitigate damage by seeking a “softer” divorce deal, will be launched later this month.

zh: 要想获得成功，这次行动需要说服幻灭的留欧派，退欧不是不可避免的。
en: To succeed, this campaign will need to persuade disillusioned Remainers that Brexit is not inevitable.

zh: 这次行动需要向抗议选民证明，不管他们的问题是什么，退欧都不是答案。
en: It will need to show protest voters that whatever their problems, Brexit is not the answer.

zh: 这次行动需要说服工党政客，参与退欧合谋就是选举自杀，还要说如亲欧盟的保守党叛徒，背叛不是徒劳。
en: It will need to convince Labour politicians that collaboration with Brexit is electoral suicide, and persuade pro-EU Tory rebels that a rebellion would not be futile.

zh: 最后，这次行动需要欧洲领导人毫不含糊地声明，英国有改变退欧想法的合法权利。
en: Finally, it will need European leaders to state unequivocally that Britain is legally entitled to change its mind about leaving.

zh: 这些要求非常具有挑战性，但并非不可能。
en: These requirements are challenging, but not impossible.

zh: 大卫·戴维斯（David Davis）是一位支持退欧的保守党，他目前主持着英国的退欧谈判。 他曾经说 ， “ 如果民主不能改变思维，那么它就不再是民主。
en: David Davis, the pro-Brexit Tory who is now leading the UK’s Brexit negotiations, once said that, “If a democracy cannot change its mind, it ceases to be a democracy.”

zh: ”英国仍然是一个民主国家，并且它仍然可以改变退欧思维。
en: Britain is still a democracy, and it can still change its mind about Brexit.

zh: 英国日益加深的迷茫
en: Britain’s Deepening Confusion

zh: 伦敦 — “ 受够了 ， ” 这是英国首相梅在伦敦桥恐怖袭击后的宣告。
en: LONDON – “Enough is enough,” proclaimed British Prime Minister Theresa May after the terrorist attack on London Bridge.

zh: 现在，形势已经清楚，近一半在6月8日的英国大选中投票的人受够了梅。 梅的保守党多数地位也在选举中消失殆尽，结果是形成了一个悬浮议会（任何政党都没能获得多数 ） 。
en: Now, it is clear, almost half of those who voted in the United Kingdom’s general election on June 8 have had enough of May, whose Conservative majority was wiped out at the polls, producing a hung parliament (with no majority for any party).

zh: 不管是“受够了移民 ” ， 还是“受够了紧缩 ” ， 英国选民显然是受够了很多事情。
en: Whether it is “enough immigrants” or “enough austerity,” Britain’s voters certainly have had enough of a lot.

zh: 但大选让英国陷入了迷茫的分歧。
en: But the election has left Britain confusingly split.

zh: 去年的英国脱欧公投表明英国存在留在欧盟-离开欧盟分歧，脱欧派略胜一筹。
en: Last year’s Brexit referendum on European Union membership suggested a Leave-Remain divide, with the Brexiteers narrowly ahead.

zh: 今年的大选则在这层分歧之上又加上了更加传统的左右分歧，卷土重来的工党利用了选民对保守党削减预算政策的不满。
en: This year’s general election superimposed on this a more traditional left-right split, with a resurgent Labour Party capitalizing on voter discontent with Conservative budget cuts.

zh: 要理解由此造成的政治局面，可以想象一个田字格，四个象限分别由留欧和预算削减派、留欧和经济扩张派、脱欧和预算削减派以及脱欧和经济扩张派组成。
en: To see the resulting political terrain, imagine a two-by-two table, with the four quadrants occupied by Remainers and Budget Cutters; Remainers and Economic Expansionists; Brexiteers and Budget Cutters; and Brexiteers and Economic Expansionists.

zh: 这四个象限无法叠加形成一致的两个半边，因此，很难搞清楚选民是在给哪个阵营投票。
en: The four quadrants don’t add up to coherent halves, so it’s not possible to make out what voters thought they were voting for.

zh: 但可以看出选民拒绝了什么。
en: But it is possible to make out what voters were rejecting.

zh: 有两件确定的事情。
en: There are two certain casualties.

zh: 一是紧缩。 即使是保守党，也表示会放弃紧缩政策。
en: The first is austerity, which even the Conservatives have signaled they will abandon.

zh: 削减公共支出以平衡预算是基于错误的理论，并且在实践中也已经失败。
en: Cutting public spending to balance the budget was based on the wrong theory and has failed in practice.

zh: 最能说明问题的迹象便是2010—2016年间担任财政大臣的乔治·奥斯本（George Osborne）无法实现任何预算目标。
en: The most telling indicator was the inability of George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer from 2010 to 2016, to achieve any of his budget targets.

zh: 赤字应该在2015年消失，然后推迟到2017年，然后再度推迟到2020—2021年。
en: The deficit was to have vanished by 2015, then by 2017, then by 2020-2021.

zh: 如今，政府干脆不再承诺任何日期了。
en: Now, no government will commit to any date at all.

zh: 这些目标是基于一个概念 ： “ 可信”的赤字学见计划将带来足够的商业信心，克服对削减政策本身的抑制效应。
en: The targets were based on the idea that a “credible” deficit-reduction program would create sufficient business confidence to overcome the depressing effects on activity of the cuts themselves.

zh: 有人说，这些目标从来都不够可信。
en: Some say the targets were never credible enough.

zh: 真相是它们永远不可能可信：赤字只有在经济增长时才会减少，而削减预算，不管是真正的发生的还是预料中的，都会阻碍增长。
en: The truth is that they never could be: the deficit cannot come down unless the economy grows, and budget cuts, real and anticipated, hinder growth.

zh: 现在的共识是，紧缩将复苏推迟了近三年，抑制了真实收入，也导致地方政府、医疗和教育等关键公共服务遭到严重拖累。
en: The consensus now is that austerity delayed recovery for almost three years, depressing real earnings and leaving key public services like local government, health care, and education palpably damaged.

zh: 因此，就等着荒谬地咬定平衡预算不放松的做法破产吧。
en: So expect the ridiculous obsession with balancing the budget to be scrapped.

zh: 从现在开始，赤字将根据经济状态调整。
en: From now on, the deficit will be left to adjust to the state of the economy.

zh: 第二件被拒绝的事情是不受限制的欧盟移民。
en: The second casualty is unrestricted immigration from the EU.

zh: 脱欧派要求“控制我们的国境 ” ， 这一口号被导向了来自东欧的经济移民流入。
en: The Brexiteers’ demand to “control our borders” was directed against the uncontrolled influx of economic migrants from Eastern Europe.

zh: 这一要求必须以某种形式得到满足。
en: This demand will have to be met in some way.

zh: 当欧盟主要由西欧组成时，欧洲内部的移民问题可以忽略不计。
en: Migration within Europe was negligible when the EU was mainly West European.

zh: 而当欧盟开始将工资较低的前共产主义国家纳入时，情况开始改变。
en: This changed when the EU began incorporating the low-wage ex-communist countries.

zh: 随后到来的移民缓解了 英国和德国等国家的劳动力短缺问题，也增加了移民本身的收入。
en: The ensuing migration eased labor shortages in host countries like the UK and Germany, and increased the earnings of the migrants themselves.

zh: 但这些收益并不适用于不受限制的 移民。
en: But such benefits do not apply to unrestricted migration.

zh: 哈佛大学的乔治·波尔加斯（George J. Borjas）和其他人的研究表明，净移民流入降低了竞争性本国劳动力的工资。
en: Studies by Harvard University’s George J. Borjas and others suggest that net immigration lowers the wages of competing domestic labor.

zh: 波尔加斯最著名的发现表明 ， “ 马里艾尔人 ” — —1980年大规模集体 移民到迈阿密的古巴人 — — 对当地工作阶级工资造成了抑制效应。
en: Borjas’s most famous study shows the depressive impact of “Marielitos” – Cubans who immigrated en masse to Miami in 1980 – on domestic working-class wages.

zh: 这些担忧长期以来一直是主权国家坚持移民管控权利的基础。
en: These fears have long underpinned sovereign states’ insistence on the right to control immigration.

zh: 对管控的支持在东道国存在劳动力盈余时更加强大，2008年危机以来的西欧大部就是如此。
en: The case for control is strengthened when host countries have a labor surplus, as has been true of much of Western Europe since the crisis of 2008.

zh: 支持脱欧实质上可以说就是要求回复对英国国境的主权。
en: Support for Brexit is essentially a demand for the restoration of sovereignty over the UK’s borders.

zh: 这一问题的症结在于它的政治遗产。
en: The crux of the issue is political legitimacy.

zh: 进入现代以前，市场基本上是本地性质，对外部人士基本关闭，哪怕是相邻的城镇。
en: Until modern times, markets were largely local, and heavily protected against outsiders, even from neighboring towns.

zh: 国家市场直到现代国家出现之后才开始形成。
en: National markets were achieved only with the advent of modern states.

zh: 但商品、资本和劳动力在主权国家内部完全不受限制的流动需要满足两个条件才能成为可能：国家身份的发展，以及出现有能力在出现不利局面时提供安全的国家机关。
en: But the completely unrestricted movement of goods, capital, and labor within sovereign states became possible only when two conditions were met: the growth of national identity and the emergence of national authorities able to provide security in the face of adversity.

zh: 这两个条件欧盟一个都不满足。
en: The European Union fulfills neither condition.

zh: 欧洲人民首先是民族国家的公民。
en: Its peoples are citizens of their nation-states first.

zh: 公民与国家之间的契约，即国家经济的基石，无法在欧洲层面复制，因为不存在可以与之达成这个协议的欧洲国。
en: And the contract between citizens and states on which national economies depend cannot be reproduced at the European level, because there is no European state with which to conclude the deal.

zh: 欧盟坚持将劳动力的自由流动作为非国家成员资格的条件很不成熟。
en: The EU’s insistence on free movement of labor as a condition of membership of a non-state is premature, at best.

zh: 这应该成为整个欧盟的规定，而不仅仅是英国脱欧协议的一部分。
en: It will need to be qualified, not just as part of the UK’s Brexit deal, but for the whole of the EU.

zh: 那么，英国大选的混乱结果会如何发展？
en: So how will the shambolic results of the British general election play out?

zh: 梅的首相是做不长了。
en: May will not last long as Prime Minister.

zh: 奥斯本已经说她是“女活死人 ” （ 当然，他没有承认他的紧缩政策也是梅黯然失色的帮凶 ） 。
en: Osborne has called her a “dead woman walking” (of course without acknowledging that his austerity policies helped to seal her demise).

zh: 最明智的结果目前绝不可能达成：保守党-工党联合政府 ， （ 比如）约翰·鲍里斯（John Boris）当首相，杰里米·科尔宾（Jeremy Corbyn）当副首相。
en: The most sensible outcome is currently a political non-starter: a Conservative-Labour coalition government, with (say) Boris Johnson as Prime Minister and Jeremy Corbyn as his deputy.

zh: 政府实施一个只包含两项内容的两年计划：完成与欧盟的“软”脱欧协议，以及在住房、基础设施和绿色能源方面大量进行公共投资。
en: The government would adopt a two-year program consisting of only two items: the conclusion of a “soft” Brexit deal with the EU and a big public investment program in housing, infrastructure, and green energy.

zh: 投资计划的出发点是涨潮可以让所有船都浮起来。
en: The rationale for the investment program is that a rising tide will lift all boats.

zh: 经济繁荣还有一个额外的好处，就是对移民的敌意会有所减弱，于是英国可以更容易地谈判明智的移民流管控政策。
en: And an added benefit of a thriving economy will be lower hostility to immigration, making it easier for Britain to negotiate sensible regulation of migrant flows.

zh: 谁知道呢：如果谈判迫使欧盟修改其自身的劳动力自由移动承诺，那么英国脱欧将不再仅仅是英国从欧洲退出，而更像是欧盟资格条件的大修。
en: And who knows: if the negotiations force the EU to re-cast its own commitment to free labor movement, Brexit may turn out to be a matter less of British exit than of an overhaul of the terms of European membership.

zh: 脆弱的英国
en: Brittle Britain

zh: 伦敦—在未来一年中，哪个欧洲国家面临最大的政治动荡和金融混乱风险？
en: LONDON – Which European country faces the greatest risk of political instability and financial turmoil in the year ahead?

zh: 在5月7日英国大选还有不到一周之际，答案既明显又令人震惊。
en: With less than a week to go before the British general election on May 7, the answer is both obvious and surprising.

zh: 作为曾经欧元危机中的政治和经济稳定的避风港，英国即将成为欧盟政治局面最难预测的成员国。
en: Once a haven of political and economic stability amid the turmoil of the euro crisis, the United Kingdom is about to become the European Union’s most politically unpredictable member.

zh: 事实上，连续性几乎可以确定从选举结果中排除。
en: Indeed, continuity is the one election outcome that can almost certainly be excluded.

zh: 除非民调结果出现英国历史上最大程度的不准确性，否则组成执政联盟的两党 — — 首相卡梅伦的保守党和自由民主党 — — 几乎不可能赢得联合议会多数席位。
en: Unless opinion polls are inaccurate to a degree unprecedented in British history, the two parties comprising the government coalition, Prime Minister David Cameron’s Conservatives and the Liberal Democrats, have almost no chance of winning a combined parliamentary majority.

zh: 一个可能性 — — 根据民调结果，这一可能性略高于50 % — —是英国，撒切尔主义的诞生地和欧盟新自由主义经济学的旗帜，很快就会出现一个决心实施自20世纪70年代以来最大增税计划的工党政府。
en: One possibility – with a probability slightly above 50% according to the polls – is that Britain, the birthplace of Thatcherism and the EU’s standard-bearer of neoliberal economics, will soon have a Labour-led government committed to the biggest tax-raising program since the 1970s.

zh: 此外，拜英国选举制度的特殊性和苏格兰和威尔士民族主义的兴起所赐，工党政府能否生存下去取决于经济日程更加激进、以分裂英国为目标的政党的支持。
en: Moreover, because of the peculiarities of the British electoral system and the rise of Scottish and Welsh nationalism, a Labour government’s survival would depend on the support of parties with even more radical economic agendas and dedicated to dismantling the UK.

zh: 另一个情景 — — 与工党领导的执政联盟情形可能性几乎相当 — — 是弱势且不稳定的保守党政府。
en: Another scenario – almost as probable as a Labour-led coalition – is a weak and unstable Conservative government.

zh: 从民调结果看，卡梅伦的最大希望是赢得比工党更多的议会席位，然后试图组建少数派政府，主要其他政党不联合起来反对，就能继续执政。
en: To judge by the opinion polls, Cameron’s best hope is to win more parliamentary seats than Labour and try to form a minority government, which could survive as long as the other parties failed to unite against it.

zh: 这也许是可能的，因为自由民主党和苏格兰民族党（Scottish Nationalist Party）也许认为允许弱势的保守党政府上台有利可图，至少暂时如此。
en: This might be possible, because the Liberal Democrats and Scottish Nationalist Party may see benefits in allowing a weak Conservative government to remain in power, at least for a while.

zh: 但少数派保守党政府会带来更多不确定性和风险。
en: But a minority Conservative government would create additional uncertainties and risks.

zh: 卡梅伦将比其他所有战后英国领导人都更容易受到本党异见派和极端分子的要挟，后两者把让英国退出欧盟视为自己的历史使命。
en: Cameron would be more vulnerable than any leader in postwar British history to blackmail by his own party’s dissidents and extremists, who see it as their historic mission to pull Britain out of the EU.

zh: 而少数派政府也将无法通过任何苏格兰民族党反对的争议立法。
en: And a minority government would be unable to pass any controversial legislation that the Scottish Nationalists opposed.

zh: 此外，英国政治制度也将无以为继。
en: Moreover, Britain’s political institutions might be unable to cope.

zh: 英国的不成文宪法完全基于传统和先例。
en: The UK’s unwritten constitution is based entirely on tradition and precedent.

zh: 这一安排永远需要以拥有明确权力的强势政府为前提。
en: That arrangement has always presupposed strong governments with clear mandates.

zh: 宪法极不适应联合政府和少数派政府，一些法律学者甚至质疑，如果政府不出几周或几个月就会被推翻，那么女王是否应该宣布议会代表“她的”新政府？
en: The constitution is so poorly adapted to coalitions and minority governments that some legal scholars question whether the Queen should address Parliament on behalf of “her” new government if there is a risk that it will be toppled within a few weeks or months.

zh: 此外，尽管选举算术意味着稳定的中间道路政府 — — 能够保持英国当前的税收、经济管理和欧洲政策的政府 — — 几乎不可能出现，但连续性仍是大部分国际商界领袖和政客所期待的结果。
en: And yet, although the electoral arithmetic makes a stable centrist government – one that could maintain Britain’s current policies on taxes, economic management, and Europe – almost impossible to imagine, continuity is the outcome that most international business leaders and politicians seem to expect.

zh: 关于这一点，最明显的证据要数金融市场。
en: The clearest evidence of this can be seen in financial markets.

zh: 尽管英镑汇率自去年9月的合1.70美元贬值了大约10 % ， 但这完全是美元强势的结果。
en: Although the pound has declined by about 10% from its peak of $1.70 last September, sterling weakness has simply reflected the dollar’s strength.

zh: 与此同时，英镑对欧元升值了近10 % ， 而英国股价正处于历史最高水平，英国政府债券的回报也高于美国、德国和日本。
en: In the same period, sterling has risen almost 10% against the euro, while British share prices have hit all-time highs and government bonds have generated better returns in Britain than in the United States, Germany, or Japan.

zh: 什么造成了这一对即将到来的英国政府风险的漠视 — — 在欧洲政客之间显然也是如此？
en: What accounts for this apparent indifference – also evident among European politicians – to the looming political risks in Britain?

zh: 许多国际观察家认为政治早已不在英国占据重要地位，因为经济基本面良好，增长率相当健康。
en: Many international observers believe that politics simply no longer matters much in Britain, because the economy is fundamentally sound and growing at a fairly healthy pace.

zh: 但这是一种非常危险的自满观点。
en: But this is a dangerously complacent argument.

zh: 是的，2014年英国经济增长为主要经合组织国家中最快的，失业率也只有欧盟平均水平的一半。
en: Yes, Britain recorded the fastest economic growth among the major OECD countries in 2014 and has an unemployment rate of only half the EU average.

zh: 但这些有利指标掩盖了一个巨大的风险源：世界首屈一指的外部赤字，去年这一赤字通过总额高达1,600亿美元的外部资本流入填补。
en: But these favorable indicators obscure a source of enormous risk: one of the world’s largest external deficits, financed last year by foreign-capital inflows totaling $160 billion.

zh: 经常项目缺口相当于GDP的5.5 % ， 目前为主要经合组织国家最高，这一水平也是金融危机爆发以来长期存在的水平 — — 英国和其他国家都是如此。
en: The current-account gap, at 5.5% of GDP, is by far the highest among the major OECD countries and is at a level long associated – both in the UK and elsewhere – with the onset of financial crises.

zh: 只要英国身为政治稳定的安全港并且税收政策有利于外国投资者，就不会出现吸引资本流入的问题。
en: As long as Britain was a haven of political stability and tax policies favorable to foreign investors, it had no problem attracting capital inflows.

zh: 但英国政坛及其与欧盟关系即将发生的改变必然会引起人们关注英国经济对外部融资的极端依赖。
en: But the impending shifts in Britain’s politics and its EU relations are bound to draw attention to the economy’s extreme dependence on foreign finance.

zh: 工党政府有一套专门用来对付私人外国投资者的税收计划，该计划必定会影响资本流入。
en: A Labour government, wielding tax proposals specifically designed to hit private foreign investors, would certainly discourage inflows.

zh: 但国际投资者也许同样会因为“恐欧派”把持的弱势保守党政府而感到沮丧。
en: But international investors might be equally put off by a weak Conservative government dominated by the party’s Europhobe wing.

zh: 无论如何，GDP增长都会随商业信心、消费和房价的不振 — — 或者因为工党的新税收政策，或者因为保守党带来的欧盟成员资格不确定性 — — 而减速。
en: In either case, GDP growth is likely to slow as business confidence, consumption, and house prices suffer – either from new taxes under Labour or from uncertainties about EU membership under the Conservatives.

zh: 另一个国际观察家忽视如此明显的风险的原因是他们的目光完全集中在希腊和乌克兰你的大事件上。
en: Another reason why international observers may be ignoring such obvious risks is that they have been preoccupied with more dramatic events in Greece and Ukraine.

zh: 政客、金融分析家和政治评论家的时间和注意力都是有限的。
en: Politicians, financial analysts, and political commentators have limited time and attention.

zh: 他们倾向于关注最大最紧迫的问题，而英国政治不在此列。
en: They tend to focus on whatever seems to be the biggest and most urgent story, and British politics has not been it.

zh: 而许多显然是非常老练的分析家可能再次完全陷入了一种心理否认的状态。
en: Then again, many apparently sophisticated analysts may simply be in a state of psychological denial.

zh: 英国商业和金融观点调查表明，这类群体中的绝对多数期望选战的最后几日会出现有利于保守党的突然转变，形成一个稳定的执政联盟和实现经济和政治环境的连续性。
en: Surveys of business and financial opinion in Britain show clear majorities in these groups expecting a sudden swing toward the Conservatives in the closing days of the election campaign, resulting in a stable coalition government and continuity in economic and political conditions.

zh: 发生最后一分钟选举倾向改变时可能的，但时间正在耗尽。
en: Such a last-minute shift in voting intentions is possible, but the time for it is running out.

zh: 事实上，英国公众观点一直惊人地稳定，不仅在官方选战期间是如此，在整个过去12个月里一直是如此。
en: In fact, British public opinion has remained uncannily stable, not only during the official election campaign, but throughout the past 12 months.

zh: 预期保守党或工党取得组建稳定政府所需要的决定性胜利绝非理性预期。
en: There are simply no rational grounds for expecting either the Conservatives or Labour to achieve the decisive victory needed to form a stable government.

zh: 因此，即将到来的选举将标志着英国政治、经济和金融不确定性时代的开始，而不是结束。
en: The upcoming election will therefore mark the beginning, not the end, of a period of uncertainty for British politics, economics, and finance.

zh: 即使再大的稳定信念也无法改变这一点。
en: No amount of lingering faith in stability will change that.

zh: 英国的混乱离婚
en: Britain’s Messy Divorce

zh: 伦敦—在英国正式启动自绝于欧洲政治和经济主流的令人忧伤的谈判之际，其首相梅却拒绝使用“离婚”来描述这一事件。
en: LONDON – As Britain formally triggers the doleful negotiations to exclude itself from the mainstream of European politics and economics, Prime Minister Theresa May refuses to use the word “divorce” to describe what is happening.

zh: 我的妻子、一位退休家庭律师兼调解员认为梅也许是正确的。
en: My wife, a retired family lawyer and mediator, thinks May could be correct.

zh: 毕竟，我们所要退出的家庭仍然包含着我们的大量历史和“传家宝 ” ， 也包含了我们的未来经济利益。
en: After all, the family house we are exiting still contains much of our history and family silver, as well as our future economic interest.

zh: 从这个角度讲，离婚绝不是好选择。
en: In that sense, divorce is scarcely an option.

zh: 英国并不像一些人认为的那样，只是一个狭隘的岛国。
en: Britain has not been as insular an island as some people take it to be.

zh: 从在位王室（日耳曼人）到出口（绝大部分流向欧洲 ） ， 我们影响了西欧其他国家的发展，也反过来受到西欧其他国家发展的影响。
en: From our reigning royal family (which is German) to our exports (overwhelmingly to Europe), we have helped to shape and in our turn been shaped by developments in the rest of Western Europe.

zh: 我们与西欧只隔着一条区区20英里多佛海峡 — — 现在，这显然是超宽的20英里。
en: We are separated by just 20 miles (33 kilometers) of water – these days, apparently a very wide 20 miles – at the Strait of Dover.

zh: 那么，我们为什么要离开？
en: So why are we leaving?

zh: 原因混合了失望、错觉、谎言和刻意作对等多种因素。
en: The cause is a mixture of frustration, delusion, mendacity, and bloody-mindedness.

zh: 我们被灌输，欧洲无力处理它所面临的一些最重大的挑战 — — 如竞争力和难民等，除非设法获得更多的核心力量（central powers ） 。
en: We were fed up with Europe’s inability to tackle some of its biggest challenges – from competitiveness to immigration – without seeking to acquire more central powers.

zh: 此外，我们的政治领袖多年来被对欧盟怀有敌意的人牵着走，对他们几乎有求必应，而事实上他们的许多批评根本就是谎言的组合体。
en: In addition, our political leaders have for years played into the hands of those hostile to the EU, by appearing to accept any and every criticism of it, many of them a compound of falsehoods.

zh: 我们拒绝承认我们的现实：我们只是一个中等规模的国家，早已不再能够支配世界大部。
en: We refuse to see ourselves for what we are: a mid-size country that no longer rules much of the world.

zh: 我们过于容易地被说服相信，只有民族主义者才可能是爱国者。
en: We are too easily persuaded that you cannot be a patriot without being a nationalist.

zh: 我们能够也应该管理好这场分家所带来的后果，并且不再给我们自己平添麻烦。
en: We can and should manage the consequences of this break-up without bringing further woes down on our heads.

zh: 但到目前为止，分离的过程让我们看不到多少希望。
en: But the process of separation thus far doesn’t offer great hope.

zh: 去年6月的英国脱欧公投本身是一场灾难。
en: The Brexit referendum last June was itself a disaster.

zh: 一个代议制民主国家根本不应该转向如此民粹主义的设计。
en: A parliamentary democracy should never turn to such populist devices.

zh: 即便如此，梅原本仍然可以对52%要求退出欧洲的选民说，她将把谈判交给相信这一结果的大臣团队，并及时将谈判结果提交给议会和人民。
en: Even so, May could have reacted to the 52% vote to quit Europe by saying that she would hand the negotiations to a group of ministers who believed in this outcome and then put the result of the talks in due course to parliament and the people.

zh: 相反，她让她的政府完全沦为脱欧机器，及时她本人一直想要留在欧盟。
en: Instead, she turned the whole of her government into a Brexit machine, even though she had always wished to remain in the EU.

zh: 如今，她的政府的格言是“要么脱欧，要么解体 ” 。
en: Her government’s motto is now “Brexit or bust.”

zh: 悲哀的是，我们可能同时得到这两样东西。
en: Sadly, we will probably get both.

zh: 那么，接下去会怎么样？
en: So what happens next?

zh: 没有人有头绪。
en: No one has a clue.

zh: 悬崖在招手；旅鼠正在集结。
en: The cliff beckons; the lemmings are lining up.

zh: 我们知道，我们的出口有将近一半流向欧盟，比流向整个英联邦的出口多五倍，比流向所有金砖国家的出口多六倍。
en: We know that almost half our exports go to the EU, five times more than go to the entire Commonwealth and six times more than to all the BRICS countries.

zh: 但我们却放弃了欧盟单一市场（这要求我们接受欧洲司法管辖和劳动力自由流动）或关税联盟的成员资格。
en: But we have given up on staying in the single market (which would require us to accept European jurisdiction and the free movement of labor) or the customs union.

zh: 显然，我们想要按照我们的要求与欧盟签订自由贸易协定，覆盖我们主要的行业和服务。
en: Apparently we want a free-trade agreement with the EU on our own terms, covering our main industries and services.

zh: 梅的外交大臣鲍里斯·约翰逊（Boris Johnson）认为我们在这些谈判中尽占优势，因为欧洲想继续卖东西给我们 — — 比如Prosecco。
en: May’s foreign secretary, Boris Johnson, argues that the cards are in our hands in these negotiations, because Europeans want to continue selling – Prosecco, for example – to us.

zh: 但即使说到底，梅的大臣们说，什么协议都不达成也无关紧要。
en: But anyway, May’s ministers say, it doesn’t matter if we have no deal at all.

zh: 我们只需要走开就是了。
en: We will simply walk away.

zh: 他们说，没有协议未必是一个坏结果，因为世界渴望与我们做更多生意，随着未来英镑稳步贬值，与我们做生意更加有利可图。
en: No deal would not necessarily be a bad outcome, they insist, because the world is eager to do more business with us, which will be cheaper in the future as sterling continues its steady decline.

zh: 所有这些，用梅不会用的话说，感觉就好像是一场非常不友好的离婚。
en: All of this, to return to the word May won’t use, feels like a rather unamicable divorce.

zh: 谈判中的每一次转折，都伴随着梅的保守党的右翼以及她现在欠着巨大人情的花边小报的冲冠仇外之怒。
en: Every twist and turn in the talks will be accompanied by xenophobic outrage on the right wing of May’s Conservative Party and in the tabloid press to which she is now so beholden.

zh: 真是坏透了，我们正准备破坏我们的经济，而这将让穷人变得更穷，有企业家精神的人变得更加脆弱。
en: It is bad enough that we are setting about wrecking our economy, which will make the poor poorer and even the enterprising more vulnerable.

zh: 除此之外，我们还颠覆了许多代议制民主的规则和传统，代议制应该鼓励寻找共识和妥协，回避多数制。
en: On top of this, we are overturning many of the rules and conventions of our parliamentary democracy, which should encourage the search for consensus and compromise, and shun majoritarianism.

zh: 去年6月，只有52%的英国选民决定要退出欧盟。
en: A mere 52% of British voters made the decision to exit the EU last June.

zh: 他们投票支持的到底是什么，仍然是个谜。
en: What exactly they voted for remains a mystery.

zh: 但梅和脱欧派坚持声称，他们发出了声音。
en: But they have spoken, May and the Brexiteers insist.

zh: 这就结了。
en: So that settles it.

zh: 他们说，不要去管“人民的敌人 ” — —我们的独立的法院中的法官 — — 要说什么。
en: Ignore, they say, what the “enemies of the people,” the judges in our independent courts, have to say.

zh: 坚决驳斥一切关于调查到底发生了什么的观点。
en: Shout down any point of view inquiring about what is actually happening to us.

zh: 攻击一切支持欧盟成员资格或公开讨论这一资格的人的名声 — — 不管是企业管理者、政客还是公民社会领袖。
en: Attack the reputation of anyone – business manager, politician, or civil-society leader – who favors EU membership or an open discussion of it.

zh: 告诉BBC，它必须热情地接受英国脱欧，否则就会触犯众怒。
en: Tell the BBC that it must accept Brexit enthusiastically or face popular wrath.

zh: 最重要的是，关闭议会争论 — — 都是以“重塑议会主权”的名义。
en: Above all, close down parliamentary debate – all in the name of “restoring parliamentary sovereignty.”

zh: 离婚进行得不顺利。
en: This divorce is not going well.

zh: 过程才刚刚开始。
en: And the proceedings have only just started.

zh: 未来还有很长的路要走。
en: There is a long road ahead.

zh: 我们最后会成为什么样的国家，只有老天爷知道。
en: Heaven knows what sort of country we will be at the end of it.

zh: 但是，和所有离婚一样，我们可以笃定地认为，最苦的还是孩子。
en: But, as with any divorce, we can be fairly confident that it is the children who will suffer the most.

zh: 英国的挪威解决方案
en: Britain’s Norway Solution

zh: 伦敦 — — 在英国首相特雷莎·梅出人意料地决定举行“脱欧大选”不久后，我曾撰文指出英国的亲欧势力仍有可能从失败中抢回胜利。
en: LONDON – Shortly after UK Prime Minister Theresa May’s decision to call an unexpected “Brexit election,” I wrote that pro-Europeans in Britain might yet snatch victory from the jaws of defeat.

zh: 但我当时所想的时间跨度是五年，而不是五个星期。
en: But the timescale I had in mind was five years, not five weeks.

zh: 很难预测梅还会在首相的位置上坚持多久。
en: How long May will survive as prime minister is impossible to predict.

zh: 不仅伦敦，而且爱丁堡和贝尔法斯特的个人仇恨和拜占庭式的斗争将决定她的命运。
en: Her fate will depend on personal vendettas and Byzantine political rivalries, not only in London, but also in Edinburgh and Belfast.

zh: 但在预测英国脱欧谈判结果时，重要的问题已经不再是梅在政治上能否继续生存。
en: But in trying to anticipate the outcome of the Brexit negotiations, the questions that matter no longer have much to do with May’s political survival.

zh: 英国的议会考量和公众舆论究竟是赞成还是反对梅在选举前策划的“硬脱欧 ” — —即严厉打击移民并退出欧洲关税同盟、单一市场和法律管辖范围？
en: Are Britain’s parliamentary arithmetic and public opinion moving in favor of or against the “hard Brexit” – a drastic clampdown on immigration and withdrawal from the European Union’s customs union, single market, and legal jurisdiction – planned by May before the election?

zh: 但如果英国人反对梅的计划，欧盟领导人能否为他们提供与挪威类似的保全颜面的妥协方案，即留在欧盟体制结构之外，但接受欧盟成员国的大部分义务和代价，以换取单一市场所带来的商业好处？
en: And if Britons are turning against May’s agenda, will EU leaders offer them a face-saving compromise similar to that offered to Norway, which remains outside the EU’s institutional structures, but accepts most of the obligations and costs of EU membership in exchange for the commercial benefits of the single market?

zh: 只有类似挪威这样的对欧关系才能吸引英国的公众和政治支持，同时不会威胁到欧盟的原则或给任何一方造成严重的经济损失。
en: An EU relationship similar to Norway’s is the only model that could attract public and political support in Britain, without threatening EU principles or inflicting serious economic costs on either side.

zh: 这一选项的制度安排已经以欧洲经济区（EEA）的形式存在，这从某种意义上讲是欧盟成员资格的前身，目前有挪威、冰岛和列支敦士登等三个繁荣的欧洲小国都在采用这种形式。
en: The institutional arrangements for this option already exist, in the form of the European Economic Area (EEA), a sort of anteroom to full EU membership, currently occupied by three small but prosperous European countries: Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein.

zh: 上述国家在20世纪80年代末考虑成为欧盟成员，但却出于不同的原因决定暂不加入。
en: These countries considered EU membership in the late 1980s, but for various reasons decided not to join.

zh: 所有国家都想在经济和劳动力市场领域与欧洲实现一体化，而且，在脱欧公投后，人们普遍认为英国将试图谈判挪威式的欧洲经济区方案，而不是像梅所提议的那样与欧洲决裂。
en: All wanted to integrate their economies and labor markets with Europe, and, after the Brexit vote, Britain was widely expected to try to negotiate a Norwegian-style EEA arrangement, rather than the rupture proposed by May.

zh: 就在去年9月就任首相三个月后，梅实际否定欧洲经济区选择的做法震惊了世界，她在保守党年会上宣布那些自称为“世界公民”的人其实“哪国公民也不是 ” ， 因此欧洲经济区成员资格所要求的人口自由流动完全不可接受。
en: It was only last September, three months after becoming prime minister, that May surprised the world by effectively ruling out the EEA option, telling the Conservative Party’s annual conference that those who call themselves “citizens of the world” are really “citizens of nowhere,” and that the free movement of people required by EEA membership was therefore unacceptable.

zh: 1月，她正式宣布英国不会寻求成为欧洲单一市场成员，因为加入欧洲单一市场的前提是人口自由流动，这一立场在保守党的竞选宣言中得到了确认。
en: In January, she officially announced that Britain would not seek membership of the EU single market, because this would require free movement, a position confirmed in the Tories’ election manifesto.

zh: 但现在6月8日大选让梅变成了跛脚鸭，动荡的议会联盟和不断变幻的公众舆论将要推动接下来的脱欧谈判，她对移民的厌恶究竟还重要与否？
en: But is May’s aversion to immigrants still relevant, now that the election on June 8 has made her a lame duck and unstable parliamentary alignments and the shifting balance of public opinion will drive the Brexit negotiations?

zh: 公众舆论对移民的态度将成为未来几个月英国欧盟政策最重要的决定因素。
en: Public opinion on immigration will be the most important determinant of Britain’s European policy in the months ahead.

zh: 而在民调中由强有力证据支持的出人意料的选举结果表明公众对人口自由流动的态度更加微妙，而不是像梅和保守党竞选宣言所认为的那样以敌对为主。
en: And the unexpected election outcome, backed by strong evidence from polling, suggests that public attitudes concerning the free movement of people are more nuanced and less hostile than May’s rhetoric and the Conservative manifesto had assumed.

zh: 事实上，英国选民多数支持人口自由流动，前提是自由流动不被宣传为外国官僚机构强加的反民主政治条件，而是被作为英国和欧盟民众共同享有的一种权利。
en: In fact, British voters mostly support free movement, if it is presented not as an anti-democratic imposition by foreign bureaucrats, but rather as a right that British and EU citizens reciprocally enjoy.

zh: 5月，最接近预测大选结果的英国民调公司YouGov在他们对1，875名选民进行的最后一轮选前民调中加上了这样一个问题 ： “ 在谈判英国脱离欧盟的过程中，你认为我们的政府是否应该为欧盟民众提供来英国旅游、工作、学习或在英国退休的权利，来换取欧盟国家赋予英国民众同样的权利？
en: In May, YouGov, the British polling company that came closest to predicting the election result, added to their final pre-election poll of 1,875 voters the following question: “In negotiating Britain’s departure from the European Union, do you think our government should offer EU citizens the right to travel, work, study, or retire in Britain, in exchange for EU countries giving British citizens the same rights?”

zh: ” （ 全面披露，这个问题由Best for Britain设计，这是一个由我本人协助建立并主持的机构。 ）
en: (Full disclosure, this question was suggested by Best for Britain, an organization I helped to establish and chair.)

zh: 答案颠覆了人们的传统认知。
en: The answers defied conventional wisdom.

zh: 选民们面对这个经过谨慎考虑的样本赞成自由流动的比例达到4:1。
en: Voters in this carefully weighted sample favored free movement by four to one.

zh: 62%的人选择“是 ” ， 17%的人选择“否 ” ， 回答“不知道”的人为21 % 。
en: Sixty-two percent said “yes,” 17% “no,” and 21% answered, “don’t know.”

zh: 不仅如此，该样本所属各个分组赞成人口自由流动的人都明显占到绝大多数，无论分组标准是年龄、地区还是政党支持，这当中仅有一个例外：那就是支持反移民的英国独立党的少数选民。
en: Moreover, there were clear majorities in favor of free movement in every sub-group of the sample, whether categorized by age, region, or political-party support, with one exception: the small minority of voters who supported the anti-immigrant UK Independence Party.

zh: 要点是基于欧洲经济区模式的新关系允许英国在容忍人口自由流动的前提下保留欧洲关税同盟和统一市场的绝大部分好处，这不仅比硬脱欧带来的经济痛苦要小；而且还能够获得绝大部分选民的支持。
en: The upshot is that a new relationship based on the EEA model, allowing Britain to keep most of the benefits of the EU customs union and single market alongside free movement of people, would not only be economically less painful than a hard Brexit; it would also be supported by a large majority of voters.

zh: 单一市场准入和人口自由流动的组合在上周首次参与投票的大批年轻人中尤其有市场，他们认为在欧洲任何地方生活、工作或学习的权利是欧盟成员资格的主要好处，而不是代价。
en: The combination of single-market membership and free movement would be particularly popular with the large cohort of young people who turned out to vote last week for the first time and who consider the ability to live, work, or study anywhere in Europe a major benefit of EU membership, not a cost.

zh: 从英国政治的角度看，欧洲经济区成员资格将可能成为未来几个月指导英国脱欧谈判的最高原则。
en: From the standpoint of British politics, it is possible that EEA membership will become the lodestar steering Brexit negotiations in the months ahead.

zh: 但欧盟将会采取何种对策？
en: But how would the EU respond?

zh: 对其他欧盟成员国来说，以欧洲经济区为基础的脱欧谈判应当是完全可以接受、甚至是令人欢迎的结果。
en: For other EU countries, a Brexit negotiation based on EEA membership should be a perfectly acceptable, even welcome, outcome.

zh: 欧洲经济区成员资格不会导致英国白白撷取欧盟福利的果实，其他国家不愿看到这种结果出现是完全可以理解的。
en: EEA membership would not amount to British “cherry picking” of EU benefits, which other countries have understandably refused to accept.

zh: 这是因为，无论按照何种标准，欧洲经济区成员资格都明显逊于完整的欧盟成员资格。
en: This is because, by almost any standard, EEA membership is clearly inferior to full EU membership.

zh: 除接受人口自由流动外，欧洲经济区成员还必须遵守欧盟的商业规则并接受欧洲法院所作出的裁决，但却在制定这些规则和决策时起不到任何正式作用。
en: In addition to accepting free movement of people, EEA members must follow EU commercial rules and accept decisions by the European Court of Justice, without any formal role in making these rules and decisions.

zh: 出于上述原因，当欧洲经济区在1994年最初成立时，其目的仅仅是作为计划成为欧盟成员、但还没有准备好最终加入的奥地利、瑞典、芬兰和挪威等国的临时过渡性制度。
en: For these reasons, when the EEA was established in 1994, it was intended only as a temporary transitional arrangement for countries – such as Austria, Sweden, Finland, and Norway – which planned to become EU members, but were not ready to join.

zh: 对奥地利、瑞典和芬兰而言，它们最终不出所料地成为了正式成员。
en: For Austria, Sweden, and Finland, full membership came as intended.

zh: 但挪威选民却在一次全民公投中拒绝成为欧盟成员，并且一直延续到现在。
en: But in Norway, voters rejected EU membership in a referendum and still do.

zh: 挪威的临时欧洲经济区成员资格现在已经持续了23年。
en: Norway’s “temporary” EEA membership has now stretched to 23 years.

zh: 这会不会成为英国的榜样？
en: Could this be a precedent for Britain?

zh: 英国人权革命的失败
en: Britain’s Failed Human Rights Revolution

zh: 发自伦敦 — — 英国新联合政府的预算紧缩计划无疑占据了各大媒体的头条，但大卫·卡梅隆内阁同时也与前任工党政府在另一个关键领域彻底决裂 — — 那就是人权。
en: LONDON – The budget-cutting austerity program of Britain’s new coalition government has been claiming all the headlines, but David Cameron’s cabinet is breaking with its Labour predecessor in another key area as well: human rights.

zh: 事实上，由东尼·布莱尔的工党政府带给英国的人权试验已经彻底宣告破产了。
en: Indeed, the human-rights experiment that Tony Blair’s Labour government brought to Britain has failed.

zh: 英国的人权法案如今是两面不讨好：一方面有人指责其无力制止“粗暴”的反恐监察措施，另一方面又被人批评其阻碍了反恐政策的顺利实施。
en: Faulted by some for its inability to prevent “illiberal” anti-terrorism measures, the Human Rights Act is criticized by just as many others for hampering counter-terrorism policy.

zh: 实际上有许多人都对人权的终极理念嗤之以鼻，认为这只会导致对罪犯和恐怖分子的“愚蠢”妥协。
en: Indeed, many people mock the very notion of human rights, which is seen as leading to “loony” concessions that favor criminals and terrorists.

zh: 总的来说，媒体和公众的反应总是介乎于理想幻灭以及冷嘲热讽之间。
en: Overall, the reaction of both press and public is one of disillusion and/or cynicism.

zh: 英国这个国家以没有成文宪法闻名，或者说，直到最近都没有形成一份类似现代《权利法案》的文件，不过我们有1215年《自由大宪章》和板球。
en: Britain famously has no written constitution, or, until recently, anything resembling a modern Bill of Rights. Instead, we have Magna Carta and cricket.

zh: 普世人权的概念其实是个舶来品 — — 它存在于《欧洲人权公约》那些笼统的原则当中，而人权法庭则远在法国斯特拉斯堡。
en: The concept of universal human rights is literally foreign – enshrined in the broad-brush principles of the European Convention on Human Rights, whose court sits in Strasbourg.

zh: 因此任何想以人权理由控告英国政府的人都得跑到法国才能立案。
en: Until recently, anyone who wished to bring a human-rights case against the British government had to go to France.

zh: 不过在布莱尔1997年上台之后，事情开始有了转机。
en: Times changed when Tony Blair came to power in 1997.

zh: 在“权利终于回家了（意指回到了发源地 ） ” 这一浮夸和理想主义口号的映衬下，英国《人权法案》终于在2000年得以颁布实施。
en: With fanfare and idealism – reflected in the slogan “Rights Brought Home” – the Human Rights Act came into effect in 2000.

zh: 但这些充满道德感的自由主义精英也有自己的小算盘：倘若英国政府违反了法案的话，那就得由英国自己的法庭来审判，不用飘洋过海去劳烦那些国际法官了。
en: But the high-minded liberalism of the then-elite had a practical point as well: should the government have any soiled linen, it should be laundered in British courts rather than be aired before a panel of international judges.

zh: 但这个法案在英国却不得人心，也从未付诸法律实践。
en: Yet the Act is unloved by the British public, which never engaged with the process.

zh: 正如布莱尔的夫人切丽·布斯（她本身就是位人权律师）哀叹道 ： “ 大部分公众认为人权法案与自己的生活毫不相关。 ”
en: As Tony Blair’s wife, Cherie Booth, herself a human rights lawyer, lamented, “the majority of people feel that human rights are not relevant to their lives.”

zh: 这个例子告诫我们：不要画蛇添足，或者说，事实胜于雄辩。
en: There is a lesson here: if it’s not broken, don’t fix it. Put another way, actions speak louder than words.

zh: 与那些真正有损人道的侵犯人权行为相比，英国法院所受理的那些人权投诉简直不值一提。
en: When compared with human-rights abuses that truly affect humanity, the complaints dealt with by the British courts are small beer.

zh: 哪个孩子应该上哪所学校，或者应该给政治避难者安排何种住宿这类的问题都会引发许多人的关注（而且观点往往会分化 ） ， 但用“人权”这个粗略的概念来解决这些问题其实是贬低了这个概念。
en: Which child goes to what school or what public housing is offered to which asylum seeker will be of concern to many people (and views will differ). But using the broad brush of “human rights” to resolve such issues trivializes the concept.

zh: 而这同时也阻碍了真正严肃的讨论。
en: It also inhibits proper debate.

zh: 最后，估计也没有哪个公共机构愿意因侵犯人权而遭到起诉。
en: After all, what responsible public body wants to be accused of violating human rights?

zh: 事实上，人权诉讼的威胁令到那些提供公共服务的机构变得过于谨慎和保守。
en: Indeed, the threat of human-rights litigation has made providers of public services overly cautious and defensive.

zh: 这使得公众媒体痛批我们正生活在一个耗资巨大，官僚习气深重，而且低效率的“人权文化”当中 — — 这可算是一个引发深层次政治回响的指控。
en: This has led the popular press to howl that we now live in a costly, bureaucratic, and inefficient “human rights culture” – a charge with profound political resonance.

zh: 而在问鼎首相之前，卡梅隆就呼吁用某种更“英国”方式的来取代《人权法案 》 。
en: Before he became Prime Minister, Cameron called for the Human Rights Act to be replaced with something more “British.”

zh: 但荒谬的是，在人权最需要得到承认的时候，有些人却认为人权是一个毫无用处的东西，许多英国议员支持将欧洲人权法案编入英国法律，但他们同时也发现：如果给人权以正式承认的话，就会在对抗基地组织这类恐怖主义行为方面遭到极大不便。
en: Paradoxically, some deem human rights to be wholly inefficacious where their recognition is most required. Many MPs who backed the incorporation of the European human-rights convention into British law came to view formal recognition of human rights as a grave inconvenience when faced with Al Qaeda-inspired terrorism.

zh: 简而言之，在“权力终于回家”之后，布莱尔政府却最终想把它塞到沙发底下藏起来。
en: In short, having brought rights home, the Blair government ended up trying to hide them under the sofa.

zh: 而这一谜局在一场辩论上得到了最终体现 — — 关于在没有起诉或审判的情况下关押恐怖主义嫌疑犯。
en: This conundrum is symbolized by the debate over detaining terrorism suspects without charge or trial.

zh: 原本布莱尔打算将拘留期设定为90天，最终议会将其定在28天 — — 但这依然是西方世界中最长的拘留期。
en: Initially, Blair attempted to force through detention without charge for up to 90 days. Parliament settled on 28 days – still the longest such period in the Western world.

zh: 但《欧洲人权公约》第6条规定：每个受到犯罪指控的人都有权“被立刻告知”自己的罪名。
en: So much, then, for Article 6 of the European Convention, which provides that everyone charged with a criminal offense has the right “to be informed promptly” of the nature of the accusation against him.

zh: 而《大宪章》里也列明“任何自由人，如未经他人之依法裁判，或经国法判决，皆不得被逮捕，监禁 … … ”
en: So much, also, for Magna Carta, which provides that “No freeman shall be taken or imprisoned…but by lawful judgment of his peers, or by the law of the land.”

zh: 不过布莱尔的所作所为可不是一个特例。
en: Blair’s behavior is not unique.

zh: 事实上，任何试图实现人权的立法手段在一个议会高于一切的政治系统中都是不堪一击的。
en: The fact is that any piece of legislation purporting to embody human rights is entirely vulnerable to a political system in which parliament is supreme.

zh: 《人权法案》必然要臣服于随后颁布的法律法规。
en: The Human Rights Act must inevitably yield to subsequent legislation.

zh: 这些法律法规可都是获得了议会简单多数通过的。
en: All legislation is passed by a simple majority.

zh: 而法官是无法与这些条文抗衡的。
en: And judges cannot strike down legislation.

zh: 结果是什么？
en: The result?

zh: 权力只回了一天家；不过嫌疑人可要在大牢里蹲上1个月，却不知道自己犯了什么罪。
en: Rights brought home one day; detention for a month without charge the next.

zh: 事实上，即便人权的原则得到了推进 ， 《 人权法案》如今却遭到了忽视。
en: Indeed, even when the cause of human rights is being advanced, the Human Rights Act is now overlooked.

zh: 在副首相尼克·克列格5月发表的第一次重要政策演说中，他声明要推翻布莱尔所建成的“老大哥”国家（意指国家监控公民一切行为 ） ： 不再有身份证或者人口登记，对DNA信息的存储设立新限制，收紧对闭路电视监控的规管（此网络已经令英国人成为全球受监控程度最严重的人民）等等。
en: In May, in his first major policy speech, Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg announced the sweeping away of the “Big Brother” state that Blair had constructed: no more ID cards or national identity register, new restrictions on the storage of DNA, tighter regulation of the closed-circuit television surveillance that had made the British the most monitored people on earth, and so on.

zh: 他说了那么多，却一句都没提到“人权 ” — —这既反映出人权在当今英国的敏感性，同时也在默默地承认：在这种关键时刻 ， 《 人权法案》可是靠不住的。
en: All this and not one mention of “human rights” – an absence that reflects the political sensitivity of human rights in Britain today, and that tacitly acknowledges that when the stakes are high, the Human Rights Act cannot be relied upon.

zh: 那么卡梅隆政府究竟将如何根除“老大哥 ” ？
en: Where, then, does that leave the Cameron government’s supposed extirpation of Big Brother?

zh: 一种方法就是比布莱尔更进一步，把某些原则特别提出来，并设立宪法法庭以维护之。
en: One way forward would be to go further than Blair by ring-fencing certain principles and creating some form of constitutional court to defend them.

zh: 但这种死板管制的成本可能会很高，而其效力，以美国飘忽不定的人权记录来看，有时比空想更靠不住。
en: But the cost of such rigid rules may be high, and their effectiveness, as witnessed by the vagaries of the United States’ record on human rights, is less fool-proof than is sometimes imagined.

zh: 因此，或许在一个成熟的民主体制内，与其虚张声势，不如采取实际行动去尊重人权；与其引入更多法律，既在民众中留下坏印象，又不堪大用，不如在需要维护自由和公平竞争时相信自己的宪政体制。
en: So, perhaps in a mature democracy, human rights should be dignified by actions rather than words. Instead of introducing more legislation that is tainted both in the popular imagination and in its utility, Britain could, after all, trust its constitution to act as and when required to safeguard liberty and fair play.

zh: 不管怎么样，民主的观点最终会胜利，而英国的人权记录，虽然算不上完美，却依然可圈可点。
en: For good or ill, democratic sentiment will win out, and Britain’s human-rights record, while imperfect, remains strong.

zh: 英国的否定之路
en: Britain’s Path of Denial

zh: 圣地亚哥 — — 如今，如果你去伦敦旅行，会发现一些奇怪的景象：英国经济越萎靡，卡梅伦政府的各位部长和保守党经济学家就越频繁地宣称严厉的支出削减政策对经济增长有利。
en: SANTIAGO – Visit London nowadays and you will notice something strange going on: the worse the British economy tanks, the more fervently Prime Minister David Cameron’s ministers and Tory economists insist that draconian spending cuts are good for economic growth.

zh: 一些观察家将其视为一种信念（大概是对不受束缚的自由市场的优点的信仰 ） 。
en: Some observers see this as an act of faith (presumably in the virtues of the unfettered market).

zh: 其他人，比如保罗·克鲁格曼（Paul Krugman ） ， 则认为这是一种欺瞒：保守党一心想要小政府，为此不惜牺牲经济增长。
en: Others, such as the economist Paul Krugman, see it as an act of bad faith: the Tories just want smaller government, regardless of the consequences for growth.

zh: 问题在于，削减支出以刺激经济到底是不是一种无信念基础的观点。
en: The question remains whether there is a non-faith-based argument for cutting back spending to stimulate an economy.

zh: 答案是肯定的。
en: The answer is yes.

zh: 事实上，这一观点存在两种类型。
en: In fact, there are two.

zh: 学术研究表明，它们在过去挺有效，比如20世纪80年代的爱尔兰和丹麦。
en: Academic research has shown them at work in the past – for example, in Ireland and Denmark during the 1980’s.

zh: 对保守党来说，不幸的是这两次刺激性支出削减都不适用英国窘迫的现状。
en: Unfortunately for the Tories, neither case for stimulative spending cuts fits Britain’s predicament today.

zh: 一种观点强调财政和货币政策之间的联系。
en: One argument emphasizes the links between fiscal and monetary policy.

zh: 如果一国有着巨大的财政赤字，那么其中央银行可能不得不维持高利率以控制通胀。
en: In a country with large fiscal deficits, the central bank may have to keep interest rates high to control inflation.

zh: 在这种情形下，预算削减将创造降息空间。
en: In this scenario, budget cuts create room for interest rates to fall.

zh: 如果该国汇率是浮动的，那么货币也会贬值。
en: If the country has a floating exchange-rate regime, the currency depreciates, too.

zh: 这些变化均有利于需求和增长。
en: Both of these changes are good for demand and growth.

zh: 如果综合作用压倒了一开始削减支出的紧缩效应，则经济就能在一轮财政紧缩后大为改善。
en: If their combined impact more than outweighs the initial contractionary effect of expenditure cuts, then the economy may well pick up after a round of fiscal tightening.

zh: 但在如今的英国，很难看到这种效应。
en: But little effort is needed to see that this not the British story today.

zh: 英格兰银行将利率维持在零区间已经超过两年半了。
en: The Bank of England’s policy interest rate has remained just above zero for more than two and a half years.

zh: 不管政府的财政政策立场如何，利率都不可能降到零以下。
en: Regardless of the government’s fiscal-policy stance, this interest rate cannot move below zero.

zh: 另一种扩张性财政收缩则更为隐蔽。
en: The second case for expansionary fiscal contraction is subtler.

zh: 在一个公共债务快速增长的经济中，财政调整被推得越迟，所需的调整规模就会变得越大，成本也会变得越高。
en: In an economy in which public debt is growing quickly, the longer fiscal adjustment is put off, the larger and costlier it will have to be.

zh: 家庭和公司都明白这一点，并预期未来会出现痛苦的支出削减和税收增加，因而停止消费和投资。
en: Households and companies understand this and cease to consume or invest in anticipation of the painful spending cuts and tax hikes to come.

zh: 因此，该观点推断，保守党政府在今天大力削减开支将有助于英国人民免于在明天遭受痛苦。
en: So, the argument goes, a courageous Tory government that cuts spending today spares citizens that future pain.

zh: 开支削减后，私人部门会感到手里的钱更多了，对前景也更乐观了，于是便会继续大手花钱，经济也将繁荣起来。
en: Then, feeling richer and brimming with optimism, the private sector goes on a spending spree and the economy booms.

zh: 换句话说，如果没有预算削减，英国大概已经和西班牙成为难兄难弟了 — — 甚至可能成为另一个葡萄牙或希腊。
en: Put differently: without the budget cuts, Britain would have been Spain – or perhaps even Portugal or Greece.

zh: 实施了预算削减并得到了市场的保证，英国将不会有步放任的地中海国家后尘的危险。
en: With the budget cuts in place and the markets reassured, Britain no longer risks resembling an unruly Mediterranean country.

zh: 因此，英国的支出很快就会复苏，经济增长也会再次启动。
en: Thus, Britons will soon start spending again and economic growth will ensue.

zh: 听起来很美妙，但这并不是如今英国的现实。
en: So far, so good – except that this story, too, does not apply to Britain.

zh: 我们看不到危机已经擦边而过的迹象。
en: There is no sign of a crisis narrowly averted.

zh: 英国国债的十年期收益率从卡梅伦上台之前很久便下跌到了历史低点。
en: Ten-year yields on British government bonds were at historic lows long before Cameron took office.

zh: 如果危机即将袭来，那么市场显然对此全无防范。
en: If a crisis was imminent, the markets clearly took no notice.

zh: 而如果联合政府的预算削减已然提高了对未来产出的预期，那么信心的提升应该显示为股价攀升 — — 这显然也得不到事实的印证。
en: And if the coalition government’s budget cuts had improved expectations about future output, that greater confidence would have shown up in higher equity prices – but there is no evidence of this, either.

zh: 简言之，英国的私人需求依然波澜不惊，并未出现大涨。
en: In short, private demand in Britain is flatlining rather than surging.

zh: 再加上因预算削减导致的公共部门需求大跌，英国已经具备了进入长期停滞的所有必要条件。
en: Add to the mix the collapse in public-sector demand that comes from deep budget cuts, and you have all the ingredients necessary for prolonged stagnation.

zh: 而停滞（如果不是倒退的话）正是近期英国经济报告所显示的信息。
en: And stagnation, if not worse, is precisely what recent British economic reports are showing.

zh: 照现在的形势发展得越久，问题就会变得更严重。
en: The longer this goes on, the more serious the problem will become.

zh: 长期失业人士会被挤出劳动力市场。
en: The long-term unemployed will drop out of the labor market.

zh: 长期不进行新投资活动的企业将丧失竞争力。
en: Firms that invest little will become uncompetitive.

zh: 用经济学家的话说，低需求会导致低供给，致使无通胀复苏难上加难。
en: In the jargon of economists, low demand will engender low supply, making a non-inflationary recovery even more difficult to achieve.

zh: 英国将如何应对？
en: What is to be done in Britain?

zh: 欧元区在没完没了的危机中苦苦挣扎，因此英国不用指望外部援手。
en: With the eurozone tumbling from crisis to crisis, salvation will not come from abroad.

zh: 而在国内，唯一可以采取的措施是非常规货币政策。
en: At home, all that is left is unconventional monetary policy.

zh: 英格兰银行最近再度通过所谓的量化宽松向经济注入750亿英镑。
en: The Bank of England recently injected an additional £75 billion into the economy via so-called quantitative easing.

zh: 这一回撒下去的可是真金白银，而不是信念了。
en: Now, that is real cash, not just an act of faith.

zh: 大选在前，现实在后
en: Britain Votes and Reality Waits

zh: 发自伦敦 — — 我可不是在这里自吹自擂，不过上一次保守党赢得英国大选还是1992年，当时的首相是约翰·梅杰，而时任党主席而又成功操办了那场大选的，正是鄙人。
en: LONDON – I don’t mean to sound as though I am bragging, but the last time the Conservative Party won an election in Britain was 1992, when John Major was Prime Minister. The chairman of the party at the time, running the winning campaign, was me.

zh: 我们赢得了大选，但我本人却在竞选议会席位时落败，并被派到香港担任这个殖民地的末代总督。
en: We won the election, but I lost my own race for a parliamentary seat and was sent off to Hong Kong as the colony’s last British governor.

zh: 因此当保守党彻底丧失了执政意志，随之在1990年代中期因英国在欧洲所扮演的角色这一问题而分裂的时候，我是不在场的。
en: So I wasn’t around when the Conservative Party, losing the will to govern, tore itself apart in the mid-1990’s over Britain’s role in Europe.

zh: 一切正如温斯顿·丘吉尔所言 ： “ 政治自杀是一个足以令人后悔一辈子的问题。 ”
en: As Winston Churchill said, the problem with committing political suicide is that you live to regret it.

zh: 虽然梅杰成功地带领英国经济实现了后衰退时代的复苏，但他却在1997年输给了东尼·布莱尔，断送了保守党18年执政并迎来了工党的13年统治，而这13年的执政似乎也将在5月6日英国人投下一票后宣告落幕。
en: Despite piloting the economy through a post-recession recovery, Major lost to Tony Blair in 1997, ending 18 years of Conservative government and bringing a 13-year Labour run, which will probably end when Britain votes for a new government on May 6.

zh: 布莱尔继承了强劲的经济发展势头，而且平心而论也没有毁掉它。
en: Blair took over a strong economic legacy, and, to be scrupulously fair, he didn’t wreck it.

zh: 他本人及其财政大臣戈登·布朗一直坚持奉行前任的公共支出计划。
en: He and his finance minister, Gordon Brown, stuck to their predecessors’ public-spending plans, for example.

zh: 在工党执政的最初九年间，财政支出占GDP的比例甚至比保守党开始执政的那几年还要低。
en: In Labour’s first nine years of governing, public expenditure as a proportion of GDP was lower than in the comparable Conservative period.

zh: 但随后我们却一如既往地陷入了英国式困境当中。
en: Then we fell into the usual British trap.

zh: 布朗在2007年任首相之后大肆花费举债，以致在金融危机冲击英伦三岛之前整个国家就已经陷入了结构性财政赤字以及信贷泡沫之中。
en: Brown, who became prime minister in 2007, let spending and borrowing rip, so that when the global crash hit Britain was already suffering from a structural fiscal deficit and a credit bubble.

zh: 英国对危机的准备工作也做得比大多数其他国家要差。
en: The country was worse prepared for disaster than most others.

zh: 因此本次大选的赢家就必须得承担一个异常棘手的工作，那就是削减预算赤字 — — 占到GDP的12 % — —并将经济带回到可持续复苏的轨道上去。
en: As a result, whoever wins the election will have an awful job cutting the country’s budget deficit – 12% of GDP – and setting the economy back on the road to sustainable recovery.

zh: 保守党人很可能在大卫·卡梅隆这个年轻领袖的领导下夺得胜利，因为卡梅隆令全党的政治立场重新回归到了中间路线，而走这个路线的政党常常能赢得竞选胜利。 而布郎率领的工党则不受欢迎，因为经济深陷泥沼且人们普遍认为该党已经黔驴技穷了。
en: The Conservatives should triumph under a young leader, David Cameron, who has hauled them back onto the middle ground of politics where elections are usually won.

zh: 而尼克·克列格率领的自由民主党则声势浩大，甚至有可能在投票中压倒工党。 然而英国的选举体制却注定了他们的大选获胜几率几乎只有统计学上的可能性。
en: Labour, under Brown, is unpopular, with the economy in deep trouble and a general sense that the party has run out of ideas.  The Liberal Democrats under Nick Clegg have surged remarkably, and may even push ahead of Labour in the popular vote.  But the structure of the British election is such that a victory for them is almost a statistical impossibility.

zh: 事实上，民意调查的数据依然胶着。
en: Indeed, the opinion polls remain tight.

zh: 结果在很大程度上将由各党领袖电视辩论的胜负来决定，而类似的辩论在英国大选中还是头一次，并将对自由民主党的竞选活动产生极大支持。
en: Much will depend on the outcome of TV debates between the leaders, which are being held for the first time in a British election campaign, and which have thus far contributed mightily to the Liberal Democrat surge.

zh: 每一位领袖都在精心准备，生怕辩论场上的任何洋相令自己的党派丢掉大选，而是至今日，还没有谁干出些搬石头砸自己脚的蠢事。
en: Each leader has been carefully groomed to avoid the sort of gaffes that could cost his party the election, and thus far, not one has shot himself in the foot.

zh: 如果说克列格的获胜几乎不可能的话，那么卡梅隆要付出的努力也比常规多得多，这是因为英国的选举系统是向工党严重倾斜的。
en: If Clegg’s job is almost impossible, Cameron’s job is also much harder than it should be because the British electoral system is tilted heavily against the Conservatives.

zh: 那些由工党所主导的地区 — — 威尔士，苏格兰和英格兰农村地区 — — 所选出的代表数量可是超出正常比例的。
en: The more Labour-oriented parts of the United Kingdom – Wales, Scotland, and urban England – are over-represented.

zh: 工党区的人口数量通常较少，而选区划分又没有充分考虑到人口流动的因素。
en: Electorates in constituencies where Labour is usually dominant are smaller, and district boundaries take insufficient account of population shifts.

zh: 因此如果一名保守党议员要获胜的话就得比工党议员赢得更多的选票。
en: Thus, more votes are needed to elect a Conservative than a Labour MP.

zh: 在上届选举中，工党的总票数只比保守党多3 % ， 却多得了150个以上的席位。
en: In the last election, Labour got 3% more of the popular vote than the Conservatives, but gained 150 more seats.

zh: 虽然如今的状况已经比从前公平许多，但卡梅隆却依然要克服极大的困难才能赢的胜利。
en: The situation is a bit fairer today, but Cameron still has a steep hill to climb if he is to win.

zh: 我想他会成功的 — — 这不仅是因为当今最有影响力的竞选口号就是“变革 ” 。
en: I think he will do so – not least because the most potent electoral argument today is “time for change.”

zh: 二是一旦选民们发现那些政府负责人失去了他们最宝贵的品质：疑罪从无（意指在不确定伊拉克是否有策划发动“9·11”的情况下发动战争）之时，就会倾向于推翻政府。
en: Voters tend to get rid of governments once the incumbents have lost their most precious attribute: the benefit of the doubt.

zh: 而工党目前似乎正处于如斯境况当中。
en: Labour seems to be in that situation today.

zh: 但无论结果如何，新政府都将面对一项令人畏惧的挑战 — — 比一个“无多数派议会”所造成的混乱更令人裹足不前的挑战，这就是选举后可能需要组建一个联合政府或者少数派政府。
en: But, whatever the outcome, a new government will face a daunting challenge – challenges that will be even more daunting in the case of a “hung parliament,” which will require either a coalition government or minority government to be formed after the vote.

zh: 不仅需要政府用强力手段去控制未来几年的公共支出，而更令人担忧的则是许多选民似乎都倾向于否定这个现实。
en: It is not just that tough measures will be required to rein in public spending for years to come. More worrying is that many voters seem to be in denial about that fact.

zh: 人们可能会发现一旦所有选举活动结束之后，真实的经济状况对他们的冲击就如同一盆冷水从头浇到腿。
en: They are likely to find that economic reality, once all the electioneering is over, is a very cold shower indeed.

zh: 尽管我本人有着相当的温和派倾向以及有点理想化，但作为一个老派保守党人，我自然是希望卡梅隆能赢。
en: As a tribal Conservative, albeit it with pretty moderate tendencies and a deep suspicion of ideology, I naturally want Cameron to win.

zh: 他这个人头脑聪明，举止得体，而且身体强健。
en: He is clever, decent, and strong. I think he will make a good prime minister.

zh: 我想他会是一个好首相，但我并不妒忌他。
en: But I don’t envy him the job.

zh: 因为要说服选民去接受为了防止国家衰退必须遏制住花费更越来越多公共支出的观点是需要非常高超的领导技巧的。
en: It will require leadership skills of a high order to persuade voters that in order to prevent national decline we must curb our appetite for more and more public spending.

zh: 那些持家过日子的老法则依旧适用，那就是你的支出不能超过收入 — — 即便是在所谓的21世纪新经济当中。
en: The old laws of household economics still apply.  You can’t spend more than you earn – even in the so-called new economy of the twenty-first century.

zh: 我猜其他国家也必须得补上这一课。
en: I suspect that other countries will have to learn that lesson as well.

zh: 在欧洲，经济一团糟的可不仅仅是希腊。
en: In Europe, it is not just Greece that is in a mess.

zh: 西班牙和葡萄牙的公共财政状况相对还好一点，但这些国家也面对着如何在提升自身在欧元区内竞争力的严峻问题。
en: The public finances of Spain and Portugal are somewhat sounder, but those countries face huge problems in increasing their competitiveness within the eurozone.

zh: 比如在西班牙，工资一再飙升，生产力却停滞不前。
en: In Spain, for example, wages have risen too fast, and productivity has lagged.

zh: 我们应当警惕那些在未来几年内可能在欧洲各国发生的政治危机，而人们则将被迫承受许多不如意的事实。
en: We should be on the lookout for political fireworks over the next few years in many European countries as people are forced to confront some uncomfortable verities.

zh: 须知有机会发生政治险情的地方，可不仅仅只有英国。
en: It won’t only be in Britain that politics, from time to time, becomes a bit too exciting.

zh: 英国之战的逃兵
en: Deserting the Battle for Britain

zh: 圣皮埃尔昂特雷蒙，法国—在英国脱欧投票之后的悲哀状态中，前“留欧派”似乎已经完全放弃了为国家未来而斗争。
en: SAINT PIERRE D’ENTREMONT, FRANCE – In the sad state of affairs following the Brexit vote in the United Kingdom, former “Remainers” – those who wished to stay in the EU – seem to have given up altogether on fighting for the future of their country.

zh: 更糟糕的是，许多人似乎接受了反欧盟“脱欧”阵营的基本前提：英国有太多的欧洲人。
en: Worse still, many seem to have accepted the fundamental premise of the anti-EU “Leave” campaign: that there are too many Europeans in Britain.

zh: 这让争论朝着恶化的方向发展，并导致了绝望的一厢情愿：也许，如果英国对欧盟公民实施移民前置，其实也不会失去多少市场准入。
en: This has changed the terms of the debate for the worse, and has led to hopelessly wishful thinking: Perhaps the UK won’t actually lose much market access if it imposes immigration restrictions on EU nationals.

zh: 也许欧盟本身也将放弃劳动力自由流动，以此安抚英国。
en: Perhaps the EU itself will abandon free labor mobility in an attempt to appease the UK.

zh: 也许欧盟会采取特例以保护英国大学，或给予英国与列支敦士登一样的待遇。 作为微型国家，列支敦士登可以进入欧盟单一市场。
en: Perhaps the EU will make special exceptions to protect the British university sector, or treat the UK like Liechtenstein, a microstate with access to the single market.

zh: 事实上，留欧派接受了英国应该将欧洲人挡在国门之外的观点，这让英国 — — 或至少是英格兰和爱尔兰，如果亲欧盟的苏格兰和爱尔兰脱离英国的话 — — 迈向了“硬”脱欧，不仅仅脱离欧盟，也脱离欧洲单一市场。
en: In fact, with Remainers accepting the argument that Britain should keep Europeans out, the UK – or at least England and Wales, if pro-EU Scotland and Northern Ireland leave – is headed for a “hard” Brexit, not just from the Union, but from Europe’s single market.

zh: 果真如此的话，英国将付出巨大代价。
en: If this happens, it will cost the country dearly.

zh: 余波到底有多广尚未可知，但可以预期许多人将感到十分痛苦，许多机构也将遭受重创。
en: The full extent of the fallout is unknown, but we can expect it to be painful for many people and damaging to many institutions.

zh: 来自其他欧盟成员国的新来者已在英国泛滥成灾，这种说法难道一无是处吗？
en: Is there any merit to the claim that the UK has become flooded with newcomers from other EU member states?

zh: 下图描述了欧盟移民占各欧盟国家的百分比。
en: The following chart shows the percentage of EU immigrants in each EU country.

zh: 英国处于分布的顶端，但与其他许多欧盟成员国等量齐观，人均欧盟移民数更是远远没有达到最多。
en: The UK is at the upper end of the distribution, but it is on par with many other EU members, and it is far from having the most EU immigrants per capita.

zh: 事实上，爱尔兰欧盟移民占总人口比例比英国高出一倍。
en: In fact, the share of EU immigrants in the total population is twice as high in Ireland.

zh: 英国决策者在处理英国脱欧后局面时，应该参考爱尔兰的例子，因为两国情况相似。
en: As British policymakers navigate the post-Brexit landscape, they should consider the Irish example, given the similarities between the two countries.

zh: 爱尔兰和英国都存在住房短缺，特别是在都柏林和伦敦等大都会中心周边。
en: Ireland and the UK both have housing shortages, especially around metropolitan centers such as Dublin and London.

zh: 它们的公共服务都不尽如人意 — — 事实上，爱尔兰比英国还要差得多。
en: And they both have public services that leave something to be desired – in fact, Ireland’s are much worse than Britain’s.

zh: 尽管爱尔兰人并不是英国人，但他们在文化上比其他欧洲人更加接近。
en: While the Irish are not British, they are closer culturally than other Europeans.

zh: 2008年，爱尔兰公投拒绝里斯本条约草案，都柏林的贫困地区成为强大的反移民票仓。
en: As we saw in 2008, when Irish referendum voters refused to ratify the Treaty of Lisbon, there is a potential anti-immigrant voting bloc in the poorer parts of Dublin.

zh: 英国脱欧公投中也有类似的群体 — — 感受不到来自全球化的好处的穷人。
en: These are the same kind of voters who turned out for the UK’s Brexit referendum – poorer people who have not felt the gains from globalization.

zh: 于是问题就在于为何爱尔兰没有没有发展出向英国那么高涨的对欧盟移民的敌意，特别是考虑到2008年金融危机后欧洲机构令人发指的对待爱尔兰的方式。
en: The question, then, is why the Irish haven’t developed UK levels of animosity toward EU immigrants, especially given the appalling way in which the country was treated by European institutions in the wake of the 2008 financial crisis.

zh: 诚然，英国媒体要为其中的区别负有相当大的责任。
en: Surely, the British media bear considerable responsibility for the difference.

zh: 爱尔兰没有遍布于英国的撒谎成性的狭隘沙文主义三流小报。
en: Ireland has nothing like the mendacious, jingoistic gutter press that thrives in the UK.

zh: 但是，很大的责任在于英国政治领导人。
en: Much of the blame, however, lies with British political leaders.

zh: 一方面，有些人靠攻击欧盟生存，他们的立论点往往似是而非。
en: One the one hand, there are those who have made careers out of attacking the EU, often on entirely specious grounds.

zh: 另一方面，有些留欧派不够热情，如前首相卡梅伦，他们从未强烈支持保留欧盟成员资格。
en: On the other, there are lukewarm Remainers, such as former Prime Minister David Cameron, who never made a strong case for continued membership in the EU.

zh: 如今，即便是铁杆留欧派也没有提出保留英国和欧盟之间的双向劳动力流动以及加入欧洲经济区（EEA ） 。
en: Now, even committed Remainers are failing to make the case for continued two-way labor mobility between the UK and the EU, and for membership in the European Economic Area (EEA).

zh: 爱尔兰没有这个问题。
en: Ireland hasn’t had this problem.

zh: 令人关注的是，爱尔兰民族主义政党、前爱尔兰共和军的政治力量新芬党也没有沉溺于英国独立党所采用的仇外论调。
en: Notably, Sinn Féin, Ireland’s nationalist party and the former political arm of the Irish Republican Army, has not indulged in the kind of xenophobic rhetoric used by the UK Independence Party.

zh: 事实上，新芬党有了很大的改观，在来自欧盟和其他地区移民的问题上采纳了进步立场。
en: In fact, to its immense credit, Sinn Féin has gone out of its way to adopt a progressive stance on the issue of immigration from the EU and elsewhere.

zh: 许多评论者正确地指出，全球化的经济影响能解释反移民情绪。
en: Many commentators have correctly pointed to the economic effects of globalization to explain anti-immigrant sentiment.

zh: 全球化创造了赢家和输家这一事实显然解释了目前在英国和其他国家显而易见的反全球化抵制。
en: The fact that globalization produces both winners and losers certainly explains much of the anti-globalization backlash now apparent in the UK and elsewhere.

zh: 但其他东西也很重要，比如文化沙文主义。
en: But other things matter, too, such as cultural chauvinism.

zh: 简单说，英国对其欧洲同胞的存在的敌意与英国社会中最阴暗的一些方面有着很大关联。
en: Put plainly, English animosity toward the presence of fellow Europeans has a lot to do with some of the worst aspects of English society.

zh: 解决公共服务短缺问题有助于减轻关于移民 — — 以及更一般地，关于全球化 — — 的经济顾虑。
en: Addressing shortfalls in public services can help to mitigate economic concerns about immigration, and about globalization more generally.

zh: 同样重要的是，前留欧派必须继续向英国人解释为何与欧洲进行商品、服务和人的自由交换有利于英国。
en: Just as important, former Remainers must continue to explain to the English why the free exchange of goods, services, and people with Europe is good for Britain.

zh: 英国投票脱离了欧盟，但脱欧可以有两种版本：获得EEA成员资格，以进入欧洲单一市场和保持人员自由流动；或退出单一市场，然后进行难以预料的贸易谈判。
en: The UK voted to leave the EU, but Brexit comes in two flavors: membership in the EEA, with access to Europe’s single market and free movement of people, or an exit from the single market, followed by unpredictable trade negotiations.

zh: 还有巨大的周旋余地：我们不知道英国选民会选择两种结果的哪一种。
en: There is still a huge amount to play for: we don’t know which of these two outcomes English voters would choose.

zh: 不幸的是，看起来英国正在默认迈向第二个选择 — — “硬”脱欧。
en: Unfortunately, it looks as though the UK is now headed for the second option – a “hard” Brexit – by default.

zh: 对于留欧派来说，在他们先前支持留在欧盟的时候没有提出争取EEA成员资格的理由是令人震惊的不负责任的行为。
en: For Remainers not to make the case for EEA membership, when they had previously been in favor of remaining in the EU, is an astonishing abdication of responsibility.

zh: 连接分裂欧洲的英国之桥
en: A British Bridge for a Divided Europe

zh: 伦敦—欧盟在英国向来不是很受欢迎。
en: LONDON – The European Union has never been very popular in Britain.

zh: 英国加入欧盟很晚，其选民将在6月23日决定是否想要早早离开。
en: It joined late, and its voters will be asked on June 23 whether they want to leave early.

zh: 此次全民公决的结果对政府不具有法律约束力；但很难想象在公众决定要退出的情况下英国仍然留在欧盟。
en: The referendum’s outcome will not be legally binding on the government; but it is inconceivable that Britain will stay if the public’s verdict is to quit.

zh: 多年来，英国关于欧洲的争论焦点几经变迁。
en: Over the years, the focus of the British debate about Europe has shifted.

zh: 20世纪60年代和70年代，问题是英国是否可以不加入当时的欧洲经济共同体。
en: In the 1960s and 1970s, the question was whether Britain could afford not to join what was then the European Economic Community.

zh: 担心之处是英国会被排除在全世界增长最快的市场之外，并且其与美国的关系也将受到威胁：西方世界将由两大支柱构成，而欧洲，而不是衰败的英国将是其中之一。
