en: With the decision about raising rates such a close call, one would think that the Fed would be inclined to do it this year, given that the chair and vice chair have pretty much told the market for months that this will happen. The real reason for not hiking by the end of the year is public relations.

zh: 让我们假设美联储会在12月的会议上提高利率0.25个基点，并尽可能弱化对市场的影响。
en: Let’s suppose the Fed raises interest rates to 0.25 basis points at its December meeting, trying its best to send a soothing message to markets.

zh: 最可能出现的结果是一切都相安无事，同时美联储不会为随之出现的适度股票价格调整而担忧。
en: The most likely outcome is that all will be fine, and the Fed doesn’t really care if a modest equity-price correction ensues.

zh: 但其实真正的风险在于，如果美联储开始加息，就要为经济在未来半年到一年内出现的所有坏情况承担罪责，并与即将举行的美国总统大选产生联动。
en: No, the real risk is that, if the Fed starts hiking, it will be blamed for absolutely every bad thing that happens in the economy for the next six months to a year, which will happen to coincide with the heart of a US presidential election campaign.

zh: 就因为一个小加息，无论造成坏结果的真实原因是什么，都要由美联储来背黑锅。
en: One small hike and the Fed owns every bad outcome, no matter what the real cause.

zh: 当然，美联储了解到，几乎每个人都讨厌加息，而且基本上都喜欢降息。
en: The Fed of course understands that pretty much everyone dislikes interest-rate hikes and almost always likes rate cuts.

zh: 所有央行行长会告诉你，无论在何种情况下，他/她每收到一个加息请求就会同时收到99个降息请求。
en: Any central banker will tell you that he or she gets 99 requests for interest-rate cuts for every request for a hike, almost regardless of the situation.

zh: 应对这些压力的最好办法是按照完全明确的标准来操作。
en: The best defense against these pressures is to operate according to utterly unambiguous criteria.

zh: 相反，无论怀着多少善意，美联储过度发言的的最终影响都是含糊和不确定性。
en: Instead, however good its intentions, the net effect of too much Fed speak has been vagueness and uncertainty.

zh: 那么美联储应该怎么办？
en: So what should the Fed do?

zh: 我的选择是让它更加直言不讳地解释为何要继续等待 ： “ 摆脱零利率底限是很难的，我们希望等到通胀率超过3％以最终确认，然后我们会采取合理的行动速度来恢复正常化。
en: My choice would be to have it explain the case for waiting more forthrightly: “Getting off the zero bound is hard, we want to see inflation over 3% to be absolutely sure, and then we will move with reasonable speed to normalize.”

zh: ”但我同时也可以忍受他们说“我们担心如果我们等待太久，我们将不得不过快过剧烈地收紧（货币政策 ） 。 ”
en: But I also could live with, “We are worried that if we wait too long, we will have to tighten too hard and too fast.”

zh: 在检讨2008年金融危机的教训时按照规则操作是有道理的，但如今已经不一样了。
en: Throwing out the rulebook made sense in the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis. It doesn’t anymore.

zh: 而今时今日的含糊其辞已经成为了导致市场波动的主要动因 — — 也是美联储最不想看到的。
en: And today’s lack of clarity has become a major contributor to market volatility – the last place the Fed should want to be.

zh: 因为美联储升息而丑化它是不对的，因为不升息而丑化它也是不对的；如果情况真的如此紧急，它可能就不那么重要了。
en: It’s wrong to vilify the Fed for hiking, and it’s wrong to vilify it for not hiking; if it is such a close call, it probably doesn’t matter so much.

zh: 但在这个临界点，就应该去要求美联储提供关于其战略，以及这对未来意味着什么的更清晰信息。
en: But, at this critical point, it is fair to ask the Fed for a much clearer message about what its strategy is, and what this implies for the future.

zh: 如果美联储主席珍妮特·耶伦（Janet Yellen）想在一段时间内凌驾于联邦公开市场委员会的话，那就只管干吧。
en: If Fed Chair Janet Yellen has to assert her will over the FOMC for a while, so be it.

zh: 总要有某个委员挺身而出把骆驼领到水边的是不？
en: Somebody on the committee has to lead the camel to water.

zh: 宏观庸医
en: Macro Malpractice

zh: 纽黑文—美国经济的药方开错了。
en: NEW HAVEN – The wrong medicine is being applied to America’s economy.

zh: 决策者诊错了病，开出了未受过检验的实验性药方，这一药方的潜在副作用巨大。
en: Having misdiagnosed the ailment, policymakers have prescribed untested experimental medicine with potentially grave side effects.

zh: 病人是美国消费者 — — 世界有史以来最大规模的消费者，但现在正陷入大萧条以来最大的不适中。
en: The patient is the American consumer – the world’s biggest by far, but now in the throes of the worst funk since the Great Depression.

zh: 最新的美国消费数据令人极其沮丧。
en: Recent data on consumer spending in the United States have been terrible.

zh: 2012年二季度经通胀调整的个人消费支出刚刚被向下修正了1.5 % ， 看起来三季度的数字也是半斤八两。
en: Growth in inflation-adjusted US personal consumption expenditures has just been revised down to 1.5% in the second quarter of 2012, and appears to be on track for a similarly anemic increase in the third quarter.

zh: 更糟糕的是，这些数字只是已经存在了四年半的趋势的最新延续。
en: Worse, these numbers are just the latest in what has now been a four-and-a-half-year-old trend.

zh: 从2008年一季度开始直到2012年二季度，年化真实消费支出增长率只有0.7 % — —与2007年危机前十年的平均数字3.6%形成鲜明对比。
en: From the first quarter of 2008 through the second quarter of 2012, annualized growth in real consumption spending has averaged a mere 0.7% – all the more extraordinary when compared with the pre-crisis trend of 3.6% in the decade ending in 2007.

zh: 病灶在于被推迟的资产负债表衰退将一代美国消费者变成了经济僵尸。
en: The disease is a protracted balance-sheet recession that has turned a generation of America’s consumers into zombies – the economic walking dead.

zh: 想想日本和日本企业僵尸吧。
en: Think Japan, and its corporate zombies of the 1990’s.

zh: 正如他们造成了日本失去的十年，现在，他们的美国同道在对美国经济做同样的事情。
en: Just as they wrote the script for the first of Japan’s lost decades, their counterparts are now doing the same for the US economy.

zh: 两场泡沫 — — 地产泡沫和信用泡沫 — — 带来了十年的过度消费。
en: Two bubbles – property and credit – enabled a decade of excessive consumption.

zh: 2007年泡沫破裂以来，美国家庭可以理解地开始不懈地修正由此造成的伤害。
en: Since their collapse in 2007, US households have understandably become fixated on repairing the damage.

zh: 这意味着偿还债务、重建储蓄，让消费需求陷入持续萎靡一蹶不振。
en: That means paying down debt and rebuilding savings, leaving consumer demand mired in protracted weakness.

zh: 但针对这一病灶的疗法却让问题更加严重了。
en: Yet the treatment prescribed for this malady has compounded the problem.

zh: 尽管美联储一再否认，但它在把这病当周期性问题在治 — — 发动全部货币调整能力填补它所认为的总需求暂时性不足。
en: Steeped in denial, the Federal Reserve is treating the disease as a cyclical problem – deploying the full force of monetary accommodation to compensate for what it believes to be a temporary shortfall in aggregate demand.

zh: 这一战略背后的复杂逻辑相当令人不安 — — 不但对美国如此，对全球经济亦然。
en: The convoluted logic behind this strategy is quite disturbing – not only for the US, but also for the global economy.

zh: 没有哪个周期性问题可以造成五年的资产负债表衰退余震，就像美国所经历的那样。
en: There is nothing cyclical about the lasting aftershocks of a balance-sheet recession that have now been evident for nearly five years.

zh: 事实上，修复资产负债表对于美国家庭来说才刚刚开始。
en: Indeed, balance-sheet repair has barely begun for US households.

zh: 2012年个人储蓄率只有3.7 % ， 较2005年的1.5%的历史低点有所上升，但与20世纪最后三十年7.5%的平均水平相去甚远。
en: The personal-saving rate stood at just 3.7% in August 2012 – up from the 1.5% low of 2005, but half the 7.5% average recorded in the last three decades of the twentieth century.

zh: 此外，债务积压状况依然十分严重。
en: Moreover, the debt overhang remains massive.

zh: 2012年年中，家庭负债总水平是可支配收入的113 % ， 较2007年危机前的峰值水平134%下降了21个百分点，但仍远高于1970—1999年间的正常水平75 % 。
en: The overall level of household indebtedness stood at 113% of disposable personal income in mid-2012 – down 21 percentage points from its pre-crisis peak of 134% in 2007, but still well above the 1970-1999 norm of around 75%.

zh: 换句话说，美国人在修复资产负债表的道路上还有极长的距离要走，这表明当前问题绝不是暂时性或周期性的消费需求短缺问题。
en: In other words, Americans have much farther to go on the road to balance-sheet repair – which hardly suggests a temporary, or cyclical, shortfall in consumer demand.

zh: 此外，美联储的办法严重受制于所谓的零利率极限。
en: Moreover, the Fed’s approach is severely compromised by the so-called zero bound on interest rates.

zh: 降息空间用完后，美联储不得不转向信用周期的量化手段 — — 给僵尸消费者已经崩溃的经脉注入大规模流动性。
en: Having run out of basis points to cut from interest rates, the Fed has turned to the quantity dimension of the credit cycle – injecting massive doses of liquidity into the collapsed veins of zombie consumers.

zh: 为了论证这一办法的功效，美联储还写了自由裁量货币政策转换机制的脚本。
en: To rationalize the efficacy of this approach, the Fed has rewritten the script on the transmission mechanism of discretionary monetary policy.

zh: 从前，降低信用价格就可以刺激借贷，但今时不同往日，刺激资产和信用市场的重任得由“量化宽松”来完成。
en: Unlike the days of yore, when cutting the price of credit could boost borrowing, “quantitative easing” purportedly works by stimulating asset and credit markets.

zh: 接着，金融市场牛市所产生的财富效应应该能够��醒长期沉睡的“动物精神 ” ， 让消费者不顾依然困扰自己的资产负债表约束重新开始花钱。
en: The wealth effects generated by frothy financial markets are then presumed to rejuvenate long-dormant “animal spirits” and get consumers spending again, irrespective of lingering balance-sheet strains.

zh: 这还没完：根据美联储的观点，只要需求问题解决了，公司就会重新开始招聘。
en: There is more: Once the demand problem is cured, according to this argument, companies will start hiring again.

zh: 到那时，大功就告成了 — — 非常规疗法魔法般地满足了美联储长期以来忽略的指导抗击失业的重任。
en: And then, presto – an unconventional fix magically satisfies the Fed’s long-neglected mandate to fight unemployment.

zh: 但美联储的政策算盘把美国引上了错误的道路。
en: But the Fed’s policy gambit has taken the US down the wrong road.

zh: 事实上，美联储的做法无异于制造更大的依赖于资产和信用的疯狂消费模式 — — 这正是2003—2006年将美国经济推向深渊的错误。
en: Indeed, the Fed has doubled down on an approach aimed at recreating the madness of an asset- and credit-dependent consumption model – precisely the mistake that pushed the US economy toward the abyss in 2003-2006.

zh: 前两轮量化宽松都没有加速美国家庭资产负债表的修复速度，因此，没有理由相信“QE3”会奏效。
en: Just as two previous rounds of quantitative easing failed to accelerate US households’ balance-sheet repair, there is little reason to believe that “QE3” will do the trick.

zh: 说得再好，量化宽松充其量也只是个钝器，其传递渠道迂回曲折，而且颇可质疑。
en: Quantitative easing is a blunt instrument, at best, and operates through highly circuitous – and thus dubious – channels.

zh: 特别是，对于负债过度和储蓄不足这一孪生问题，它根本没有疗效。
en: Significantly, it does next to nothing to alleviate the twin problems of excess leverage and inadequate saving.

zh: 直接以债务豁免和强化储蓄激励为目标的政策 — — 平心而论，这样说可能会引起争议 — — 至少能够修正僵尸消费者的一部分资产负债表问题。
en: Policies aimed directly at debt forgiveness and enhanced saving incentives – contentious, to be sure – would at least address zombie consumers’ balance-sheet problems.

zh: 此外，量化宽松的副作用很大。
en: Moreover, the side effects of quantitative easing are significant.

zh: 不过，在全球经济萎靡不振的情况下，许多人所担心的通胀大爆发并延续多年的情景并不在我的预料名单中。
en: Many worry about an upsurge in inflation, though, given the outsize slack in the global economy – and the likelihood that it will persist for years to come – that is not high on my watch list.

zh: 比通胀问题危险得多的是主要央行 — — 不只包括美联储，也包括欧洲央行、英格兰银行和日本银行 — — 准备向资产市场注入巨量过剩流动性，远超停滞不前的实体经济所能吸收的程度。
en: Far more disconcerting is the willingness of major central banks – not just the Fed, but also the European Central Bank, the Bank of England, and the Bank of Japan – to inject massive amounts of excess liquidity into asset markets – excesses that cannot be absorbed by sluggish real economies.

zh: 这样做会让央行地位不稳，丢掉对未来金融市场的控制权。
en: That puts central banks in the destabilizing position of abdicating control over financial markets.

zh: 在世界正被地方性金融不稳定困扰的时候，这将是最危险的情景。
en: For a world beset by seemingly endemic financial instability, this could prove to be the most destructive development of all.

zh: 发展中世界正在竭力反对主要央行的鲁莽策略。
en: The developing world is up in arms over the major central banks’ reckless tactics.

zh: 新兴国家领导人担心商品市场的溢出效应、汇率的扭曲，以及干扰他们对金融稳定性专注度的资本流动。
en: Emerging economies’ leaders fear spillover effects in commodity markets and distortions of exchange rates and capital flows that may compromise their own focus on financial stability.

zh: 尽管追踪所谓发达国家的量化宽松所引起的跨境资本流十分困难，但这些担忧绝不是杞人忧天。
en: While it is difficult to track the cross-border flows fueled by quantitative easing in the so-called advanced world, these fears are far from groundless. Liquidity injections into a zero-interest-rate developed world send return-starved investors scrambling for growth opportunities elsewhere.

zh: 近几年来，全球经济在一个又一个危机中挣扎，药方本身也成了病源的一部分。
en: As the global economy has gone from crisis to crisis in recent years, the cure has become part of the disease.

zh: 在零利率和量化宽松的时代，危机后的现实令宏观经济政策精神错乱。
en: In an era of zero interest rates and quantitative easing, macroeconomic policy has become unhinged from a tough post-crisis reality.

zh: 未受检验的药方被用于在了错误的小病上，而病人的心腹大患却一直被忽视了。
en: Untested medicine is being used to treat the wrong ailment – and the chronically ill patient continues to be neglected.

zh: 美联储逃离纽约
en: The Federal Reserve’s Escape from New York

zh: 华盛顿—美国联邦储备体系是世界上最重要的中央银行。
en: WASHINGTON, DC – The US Federal Reserve System is the world’s most important central bank.

zh: 它的利率和金融监管决定会影响全球市场和数百万人的生活。
en: Its decisions about interest rates and financial regulation reverberate through global markets and affect millions of lives.

zh: 但它的治理结构早已不合时宜 — — 陈腐不堪、问题日益严重、急需明智改革。
en: Yet its governance structure is of another age – antiquated, increasingly problematic, and urgently in need of sensible reform.

zh: 美联储在2007—2008年全球经济危机酝酿阶段犯下了严重错误，其中最显著的便是对重要金融机构的监督采取了“松”政策以及坐视一些巨型银行变得极为脆弱。
en: The Fed made major mistakes in the run-up to the global economic crisis of 2007-08, most notably by adopting a lax approach to the supervision of key financial institutions, and by allowing some very large banks to become extremely fragile.

zh: 现代美国政治的一个巨大讽刺便是危机后的2010年多德-弗兰克（Dodd-Frank）金融改革实际上给了美联储更大的权力，这主要是因为其他美国监管机构被认为做得比美联储还要糟糕。
en: In one of the great ironies of modern American politics, the post-crisis Dodd-Frank financial reforms of 2010 actually gave more power to the Fed, mostly because other US regulatory agencies were regarded as having done a worse job.

zh: 自多德-弗兰克改革以来，美联储的历史记录表现出明显的分化，一些官员显然认为这一国会的违约是让一切回归常态的指令。
en: In view of the Fed’s decidedly mixed track record since the Dodd-Frank reforms, some officials evidently regarded that default by Congress as a mandate to conduct business as usual.

zh: 最新新闻报道着重于监督方面的不足，特别是纽约联邦储备银行内部和周边的不足。 纽约联储银行是美联储体系12家地区银行之一，它在华盛顿也有一个理事会。
en: Recent press reports have highlighted lapses in supervision, particularly in and around the Federal Reserve Bank of New York – one of 12 regional banks in the Fed System, which also has a Board of Governors in Washington, DC.

zh: 这一地区结构是1913年美联储成立以及20世纪30年代起治理结构最后一次修订时立法妥协的结果。
en: This regional structure is the result of legislative compromise in 1913, when the Fed was created, and again in the mid-1930s, when its governance was last overhauled.

zh: 美联储的华盛顿理事会由美国总统提名并需经过参议院确认，但地区联储银行行长是由当地委员会任命的。
en: Whereas members of the Fed’s Washington-based Board of Governors are nominated by the US president, subject to Senate confirmation, the presidents of the regional Federal Reserve banks are appointed by local boards.

zh: 在现实中，纽约联储可谓炙手可热；并非所有地区美联储行长都是平等的。
en: In reality, the New York Fed has always had disproportionate sway; not all regional Fed presidents are created equal.

zh: 纽约联储行长拥有联邦公开市场委员会永久投票资格并自动成为副主席；而其他地区联储行长只能轮流拥有投票权。
en: The president of the New York Fed is a permanent voting member and vice chairman of the Federal Open Market Committee, which sets interest rates, whereas other regional Fed presidents are voting members only on a rotating basis.

zh: 纽约联储在银行监督方面也扮演着特别重要的角色 — — 大部分“太大而不能倒”的银行位于其管辖区中（大部分全球银行也在这片地区设有分支 ） 。
en: The New York Fed also has a particularly important role in bank supervision – most of America’s “too big to fail” banks are located in its jurisdiction (and most global banks have a presence there).

zh: 纽约联储也一直是美联储体系在华尔街的耳目。
en: And the New York Fed has long been the Fed System’s eyes and ears on Wall Street.

zh: 或许反着说才对。
en: Or perhaps it has become the other way around.

zh: 至少在过去十年中，纽约联储官员一直站在巨型银行利益一边。
en: At least over the past decade, senior New York Fed officials have consistently sided with the interests of very large banks.

zh: （声明，我也知道许多美联储官员是杰出的公务员 ） 。
en: (To be clear, I also know many Fed officials who are outstanding public servants).

zh: 尽管华尔街利益已占据纽约联储理事会相当大的部分，但在其2003—2009年主席蒂莫西·盖特纳（Timothy Geithner）的领导下，大银行权力变得更大了 — — 也给我们其他人带来了不幸的后果。
en: Though Wall Street interests have long been well represented on the board of the New York Fed, under Timothy Geithner, its president from 2003 to 2009, the big players became even more powerful – with some rather unfortunate consequences for the rest of us.

zh: 在其最新的回忆录《压力测试 》 （ Stress Test）中，盖特纳说 ： “ 我基本上重建了纽约联储理事会，让其回归了地方金融系统精英俱乐部的历史根源。
en: In his recent memoir, Stress Test, Geithner says, “I basically restored the New York Fed board to its historic roots as an elite roster of the local financial establishment.”

zh: ”他的选择包括迪克·福尔德（Dick Fuld，在2008年9月轰然倒闭的雷曼兄弟公司CEO）和史蒂芬·弗里德曼（Stephen Friedman，高盛董事会成员，在金融危机期间被控不当交易高盛股票，因此辞去了纽约联储理事会主席之职 ） 。
en: His choices included Dick Fuld, CEO of Lehman Brothers, which failed spectacularly in September 2008, and Stephen Friedman, a Goldman Sachs board member, who resigned as chair of the New York Fed’s board after being accused of inappropriately trading Goldman stock during the financial crisis.

zh: 盖特纳还建立了一个纽约联储和摩根大通之间的复杂网络，其中一部分至今仍然存在。
en: Geithner also established a tangled web of connections between the New York Fed and JPMorgan Chase, some of which linger to this day.

zh: 一些美联储高级官员在阐述这一现实时十分愤怒。
en: Some senior Fed officials become angry when pressed about this reality.

zh: 但美联储的合法性 — — 以及其做出明智决策的能力 — — 并没有因为让大银行获得遴选和监督重要决策者的理事会席位而直接或间接地得到增强。
en: But the Fed’s legitimacy – and its ability to make sensible policy – is not boosted by having major banks represented, directly or indirectly, on a board that chooses and oversees a key policymaker.

zh: 如今，美国左翼和右翼政客终于开始将注意力集中到长期缺失的美联储治��改革上了。
en: Now, finally, US politicians on both the left and the right are focusing their attention on a long-overdue reform of the Fed’s governance.

zh: 一个重要提案来自罗德岛民主党参议员杰克·里德（Jack Reed ） ， 他十分合理地提出，纽约联储行长应该由总统提名并由参议院确认，与其他理事会成员（或任何其他重要的经济决策者）一样。
en: One important proposal comes from Senator Jack Reed, a Democrat from Rhode Island, who proposes, quite reasonably, that the president of the New York Fed should be nominated by the president and confirmed by the Senate, just like members of the Board of Governors – or any other important economic policymaker.

zh: 纽约联储行长也应该需要定期在国会面前听证。
en: The president of the New York Fed would also be required to testify before Congress on a regular basis.

zh: 美联储的捍卫者会如此回应：改变现状是危险的。
en: The Fed’s defenders will respond that it would be dangerous to alter the status quo.

zh: 但如今变得危险的是美联储的现有治理结构。
en: But it is the Fed’s current governance that has become dangerous.

zh: 马萨诸塞州参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦（Elizabeth Warren）和西弗吉尼亚州参议员乔·曼勤（Joe Manchin）令人十分信服地指出，美联储理事会的构成应该将与华尔街大公司有关联的人剔除。
en: Senators Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Joe Manchin of West Virginia argue, entirely convincingly, that the composition of the Fed’s Board of Governors should be tilted away from people who are connected with big Wall Street firms.

zh: 与此同时，众议院正在准备其自身的美联储治理改革方案 — — 这一方案将更加激进，有可能不明智地约束货币政策。
en: Meanwhile, House Republicans are preparing their own Fed governance reforms, which would be even more radical – and would likely constrain monetary policy unwisely.

zh: 无论如何，美联储应该发生改变。
en: In any case, it is time for change at the Fed.

zh: 正如金融界通常的情况，起点就在华尔街。
en: And, as is often the case with finance, the place to start is New York.

zh: 美联储下注剩余劳动力
en: The Fed’s Gamble on Surplus Labor

zh: 伦敦—最近几周，美联储采取了更加渐进的政策正常化方针，这提振了市场。
en: LONDON – In recent weeks, the US Federal Reserve has buoyed markets by adopting a more gradual approach to policy normalization.

zh: 美联储主席耶伦3月底的最新公开讲话比预期更加“鸽派 ” 。
en: Fed Chair Janet Yellen’s most recent public remarks, in late March, were more dovish than anticipated.

zh: 此外，在上一次会议上，美联储表示将在2016年实施两次而不是四次四分之一个百分点的升息。
en: And, at its last meeting, the Fed suggested that it would pursue two, rather than four, quarter-point interest-rate hikes in 2016.

zh: 结果是投资者出售美元，买入提振股价和美国国债，大宗商品和新兴市场资产也大幅上扬。
en: In response, investors have sold the US dollar and bid up equity prices and US Treasuries, and commodities and emerging-market assets have surged.

zh: 乍一看，这些情况相当有趣。
en: At first glance, these developments are curious.

zh: 一方面，美联储的决定似乎与美国通胀正在加速的信号相悖。
en: For one thing, the Fed’s decision appears to be at odds with signs that US inflation is accelerating.

zh: 如果如一些人所认为的那样，美联储是在应对全球增长担忧，那么风险资产 — — 首先是大宗商品和新兴市场 — — 反弹就没有依据。
en: If, as some have suggested, the Fed is responding to fears about global growth, it would not make sense that risk assets – above all commodities and emerging markets – are rallying.

zh: 但有一个逻辑线条可以解释这些显而易见的不一致，其核心是一个潜在后果巨大的美联储赌注。
en: But there is a logical thread that explains these apparent inconsistencies, one that centers on a potentially high-stakes Fed gamble.

zh: 在审视这一赌注之前，不妨考虑以下对市场反弹的其他解释。
en: Before we get to that wager, it is worth considering other proposed explanations for the market rally.

zh: 第一种解释的核心是欧洲央行和日本银行的货币宽松。
en: The first centers on monetary easing by the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan.

zh: 但负利率和平坦收益率曲线伤害了银行利润；反常货币政策与增长或通胀之间的联系仍然模糊；并且显然如今货币政策的回报已在逐渐下降。
en: But negative interest rates and flat yield curves harm banks’ earnings; links between extraordinary monetary policies and growth or inflation remain tenuous; and surely monetary policy is subject to diminishing returns by now.

zh: 另一个观点聚焦于欧佩克国家的石油供给减少，认为这有助于支持石油价格，从而支持北美高成本生产商。
en: Another view focuses on OPEC countries’ oil-supply restraint, claiming that it is helping to support oil prices and thus high-cost producers in North America.

zh: 但这一逻辑与其说是因果关系，不如说是相关关系。
en: But this logic rests more on correlation than causation.

zh: 欧佩克尚未决定减产，并且只有少数成员国同意冻结产出。
en: OPEC has not decided to cut production, and only a handful of its members have agreed to freeze output.

zh: 全球过剩供给的真正下降要等到产出下降，而产出下降要等到现有油井因为资本投资不足而干涸。
en: A genuine reduction in global excess supply awaits a decline in output, as existing wells, deprived of capital investment, run dry.

zh: 对市场表现改善的更有道理的解释是悲观心理的消失。
en: A more plausible explanation for improved market performance is waning pessimism.

zh: 对美国、英国或德国衰退的恐慌 — — 这些国家就业充分，真实家庭收入也在增加 — — 总是有些不合常理。
en: Fears of recession in the United States, the United Kingdom, or Germany – countries with full employment and rising real household incomes – were always a bit odd.

zh: 金融市场轮转将产生大幅遏制家庭或公司支出的非典型影响的概念也不合常理。
en: So was the notion that financial-market gyrations would have the atypical impact of significantly denting household or corporate spending.

zh: 而在中国 — — 它可能正在经历GDP增长放缓，但距离衰退还十分遥远 — — 家庭收入和消费的增加正在帮助抵消固定资产下降的影响。
en: And in China – a country that may be experiencing slowing GDP growth, but is nowhere near recession – rising household income and consumption are helping to offset the decline in fixed-asset investment.

zh: 这就让我们回到美联储和它的赌注上。
en: This brings us back to the Fed and its gamble.

zh: 决策者看法的改变可能来自对美国经济弱势的反思，也别是美国劳动力市场。
en: Policymakers’ change of heart likely arose from a re-think about slack in the US economy, especially in the labor market.

zh: 事实上，在其最近的讲话中，耶伦指出劳动力参与率“上升 ” ， “改进空间”仍然存在。
en: Indeed, in her recent remarks, Yellen noted that the labor-force participation rate had “turned up” and that “room for improvement” remained.

zh: 如果现在美联储认为经济具备了更大的不引起剧烈通胀的超趋势扩张容量，那么，用约翰·列侬（John Lennon）的话说，可以“给增长一个机会 ” 。
en: If the Fed now believes that the economy has greater capacity for above-trend expansion without generating much inflation, it can, to paraphrase John Lennon, “give growth a chance.”

zh: 加速增长和放缓政策收紧对资产价格来说是好消息。
en: Faster growth and slower policy tightening are great news for asset prices.

zh: 更加温和的美联储也意味着美元升值风险降低 — — 毫无疑问，这对于大宗商品市场和负有美元债务的新兴经济体来说是好消息。
en: A gentler Fed also means less risk of dollar appreciation – an unambiguous benefit for commodity markets and dollar-indebted emerging economies.

zh: 最后，稳定的美元减轻人民币压力，从而放缓“热”资本流出中国的势头，消除全球金融体系的另一个风险源。
en: Finally, a stable dollar takes pressure off the renminbi, which should slow outflows of “hot” capital from China, removing another source of risk from the global financial system.

zh: 考虑到这些影响，毫不奇怪市场会上扬。
en: Given these implication, it is little wonder that markets turned up.

zh: 但随着美国核心通胀率的上升，美联储正在冒一个很大的险。
en: But with US core inflation on the rise, the Fed is taking a big risk.

zh: 毕竟，核心消费物价指数已经达到了2.3 % ， 原因是服务价格上升了3.1 % （ 两个数字同比均增加1.5个百分点以上 ） 。
en: After all, the core consumer-price index is already at 2.3%, led by 3.1% inflation in services (both figures are up by more than half of a percentage point year on year).

zh: 占消费物价指数四分之一权重的住房通胀也加速至3.2 % 。
en: Housing inflation, which comprises about a quarter of the CPI index, has also accelerated, to 3.2%.

zh: 而最近几年有所放缓的医疗服务价格涨幅升高到3.9 % ， 比一年前扩大了一倍。
en: And price growth in health-care services, which had slowed in recent years, has jumped to 3.9%, double the rate recorded a year ago.

zh: 美联储喜欢关注核心“私人消费支出”通胀，该数字较低，为1.7 % 。
en: The Fed prefers to watch core “private consumption expenditure” inflation, which stands at a more subdued 1.7%.

zh: 私人消费支出商品价格仍在下跌，而服务价��涨幅只有2.1 % ， 与过去一年基本持平。
en: PCE goods prices are still falling, and services prices are rising just 2.1%, roughly unchanged over the past year.

zh: 但美联储的焦点是劳动力市场。
en: But the focal point for the Fed is the labor market.

zh: 据3月份的报告，公民参与率较2015年9月的低位增加了1.5个百分点，目前为63 % 。
en: According to a March report, the civilian participation rate has increased by half a percentage point from its September 2015 lows, and now stands at 63%.

zh: 同一份报告显示，近六百万目前身处劳动力大军之外的美国人想要工作。
en: The same survey indicates that nearly six million Americans, who are not currently in the labor force, want to work.

zh: 还有六百万因为经济原因而从事兼职工作。
en: Another six million are working part-time for economic reasons.

zh: 从某种意义上说，美国劳动力参与水平低下反映了结构因素。
en: In part, low levels of US labor-force participation reflect structural factors.

zh: 2000年以来，美国的几乎所有子分类 — — 如性别、教育水平、年龄段或种族 — — 都在下降。
en: Nearly every sub-category – by gender, education level, age cohort, or race – has been declining in the US since 2000.

zh: 但劳动力供给通常也呈现周期性，随着经济改善、就业机会的增加而增加。
en: Yet labor supply is typically also cyclical, picking up as the economy improves and job opportunities arise.

zh: 到目前为止，这一周期模式尚未体现在危机后“新常态”中。
en: Until now, that cyclical pattern has been absent in the post-crisis “new normal.”

zh: 弹性日益增加的劳动力供给对美联储政策意味着什么？
en: What might an increasingly elastic labor supply mean for Fed policy?

zh: 答案取决于有多少剩余劳动力可用。
en: The answer depends on how much surplus labor is available.

zh: 假设剩余劳动力为150万 — — 这个数字较为保守，民用就业-人口比例仍远低于战后峰值 — 。
en: Suppose it is 1.5 million workers – a conservative figure that would still leave the civilian employment-to-population ratio well below its post-war peak.

zh: 按照可信的美国就业创造速度，将需要12—18个月时间吸收这些新来者。
en: At plausible rates of US job creation, it would take 12-18 months to absorb those new entrants.

zh: 这一劳动力的大量涌入将压低工资和物价压力，让美联储逐步实现利率正常化。
en: That labor influx would dampen wage and price pressures, allowing the Fed to proceed gradually with interest-rate normalization.

zh: 可用劳动力储备越大，美联储可以放缓利率正常化的时间越长。
en: The bigger the pool of available labor, the longer the Fed can go slow.

zh: 这让人想起了美联储前主席艾伦·格林斯潘在20世纪90年代的实验，他直觉地认为 — — 最后证明是正确的 — — 生产率正在加速，因此放任美国经济繁荣。
en: This recalls former Fed Chair Alan Greenspan’s experiment in the late 1990s, when he let the US economy boom, on the hunch – which proved to be right – that productivity was accelerating.

zh: 耶伦也许也想在劳动力供给上下类似的赌注？
en: Might Yellen be willing to make a similar wager on labor supply?

zh: 目前，民粹主义不满的政治 — — 从唐纳德·特朗普的总统选战到英国可能退出欧盟 — — 正在吸引全世界的关注。
en: For now, the politics of populist discontent – from Donald Trump’s presidential campaign to the potential of a British exit from the European Union – are capturing the world’s attention.

zh: 但美国就业和通胀报告才是未来线索的真正来源。
en: But the US employment and inflation reports are the real sources of clues about the future.

zh: 你可以在这里找到最有可能驱动最大赌注 — — 不管是政策还是市场 — — 的因素
en: It is there that one should look for the factors most likely to drive the biggest wagers – for policy and for markets alike.

zh: 美联储与价格稳定
en: The Fed Versus Price Stability

zh: 旧金山—美联储维持“物价稳定”的使命（由联邦储备法明文规定）和美联储自己选择的2%通胀目标之间有一个极大的不同点。
en: SAN FRANCISCO – There is a big difference between the Federal Reserve’s mandate to maintain “stable prices” – as enunciated in the Federal Reserve Act – and the Fed’s self-selected target of 2% annual inflation.

zh: 那么，决策者为何用后者代替前者呢？
en: So how is it that policymakers have managed to substitute the latter for the former?

zh: “物价稳定”一词顾名思义是指一揽子商品今后十年、50年甚至100年价格都不会变。
en: The term “stable prices” is self-explanatory: a bundle of goods will cost the same ten, 50, or even 100 years from now.

zh: 相反，如果一国以每年2%的通胀度过十年吗，那么今天100美元可以买到的东西，十年好需要花122美元购买。
en: By contrast, if a country experiences 2% inflation over a ten-year period, the same items that $100 can buy today will cost $122 at the end of the decade.

zh: 100年后，价格标签将变成724美元。
en: After 100 years, the price tag will be a whopping $724.

zh: 在最新的国会听证中，美联储主席耶伦数次提到保持“物价稳定”的使命，但提到美联储2%的通胀目标的次数是前者的两倍。
en: In her recent Congressional testimony, Fed Chair Janet Yellen referred several times to the mandate of maintaining “stable prices”; but she mentioned the Fed’s 2% inflation objective twice as often.

zh: “美国通胀仍低于委员会2%的目标 ， ” 她说，当前的“高度政策协调仍然有利于刺激劳动力市场条件进一步改善、促使通胀在中期回到2 % 。 ”
en: “US inflation continues to run below the Committee’s 2% objective,” she said, and the current “high degree of policy accommodation remains appropriate to foster further improvement in labor market conditions and to promote a return of inflation toward 2% over the medium term.”

zh: 美联储真的想让年通胀率增加到2 % ， 即让美国物价水平在未来一百年中上涨700%多吗？
en: Does the Fed really want to increase annual inflation to 2%, such that the price level of the country will increase by more than 700% over the next century?

zh: 这就是国会在授予美联储实现“物价稳定”目标的任务时所想的吗？
en: Is that what Congress had in mind when it tasked the Fed with achieving “stable prices”?

zh: 美联储前主席格林斯潘（Alan Greenspan）知道，答案是否定的。
en: Former Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan knew that it did not.

zh: 1996年7月2日，在联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC，该委员会通过广泛讨论为美联储确定合适的通胀目标）会议上提出了一个简单的问题 ： “ 我们是在讨论物价稳定，还是在讨论零通胀？
en: On July 2, 1996, at a meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), which was devoted to extensive discussion of the appropriate inflation target for the Fed, Greenspan posed a simple question: “Are we talking about price stability or are we talking about zero inflation?” he asked.

zh: ”他说 ， “ 我们都知道这是两个不同的东西。 ”
en: “As we all know, those are two separate things.”

zh: 讨论很快转向了准确衡量通胀的困难性和建立避免通缩的“安全缓冲”的必要性。
en: The discussion quickly turned to the difficulty of measuring inflation accurately and the need to build in a “safety cushion” to avoid deflation.

zh: 根据格林斯潘的说法 ， “ 物价稳定是一种状态，在这种状态下，总体物价水平的预期变化不会有效改变企业和家庭决策。
en: According to Greenspan, “Price stability is that state in which expected changes in the general price level do not effectively alter business and household decisions.”

zh: ”当时还是美联储理事的耶伦对此并不满足 ： “ 您可以具体说一个数字吗？ ”她问。
en: Yellen, then a Fed governor, was not satisfied: “Could you please put a number on that?” she asked.

zh: 格林斯潘满足了她 ： “ 我得说这个数字是零，如果通胀可以合理衡量的话。 ”他回答说。
en: Greenspan did: “I would say that number is zero, if inflation is properly measured,” he replied.

zh: 那次FOMC会议举行时，消费者物价指数正在以每年约3%的速度增加。
en: At the time of that FOMC meeting, the consumer price index was increasing at about 3% per year.

zh: 大部分讨论集中在美联储是否应该将年物价增长减缓至2%甚至更低，以巩固过去15年中决策者苦苦缠斗通胀所取得的战果。
en: Most of the discussion focused on whether the Fed should slow annual price growth to 2% or even lower, thereby consolidating the gains made in the difficult fight against inflation that policymakers had waged for the previous 15 years.

zh: 格林斯潘总结陈词 ： “ … … 现在，我们全体同意2 % … … ”
en: Greenspan summarized the consensus: “...we have now all agreed on 2%...”

zh: 于是，美联储的2%通胀目标就这样诞生了。
en: Thus, the Fed’s 2% inflation objective was born.

zh: 在随后的讨论中，一些FOMC成员认为通胀率应该调低至2%以下，但没有人认为如果通胀比这更低（但仍然为正）的话应该让通胀增加一点。
en: During the ensuing discussion, several FOMC members argued that the inflation rate might be reduced to less than 2%, but nobody argued that inflation should be pushed higher if a lower, but still positive, rate was achieved.

zh: 讨论结束后，格林斯潘要求FOMC成员们对关于通胀目标的讨论保密。
en: Following the discussion, Greenspan exhorted the FOMC members to keep the discussion of the inflation target secret.

zh: “我告诉你们，如果2%的通胀数字流出这个房间 ， ” 他警告说 ， “ 给我们造成的问题将超过你们的预期。
en: “I will tell you that if the 2% inflation figure gets out of this room,” he warned, “it is going to create more problems for us than I think any of you might anticipate.”

zh: ”这次会议的官方记录没有提到为期数小时的通胀目标的全部讨论过程，FOMC也从未正式宣布2%为其年通胀目标，直到2012年，耶伦的前任伯南克（Ben Bernanke）才将这一目标公之于众。
en: The official minutes of the meeting make no reference to the entire discussion of the inflation target, which took up several hours, and the FOMC never formally announced its 2% target for annual inflation until Chairman Ben Bernanke, Yellen’s predecessor, finally did so in 2012.

zh: 如今，2%的通胀目标已成为FOMC决策的最前沿。
en: The 2% inflation target now is at the forefront of FOMC decision-making.

zh: 比如，尽管2014年12月年通胀率为0.8 % ， 但2015年1月FOMC会议记录数次提到FOMC需要通过保持高度合适政策立场以 “接近就业最大化和2%的通胀目标 ” 。
en: For example, while annual inflation stood at 0.8% in December 2014, the minutes of the January 2015 FOMC meeting refer several times to the Committee’s need to make “progress toward its objectives of maximum employment and 2% inflation” by maintaining a highly accommodative policy stance.

zh: 增加通胀率如今已成为美联储政策的具体目标。
en: Increasing the rate of inflation is now the stated objective of Fed policy.

zh: 国会并未授权美联储追求这一目标。
en: Congress did not give the Fed a mandate to pursue that goal.

zh: 联邦储备法说的很明确：美联储应该为美国货币实现“物价稳定 ” ， 以及温和的利率和最大化的就业。
en: The Federal Reserve Act is explicit: the Fed should achieve “price stability” for the US currency, along with moderate interest rates and maximum employment.

zh: 只要通胀处于零和2%之间，美联储就应该认为自己是成功的，并采取放任不管的态度。
en: As long as inflation is somewhere between zero and 2%, the Fed should declare victory and leave it at that.

zh: 错误的央行战争
en: The Wrong War for Central Banking

zh: 北京—在一个没有通胀的世界以通胀目标为核心，这让央行迷失了方向。
en: BEIJING – Fixated on inflation targeting in a world without inflation, central banks have lost their way.

zh: 基准利率被锁定在骇人听闻的零区间，货币政策已经从物价稳定的代表转变成金融动荡的发动机。
en: With benchmark interest rates stuck at the dreaded zero bound, monetary policy has been transformed from an agent of price stability into an engine of financial instability.

zh: 我们急需新的方针。
en: A new approach is desperately needed.

zh: 美联储是这一政策两难的写照。
en: The US Federal Reserve exemplifies this policy dilemma.

zh: 9月，美联储公开市场委员会决定再次推迟人们翘首以待的货币政策正常化，而如今，其中的通胀鸽派仍在公开呼吁再次推迟。
en: After the Federal Open Market Committee decided in September to defer yet again the start of its long-awaited normalization of monetary policy, its inflation doves are openly campaigning for another delay.

zh: 对通胀目标孜孜以求的人来说，这一目标是无可挑剔的。
en: For the inflation-targeting purists, the argument seems impeccable.

zh: 标题消费物价指数（CPI）接近于零 ， “ 核心”或基础通胀 — — 美联储最喜欢用的指标 — — 仍显著低于堪称神圣的2%的目标。
en: The headline consumer-price index (CPI) is near zero, and “core” or underlying inflation – the Fed’s favorite indicator – remains significantly below the seemingly sacrosanct 2% target.

zh: 长期萎靡不振的复苏眼看就要再次夭折，鸽派认为没有理由急于提高利率。
en: With a long-anemic recovery looking shaky again, the doves contend that there is no reason to rush ahead with interest-rate hikes.

zh: 当然，事情没那么简单。
en: Of course, there is more to it than that.

zh: 货币政策操作存在时滞，因此央行必须避免只着眼于当下，而是要利用不完美的预测来推断它们的决策的未来影响。
en: Because monetary policy operates with lags, central banks must avoid fixating on the here and now, and instead use imperfect forecasts to anticipate the future effects of their decisions.

zh: 对美联储来说，美国即将接近充分就业这一前提导致了所谓的双重使命变成了单一目标：让通胀回到2 % 。
en: In the Fed’s case, the presumption that the US will soon approach full employment has caused the so-called dual mandate to collapse into one target: getting inflation back to 2%.

zh: 在这方面，美联储正在犯致命的错误，它严重依赖过时的通胀预测方法，该方法忽略推动食品和能源等商品价格时常剧烈波动的“特殊因素 ” 。
en: Here, the Fed is making a fatal mistake, as it relies heavily on a timeworn inflation-forecasting methodology that filters out the “special factors” driving the often volatile prices of goods like food and energy.

zh: 美联储的逻辑是，价格波动最终将抹平，标题物价指标将趋同于核心通胀率。
en: The logic is that the price fluctuations will eventually subside, and headline price indicators will converge on the core rate of inflation.

zh: 这一方针在20世纪70年代开始采用时就是一场彻头彻尾的失败，导致美联储低估了恶性通胀。
en: This approach failed spectacularly when it was adopted in the 1970s, causing the Fed to underestimate virulent inflation.

zh: 今天，它也是一场失败，导致美联储持续高估基础通胀。
en: And it is failing today, leading the Fed consistently to overestimate underlying inflation.

zh: 事实上，去年油价暴跌50 % ， 但美联储顽固地坚持认为物价上升加速 — — 以及2%这一神奇通胀率 — — 就在眼前。
en: Indeed, with oil prices having plunged by 50% over the past year, the Fed stubbornly maintains that faster price growth – and the precious inflation rate of 2% – is just around the corner.

zh: 这一逻辑的漏洞是没有认识到正在压制通胀的强大的全球性新力量。
en: Missing from this logic is an appreciation of the new and powerful global forces that are bearing down on inflation.

zh: 据国际货币基金组织（IMF）的最新展望，从现在到2020年，全体发达经济体的物价平减指数平均每年只上升1.5 % — —比过去六年饱受危机遏制的速度1.1%高不了多少。
en: According to the International Monetary Fund’s latest outlook, the price deflator for all advanced economies should increase by just 1.5% annually, on average, from now to 2020 – not much higher than the crisis-depressed 1.1% pace of the last six years.

zh: 此外，全球大部分批发物价指数仍陷在严重的通缩中。
en: Moreover, most wholesale prices around the world remain in outright deflation.

zh: 但是，美联储没有看到这些发展态势背后可能的驱动力 — — 即，在供给过剩和大量科技创新和新供应链带来的通缩效应下，全球总需求可能进入了长期萎靡 — — 而是继续致力于尽量降低全球力量的通缩效应。
en: But, rather than recognize the likely drivers of these developments – namely, a seemingly chronic shortfall of global aggregate demand amid a supply glut and a deflationary profusion of technological innovations and new supply chains – the Fed continues to minimize the deflationary impact of global forces.

zh: 它宁愿将低通胀归因于成功的通胀目标政策，以及很可能是因此形成的大稳健（Great Moderation ） 。
en: It would rather attribute low inflation to successful inflation targeting, and the Great Moderation that it presumably spawned.

zh: 这一骄傲的解释成为极度宽松的货币政策的引诱剂。
en: This prideful interpretation amounted to the siren song of an extremely accommodative monetary policy.

zh: 眼中只有物价目标的美联储无法理清遏制通胀的全球和国内压力，一直犯着宽松货币的错误。
en: Unable to disentangle the global and domestic pressures suppressing inflation, a price-targeting Fed has erred consistently on the side of easy money.

zh: 这明显地体现在一个事实中：过去15年来，真实联邦基金利率（美联储的基准政策利率，经通胀调整）在超过六成的时间里位于负区间，自2001年5月以来的平均水平为-0.6 % 。
en: This is apparent in the fact that, over the last 15 years, the real federal funds rate – the Fed’s benchmark policy rate, adjusted for inflation – has been in negative territory more than 60% of the time, averaging -0.6% since May 2001.

zh: 相反，1990—2000期间，真实联邦利率平均为2.2 % 。
en: From 1990 to 2000, by contrast, the real federal funds rate averaged 2.2%.

zh: 简言之，在过去十五年里，美联储通过其政策利率制造了强大的反通胀。
en: In short, over the last decade and a half, the Fed has gone well beyond a powerful disinflation in setting its policy interest rate.

zh: 其结果往好了说是值得商榷。
en: The consequences have been problematic, to say the least.

zh: 在这15年中，金融市场变得十分混乱，各种资产和信用泡沫导致了一系列危机，几乎在2008—2009年将世界经济推向万劫不复。
en: Over the same 15-year period, financial markets have become unhinged, with a profusion of asset and credit bubbles leading to a series of crises that almost pushed the world economy into the abyss in 2008-2009.

zh: 但美联储并没有认识到危机前的过度情况，更不用说采取应对措施了，它一只持有不可知论，认为识别泡沫充其量只是不完美的科学。
en: But rather than recognize, let alone respond to, pre-crisis excesses, the Fed has remained agnostic about them, pointing out that bubble-spotting is, at best, an imperfect science.

zh: 这绝不是央行继续坚持通胀目标令人信服的理由。
en: That is hardly a convincing reason for central banks to remain fixated on inflation targeting.

zh: 它们不但一再无法正确预测通胀；如今还有可能助长卷土重来的金融动荡、引发另一场危机。
en: Not only have they failed repeatedly to get the inflation forecast right; they now risk fueling renewed financial instability and sparking another crisis.

zh: 正如我们少数人在2003—2006年期间发出的危机迫在眉睫的警告，一些人 — — 包括国际清算银行和IMF — — 今天也在大声疾呼，但没有人听他们的。
en: Just as a few of us warned of impending crisis in the 2003-2006 period, some – including the Bank of International Settlements and the IMF– are sounding the alarm today, but to no avail.

zh: 诚然，通胀目标曾经对于遏制物价增长失控至关重要。
en: To be sure, inflation targeting was once essential to limit runaway price growth.

zh: 但是，在今天无通胀的环境下，它只能适得其反。
en: In today’s inflationless world, however, it is counterproductive.

zh: 但主宰当今主要央行的通胀目标派坚持要继续打昨天的战争。
en: Yet the inflation targeters who dominate today’s major central banks insist on fighting yesterday’s war.

zh: 从这个角度讲，现代央行官员与1942年新加坡战役中的英军十分相似。
en: In this sense, modern central bankers resemble the British army in the Battle of Singapore in 1942.

zh: 当时，英国算定日本只能从海上发动袭击，建造了无法突破的混凝土掩体和只能朝南开火的炮台。
en: Convinced that the Japanese would attack from the sea, the British defenses were encased in impenetrable concrete bunkers, with fixed artillery that could fire only to the south.

zh: 因此，当日本人穿过马来半岛的热带雨林和红树林沼泽，从北面出现时，英国人毫无还手之力。
en: So when the Japanese emerged from the jungle and mangrove swamps of the Malay Peninsula in the north, the British were powerless to stop them.

zh: 新加坡很快就沦陷了，至今仍被广泛视为丘吉尔首相最难堪的军事失败。
en: Singapore quickly fell, in what is widely considered Prime Minister Winston Churchill’s most ignominious military defeat.

zh: 央行官员就像是新加坡的英军，将火炮对准了错误的方向。
en: Central bankers, like the British army in Singapore, are aiming their weapons in the wrong direction.

zh: 他们应该改变政策军火库，让它们对准今天的敌人：金融动荡。
en: It is time for them to turn their policy arsenal toward today’s enemy: financial instability.

zh: 光凭这一点，货币政策正常化就是一个十分紧迫的任务。
en: On that basis alone, the case for monetary-policy normalization has never been more compelling.

zh: 美联储升息后的新兴市场
en: Emerging Markets After the Fed Hikes Rates

zh: 纽约—美联储将于今年晚些时候开始退出零利率政策，这一前景让人们日益担心新兴经济体货币、债券和股市波动将卷土重来。
en: NEW YORK – The prospect that the US Federal Reserve will start exiting zero policy rates later this year has fueled growing fear of renewed volatility in emerging economies’ currency, bond, and stock markets.

zh: 这一担心不难理解：2013年美联储放出信号表示即将结束量化宽松政策时，由此到来的“缩减恐慌 ” （ taper tantrum）在诸多新兴国家金融市场和经济中引起余震。
en: The concern is understandable: When the Fed signaled in 2013 that the end of its quantitative-easing (QE) policy was forthcoming, the resulting “taper tantrum” sent shock waves through many emerging countries’ financial markets and economies.

zh: 事实上，人们担心，美国利率的上升以及美元价值的继续上升可能重创新兴市场政府、金融机构、公司甚至家庭。
en: Indeed, rising interest rates in the United States and the ensuing likely rise in the value of the dollar could, it is feared, wreak havoc among emerging markets’ governments, financial institutions, corporations, and even households.

zh: 在过去几年中，所有这些部门借入了数以万亿计的美元，如今，它们将面临债务实际本币价值的上升，而与此同时，美国利率的升高将进一步推高新兴市场国内利率，从而进一步增加债务维持负担。
en: Because all have borrowed trillions of dollars in the last few years, they will now face an increase in the real local-currency value of these debts, while rising US rates will push emerging markets’ domestic interest rates higher, thus increasing debt-service costs further.

zh: 但是，尽管美联储升息的前景可能造成新兴国家金融市场的剧烈动荡，但爆发全面危机和灾难的风险比较有限。
en: But, although the prospect of the Fed raising interest rates is likely to create significant turbulence in emerging countries’ financial markets, the risk of outright crises and distress is more limited.

zh: 首先，2013年的削减恐慌让市场措手不及，但美联储在今年升息的意图已经明确表态了好几个月，不会再让市场措手不及。
en: For starters, whereas the 2013 taper tantrum caught markets by surprise, the Fed’s intention to hike rates this year, clearly stated over many months, will not.

zh: 此外，美联储升息时机和节奏可能会比此前几个周期更晚更慢，采取逐步响应的方式，以符合美国经济增长之稳健足以维持更高的借贷成本的信号。
en: Moreover, the Fed is likely to start raising rates later and more slowly than in previous cycles, responding gradually to signs that US economic growth is robust enough to sustain higher borrowing costs.

zh: 更加强劲的增长将有益于向美国出口商品和服务的新兴市场。
en: This stronger growth will benefit emerging markets that export goods and services to the US.

zh: 另一个不必恐慌的理由是，2013年许多脆弱新兴经济体的政策利率很低，而如今，各国央行已经大大收紧了货币政策。
en: Another reason not to panic is that, compared to 2013, when policy rates were low in many fragile emerging economies, central banks already have tightened their monetary policy significantly.

zh: 许多新兴经济体政策利率接近或超过了两位数，当局不再像2013年那样滞后于美联储行动。
en: With policy rates at or close to double-digit levels in many of those economies, the authorities are not behind the curve the way they were in 2013.

zh: 宽松的财政和信用政策也已经有所收紧，降低了大规模经常项目和财政赤字。
en: Loose fiscal and credit policies have been tightened as well, reducing large current-account and fiscal deficits.

zh: 此外，2013年货币、股票、大宗商品和债券价格均处于过高状态，而如今大部分新兴市场都已出现修正走势，采取进一步调整以适应美联储动作的必要性不再那么强。
en: And, compared to 2013, when currencies, equities, commodity, and bond prices were too high, a correction has already occurred in most emerging markets, limiting the need for further major adjustment when the Fed moves.

zh: 最重要的是，如今大部分新兴经济体的金融状况要比十年或二十年前可靠得多。 当时，金融脆弱性导致了货币、银行和主权债务危机。
en: Above all, most emerging markets are financially more sound today than they were a decade or two ago, when financial fragilities led to currency, banking, and sovereign-debt crises.

zh: 而如今，大部分新兴经济体采取了浮动汇率，这意味着它们不会再轻易地受到盯住汇率崩溃的冲击；并且它们也拥有足够的储备以抵御本币、政府债务和银行存款挤兑。
en: Most now have flexible exchange rates, which leave them less vulnerable to a disruptive collapse of currency pegs, as well as ample reserves to shield them against a run on their currencies, government debt, and bank deposits.

zh: 大部分新兴经济体的美元债务/本币债务之比也低于十年前，这有助于遏制因为本币贬值导致的债务负担增加。
en: Most also have a relatively smaller share of dollar debt relative to local-currency debt than they did a decade ago, which will limit the increase in their debt burden when the currency depreciates.

zh: 它们的金融体系也往往更加稳固，比遭遇银行危机时拥有更多的资本和流动性。
en: Their financial systems are typically more sound as well, with more capital and liquidity than when they experienced banking crises.

zh: 此外，除了少数例外，大部分新兴经济体都不存在偿债能力问题；尽管近几年来公私债务迅速增加，但相对水平仍然较低。
en: And, with a few exceptions, most do not suffer from solvency problems; although private and public debts have been rising rapidly in recent years, they have done so from relatively low levels.

zh: 事实上，一些新兴经济体 — — 主要是受中国减速影响的石油和大宗商品生产国 — — 的严重金融问题与美联储的动作无关。
en: In fact, serious financial problems in several emerging economies – particularly oil and commodity producers exposed to the slowdown in China – are unrelated to what the Fed does.

zh: 将在今年出现衰退和高通胀的把戏在美联储启动量化宽松和停止量化宽松时都怨声载道��它的问题大部分是自我造成的 — — 是总统罗塞夫在第一个任期中采取了宽松的货币、财政和信用政策的结果，这三大政策如今都必须收紧。
en: Brazil, which will experience recession and high inflation this year, complained when the Fed launched QE and then when it stopped QE. Its problems are mostly self-inflicted – the result of loose monetary, fiscal, and credit policies, all of which must now be tightened, during President Dilma Roussef’s first administration.

zh: 俄罗斯的麻烦也与美联储政策无关。
en: Russia’s troubles, too, do not reflect the impact of Fed policies.

zh: 其经济萎靡不振的原因是油价下跌和因其入侵乌克兰而遭受的国际制裁 — — 这场战争也迫使乌克兰重组其对外债务，战争、严重衰退和货币贬值让乌克兰外债变得不可持续。
en: Its economy is suffering as a result of the fall in oil prices and international sanctions imposed following its invasion of Ukraine – a war that will now force Ukraine to restructure its foreign debt, which the war, severe recession, and currency depreciation have rendered unsustainable.

zh: 类似地，委内瑞拉甚至在石油价格高居100美元/桶以上时就存在巨大的财政赤字和高通胀；而在当前的油价水平上，要不是中国出手救援，委内瑞拉也许将不得不对其公共债务违约。
en: Likewise, Venezuela was running large fiscal deficits and tolerating high inflation even when oil prices were above $100 a barrel; at current prices, it may have to default on its public debt, unless China decides to bail out the country.

zh: 类似地，南非、阿根廷和土耳其所面临的一些经济和金融压力也是拜不当政策和国内政治不确定性所赐，而不是美联储的动作引起的。
en: Similarly, some of the economic and financial stresses faced by South Africa, Argentina, and Turkey are the result of poor policies and domestic political uncertainties, not Fed action.

zh: 简言之，美联储退出零政策利率将给存在巨量内部和外部借贷需求、巨量美元计价债务存量以及宏观和政策脆弱性的新兴市场经济体造成严重问题。
en: In short, the Fed’s exit from zero policy rates will cause serious problems for those emerging market economies that have large internal and external borrowing needs, large stocks of dollar-denominated debt, and macroeconomic and policy fragilities.

zh: 中国经济的减速，加上大宗商品超级周期的结束，将给新兴经济体带来更多阻力，大部分新兴经济体都还没有采取提振潜在增长所需要的结构改革。
en: China’s economic slowdown, together with the end of the commodity super-cycle, will create additional headwinds for emerging economies, most of which have not implemented the structural reforms needed to boost their potential growth.

zh: 但是，这些问题也是自我造成的，许多新兴经济体确实有着更强大的宏观和机构基本面，这将让它们面对美联储开始升息时拥有更强的恢复力。
en: But, again, these problems are self-inflicted, and many emerging economies do have stronger macro and structural fundamentals, which will give them greater resilience when the Fed starts hiking rates.

zh: 当美联储真的开始升息时，一些经济体将比其他经济体受到更大的冲击；但是，除了少数不具备系统重要性的例外，大面积灾难和危机不一定会发生。
en: When it does, some will suffer more than others; but, with a few exceptions lacking systemic importance, widespread distress and crises need not occur.

zh: 美联储为美元分心
en: The Fed’s Dollar Distraction

zh: 坎布里奇—在9月的政策陈述中，美联储考虑了 — — 以非常重点的方式 — — 全球经济发展对美国、进而对美国货币政策的影响。
en: CAMBRIDGE – In its September policy statement, the US Federal Reserve took into consideration – in a major way – the impact of global economic developments on the United States, and thus on US monetary policy.

zh: 事实上，美联储决定推迟升息的部分原因正是美国决策者预期美元升值将拉低进口品价格，从而妨碍其实现2%通胀目标的能力。
en: Indeed, the Fed decided to delay raising interest rates partly because US policymakers expect dollar appreciation, by lowering import prices, to undermine their ability to meet their 2% inflation target.

zh: 在现实中，其他国家的货币波动可能给它们的通胀造成重大影响，但美元波动很少对美国物价造成有意义的或持久的影响。
en: In reality, while currency movements can have a significant impact on inflation in other countries, dollar movements have rarely had a meaningful or durable impact on prices in the US.

zh: 当然，这当中的差别原因在于美元是国际贸易的主要结算货币：价格都是用美元定的。
en: The difference, of course, lies in the US dollar’s dominant role in the invoicing of international trade: prices are set in dollars.

zh: 正因美元常常作为债务合同记账单位，即使是借贷双方都不是美国实体的情况下也是如此，所以国际贸易结算的美元占比高达美国的世界进口占比的4.5倍和世界出口占比的三倍左右。
en: Just as the dollar is often the unit of account in debt contracts, even when neither the borrower nor the lender is a US entity, the dollar’s share in invoicing for international trade is around 4.5 times America’s share of world imports, and three times its share of world exports.

zh: 93%左右的美国进口品用美元计价。
en: The prices of some 93% of US imports are set in dollars.

zh: 在这样的情况下，美元波动对非燃料美国进口品的价格渗透作用为全球最低之一，不管是短期（一季度）还是较长时期（两年）都是如此，主要原因有三。
en: In this environment, the pass-through of dollar movements into non-fuel US import prices is one of the lowest in the world, in both the short term (one quarter out) and the longer term (two years out), for three key reasons.

zh: 首先，国际贸易合同不会频发重订，这意味着美元价格会在相当长的时间 — — 大约十个月 — — 内保持“粘性 ” ， 尽管汇率会发生波动。
en: First, international trade contracts are renegotiated infrequently, which means that dollar prices are “sticky” for an extended period – around ten months – despite fluctuations in the exchange rate.

zh: 其次，由于大部分出口国同时也进口用美元计价的中间投入品，汇率波动对于它们的成本影响有限，因此对它们更改美元价格的刺激也有限。
en: Second, because most exporters also import intermediate inputs that are priced in dollars, exchange-rate fluctuations have a limited impact on their costs and thus on their incentive to change dollar prices.

zh: 第三，欲保持其在世界市场 — — 价格主要用美元计价 — — 占比的出口国选择保持美元价格稳定以避免成为不利汇率波动的受害者。
en: And, third, exporters who wish to preserve their share in world markets – where prices are largely denominated in dollars – choose to keep their dollar prices stable, to avoid falling victim to idiosyncratic exchange-rate movements.

zh: 进口价格对美国通胀的微小冲击基本上都是暂时性的，大多在两个季度后便已消失。
en: What little impact import price shocks have on US inflation is highly transitory, with most of the effect tapering off after just two quarters.

zh: 比如，美元急剧升值10%将在此后2—3个季度内累计造成非燃料进口品通胀下降4.4 % ， 但此后对通胀的影响便可忽略不计。
en: A sharp 10% appreciation of the US dollar, for example, would reduce inflation for non-fuel imports by 4.4% cumulatively over the next 2-3 quarters, but would have only a negligible impact on inflation after that point.

zh: 如果你考虑进口消费品支出，那么10%的升值在前两个季度内将仅仅让通胀 — — 用消费物价指数（CPI）衡量 — — 下降0.5个百分点。
en: If one accounts for consumer goods expenditure on imports, that 10% appreciation would lower inflation, as measured by the consumer price index (CPI), by just 0.5 percentage points in the first two quarters.

zh: 而这可能是其影响的上限，因为其中假设美国零售商将把所有进口价格上涨的因素转嫁给消费者。
en: And that is likely to be an upper bound, because it assumes that US retailers will pass through to consumers the full amount of any increase in import prices.

zh: 在实践中，这更有可能提高零售售价而降低成本转嫁。
en: In practice, they are more likely to increase retail markups and lower cost pass-through.

zh: 据估计，进口制造品价格转嫁 — — 该指标更好地体现消费选择集所受到的影响 — — 甚至比非燃料进口品总体水平更低。
en: The estimated price pass-through for imported manufactured goods, which would better represent what enters the consumption bundle, is even lower than that for all non-fuel imports.

zh: 尽管这些因素使美国与来自汇率波动的通胀压力隔离开来，但它们加剧了其他国家的弱点，特别是新兴经济体。
en: Although these factors insulate the US from the inflationary pressures stemming from exchange-rate fluctuations, they increase the vulnerability of other countries, especially emerging economies.

zh: 由于这些国家大部分进口品的美元价格对汇率波动不十分敏感，因此汇率波动对本币计价的进口品的价格转嫁效应接近100 % 。
en: Because the dollar prices of most of these countries’ imports are not very responsive to exchange-rate movements, the pass-through of those movements into import prices denominated in their home currencies is close to 100%.

zh: 因此，大部分国家的汇率波动影响比美国要大3—4倍。
en: The impact of exchange-rate movements on inflation in most countries is thus 3-4 times larger than in the US.

zh: 比如，保持其他情况一致，土耳其里拉升值10%将导致土耳其CPI通胀在两年中累计增加1.65-2.03个百分点。
en: A 10% depreciation of the Turkish lira, for example, would raise cumulative CPI inflation by 1.65-2.03 percentage points, over two years, all else being equal.

zh: 尽管存在这一失衡，美元作为主要结算货币的地位在近期不可能改变 — — 因为要做出改变需要全世界大量出口国和进口国的合作。
en: Despite this imbalance, the US dollar’s dominance as an invoicing currency is unlikely to change anytime soon – not least because bringing about a shift would require coordination among a huge number of exporters and importers worldwide.

zh: 从欧元区国家之间的贸易量看，欧元也许是一个强大的竞争对手；但是，在欧洲之外，欧元的使用范围远远不及美元。
en: The euro might seem like a strong contender, given the volume of trade among eurozone countries; but, outside Europe, the currency is not used nearly as widely as the dollar.

zh: 在决定何时实现利率正常化时，美联储着重考虑了通货膨胀的颓势及其全球成因。
en: In deciding when to normalize interest rates, the Fed has placed considerable weight on the weakness of inflation, and its global underpinnings.

zh: 的确，一些全球发展趋势 — — 特别是大宗商品价格下跌，也许还有新兴经济体增长放缓和金融波动增加 — — 可能在遏制通胀，但美元贬值不会，至少不会有效遏制通胀。
en: But while it is true that some global developments – especially falling commodity prices, and perhaps also slowing emerging-economy growth and rising financial volatility – may push down inflation, dollar appreciation will not, at least not in any meaningful way.

zh: 因此，强势美元不是推迟美国利率正常化的合理理由。
en: A stronger dollar thus is not a legitimate reason to delay the normalization of US interest rates.

zh: 美联储货币紧缩会不会搞垮新兴市场？
en: Will Fed Tightening Choke Emerging Markets?

zh: 坎布里奇 — — 随着被外界广为期待和猜测的美联储在美启动短期利率上调的日子越来越近，很多人都无法确定新兴市场经济将受到哪些冲击。
en: CAMBRIDGE – As the Federal Reserve moves closer to initiating one of the most long-awaited and widely predicted periods of rising short-term interest rates in the United States, many are asking how emerging markets will be affected.

zh: 事实上，这个问题的提出始于2013年5月，时任美联储主席伯南克公开宣布将在当年晚些时候“收紧”量化宽松政策。 该声明使美长期利率攀升，并导致资金流出新兴市场。
en: Indeed, the question has been asked at least since May 2013, when then-Fed Chairman Ben Bernanke famously announced that quantitative easing would be “tapered” later that year, causing long-term US interest rates to rise and prompting a reversal of capital flows to emerging markets.

zh: 国际货币基金组织总裁克里斯蒂娜·拉加德提醒我们这种担忧已经不是第一次，比方说在1982和1994年，当时美联储货币政策收紧导致发展中国家陷入金融危机。
en: The fear, as IMF Managing Director Christine Lagarde has reminded us, is of a repeat of previous episodes, notably in 1982 and 1994, when the Fed’s policy tightening helped precipitate financial crises in developing countries.

zh: 如果美联储今年决定加息，哪些新兴经济体最容易受到资本流出的打击？
en: If the Fed decides to raise interest rates this year, which emerging markets are most vulnerable to a capital-flow reversal?

zh: 新兴市场无疑对全球市场波动极为敏感，这当中不仅包括美国的利率变化，还包括波动指数等其他金融风险。
en: There is no question that emerging markets are highly sensitive to global market conditions, including not only changes in short-term US interest rates, but also other financial risks, as measured, for example, by the volatility index VIX.

zh: 美国低利率所带来的充足现金流往往能稳定全球金融市场，但一旦条件逆转却会导致资金流突然枯竭。
en: Capital-flow bonanzas, often spurred by low US interest rates and calm global financial markets, end abruptly when these conditions reverse.

zh: 到20世纪90年代东亚和其他国家货币危机结束，新兴市场国家政府已经记取了某些重要教训。
en: By the end of the currency crises in East Asia and elsewhere in the late 1990s, emerging-market governments had learned some important lessons.

zh: 其中的五项改革尤为有效：放开汇率、增持外汇、控制顺周期财政政策、巩固经常账户和减少以美元及其他外币计价的借债。
en: Five reforms were particularly effective: more flexible exchange rates, larger foreign-currency holdings, less pro-cyclical fiscal policy, stronger current accounts, and less debt denominated in dollars or other foreign currencies.

zh: 很多发展中国家都积极推行上述合理措施。
en: Many, but not all, developing and emerging-market countries took steps to implement these desirable policies.

zh: 2008-2009年全球金融危机考验了他们选择的正确性。
en: Their choice was put to the test during the 2008-2009 global financial crisis.

zh: 推行了上述改革的国家平均而言没有受到那么强的冲击。
en: Countries that had adopted such reforms were, on average, less adversely affected.

zh: 那些未进行改革的国家，特别是地处中欧及欧洲边缘的中等收入国家却往往沦为重灾区。
en: Those that had not, particularly middle-income countries in Central Europe and the continent’s periphery, tended to be hit the hardest.

zh: 尤其在2001年后，许多发展中国家成功走出了利用资金流入赞助大规模财政及经常项目赤字的历史格局。
en: In particular, after 2001, many developing countries overcame their historic pattern of using periods of capital inflows to finance large fiscal and current-account deficits.

zh: 正因为减少负债、增加储备，2003-2007年的繁荣期改善了发展中国家的信誉。
en: As a result of reduced debt and enhanced reserves, their creditworthiness improved during the 2003-2007 boom.

zh: 到2008年，他们已经强大到可以用扩大财政赤字缓解2009年经济衰退来破解金融危机。
en: By 2008, they were in a strong enough position to respond to the financial crisis by allowing larger budget deficits and thus mitigating the downturn in 2009.

zh: 除改革明星智利外，博茨瓦纳、中国、哥斯达黎加、马来西亚、菲律宾和韩国也都避免了采取顺周期的财政措施。
en: Chile was the star reformer, but other countries – including Botswana, China, Costa Rica, Malaysia, the Philippines, and South Korea – also avoided pro-cyclical fiscal policies.

zh: 不幸的是，政策倒退正危及“摆脱”顺周期操作的历史进程。
en: Unfortunately, policy backsliding is jeopardizing this historic “graduation” from pro-cyclicality.

zh: 巴西等国并未利用2010到2014年这段时间强化预算，因此现在正在落入困难的境地。
en: Countries like Brazil did not take advantage of the recovery from 2010 to 2014 to strengthen their budgets, and are now in a difficult position.

zh: 有些国家利用资本再次流入的机遇扩大经常账户的赤字规模。
en: Some of these countries used the renewed capital inflows to run large current-account deficits after 2010 as well.

zh: 上述赤字加之通胀率高企，使巴西、土耳其、南非等脆弱五国在2013年伯南克宣布加息预期时受到最沉重的打击。
en: Such deficits, together with high inflation rates, earned Brazil, Turkey, and South Africa their membership on the Fragile Five list of countries that were hit particularly hard by Bernanke’s announcement in 2013.

zh: 印度和印尼也同样如此，但他们从那以后就开始朝正确的方向前进（这在很大程度上应该感谢新一届政府的努力 ） 。
en: India and Indonesia were on this list as well, though they have begun to move in the right direction since then (thanks in part to new governments).

zh: 此外还有委内瑞拉、阿根廷和俄罗斯等从未走上改革道路的经济体。
en: Then there are the countries – including Venezuela, Argentina, and Russia – that never moved in the reform direction in the first place.

zh: 他们暂时为出口商品价格强势所救，但商品价格强势已经在去年成为历史。
en: They were temporarily bailed out by strong world prices for their export commodities, but that ended last year.

zh: 以美元和其他外币计价的债务也构成了不那么明显的威胁。
en: A less visible threat is the denomination of debt in dollars and other foreign currencies.

zh: 二十世纪八九十年代的危机具有毁灭性，因为身负美元债务的经济体往往特别容易受到贬值冲击。
en: The currency crises of the 1980s and 1990s were particularly devastating because devaluations so often hit countries that had borrowed in dollars.

zh: 这导致美元债务和往往以当地货币计价的收入形成“货币错配 ” 。
en: This resulted in a “currency mismatch” between dollar liabilities and revenues that were often denominated in local currencies.

zh: 当美元兑比索或印尼盾的汇价翻番，原本有偿付能力的银行和企业再也无力偿还其美元负债。
en: When the cost of dollars doubled in terms of pesos or rupiah, otherwise-solvent local banks and manufacturers could no longer service their dollar debts.

zh: 由于不良资产负债表影响，贬值的结果带来紧缩，并由此导致严重的经济衰退。
en: Owing to this adverse balance-sheet effect, devaluation turned out to be contractionary, leading to severe recessions.

zh: 截止世纪之交，随着汇率波动凸显货币错配风险，多数新兴市场借款人已经吸取了教���。
en: Most emerging-market borrowers had learned their lesson by the turn of the century, as exchange-rate volatility had made the risks of currency mismatch more tangible.

zh: 当国际投资者2003年再次上门推销贷款时，很多新兴经济体都谢绝借款采取美元或其他外汇形式。
en: When international investors came knocking again in 2003, many emerging markets declined to borrow in dollars or other foreign currencies.

zh: 相反，他们关注那些采取直接投资、股权或以本币形式计价的债务。
en: Instead, they took the inflows in the form of direct investment, equity, or debt denominated in local currency.

zh: 2008-2009年新兴市场货币贬值时错配问题没那么严重是新兴国家日子好过的合理解释。
en: The relative absence of mismatch was one of the reasons why emerging markets did much better when their currencies depreciated in 2008-2009 than in past crises.

zh: 但也存在匈牙利这样的特例，那里的房主愚蠢地借入了看似便宜的欧元和瑞士法郎贷款，又一次证明了这条颠扑不破的真理。
en: Exceptions like Hungary, where homeowners had foolishly borrowed in seemingly cheap euros and Swiss francs, proved the rule.

zh: 不幸的是在过去五年中，很多新兴市场已经恢复了外币借款的惯例。
en: Unfortunately, in the last five years, many emerging markets have reverted to borrowing in foreign currency.

zh: 虽然多数情况下政府仍尽量避免以美元计价，但据国际清算银行警告企业部门美元借贷似乎未能抵御住超低利率的诱惑。
en: Though, for the most part, governments have continued the shift away from dollar debt, the corporate sector, as the Bank for International Settlements has warned, has been tempted by ultra-low interest rates.

zh: 中国的私营部门可能面临最严重的问题。
en: The Chinese private sector may have the biggest problem.

zh: 很多近期借贷违反了过去危机中来之不易的重要原则：债务以外币计价、期限较短、由影子银行居中撮合并以房屋作为抵押。
en: Much of its recent borrowing violates key tenets of hard-earned wisdom gained in past crises: it is foreign exchange-denominated, short-term, shadow-bank-intermediated, and housing-backed.

zh: 尽管美联储尚未开始加息，但美国稳固的经济复苏和货币紧缩预期已经在过去一年中造成美元兑多数新兴市场和发达国家货币大幅升值。
en: Even though the Fed has not yet started raising interest rates, the well-established US economic recovery and the prospect of monetary tightening have, over the last year, caused the dollar to appreciate sharply against most currencies, those of emerging markets and advanced countries alike.

zh: 如果美联储于年中收紧货币政策，有很大可能美元还会进一步升值。
en: If the Fed tightens as early as the middle of this year, further dollar appreciation is likely.

zh: 那些一直在玩货币错配的人很可能将引火烧身。
en: Those who have been playing with mismatches may be about to get burned.

zh: 美联储又挖坑
en: The Fed Sets Another Trap

zh: 纽黑文—美联储正在走一条熟悉的高危之路。
en: NEW HAVEN – America’s Federal Reserve is headed down a familiar – and highly dangerous – path.

zh: 它完全否认过去的错误，正在追求渐进方针 — — 同样的方针为2008—2009年金融危机创造了条件。
en: Steeped in denial of its past mistakes, the Fed is pursuing the same incremental approach that helped set the stage for the financial crisis of 2008-2009.

zh: 这一回的结果也可能具有同样的灾难性。
en: The consequences could be similarly catastrophic.

zh: 以12月的联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）会议为例。 会议对提高联邦基金利率的讨论充斥着形容词而不是明白无误的行动。
en: Consider the December meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), where discussions of raising the benchmark federal funds rate were couched in adjectives, rather than explicit actions.

zh: 美联储此前曾发布前瞻指引，表示在10月份结束长期资产购买操作后的“相当长”时间内保持近零利率。 与此相应，FOMC宣布它现在可以“耐心”等待提高利率的合适条件。
en: In line with prior forward guidance that the policy rate would be kept near zero for a “considerable” amount of time after the Fed stopped purchasing long-term assets in October, the FOMC declared that it can now afford to be “patient” in waiting for the right conditions to raise the rate.

zh: 此外，美联储主席耶伦声称在任何利率“升空”发生前，FOMC至少还要开好几次会议，而美联储似乎也在暗示拖延政策正常化进程。
en: Add to that Fed Chair Janet Yellen’s declaration that at least a couple more FOMC meetings would need to take place before any such “lift-off” occurs, and the Fed seems to be telegraphing a protracted journey on the road to policy normalization.

zh: 这与2004—2006年期间的政策惊人地相似。 当时，美联储的渐进方针导致了几乎致命的错误 — — 纵容金融市场和实体经济的过度行为。
en: This bears an eerie resemblance to the script of 2004-2006, when the Fed’s incremental approach led to the near-fatal mistake of condoning mounting excesses in financial markets and the real economy.

zh: 21世纪初股市泡沫破裂后，美联储将联邦基金利率降低到45年来的低点1 % ， 并且在非常长的时间内一直没有将政策正常化。
en: After pushing the federal funds rate to a 45-year low of 1% following the collapse of the equity bubble of the early 2000s, the Fed delayed policy normalization for an inordinately long period.

zh: 而当美联储最终开始提高基准利率时，又做得过于缓慢。
en: And when it finally began to raise the benchmark rate, it did so excruciatingly slowly.

zh: 2004年后的24个月里，FOMC以每次25个基点的节奏通过17次操作将联邦基金利率从1%提高到5.25 % 。
en: In the 24 months from June 2004, the FOMC raised the federal funds rate from 1% to 5.25% in 17 increments of 25 basis points each.

zh: 与此同时，房地产和信用泡沫出现了快速扩大，助长了家庭过度消费、个人储蓄急剧减少和创纪录的经常项目赤字 — — 这些失衡为随后到来的崩溃埋下了伏笔。
en: Meanwhile, housing and credit bubbles were rapidly expanding, fueling excessive household consumption, a sharp drop in personal savings, and a record current-account deficit – imbalances that set the stage for the meltdown that was soon to follow.

zh: 当然，美联储不承认任何关于它造成了美国和全球经济大危机的指控。
en: The Fed, of course, has absolved itself of any blame in setting up the US and the global economy for the Great Crisis.

zh: 两位前主席格林斯潘（Alan Greenspan）和伯南克（Ben Bernanke）都说这不是货币政策的错；他们坚持认为，要错也是缺乏监督监管的错。
en: It was not monetary policy’s fault, argued both former Fed Chairmen Alan Greenspan and Ben Bernanke; if anything, they insisted, a lack of regulatory oversight was the culprit.

zh: 这一观点在政策和政治圈中很有影响，导致官员关注一套以所谓的宏观审慎工具 — — 包括资本要求和贷款比率 — — 遏制银行过度冒险行为为核心的新方针。
en: This argument has proved convincing in policy and political circles, leading officials to focus on a new approach centered on so-called macro-prudential tools, including capital requirements and leverage ratios, to curb excessive risk-taking by banks.

zh: 这一方针有其优点，但并不完善，因为它没有解决过于舒适的货币政策及其所造成的历史最低利率导致的风险定价严重错误。
en: While this approach has some merit, it is incomplete, as it fails to address the egregious mispricing of risk brought about by an overly accommodative monetary policy and the historically low interest rates that it generated.

zh: 从这个角度讲，美联储在2004—2006年所采取的渐进主义是一个足以遗臭万年的政策错误。
en: In this sense, the Fed’s incrementalism of 2004-2006 was a policy blunder of epic proportions.

zh: 从当前环境看，美联储可能要重蹈覆辙 — — 后果可能更加严重。
en: The Fed seems poised to make a similar – and possibly even more serious – misstep in the current environment.

zh: 首先，由于人们一直担心后危机时代的脆弱性和通缩风险，今天的美联储可能会寻找一切借口延长其渐进式正常化，采取比十年前还要慢的正常化节奏。
en: For starters, given ongoing concerns about post-crisis vulnerabilities and deflation risk, today’s Fed seems likely to find any excuse to prolong its incremental normalization, taking a slower pace than it adopted a decade ago.

zh: 更重要的是，美联储4.5万亿美元规模的资产负债表已经增长了五倍多。
en: More important, the Fed’s $4.5 trillion balance sheet has since grown more than fivefold.

zh: 尽管美联储已经停止购买新资产，但并未表现出缩减巨额持有量的意图。
en: Though the Fed has stopped purchasing new assets, it has shown no inclination to scale back its outsize holdings.

zh: 与此同时，它将量化宽松的接力棒传给了日本银行和欧洲央行，后两者都会在利率位于创纪录低水平的情况下创造出更多的流动性。
en: Meanwhile it has passed the quantitative-easing baton to the Bank of Japan and the European Central Bank, both of which will create even more liquidity at a time of record-low interest rates.

zh: 在这些泡沫时期，在充斥着流动性的金融体系中坚持过度政策便利导致了一个巨大风险。
en: In these days of froth, the persistence of extraordinary policy accommodation in a financial system flooded with liquidity poses a great danger.

zh: 事实上，这可能正是当前股市和货币市场波动 — — 当然还有油价崩跌 — — 的教训。
en: Indeed, that could well be the lesson of recent equity- and currency-market volatility and, of course, plummeting oil prices.

zh: 风大柴干，只需要一点火花就可以带来一场新的大火。
en: With so much dry kindling, it will not take much to spark the next conflagration.

zh: 中央银行迷失了方向。
en: Central banking has lost its way.

zh: 世界主要央行陷入了后危机时代的零利率和��产负债表膨胀的陷阱，拿不出有效战略重新控制应该由它们进行管理的金融市场和实体经济。
en: Trapped in a post-crisis quagmire of zero interest rates and swollen balance sheets, the world’s major central banks do not have an effective strategy for regaining control over financial markets or the real economies that they are supposed to manage.

zh: 政策杠杆 — — 基准利率和央行资产负债表 — — 仍然处于紧急状况设定中，虽然紧急状况早就结束了。
en: Policy levers – both benchmark interest rates and central banks’ balance sheets – remain at their emergency settings, even though the emergency ended long ago.

zh: 这一方针成功地提振了金融市场，但并未治愈伤痕累累的发达经济体，它们仍困于复苏萎靡和通缩风险。
en: While this approach has succeeded in boosting financial markets, it has failed to cure bruised and battered developed economies, which remain mired in subpar recoveries and plagued with deflationary risks.

zh: 此外，央行鼓吹金融市场泡沫越久，经济对这些危险的市场的依赖程度就越大，政客和财政当局满足资产负债表修正和结构改革的需要的激励就越弱。
en: Moreover, the longer central banks promote financial-market froth, the more dependent their economies become on these precarious markets and the weaker the incentives for politicians and fiscal authorities to address the need for balance-sheet repair and structural reform.

zh: 我们需要新方针。
en: A new approach is needed.

zh: 中央银行应该尽快将引发危机的政策正常化。
en: Central banks should normalize crisis-induced policies as soon as possible.

zh: 当然，金融市场会大声反对。
en: Financial markets will, of course, object loudly.

zh: 但独立的中央银行如果不准备直面市场、做出负责任的经济管理工作所要求的严守纪律的艰难抉择，还要它们做什么？
en: But what do independent central banks stand for if they are not prepared to face up to the markets and make the tough and disciplined choices that responsible economic stewardship demands?

zh: 过去六年中，前所未有的央行金融工程成为全球主要市场资产价格的主要决定因素。
en: The unprecedented financial engineering by central banks over the last six years has been decisive in setting asset prices in major markets worldwide.

zh: 但如今，美联储以及其他央行需要放弃金融工程，开始准备应对难以避免的下一场危机所需要的工具。
en: But now it is time for the Fed and its counterparts elsewhere to abandon financial engineering and begin marshaling the tools they will need to cope with the inevitable next crisis.

zh: 零利率和庞大资产负债表意味着这才是它们所缺少的。
en: With zero interest rates and outsize balance sheets, that is exactly what they are lacking.

zh: 当前美国通胀数字背后的真相
en: The Truth Behind Today’s US Inflation Numbers

zh: 发自伯克利 — — 2015年12月，美联储启动货币紧缩周期，将短期名义联邦基金利率的目标范围调高了25个基点（1/4个百分点 ） 。
en: BERKELEY – In December 2015, the US Federal Reserve embarked on a monetary-tightening cycle, by raising the target range for the short-term nominal federal funds rate by 25 basis points (one-quarter of a percentage point).

zh: 当时联邦公开市场委员会 — — 美联储设定货币政策的机构 — — 发布了一份中期预测并预测了三个事件。
en: At the time, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) – the Fed body that sets monetary policy – issued a median forecast predicting three things.

zh: 首先，联邦公开市场委员会表示2015年12月的利率增长将是在随后一年内合共五轮利率上升中的第一轮，也是2017年9月之前九轮上升的第一轮。
en: First, the FOMC indicated that the December 2015 rate increase would be the first of five such increases that it would make within the subsequent year, and the first of nine that would take place by, say, September 2017.

zh: 其次，联邦基金利率将在2015年12月份调高后的三个月内达到2.25~2.5 ％ 。
en: Second, the federal funds rate would reach 2.25-2.5% within three months of the December 2015 increase.

zh: 第三，美联储衡量通货膨胀压力的首选指标 — — 核心个人消费支出价格指数 — — 将在目前实现每年1.9％的增长。
en: And, third, the Fed’s preferred measure of inflationary pressure – the core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index – would be at 1.9% per year by now.

zh: 总的来说，联邦公开市场委员会的预测还没有得到证实。
en: All told, the FOMC’s forecast has not been borne out.

zh: 如果美联储确实在本月升高利率，也只是在九轮预期加息中的四轮。
en: If the Fed actually does increase interest rates this month, it will have undertaken only four of the nine anticipated rate hikes.

zh: 此外它认为在今年夏天之前必须进行九轮加息以确保通胀率低于其每年2％的目标，但预计在今年余下时间和明年之内通胀都将保持在每年1.5％的水平。
en: Moreover, it believed that nine rate hikes before the end of this summer would be necessary to keep inflation below its target of 2% per year. But inflation is expected to rise at an annual rate of just 1.5% for the rest of this year, and next year.

zh: 在通胀压力方面，美联储的预测似乎过分高估了美国经济的动力。
en: In terms of inflationary pressure, the Fed’s forecast seems to have significantly overstated the strength of the US economy.

zh: 即使美联储改变了进程（目前将联邦基金利率较2015年12月的计划调低1.5个百分点 ） ， 通胀压力仍然相对较弱。
en: Even with the Fed’s change of course (it is now pursuing a federal funds rate that is 1.5 percentage points below its December 2015 plan), inflationary pressure is still relatively weak.

zh: 事实上，虽然政策紧缩政策的逐渐松绑推动了经济增长，但通货膨胀率仍然不及2013~14年期间的高位 — — 当时很多人还担心美联储不能提供足够的刺激政策。
en: Indeed, despite the economic boost implied by slower policy tightening, the rate of inflation is still no higher than it was in the 2013-2014 period, when many worried that the Fed wasn’t providing enough stimulus.

zh: 我们可以就当前状况得出三个结论。
en: We can draw three conclusions about the current situation.

zh: 首先，当今疲软的通货膨胀前景表明美联储的货币政策以及与之相结合的财政政策并未能为美国经济提供足够的刺激 — — 正如2013年时一样。
en: First, today’s weak inflation outlook suggests that the Fed’s monetary policies, in combination with fiscal policies, are not providing sufficient stimulus for the US economy – as was the case in 2013.

zh: 不幸的是，联邦公开市场委员会似乎并不特别在意这种可能性。
en: Unfortunately, the FOMC does not appear to be particularly concerned about this possibility.

zh: 其成员之一，观点鲜明的明尼阿波利斯联邦储备银行主席尼尔·卡什加里（Neel Kashkari）是唯一一个对此持反对意见的人，还呼吁美联储采取更多的刺激政策。
en: Among FOMC members, Neel Kashkari, the impressive president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, is the only one who has dissented, calling on the Fed to pursue more stimulative policies.

zh: 而委员会的盲目源于这样一个事实，它更多地依赖于对其认为处于或超过“​​充分就业”的劳动力市场的评估，而不是纷繁的每月通货膨胀数据。
en: The FOMC’s blind spot stems from the fact that it is relying more on its assessment of the labor market, which it considers to be at or above “full employment,” than on noisy month-to-month inflation data.

zh: 然而“充分就业”是一个相当脆弱且不可靠的概念架构。
en: But “full employment” is a rather tenuous and unreliable construct.

zh: 早在20年前经济学家道格拉斯·斯塔格（Douglas Staiger ） ， 詹姆斯·司徒克（James Stock）和马克·沃森（Mark Watson）就表明美联储决策者不应对“充分就业”的估计如此自信。
en: It has now been 20 years since economists Douglas Staiger, James Stock, and Mark Watson showed that Fed policymakers should not be so confident in estimates of “full employment.”

zh: 然而由于某种原因，美联储却未能采纳这一基本信息。
en: And yet, for some reason, the Fed community has not let this essential message sink in.

zh: 从目前情况得出的第二个结论是美联储已连续11年高估了美国经济的动力。
en: A second conclusion to be drawn from the current situation is that the Fed has now overestimated the strength of the US economy for 11 consecutive years.

zh: 初等数学要求一个可靠的预测应至少在一半的时间内出现高估而另一半时间低估。
en: Elementary mathematics dictates that credible forecasts should at least overestimate half the time and undershoot half the time.

zh: 如果每年的美联储预测都是由抛硬币决定，意味着我们如今已经连续开出了11个正面，一个背面也没有，而出现这种情况的概率是1/2048。
en: If each year of Fed forecasting were a coin toss, we would now have had eleven heads in a row, and zero tails. The odds of that happening are one in 2,048.

zh: 美联储显然需要深入研究其预测方法和决策流程。
en: The Fed clearly needs to take a deep look at its forecasting methodology and policymaking processes.

zh: 它应该质疑当前的体系是否为美联储的技术官僚们附加了不可抗拒的激励因素来高估通胀率，也应该确保其决策者将2％的年通胀率目标视为渴望达成的目标，而非避免触及的上限。
en: It should ask if the current system is creating irresistible incentives for Fed technocrats to highball their inflation forecasts. And it should ensure that its policymakers view the 2% target for annual inflation as a goal to aspire to, rather than a ceiling to avoid.

zh: 最后的结论是，过去两年来还提供了更多的数据来支持前美国财政部长拉里·萨默斯（Larry Summers）的深切怀疑，认为北方富国（global North，此概念意指美国，加拿大，西欧，亚洲发达国家以及澳洲，新西兰）的经济如今已经陷入“长期停滞”状态。
en: A final conclusion is that the past two years have provided still more data to support former US Secretary of the Treasury Larry Summers’ grave suspicion that the economies of the global North are now trapped in a state of “secular stagnation.”

zh: 而那些持反对意见者，比如哈佛大学的肯尼思·罗格夫（Kenneth Rogoff）则告诉我们：所有这一切都会很快好起来的，金融危机过去8年后也不会有人再提起“长期停滞”这个词。
en: Those who disagree, such as Kenneth Rogoff of Harvard University, tell us that all will soon be well, and that nobody will be talking about “secular stagnation” eight years hence.

zh: 后者可能会是正确的 — — 但这只有当美联储能够采取以足够激进的姿态执行其激励政策的时候。
en: They may turn out to be right – but only if the Fed can bring itself to pursue stimulus policies that are as radical as they are necessary.

zh: 美国的高风险复苏
en: America’s Risky Recovery

zh: 美国剑桥—美国经济正在走向充分就业，也许已经达到了这一水平。
en: CAMBRIDGE – The United States’ economy is approaching full employment and may already be there.

zh: 但美国有利的就业趋势伴随着金融部门风险的大幅增加，这是因为为了实现目前的经济复苏而实施了过于宽松的货币政策。
en: But America’s favorable employment trend is accompanied by a substantial increase in financial-sector risks, owing to the excessively easy monetary policy that was used to achieve the current economic recovery.

zh: 总体失业率已降至5.5 % ， 大学毕业生失业率更是只有2.5 % 。
en: The overall unemployment rate is down to just 5.5%, and the unemployment rate among college graduates is just 2.5%.

zh: 经济达到如此就业水平时常常出现的通胀的增加因为石油价格下跌和美元升值20%而被暂时遏制。
en: The increase in inflation that usually occurs when the economy reaches such employment levels has been temporarily postponed by the decline in the price of oil and by the 20% rise in the value of the dollar.

zh: 升值的美元不但降低了进口品的成本，也给予进口品竞争的国产商品造成了降价压力。
en: The stronger dollar not only lowers the cost of imports, but also puts downward pressure on the prices of domestic products that compete with imports.

zh: 通胀可能在未来一年中开始上升。
en: Inflation is likely to begin rising in the year ahead.

zh: 回归充分就业反映了美联储的“非常规货币政策 ” — —被称为量化宽松的大规模长期资产购买计划与承诺将短期利率维持在近零水平的组合。
en: The return to full employment reflects the Federal Reserve’s strategy of “unconventional monetary policy” – the combination of massive purchases of long-term assets known as quantitative easing and its promise to keep short-term interest rates close to zero.

zh: 这一政策让所有利率都呈现出低水平，促使投资者购买股票，并提高了自住住房的价格。
en: The low level of all interest rates that resulted from this policy drove investors to buy equities and to increase the prices of owner-occupied homes.

zh: 结果，2013年美国家庭净财富增加了10万亿美元，促使消费支出和商业投资增加。
en: As a result, the net worth of American households rose by $10 trillion in 2013, leading to increases in consumer spending and business investment.

zh: 在非常缓慢的初始复苏后，2013年下半年，实际GDP开始以超过4%的年率增长。
en: After a very slow initial recovery, real GDP began growing at annual rates of more than 4% in the second half of 2013.

zh: 2014年，消费支出和商业投资继续保持这一增幅（第一季度除外，原因是极寒冬季所造成的天气影响 ） 。
en: Consumer spending and business investment continued at that rate in 2014 (except for the first quarter, owing to the weather-related effects of an exceptionally harsh winter).

zh: 这一强劲增长提高了就业，让经济回归充分就业。
en: That strong growth raised employment and brought the economy to full employment.

zh: 但美联储的非常规政策也为金融部门和整个经济制造了高危风险。
en: But the Fed’s unconventional monetary policies have also created dangerous risks to the financial sector and the economy as a whole.

zh: 目前的极低利率让投资者承担过多风险追求投资组合的高收益，而这往往是为了实现退休金和保险合同所规定的回报责任。
en: The very low interest rates that now prevail have driven investors to take excessive risks in order to achieve a higher current yield on their portfolios, often to meet return obligations set by pension and insurance contracts.

zh: 这一追求收益率的行为将长期债券价格推高至不可持续的水平，缩小了公司债券和新兴市场债务的信用利差，提升了商业地产的相对价格，也让股市市盈率增加到历史平均水平以上25%的程度。
en: This reaching for yield has driven up the prices of all long-term bonds to unsustainable levels, narrowed credit spreads on corporate bonds and emerging-market debt, raised the relative prices of commercial real estate, and pushed up the stock market’s price-earnings ratio to more than 25% higher than its historic average.

zh: 低利率环境还让贷款人为了保持利润而承担过多风险。
en: The low-interest-rate environment has also caused lenders to take extra risks in order to sustain profits.

zh: 银行和其他贷款人授信给低质量借款人、存在大量未偿还债务的借款人，或者降低价款人贷款条件（所谓的“低门槛贷款 ” ） 。
