zh: 我读到的可不是这样。
en: That is not how I read it.

zh: 研究说十年违约概率不到500,000分之一；认为即使分析与实际情况相差一个数量级，政府的风险也非常有限；并要求当时在位的监管体系尽量缩小，以至于它们没有发现风险。
en: It speaks to ten-year default probabilities of less than one in 500,000; notes that even if the analysis is off by an order of magnitude, any risks to government are very modest; and appeals to the regulatory system in place at the time to minimize that their model missed risks.

zh: 他反对国会预算办公室、财政部和 美联储的看法，后三者都根据斯蒂格利茨写这篇文章时所能得到的相同的信息，做出了建议为房利美提供隐性担保可能代价高昂的结论。
en: He makes arguments against the Congressional Budget Office, the Department of the Treasury, and the Federal Reserve, all of which had suggested – based on the same information available to Stiglitz when he wrote his paper – that implicit guarantees to Fannie Mae were potentially costly.

zh: 我不确定斯蒂格利茨对衍生品的态度如何。
en: I am not sure what point Joe is making with respect to derivatives.

zh: 我在他回应的拙文中明确指出，我但愿我们当初没有支持2000年立法。
en: I was clear in my article to which he is responding that I wish we had not supported the 2000 legislation.

zh: 但我又指出，没有理由认为2000年立法不通过的话，小布什政府的商品期货交易委员会就一定会拥有对衍生品的绝对新权力，同时我还指出了职业律师认为必须解决的法律确定性问题。
en: But I also noted that there is no reason to think that, in the absence of the legislation, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission under the Bush administration would have asserted sweeping new authority over derivatives and pointed to the legal certainty problem that career lawyers thought was important to address.

zh: 那么长期停滞理论呢？
en: What about secular stagnation theory?

zh: 斯蒂格利茨和我都认为，阿尔文·汉森（Alvin Hansen）的预言之所以没有在二战后成为现实，是因为扩张性政策和经济的结构性变化的联合结果。
en: Stiglitz and I agree that Alvin Hansen’s prediction was not borne out after World War II because of a combination of expansionary policy and structural changes in the economy.

zh: 这就是我五年前重新提出长期停滞时的观点 — — 2013年的经济状态需要财政扩张和结构变革相结合来保持充分就业。
en: This was my point five years ago in renewing the idea of secular stagnation – to suggest that the economy as it was in 2013 required some combination of fiscal expansion and structural change to sustain full employment.

zh: 我对长期停滞的讨论全都强调多重结构性因素，包括不平等性、高利润股票、相对价格变化和全球储蓄模式等。
en: My discussions of secular stagnation have all emphasized a variety of structural factors, including inequality, high profit shares, changes in relative prices, and global saving patterns.

zh: 斯蒂格利茨与我的分歧在哪里？
en: Where does Stiglitz disagree?

zh: 法尔莫在他的洞见深邃的评论中指出，他在最近几年中率先提出的模型是思考长期过度失业的最正确的思路，再加上正确的微观基础，就能认定财政政策是无效的。
en: Farmer, in his thoughtful commentary, argues that models of the type he has pioneered in recent years are the right way to think about chronically excessive unemployment and that, with the right microfoundations, one can conclude that fiscal policies are ineffective.

zh: 我认为他的建模方法也许确实成果累累，但我好像并不明白。
en: I think his modeling approach may well prove very fruitful, and I wish I understood it better.

zh: 但对于现在，我看见实证证据、国际比较、时间序列研究和美国国内地方差异研究都一边倒地表明财政政策是有作用的。
en: But, for now, I find the empirical evidence, international comparisons, time-series studies, and studies of local variation within the United States compelling in suggesting that fiscal policy works.

zh: 但我确实认为，法尔莫对于用货币政策稳定资产价格的观点值得认真考虑。
en: I do think, however, that Farmer’s views on the use of monetary policy to stabilize asset prices deserve serious consideration.

zh: 最后，我希望斯蒂格利茨能够积极评价我反复强调的观点，我们可以在哥伦比亚大学或哈佛大学期间以及其他合适场合进行私下探讨。
en: Finally, I hope Stiglitz will respond positively to my repeated suggestions that we debate these matters in person at Columbia or Harvard or some other suitable venue.

zh: 我们也许都同意，更好地理解宏观经济史的教训、避免过去十年中发生的事件在未来重演至关重要。
en: We can all agree that the stakes in a better understanding of the lessons of macroeconomic history, and in avoiding future events like those of the last decade, are very high.

zh: 收缩的金融业
en: Finance Agonistes

zh: 伦敦 — — 至少在最近的二十五年中，发达国家以及大部分发展中国家的金融产业取得了比整体经济快得多的增长速度。
en: LONDON – For at least a quarter-century, the financial sector has grown far more rapidly than the economy as a whole, both in developed and in most developing countries.

zh: 1980年，英国金融资产总额（包括股票、债券和银行存款）与国内生产总值的比例约为100 % ， 而到了2006年，这一比例上升到440%左右。
en: The ratio of total financial assets (stocks, bonds, and bank deposits) to GDP in the United Kingdom was about 100% in 1980, while by 2006 it had risen to around 440%.

zh: 在同一时期内，中国的金融资产则从一无所有上升至GDP的300%以上。
en: In China, financial assets went from being virtually non-existent to well over 300% of GDP during this period.

zh: 随着金融行业规模扩大，其盈利水平也随之提高。
en: As the size of the financial industry grew, so, too, did its profitability.

zh: 金融公司所获利润占美国各公司全部利润总额的比重从1980年的10%窜升至2006年的40 % 。
en: The share of total profits of companies in the United States represented by financial firms rocketed from 10% in 1980 to 40% in 2006.

zh: 在这一背景下，金融领域薪酬的飙升便不足为奇了。
en: Against that background, it is not surprising that pay in the financial sector soared.

zh: 伦敦金融城、曼哈顿金融区以及其他一些金融中心化身为印钞机，使得投资银行家、对冲基金经理以及私人股本运作者赚得盆满钵满。
en: The City of London, lower Manhattan, and a few other centers became money machines that made investment bankers, hedge-fund managers, and private equity folk immoderately wealthy.

zh: 像我这样的大学领导便会花费大量时间，劝说这些人将收益的一部分回馈母校。
en: University leaders like me spent much of our time persuading them to recycle a portion of their gains to their old schools.

zh: 但在过去的两年间，情况发生了变化。
en: For the last two years, things have been different.

zh: 许多金融公司的资产负债表出现了戏剧性的缩水，当然还有一些公司干脆关门大吉。
en: Many financial firms have shrunk their balance sheets dramatically, and of course some have gone out of business altogether.

zh: 金融杠杆大幅降低，在2007年早期，投资银行的杠杆超过其资本三十倍有余，现在则下降到十倍刚出头的水平。
en: Leverage is down sharply. Investment banks with leverage of more than 30 times their capital in early 2007 are now down to little more than ten times.

zh: 交易量与银行信贷量一并萎缩，全球各地的金融中心都进行了大规模的裁员。
en: Trading volumes are down, as is bank lending, and there have been major layoffs in financial centers around the globe.

zh: 这只是一个短期现象吗？ 一旦世界经济开始复苏，我们会看到金融部门很快重返高速发展的局面吗？
en: Is this a short-term phenomenon, and will we see an early return to rapid financial-sector growth as soon as the world economy recovers?

zh: 目前市场中关于年终奖金正卷土重来，对冲基金实现了两位数的收益以及私人股本市场的复苏等传闻已在满天飞。
en: Already the market is full of rumors that guaranteed bonuses are returning, that hedge funds are making double-digit returns, and that activity is reviving in the private equity market.

zh: 这些现象是金融部门强劲恢复的先兆，抑或仅仅只是都市神话？
en: Are these harbingers of a robust recovery for the financial sector, or just urban myths?

zh: 对于这个问题，我们并没有肯定的答案，但也许经济史可以为我们提供一些线索。
en: There is no certain answer to that question, but perhaps economic history can offer some clues.

zh: 近期由英格兰银行的安迪·霍尔丹对英国金融部门股票长期收益情况所作的分析暗示人们：过去的二十五年极不寻常。
en: A recent analysis by Andy Haldane of the Bank of England of long-term returns on UK financial sector equities suggests that the last 25 years have been very unusual.

zh: 假设你在1900年对金融类股票投下了长期赌注，同时对一般股票下了短期赌注 — — 实际上这就成了一场关于英国金融产业能否比市场其他行业表现得更为出色的赌博。
en: Suppose you had placed a long-term bet on financial equities in 1900, along with a short bet on general equities – in effect a gamble on whether the UK financial sector would outperform the market.

zh: 在起初的八十五年间，这场赌博会显得索然无味，年平均回报率仅在2%左右。
en: For the first 85 years, this would have been a very uninteresting gamble, generating an average return of only around 2% a year.

zh: 但在1986年至2006年这一时段，情况与此前截然不同。
en: But the period from 1986 to 2006 was radically different.

zh: 在这二十年间，你的年均回报率将超过16 % 。
en: During those two decades, your annual average return would have been more than 16%.

zh: 按霍尔丹的话说 ： “ 银行业成了下金蛋的鹅。
en: As Haldane puts it, “banking became the goose laying the golden eggs.”

zh: ”确实，在近代的英国金融史上，这狂欢一般的二十年可谓绝无仅有。
en: Indeed, there is no period in recent UK financial history that bears any comparison to those jamboree decades.

zh: 如果你在三年前解除了赌注，那么现在你将处于很有利的位置 — — 当然前提是你已经将之转为现金 — — 因为2006年之后的时期，此前那些收益将大部分化为乌有。
en: If you had unwound your bet three years ago, you would now be sitting pretty – as long as you had gone into cash, of course – because the period since 2006 has undone most of these gains.

zh: 因此如果你一直到去年年底还持有银行股，那么你在这110年中的投资年均回报率将低于3 % ， 仍然大体上属于不赚不赔的策略。
en: So if you had held your bank stocks up to the end of last year, over 110 years your investment would have yielded an annual average return of less than 3%, still broadly a break-even strategy.

zh: 为何这二十年的经历如此不同寻常，会出现比上世纪任何时候都要高得多的回报？
en: Why was this 20-year experience so unusual, with returns so much higher than at any time in the last century?

zh: 看起来，最直截了当的答案是杠杆。
en: The most straightforward answer seems to be leverage.

zh: 在这场竞速比赛中，各家银行为了创造更高的回报，明显地开足了马力。
en: Banks geared up dramatically, in a competitive race to generate higher returns.

zh: 霍尔丹将这一举动形容为进行轮盘赌博。
en: Haldane describes this as resorting to the roulette wheel.

zh: 也许这一类比是对那些轮盘赌徒的巨大侮辱。
en: Perhaps that analogy is rather insulting to those who play roulette.

zh: 确实 ， “ 赌场银行业”这一表述忽视了赌场对其收益情况有着相当不错的控制这一事实。
en: Indeed, the phrase “casino banking” tends to ignore the fact that casinos have a rather good handle on their returns.

zh: 他们往往在风险管理方面非常精明，在这一点上，他们不同于许多在过去二十年间显著增加其杠杆（由此也增加其风险）的银行。
en: They are typically very astute at risk management, unlike many of the banks that dramatically increased their leverage – and thus their risks – during the last 20 years.

zh: 对于未来而言，我们能总结出的结论在很大程度上取决于中央银行以及监管者是如何应对这一危机的。
en: The conclusions that we might draw for the future depend heavily on how central banks and regulators react to the crisis.

zh: 在现阶段，金融公司正在为自己吸取教训，削减杠杆、储备资本与现金，然而当局却正在试图说服银行扩大贷款规模 — — 而这正是导致目前此次危机的原因。
en: At present, financial firms are learning the lessons for themselves, reducing leverage and hoarding capital and cash, whereas the authorities are trying to persuade banks to expand lending – precisely the strategy that led to the current crisis.

zh: 当然，我们知道银行业发展的长期目标。
en: Of course, we know that a different approach will be needed in the longer run.

zh: 实际上，监管当局正沿着最早由圣奥古斯丁描绘出的道路前进。
en: In effect, the authorities are following the approach first outlined by St. Augustine.

zh: 他们希望银行变得“贞洁 ” ， 不过不是现在。
en: They would like banks to be “chaste,” but not yet.

zh: 但当银行业再次出现增长时，杠杆将受到比以往严格得多的约束。
en: But when growth does return, leverage will be far more tightly constrained than it was before.

zh: 监管机构已经在商讨有关对金融杠杆征税以及对风险加权资产设限等议题。
en: Regulators are already talking about imposing leverage ratios, as well as limits on risk-weighted assets.

zh: 如果他们一直做的话，我估计，像过去二十年那样的飞速增长期将一去不复返。
en: If they follow through, as I expect, there will be no return to the strategies of the last two decades.

zh: 如果这样的话，金融业的整体表现也不再可能超过其他行业。
en: In that case, finance will no longer be an industry that systematically outpaces the rest of the economy.

zh: 金融公司有的赔钱，有的盈利，所有金融公司都赚钱的现象几乎不可能出现。
en: There will be winners and losers, of course, but systematic sectoral out-performance looks unlikely.

zh: 这将对金融业薪酬水平影响有多大，这一问题略显复杂，我将在今后再行讨论。
en: What that will mean for financial-sector pay is a slightly more complex question, to which I will return.

zh: 为气候变化转型提供融资
en: Financing the Climate-Change Transition

zh: 波茨坦、巴黎、苏黎世—除非世界迅速降低温室气体排放量，否则人类将进入前所未有的气候风险期。
en: POTSDAM, PARIS, ZURICH – Unless the world reduces greenhouse-gas emissions rapidly, humanity is likely to enter an era of unprecedented climate risks.

zh: 灾难性极端天气事件频率已经开始上升，但最糟糕的气候相关伤害，比如海平面持续升高，等我们认识到它们出现的时候已经太迟了。
en: Devastating extreme-weather events are already increasing in frequency, but much of the worst climate-related damage, such as a sustained rise in sea levels, will be recognized only once it is too late to act.

zh: 显然，气候系统的考虑时界很长，二政治和经济周期很短，两者恨不匹配。
en: Clearly, the climate system’s time horizon does not align well with the world’s much shorter political and economic cycles.

zh: 上市公司按季度披露报告，而最新监管变化，如越来越多的强制使用按市值计价会计规则，限制了长期思考。
en: Listed companies report on a quarterly basis, and recent regulatory changes, such as those mandating increased use of mark-to-market accounting, limit long-term thinking.

zh: 政府立法周期通常不超过四年，并且还必须对眼前的发展趋势立刻做出反应。
en: Governments usually have legislative cycles of no more than four years, and they must also respond to immediate developments.

zh: 但稳定气候要求在相当长的时期内采取持续一致的行动。
en: Yet stabilizing the climate requires sustained and consistent action over an extended period.

zh: AXA和UBS，再加上波茨坦气候影响研究所（Potstam Institute for Climate Impact Research ） 、 CDP（碳披露计划）以及欧盟气候-KIC（知识和情报协会）最近在柏林召开了一次会议。
en: AXA and UBS, together with the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, CDP (formerly the Carbon Disclosure Project), and the EU’s Climate-KIC (Knowledge and Information Community) recently organized a conference in Berlin.

zh: 会上，他们与绿色投资和减少化石燃料投资顶级专家讨论了金融媒介如何帮助解决气候风险。
en: There, they discussed with leading experts in green investments and fossil-fuel divestment how financial intermediaries can help to address climate risks.

zh: 世界急需金融业的积极参与。
en: The financial industry’s active involvement is urgently needed.

zh: 在去年12月达成的巴黎气候协定上，世界各国同意将全球变暖幅度控制在2℃以内，这决定了世界必须做出快速进展的方向。
en: In the Paris climate agreement reached last December, countries worldwide agreed to limit global warming to well below 2° Celsius, thereby defining the track on which the world must progress rapidly.

zh: 在未来十五年中，据估计需要93万亿美元用于低碳基础设施投资。
en: Over the next 15 years, an estimated $93 trillion will be needed for investments in low-carbon infrastructure.

zh: 光靠政府出资无法满足这一需求，因此金融业必须帮助弥补缺口。
en: Government funding alone cannot meet this demand, so the financial sector must help fill the gap.

zh: 金融机构可以引导资本流向减轻和适应气候变化的前瞻性计划，从而保护客户资产免收气候风险和与地球变暖有关的经济风险的影响。
en: By redirecting capital flows toward proactive efforts to mitigate and adapt to climate change, financial institutions can protect client assets from global climate risks, and from the economic risks that will attend a warming planet.

zh: 它们也在彰显对子孙后代福祉的社会责任。
en: They are also demonstrating their social responsibility for the wellbeing of future generations.

zh: 但为变化融资需要改变金融。
en: But financing change requires changing finance.

zh: 而这一过程已经“上路 ” 。
en: And this process is already underway.

zh: 世界银行等开发机构正在重新考虑投资政策。
en: Development institutions such as the World Bank are reconsidering their investment policies.

zh: 而私人部门越来越热衷于“绿色”债券、贷款、指数和基础设施投资。
en: And, in the private sector, there is growing enthusiasm for “green” bonds, loans, indices, and infrastructure investments.

zh: 但是，欧盟委员会指出，全世界只有不到1%的机构资产投资于环境友好型基础设施资产。
en: Still, as the European Commission notes, less than 1% of institutional assets worldwide are invested in environmentally friendly infrastructure assets.

zh: 目前利率处于历史低位，有吸引力的投资机会也全面短缺，因此这是利用投资者对绿色金融产品兴趣日涨的理想实际。
en: Given historically low interest rates and the general lack of attractive investment options, this is an ideal moment to tap into investors’ growing appetite for green financial products.

zh: 许多大型金融机构最近联手参与了一个促进减少化石燃料投资的全球性计划。
en: Many large financial institutions have recently joined a global initiative promoting fossil-fuel divestment.

zh: 研究发现表明，要想满足巴黎协定，将全球变暖幅度限制在2℃之内，从2010年到本世纪末全球二氧化碳排放量必须限制在一万亿吨以内。 这意味着大部分可用煤炭、石油和天然气储量都必须留在地下。
en: Research findings indicate that global CO2 emissions must be restricted to less than one trillion metric tons between 2010 and the end of the century to comply with the Paris agreement and limit global warming to below 2°C. This means that most available coal, oil, and gas reserves must stay in the ground.

zh: 因此，化石燃料能源资源投资将继续逐渐丧失价值，最终被搁置。
en: As a result, investments in fossil-fuel energy sources will continue to lose value over time, eventually becoming stranded.

zh: 因此，金融业对这类投资进行重新评估不但有助于稳定气候，也能更好地保护客户的投资，还能通过防止“碳泡沫”卷土重来帮助稳定经济。
en: Thus, the financial sector’s revaluation of such holdings not only helps to stabilize the climate, but also better protects its clients’ investments, and, by preventing the creation of a “carbon bubble,” helps to stabilize economies.

zh: 但甩卖这些投资仍然不够，所解放出来的资产必须重新引导流向更加可持续的企业。
en: But selling off these holdings will not suffice; the freed-up assets must also be redirected to more sustainable businesses.

zh: 对于有志于此的金融机构和投资者来说，他们急切地需要更好地理解重要其后相关投资的风险，金融稳定局（FSB）将该风险分为三类：物理风险、过度风险和责任风险。
en: For financial institutions and investors to do their part, they urgently need a better understanding of the relevant climate-related investment risks, which the Financial Stability Board (FSB) has divided into three categories: physical, transitional, and liability.

zh: 消息灵通的投资决策需要有科学基础的可靠数据和统一的标准评估这些风险，并量化分析其中的机会。
en: Informed investment decisions will require sound, scientifically grounded data and uniform standards to assess these risks, and to quantify opportunities against them.

zh: 因此，有效的披露是新框架的关键部分。
en: Effective disclosure will hence be a key part of any new framework.

zh: 一个由银行、保险、机构投资者、评级机构、咨询公司和审计机构代表组成的FSB小组目前正在制定自愿标准，以便公司向相关利益者（不管是投资者还是贷款人）提供一致和可比较的气候相关气候披露。
en: An FSB taskforce – comprising representatives from banks, insurers, institutional investors, rating agencies, consultants, and auditors – is currently shaping voluntary standards, so that companies provide consistent and comparable climate-related financial disclosures to their stakeholders, whether investors or lenders.

zh: 这还将让公司能够获得关于自身变革潜力的宝贵洞见，体现一个经过时间考验的原则：可测量方可管理。
en: This will also allow companies to gain valuable insights into their own potential for change, reflecting a time-honored principle: what gets measured, gets managed.

zh: 这绝非易事。
en: This is no easy task.

zh: 比如，它们自身的碳足迹无法引导投资流向正确方向。
en: For example, carbon footprints on their own will not steer investments in the right direction.

zh: 这些数字并不能识别最优秀的环境友好型解决方案，只能揭示哪些公司目前排放了最多的温室气体。
en: Instead of identifying the champions of environmentally friendly solutions, these figures merely reveal which companies currently emit the most greenhouse gases.

zh: 有意义的披露标准必须考虑因行业而异的信息，以及对低碳经济转型的商业战略的影响。
en: Meaningful disclosure standards must take account of sector-specific information and the impact on business strategies of the transition toward a low-carbon economy.

zh: 所有签署了巴黎协定的国家我们，都可以期待它们采取各种措施以使其能够实施去碳化战略。
en: All the governments that signed the Paris agreement can now be expected to adopt a range of measures to enable them to implement their de-carbonization strategies.

zh: 在这样的背景下，碳定价将是政策工具箱中的关键工具。
en: In this context, carbon pricing will be an essential part of the policy toolbox.

zh: 一些政府已经采取措施，通过税收或市场激励促进绿色产品开发。
en: Some governments have already taken steps to promote the development of green products, via tax or market incentives.

zh: 总体而言，这些法律框架变化必须支持而不是阻挠私人金融部门对抗气候变化的努力。
en: Overall, such changes to legal frameworks must support, not impede, the private financial sector’s efforts to tackle climate change.

zh: 为对一些国家的政府来说过于昂贵、因而无法独力融资，但又对我们的能源体系转型至关重要的基础设施项目 — — 比如风力发电厂和长途输电线 — — 提供融资需要新类型的全球基础设施债券。
en: Financing the infrastructure projects that are too expensive for some national governments to finance on their own, but that are essential to the transformation of our energy system – such as wind farms and long-distance power lines – will require a new class of global infrastructure bonds.

zh: 在过去，政府鼓励政府债券的投资。
en: In the past, governments have encouraged investment in government bonds.

zh: 如今，为了增加清洁基础设施的私人投资，必须考虑投资者保护措施和纠纷解决机制。
en: Now, in order to increase private investment in building up clean infrastructure, investor-protection measures and dispute-resolution mechanisms must be considered.

zh: 金融业已经准备好引领向可持续性的转变。
en: The financial sector is ready to spearhead the shift to sustainability.

zh: 在未来一年中，德国将担任G20主席国，它将有机会说服合作伙伴成立完善的框架鼓励金融业发生能确保平稳过渡到低碳经济的转变。
en: When Germany takes over the G20 presidency next year, it will have the opportunity to convince its partners to create an adequate framework to encourage change in the financial sector that ensures a smooth adjustment to a low-carbon economy.

zh: 对公共和私人行动方而言，现在正是行动良机。
en: For both public and private actors, the time to act is now.

zh: 一个气候友好的金融体系
en: A Climate-Friendly Financial System

zh: 北京／法兰克福 － 作为2015年巴黎会议之后最重要的一届气候大会，今年的谈判正在波兰城市卡托维兹展开。
en: BEIJING/FRANKFURT – The climate conference now underway in Katowice, Poland, has been billed as the most consequential since the 2015 summit, which produced the Paris climate agreement.

zh: 政府间气候变化专门委员会（IPCC）发布的特别报告和全球各地此消彼长的自然灾害，引起了全球民众对气候变化前所未有的关切。
en: Amid unprecedented public concern over the threat posed by climate change – fueled by an alarming recent report by the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), not to mention devastating natural disasters around the world – negotiators are seeking to establish a set of rules for meeting the Paris commitments.

zh: 在这一背景下，各国代表正在寻求确立一系列规则以落实《巴黎协定 》 ， 而关乎成败的往往是资金问题。
en: But, as is so often the case, success will depend on finance.

zh: 在此前的气候谈判中，发达国家曾许下提供资金援助的承诺 — — 在2020年前实现向发展中国家每年提供1000亿美元资金支持，并在之后持续增加。
en: The world’s advanced economies have made major financial commitments in previous climate negotiations. Yet it is far from certain that they will fulfill their promises, beginning with the provision of $100 billion annually to developing countries by 2020.

zh: 很难说发达国家能否真正履行承诺。 《联合国气候变化框架公约》融资问题常设委员会最新发布的《气候融资两年期评估》显示， 发达国家在2016年向发展中国家提供的公共资金支持达到570亿美元。
en: According to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change’s Standing Committee on Finance (SCF), public finance from developed to developing countries to support climate-change mitigation and adaptation amounted to $57 billion in 2016.

zh: 如果将被动员起来的私人投资计算在内，则有700亿美元。
en: When taking account of private finance mobilized by public support, flows reached over $70 billion in 2016.

zh: 但是，IPCC特别报告指出，为实现将全球温升控制在1.5摄氏度以内，从现在至2035年，全球每年在清洁能源领域的投资需求就有2.4万亿美元。
en: However, that is a small fraction of the $2.4 trillion that the world needs to invest in clean energy every year between now and 2035 to keep global temperatures within 1.5°C of pre-industrial levels, as calculated by the IPCC.

zh: 与这一估算相比，融资问题常设委员会估算的气候融资实际规模依然微不足道。
en: Whether rich countries honor climate financing commitments made in previous negotiations, and the degree to which developing countries can accept flexibility in how financial flows are measured, will be key to advancing the climate talks at this critical time. But, above all, climate risk and consideration of long-term sustainability will need to be embedded in the world’s financial system – from banks, asset owners, and managers to insurance companies and the capital markets that facilitate financial actors’ transactions.

zh: 发达国家如何尊重其就提供资金支持的许下承诺，以及发展中国家能接多大程度上接受衡量资金支持中的灵活度，这两点是推动此刻气候谈判的关键。
en: The good news is that the world is already moving in this direction, thanks partly to the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, formed in 2015 by the Financial Stability Board and the G20 Sustainable Finance Study Group.

zh: 但不管怎样，气候风险以及长期可持续发展的思想都需要被纳入全球金融体系，这个系统包括银行、资产所有者及管理者、保险公司以及促进各方交易的资本市场。
en: Already, the task force has done much to encourage financial institutions and companies to understand, assess, and disclose the extent of the climate risks they face.

zh: 好消息是，全球在这一方向上取得了一定进展：比如G20金融稳定委员会于2015年组成的气候相关金融信息披露工作组，以及G20可持续金融研究小组，这些机制鼓励金融机构和企业去理解、评估和披露其面临的气候风险程度。
en: The China-United Kingdom Green Finance Taskforce, for example, has established a group of British and Chinese financial institutions to pilot TCFD reporting. It has also developed a set of “Green Investment Principles” to promote low-carbon investments in the region comprising China’s Belt and Road Initiative.

zh: 还有其他的一些框架机制正在发挥作用：中英绿色金融工作组确立了多个中国和英国金融公司开展气候信息披露试点 ； 《 “一带一路”绿色投资原则》推动全球投资者在“一带一路”沿线国家开展低碳投资。
en: Then there is Climate Action 100+, an investor-led initiative that seeks to motivate companies to achieve the Paris agreement’s goals by improving corporate governance on climate change, curbing emissions, and strengthening climate-related financial disclosures.

zh: 管理资产超过32万亿美元的310个投资机构已经加入了“气候行动100+”倡议，呼吁企业改善气候变化治理，控制排放并加强气候相关金融信息披露。
en: So far, 310 investors with more than $32 trillion in assets under management have signed on to the initiative.

zh: 虽然基于市场的倡议是推动创新的重要因素，但在激活绿色金融、确保气候风险披露等工作需要政府和监管者更多地开展交流合作。
en: While market-based initiatives are important drivers of innovation, governments and regulators also have a crucial role to play in activating green finance and ensuring that climate risks are measured and reported accurately.

zh: 因此，欧盟和中国引导低碳融资的措施特别引人注目。
en: Here, steps taken by the European Union and China to steer finance toward low-carbon assets stand out.

zh: 欧盟的《发展绿色和清洁经济行动计划》促进各方制定更具雄心的议程，推动向可持续金融体系转型。
en: The EU’s Action Plan for a greener and cleaner economy has spurred an ambitious agenda to advance the transition to a sustainable financial system.

zh: 欧盟在完善金融领域评估和披露可持续发展风险相关法规的同时，还在推动制定共同标准，发展绿色债券等金融工具，促进融资直接流向环保型项目和企业。
en: Draft regulations are designed to encourage financial actors to assess and disclose sustainability risk, while moving toward the establishment of common standards to promote the financial instruments – such as green bonds – that can help direct funding to environment-friendly projects and companies.

zh: 不久前欧盟国家财政部长们同意在三年内将要求银行强制性披露环境、社会和治理风险。
en: EU finance ministers have also just agreed to begin requiring banks to disclose environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks within three years.

zh: 在中国，国务院在2016年宣布了一套全面的绿色金融发展指导意见，中央银行和部分地方政府已经对绿色贷款和绿色债券给予货币或财政激励措施。
en: As for China, in 2016 the State Council announced a set of comprehensive guidelines for green finance, and the central bank and some local governments have introduced monetary and fiscal incentives for green loans and bonds.

zh: 此外，中国证监会证券投资基金业协会最近发布了基金行业绿色投资指引，呼吁机构投资者将环境、社会和治理（ESG）因素纳入决策过程。
en: Moreover, the Asset Management Association of the China Securities Regulatory Commission recently released green investment guidelines for the asset-management industry, calling for ESG considerations to be integrated into institutional investors’ decision-making.

zh: 证监会宣布还宣布了于2020年前要求所有上市公司强制性披露环境信息的计划。
en: The CSRC has also announced a plan to require all listed companies to disclose environmental information by 2020.

zh: 在国际范围来看，去年底成立的监管机构绿色金融网络汇集了法国、中国、德国等21个国家的金融监管机构和央行。
en: At the international level, there is the Central Banks and Supervisors Network for Greening the Financial System.

zh: 该网络的成员意识到气候变化对金融稳定的威胁，承认必须通过审慎监管等方式评估和管理风险。
en: Created at the end of last year, the NGFS brings together financial regulators and central banks from 21 countries – including France, China, and Germany – that recognize the threat to financial stability posed by climate change, and the need to assess and manage that risk, in part through prudential supervision.

zh: 风险管理的一个核心因素是，银行和投资者必须将投资组合从高排放企业和项目向低碳资产转移。
en: A central element of such risk management is for banks and investors to shift their portfolios away from high-emitting companies and projects, toward low-carbon assets.

zh: IPCC1.5摄氏度特别报告明确指出，我们必须付出前所未有的努力，才能避免气候变化的最坏影响。
en: As the IPCC’s recent report makes plain, avoiding the worst effects of climate change will require action on an unprecedented scale – starting immediately.

zh: 各国的政策制定者必须确保公共和私有资金的流向与气候议程相一致，并创造良好条件使金融产业成为低碳未来的促成者而非阻挠者。
en: Policymakers in national capitals must ensure that both public and private financial flows align with the climate agenda, and that the right conditions are created to make the global financial sector the facilitator of, rather than a barrier to, a low-carbon future.

zh: 银行业的合法性危机
en: Finance’s Crisis of Legitimacy

zh: 华盛顿特区 — — 巴克莱银行前CEO博达文（Robert Diamond）日前的辞职标志着一个分水岭。
en: WASHINGTON, DC – The recent departure of Robert Diamond from Barclays marks a watershed.

zh: 当然，大银行的CEO被迫辞职并非没有先例。
en: To be sure, CEOs of major banks have been forced out before.

zh: 普林斯（Charles Prince）丢掉花旗集团CEO的工作，是因为在2008年金融危机的酝酿阶段，他的决策过于冒险。 瑞银集团前CEO郭儒博（Oswald Grübel）则由于没能防止规模为23亿美元的无授权交易而被扫地出门。
en: Chuck Prince lost his job at Citigroup over excessive risk-taking in the run-up to the financial crisis of 2008, and, more recently, Oswald Grübel of UBS was pushed out for failing to prevent unauthorized trading to the tune of $2.3 billion.

zh: 可博达文是银行家中的翘楚。
en: But Diamond was a banker supposedly at the top of his game.

zh: 据说，巴克莱银行没靠政府支持就挺过了2008~2009年的危机。
en: Barclays, it was claimed, had come through the 2008-2009 crisis without benefiting from government support.

zh: 而且，即便这家银行近期被查出多项违规，包括违规向客户销售产品和虚报利率，博达文仍能将自己洗脱干系。
en: And, while his bank had been found in violation of various rules recently, including on products sold to consumers and on how it reported interest rates, Diamond had managed to distance himself from the damage.

zh: 媒体报道认为，监管机构原本想放博达文一马 — — 直到遭遇严重的政治反弹。
en: Press reports indicate that regulators were willing to give Diamond a free pass – right up to the moment when a serious political backlash took hold.

zh: 博达文开始反击，指责起英格兰银行来。
en: Diamond started to fight back, pointing an accusatory finger at the Bank of England.

zh: 事情到了这个份儿上，他非走不可了。
en: At that point, he had to go.

zh: 博达文在巴克莱的垮台，人们可以从中得出三个教训。
en: There are three broader lessons of Diamond’s demise at Barclays.

zh: 首先，他遭遇的政治反弹并非来自后座议员或军方观察员（uniformed spectators）此类边缘角色。
en: First, the political backlash was not from backbenchers or uninformed spectators on the margins of the mainstream.

zh: 英国各党派的顶尖政治家都众口一词谴责巴克莱的行径，尤其是谴责其在Libor丑闻中被暴露出来的系统性虚报利率一事。
en: Top politicians from all parties in the United Kingdom were united in condemning Barclays’ actions, particularly with regard to its systemic cheating on the reporting of interest rates, exposed in the Libor scandal.

zh: （Libor，伦敦银行同业拆放利率是全世界金融活动的一项关键指标，其作用包括为衍生品定价等等。 ）
en: (The London Interbank Offered Rate is a key benchmark for borrowing and lending around the world, including for the pricing of derivatives).

zh: 说真的，英国财政大臣欧思邦（George Osborne）甚至说 ： “ 在一般商业里，欺骗是一宗罪，为什么在银行业就不该是呢？
en: Indeed, Chancellor of the Exchequer George Osborne went so far as to say, “Fraud is a crime in ordinary business; why shouldn’t it be so in banking?”

zh: ”他这几乎是在明说巴克莱有欺诈行径 — — 这可是来自英国财相的严重指控。
en: His clear implication is that fraud was committed at Barclays – a serious allegation from Britain’s finance minister.

zh: 经过了金融行业丑闻大规模爆发的5年，人们的容忍度已被消磨殆尽。
en: After five years of global financial-sector scandals on a grand scale, patience is wearing thin.

zh: 诚如埃德瓦多·波特（Eduardo Porter）在《纽约时报》上写的：
en: As Eduardo Porter of The New York Times put it,

zh: “市场越大，孕育的欺诈越大。
en: “Bigger markets allow bigger frauds.

zh: 公司越大，资产负债表越复杂，就有越多的地方去藏匿骗局。
en: Bigger companies, with more complex balance sheets, have more places to hide them.

zh: 而银行，一旦大到没有一个政府敢让它们垮掉的程度，就有最大的动机去行骗。 ”
en: And banks, when they get big enough that no government will let them fail, have the biggest incentive of all.”

zh: 其次，博达文显然认为，他可以挑战英国的权势集团。
en: Second, Diamond apparently thought that he could take on the British establishment.

zh: 巴克莱员工泄漏出来一段据称是博达文同英格兰银行副行长保罗·塔克（Paul Tucker）的谈话，其内容似乎意味着，是英格兰银行授意巴克莱虚报利率的。
en: His staff leaked the contents of a conversation he claimed to have had with Paul Tucker, a senior Bank of England official, suggesting that the BoE had told Barclays to report inaccurate interest-rate numbers.

zh: 博达文显然忘记了，任何一家银行，只要它的资产负债表同所在国经济高度相关，那么它的持续存在和为股东盈利的能力就全然依赖同监管者维持良好关系。
en: Diamond apparently forgot that the continued existence of any bank with a balance sheet that is large relative to its home economy – and its ability to earn a return for shareholders – depends entirely on maintaining a good relationship with regulators.

zh: 巴克莱的总资产约有2.5万亿美元，同英国的年均GDP规模相近，以不同的方式衡量，是世界第五大或第八大银行。
en: Barclays has total assets of around $2.5 trillion – roughly the size of the UK’s annual GDP – and is either the fifth- or eighth-largest bank in the world, depending on how one measures balance sheets.

zh: 这个规模的银行都得仰赖巨大的隐性政府担保，这就是“大到倒不得”的意义。
en: Banks at this scale benefit from huge implicit government guarantees; this is what it means to be “too big to fail.”

zh: 博达文显然被自己的修辞说服了 — — 真的以为他和他的银行对英国的经济繁荣不可或缺。
en: Diamond apparently believed his own rhetoric – that he and his bank are critical to economic prosperity in the UK.

zh: 监管者们将计就计，顺势把他赶下台。
en: The regulators called his bluff and forced him to resign.

zh: 巴克莱的股价随之略有回升。
en: Barclays’ stock price rose slightly on the news.

zh: 最后一个教训是，不论是在美国还是在欧洲大陆，民主政治和银行巨头之间还会有一场大决战。
en: The final lesson is that the big showdowns between democracy and big bankers are still to come – both in the United States and in continental Europe.

zh: 表面上看，银行依然强大，然而它们的合法性不断瓦解。
en: On the surface, the banks remain powerful, yet their legitimacy continues to crumble.

zh: 摩根大通的CEO詹姆斯·戴蒙（James Dimon）今年早些时候由于轻率冒险导致将近60亿美元的巨亏（也许可以把那称为“三个郭儒博”的大失败 ） ， 可他的工作显然还比较稳固。
en: Jamie Dimon, CEO of JP Morgan Chase, presided this year over reckless risk-taking to the tune of nearly $6 billion (we might call it a “three Grübel” debacle), yet his job apparently remains secure.

zh: 戴蒙甚至仍然保留了在纽约联储银行董事会的席位，尽管纽约联储不仅深度参与了对摩根大通交易亏损的调查，而且也参与了后者可能卷入Libor丑闻的调查。
en: Dimon even remains on the board of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, despite the fact that the New York Fed is deeply involved in the investigation not only of JP Morgan Chase’s trading losses, but also of its potential involvement in the broadening Libor scandal.

zh: 正如游说机构Better Markets的主席丹尼斯·凯勒赫（Dennis Kelleher）在近期国会听证会上所言，多德—弗兰科法案已经通过两年了，可是美国的银行体系依然在不遗余力地瓦解���何实质性的改革，而且卓有成效。
en: As Dennis Kelleher, the president of the advocacy group Better Markets, documented in recent congressional testimony, two years after the passage of the Dodd-Frank legislation, the US banking system continues to fight hard – and effectively – to undermine meaningful reform.

zh: （凯勒赫的证词及公开陈述都是必读的好材料。 ）
en: (Kelleher’s testimony is a must-read assessment, as is his opening statement to the hearing).

zh: 但是，进步毕竟还是有的。
en: But progress is nonetheless being made.

zh: 在公众眼里，戴蒙是大银行抵制改革的代表形象，反复而且公开地朝他“扔臭鸡蛋”可以大壮主张改革者的声势，后者主张节制银行过度且不负责任的冒险。
en: Dimon is the public face of megabanks’ resistance to reform; repeated and public egg on this particular face strengthens those who want to rein in these banks’ excessive and irresponsible risk-taking.

zh: 与此同时，欧洲的局势似乎是爆炸性的。
en: Meanwhile, the European situation looks explosive.

zh: 欧盟的银行监管手段鼓励金融机构囤积政府债券，所谓“无风险”资产。
en: The European Union’s approach to bank regulation encouraged financial institutions to load up on government debt – supposedly a “risk-free” asset.

zh: 如今，鉴于欧元区外围国家的主权债务危机加深，政府违约有可能拖垮那些大银行。
en: Now, given the profound sovereign-debt crisis in the eurozone periphery, government defaults threaten to take down the big banks.

zh: 欧洲央行向银行注入了大量紧急“流动性 ” 。 这些钱却被后者用来购买更多的政府债券。
en: The European Central Bank has provided a great deal of emergency “liquidity” funding to banks, which they use to buy even more government debt.

zh: 这虽然短期内压低了那些债券的利率，但也令一旦违约后的潜在损失变得更大。
en: This holds down interest rates on that debt in the short run, but creates even bigger potential losses in the case of potential default.

zh: 在所有发达经济体，银行和政治的关系都是剪不断理还乱。
en: Banks and politics are deeply intertwined in all advanced economies.

zh: 博达文最终发现，政治家的牌大过银行家 — — 至少在英国是如此。
en: Diamond discovered that, ultimately, politicians trump bankers – at least in the UK.

zh: 然而真正重要的是合法性和公众舆论。
en: But what really matters is legitimacy and informed public opinion.

zh: 你当真相信以当前形式存在的大银行，对其他的私营部门是有益的，因此有助于经济增长和创造就业？ 这个想法似乎变得日益可疑。
en: Do you really believe the increasingly dubious notion that megabanks, as currently constituted, are good for the rest of the private sector, and thus for economic growth and job creation?

zh: 或者说，你已经开始认真思考一种日趋主流的论调 — — 全球大银行和它们的领导，已经变得过于强大和危险了？
en: Or do you begin to consider more seriously the increasingly mainstream proposition that global megabanks and their leaders have simply become too powerful and dangerous?

zh: 瓦鲁法基斯效应？
en: The Varoufakis Effect?

zh: 雅典—汉堡贝伦堡（Berenberg）投资银行的霍格尔·施米丁（Holger Schmieding）在其2015年年终总结中警告客户，现在应该担心政治风险。
en: ATHENS – In his end-of-2015 missive, Holger Schmieding of the Hamburg investment bank Berenberg warned his firm’s clients that what they should be worrying about now is political risk.

zh: 他拿出下面的图表来说明问题：该图标显示希腊商业信心在2015年春崩溃，直到我从财政部长任上辞职后才开始反弹。
en: To illustrate, he posted the diagram below, showing how business confidence collapsed in Greece during the late spring of 2015, and picked up again only after my resignation from the finance ministry.

zh: 施米丁将这称为“瓦鲁法基斯效应 ” 。
en: Schmieding chose to call this the “Varoufakis effect.”

zh: 毫无疑问，投资者应该担心当下的政治风险 — — 非常担心才对，包括政客和官僚给经济造成巨大伤害的能力。
en: There is no doubt that investors should be worried – very worried – about political risk nowadays, including the capacity of politicians and bureaucrats to do untold damage to an economy.

zh: 但他们还应该担心既没有能力，也没有兴趣区分因果关系和相关性，或者资不抵债和流动性不足的分析师。
en: But they must also be wary of analysts who are either incapable of, or uninterested in, distinguishing between causality and correlation, and between insolvency and illiquidity.

zh: 换句话说，他们应该担心施米丁之流。
en: In other words, they must be wary of analysts like Schmieding.

zh: 希腊商业信心确实在我担任财政部长后几个月发生了崩溃。
en: Business confidence in Greece did indeed plummet a few months after I became Finance Minister.

zh: 并且在我辞职后一个月，它就反弹了。
en: And it did pick up a month after my resignation.

zh: 相关性显而易见。
en: The correlation is palpable.

zh: 但其中存在因果关系吗？
en: But is the causality?

zh: 考虑以下例子。
en: Consider the following example.

zh: 2001年9月（在纽约和华盛顿发生恐怖袭击后）商业信心有所下降，当时美国财政部长是保罗·奥尼尔（Paul O’Neill ） 。
en: Business confidence fell in September 2001 (following the terror attacks on New York and Washington, DC), while Paul O’Neill was US Treasury Secretary.

zh: 施米丁会因此拿出一张图表来证明这一下降是“奥尼尔效应”吗？
en: Would Schmieding label a chart showing that decline the “O’Neill Effect”?

zh: 当然不会：商业信心的下降与奥尼尔毫无关系，完全是因为对全球安全的恐慌造成的。
en: Of course not: the drop in business confidence had nothing to do with O’Neill and everything to do with fears about global security.

zh: 与奥尼尔任职的相关性完全不重要。
en: The correlation with O’Neill’s tenure was irrelevant.

zh: 类似地，在希腊的例子中，商业信心的崩溃就发生在我的眼皮底下。
en: Similarly, in the case of Greece, the collapse in business confidence happened under my watch.

zh: 但原因是我国债权人，即所谓的三驾马车（欧盟委员会、欧洲央行和IMF）明确表示它们将关掉我国银行系统，以迫使我国政府接受新的“延期大吉 ” （ extend-and-pretend）贷款协议。
en: But the cause was that our creditors, the so-called Troika (the European Commission, the European Central Bank, and the International Monetary Fund), made clear that they would close down our banking system to force our government to accept a fresh extend-and-pretend loan agreement.

zh: 在做出这些威胁前，希腊的商业信心其实是上升的。
en: Before these threats were issued, business confidence was actually picking up in Greece.

zh: 事实上，在我向伦敦金融城投资界展示我的改革和财政方案后的那一天，希腊股市大幅反弹。
en: Indeed, the day after I presented my reform and fiscal proposals to the City of London investor community, stocks rallied impressively.

zh: （事实上，在我担任财政部长期间，真实GDP增长要快于2014年后两个季度，也就是施米丁定义为信心增加的时期。 ）
en: (Indeed, during my tenure in the finance ministry, real GDP grew more than it had done during the last two quarters of 2014, which Schmieding identifies as a period of increasing confidence.)

zh: 那么，是什么导致我的任期中商业信心的大幅下跌？
en: So, what caused the huge drop in business confidence during my tenure?

zh: 是我的政策方案 — — 由我的杰弗里·萨克斯（Jeff Sachs）联合执笔（英国前保守党财政大臣诺曼·拉蒙特（Norman Lamont ） 、 哈佛大学的拉里·萨默斯（Larry Summers）和特克萨斯大学的詹姆斯·加尔布雷斯（James K. Galbraith）等人亦有贡献 ） — —造成的吗？
en: Was it my policy proposals – jointly authored with Jeff Sachs (with input from Norman Lamont, a former Tory Chancellor of the Exchequer in the United Kingdom, Harvard’s Larry Summers, and James K. Galbraith of the University of Texas) – that were responsible?

zh: 还是由三驾马车明确的银行关门威胁造成的？ （在我们敢于在去年7月让全民公决决定我国债权人的最后通牒时真���实施了。
en: Or was it the Troika’s explicit threat of bank closures (which were actually imposed when we dared to put our creditors’ ultimatum to the Greek people in a referendum last July)?

zh: ）换句话说，这是“瓦鲁法基斯效应”还是“三驾马车效应 ” ？
en: In other words, was it the “Varoufakis effect” or the “Troika effect”?

zh: 要以有助于投资者的方式回答这个问题，分析师必须至少研究一下观察到的相关性是否指向因果关系。
en: To answer this question in ways that are helpful to investors, an analyst must at least make an effort to establish whether the observed correlation points to a causal link.

zh: 读一读我们的政策方案，并将之与三驾马车的计划相比较会有所助益。
en: Reading our policy proposals and comparing them to the Troika’s program would have helped.

zh: 不幸的是，这需要艰苦的工作，一些分析师不愿意去做。
en: Unfortunately, this would have required work that some analysts prefer not to do.

zh: 重要的问题是我们与三驾马车对着干 — — 我国2015年1月选举的中心话题 — — 是否正确，或者我国是否应该在债权人的“希腊计划”上签字。
en: The relevant question is whether we were right to confront the Troika – a central plank in our January 2015 electoral platform – or whether we should have signed up to our creditors’ “Greek program.”

zh: 我的关电视，我们别无选择，只能抵制三驾马车的计划。
en: My view is that we had no alternative but to resist the Troika’s plan.

zh: 原因很简单：希腊国在2010年初已经破产。
en: The reason is simple: the Greek state became insolvent in early 2010.

zh: 从2010年5月开始，这一破产状态被一而再、再而三的“延期大吉”贷款所解决，这些贷款的条件是我国保证降低国民收入、投资和信用。
en: From May 2010, this insolvency was addressed by means of sequential extend-and-pretend loans on conditions that were guaranteed to shrink national income, investment, and credit.

zh: 一个偿债能力问题因为一直被装作仅仅是流动性问题而愈演愈烈。
en: A case of insolvency was made increasingly worse by continuing to pretend that it was a mere liquidity problem.

zh: 希腊经济在2014年底有所好转了吗？
en: Was the Greek economy on the mend in late 2014?

zh: 当然没有。
en: Of course not.

zh: 名义GDP从未停止下跌，公共和私人债务越来越不可持续，投资和信用一直萎靡不振。
en: Nominal GDP never stopped shrinking, public and private debt continued to become less and less sustainable, and all along investment and credit remained comatose.

zh: 如果不进行债务重组，降低初级预算盈余（扣除债务偿付）目标，成立“坏银行”处理不良贷款，拿出全面改革日程解决最糟糕的寻租问题，希腊必将陷入持久萧条。
en: Without debt restructuring, a low target for the primary budget surplus (net of debt payments), a “bad bank” to deal with non-performing loans, and a comprehensive reform agenda that tackles the worst cases of rent seeking, Greece is condemned to permanent depression.

zh: 可惜，担架马车出于政治动机否定了我国的政策方案，对它们丝毫不感兴趣。
en: Alas, the Troika was in politically motivated denial and deeply uninterested in our policy proposals.

zh: 一次又一次，它们所要的只是投降。
en: Time and again, they simply demanded capitulation.

zh: 平心而论，我们本可以更好地处理这一冲突。
en: To be sure, we could have handled that confrontation better.

zh: 但对一名分析师来说，谴责这一金融暴力的受害者不仅道德不正确，对其客户来说也是非常糟糕的服务（比如，其客户可能因此错误地认为希腊的情况正在因为瓦鲁法基斯被迫下台而好转 ） 。
en: But for an analyst to blame the victim of such financial violence is not only morally reprehensible, but also constitutes terrible service to his clients (who, for example, may be lulled into a false sense that Greece is on the mend now that Varoufakis has been forced out).

zh: 谢天谢地，勤勉的分析师还是有的，比如，穆罕默德·艾利安（Mohamed El-Erian）就是明智的投资者可以信赖的对象。
en: Thankfully, there are diligent analysts, like Mohamed El-Erian, to whom sensible investors can turn.

zh: 这些分析师的结论很明确：2015年希腊衰退是拜“三驾马车效应”所赐。
en: And their verdict is clear: Greece’s downturn in 2015 was due to the “Troika effect.”

zh: 是的，欧洲的政治风险显而易见。
en: Yes, political risk in Europe is clear and present.

zh: 但它源自三驾马车不愿改革自身、反思失败的政策。
en: But it emanates from the Troika’s unwillingness to reform itself and to rethink its failed policies.

zh: 作者补充：本文发表后，据披露，施米丁用来说明“瓦鲁法基斯效应”的图表对于真相做了诸多保留，这更加清楚地揭示了“三架马车效应”的险恶。
en: Author’s postscript: Following the publication of this article, the pernicious “Troika effect” became even clearer when it was revealed that the chart Holger Schmieding used to demonstrate the “Varoufakis effect” was rather economical with the truth.

zh: 原始图表（发布在这里）清楚地表明，2014年底商业信心就已经崩盘，远早于希腊选举和我被任命为财政部长。
en: The original chart (published here) shows clearly that business confidence dove at the end of 2014, well before the Greek election and my appointment as Minister of Finance.

zh: 在施米丁致投资者的信中，横轴被拉长，以显示商业信心在进入2015年后的下跌，当时我在任。
en: In Schmieding’s letter to his investors, the horizontal axis was stretched to show that business confidence fell well into 2015, once I was in office.

zh: 没有比这更能说明投资者绝对需要更加担心施米丁这样的分析师得了。
en: Nothing could better illustrate that investors have much to fear from analysts like Schmieding.

zh: 金融危机的政治后果
en: The Political Consequences of Financial Crises

zh: 伦敦—我想必绝非唯一这样的金融学教授：在为学生设定文论主题时，会提出诸如“在你看来，全球金融危机的主因是政府对金融市场的干预太多还是太少？ ”这样的问题。
en: LONDON – I may not be the only finance professor who, when setting essay topics for his or her students, has resorted to a question along the following lines: “In your view, was the global financial crisis caused primarily by too much government intervention in financial markets, or by too little?”

zh: 在面对这类是/还是问题时，我最近带的一批学生分成了三个阵营。
en: When confronted with this either/or question, my most recent class split three ways.

zh: 大概有三分之一的学生被有效市场假说的故弄玄虚所折服，他们认为政府有原罪。
en: Roughly a third, mesmerized by the meretricious appeal of the Efficient Market Hypothesis, argued that governments were the original sinners.

zh: 政府的考虑不周的干预 — — 特别是美国政府支持的按揭承销商房利美和房地美，以及社区再投资法（Community Reinvestment Act ） — —扭曲了市场激励。
en: Their ill-conceived interventions – notably the US-backed mortgage underwriters Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, as well as the Community Reinvestment Act – distorted market incentives.

zh: 有些人甚至信奉美国自由派罗恩·保罗（Ron Paul）的观点，批判美联储作为最后贷款人的存在。
en: Some even embraced the argument of the US libertarian Ron Paul, blaming the very existence of the Federal Reserve as a lender of last resort.

zh: 另有三分之一的学生的政治立场正好相反，他们认为美联储前主席艾伦·格林斯潘（Alan Greenspan）是罪魁祸首。
en: Another third, at the opposite end of the political spectrum, saw former Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan as the villain.

zh: 格林斯潘以不愿意干预金融市场而闻名，即使在杠杆大幅提高、资产价格看起来早已脱离现实支撑的情况下也是如此，这才是问题的根源。
en: It was Greenspan’s notorious reluctance to intervene in financial markets, even when leverage was growing dramatically and asset prices seemed to have lost touch with reality, that created the problem.

zh: 更广泛地说，西方政府的其象征性监管方针导致了市场在本世纪初失控。
en: More broadly, Western governments, with their light-touch approach to regulation, allowed markets to career out of control in the early years of this century.

zh: 剩下三分之一学生则两可之，认为政府在某些方面干预过多，在另一些方面干预过少。
en: The remaining third tried to have it both ways, arguing that governments intervened too much in some areas, and too little in others.

zh: 回避问题可不是通过考试的好办法；但学生们也许已经做过了深入思考。
en: Avoiding the question as put is not a sound test-taking strategy; but the students may have been onto something.

zh: 如今，危机已经过去了七年，政府和欧洲及美国的选民如何回答这一重要问题？
en: Now that the crisis is seven years behind us, how have governments and voters in Europe and North America answered this important question?

zh: 他们用行动证明了他们认为金融市场需要更严格的监管，还是相反，国家应该拒绝提供援助，让金融企业直面自身错误的全部后果？
en: Have they shown, by their actions, that they think financial markets need tighter controls or that, on the contrary, the state should repudiate bailouts and leave financial firms to face the full consequences of their own mistakes?

zh: 从政府的言辞和监管政策看，大部分政府属于骑墙派的那三分之一。
en: From their rhetoric and regulatory policies, it would appear that most governments have ended up in the third, fence-sitting camp.

zh: 诚然，它们实施了众多详细的控制，以前所未有的力度检查了银行的账目，并批准派发现金、任命重要董事甚至对董事会成员的职业描述。
en: Yes, they have implemented a plethora of detailed controls, scrutinizing banks’ books with unprecedented intensity and insisting on approving cash distributions, the appointment of key directors, and even job descriptions for board members.

zh: 但它们排除了一切未来政府或央行对告急金融机构的支持。
en: But they have ruled out any future government or central-bank support for ailing financial institutions.

zh: 现在，银行必须订好“生前遗嘱 ” ， 说明在没有当局支持的情况下如何进行清算和关门。
en: Banks must now produce “living wills” showing how they can be wound down without the authorities’ support.

zh: 当它们陷入麻烦时，政府将袖手旁观 ： “ 太大而不能倒”的时代已经结束了。
en: The government will wash its hands of them if they run into trouble: the era of “too big to fail” is over.

zh: 也许这一双轨制方针是不可避免的，不过了解其预期终点仍然是有裨益的。
en: Perhaps this two-track approach was inevitable, though it would be good to know the desired end-point.

zh: 这是一套市场纪律再次成为主导的制度，还是监管者将在可预见的未来凌驾于管理层之上？
en: Is it a system in which market discipline again dominates, or will regulators sit on the shoulders of management for the foreseeable future?

zh: 但选民的结论是什么？
en: But what have voters concluded?

zh: 在危机后的第一波选举中，从某种程度上看结论是明确的，但从另一个角度看又有些模糊。
en: In the first wave of post-crisis elections, the message was clear in one sense, and clouded in another.

zh: 危机爆发时在台上执政的���府，不管是左翼还是右翼，都被赶下了台，取而代之的是政治口号相反的政府。
en: Whichever government was in power when the crisis hit, whether left or right, was booted out and replaced by a government of the opposite political persuasion.

zh: 并非全部如此 — — 德国的默克尔可以证明 — — 但显然在美国、英国、法国和其他国家是如此。
en: That was not universally true – see Germany’s Angela Merkel – but it certainly was true in the United States, the United Kingdom, France, and elsewhere.

zh: 法国从右转向左，而英国从左转向右。
en: France moved from right to left, and the UK went from left to right.

zh: 但选民对政府的评价或多或少是一样的：你在台上，情况不好，所以请你下台。
en: But voters’ verdict on their governments was more or less identical: things went wrong on your watch, so out you go.

zh: 但如今，我们可以看到一个更加一致的趋势正在发展。
en: But now we can see a more consistent trend developing.

zh: 三位德国经济学家 — — 曼努埃尔·芬克（Manuel Funke ） 、 莫里茨·舒拉里克（Moritz Schularik）和克里斯托弗·特雷贝施（Christoph Trebesch）最近对西方国家过去150年中的800多次选举进行了出色的评估，并根据100起金融危机进行了排列分析。
en: Three German economists, Manuel Funke, Moritz Schularik, and Christoph Trebesch, have just produced a fascinating assessment based on more than 800 elections in Western countries over the last 150 years, the results of which they mapped against 100 financial crises.

zh: 他们的结论十分醒目 ： “ 金融危机后政治会急转向右。
en: Their headline conclusion is stark: “politics takes a hard right turn following financial crises.

zh: 平均而言，极右翼选票在系统性银行困境出现五年内会增加三分之一。 ”
en: On average, far-right votes increase by about a third in the five years following systemic banking distress.”

zh: 1929年华尔街崩盘后发生的20世纪30年代的大萧条是最显著、最令人担忧的例子，但这一趋势即便在斯堪的纳维亚国家也有迹可循，比如20世纪90年代银行危机之后。
en: The Great Depression of the 1930s, which followed the Wall Street crash of 1929, is the most obvious and worrying example that comes to mind, but the trend can be observed even in the Scandinavian countries, following banking crises there in the early 1990s.

zh: 因此，试图用法国总统奥朗德个人和政治上的不受欢迎来解释法国国民阵线的崛起是很牵强的。
en: So seeking to explain, say, the rise of the National Front in France in terms of President François Hollande’s personal and political unpopularity is not sensible.

zh: 有比奥朗德混乱的私生活和无力连同选民更加深刻的因素在起作用。
en: There are greater forces at work than his exotic private life and inability to connect with voters.

zh: 芬克、舒拉里克和特雷贝施的第二个重要结论是治理在金融危机后会更加困难，原因有二。
en: The second major conclusion that Funke, Schularik, and Trebesch draw is that governing becomes harder after financial crises, for two reasons.

zh: 极右翼的崛起带来了常常是支离破碎的政治局面，政党数量增加，执政党（不管是左翼还是右翼）所获选票比重降低。
en: The rise of the far right lies alongside a political landscape that is typically fragmented, with more parties, and a lower share of the vote going to the governing party, whether of the left or the right.

zh: 因此决定性的立法行动更加难以做出。
en: So decisive legislative action becomes more challenging.

zh: 与此同时，院外动员情况会出现爆发式增长：罢工更加普遍，时间更长；游行示威规模也会更大。
en: At the same time, a surge of extra-parliamentary mobilization occurs: more and longer strikes and more and larger demonstrations.

zh: 政府的街头管制未必管用。
en: Control of the streets by government is not as secure.

zh: 平均而言，反政府游行示威数量会增加两倍，暴力动乱的频率会增加一倍，大罢工至少会增加三分之一。
en: The average number of anti-government demonstrations triples, the frequency of violent riots doubles, and general strikes increase by at least a third.

zh: 最近的希腊把这些数字又提高了一些。
en: Greece has boosted those numbers recently.

zh: 三位经济学家唯一令人放心的结论是这些影响会逐渐消散。
en: The only comforting conclusion that the three economists reach is that these effects gradually peter out.

zh: 数据表明，五年后，最坏的情况就过去了。
en: The data tell us that after five years, the worst is over.

zh: 而目前的欧洲似乎并非如此，法国最近的选举恐慌就是明证，更不用说芬兰和波兰了，那里的极右翼民粹主义者已经掌权。
en: That does not seem to be the way things are moving now in Europe, if we look at France’s recent election scare, not to mention Finland and Poland, where right-wing populists have now come to power.

zh: 也许答案在于时间要从危机完全结束后开始计算，而目前欧洲的危机显然还没有结束。
en: Maybe the answer is that the clock starts ticking on the five years when the crisis is fully over, which is not yet true in Europe.

zh: 因此，在一段时间内，政治似乎会继续焦灼。
en: So politics seems set to remain a difficult trade for some time.

zh: 被广泛指责为危机原因的银行家和金融家将继续背负罪名，直到选民对经济和金融稳定的预期得到更加一致的满足。
en: And the bankers and financiers who are widely blamed for the crisis will remain in the sin bin for a while yet, until voters’ expectations of economic and financial stability are more consistently satisfied.

zh: 金融危机与战争
en: Financial Crisis and War

zh: 普林斯顿 — — 随着1914年一战百年庆典在即，政界及评论界人士正为当前脆弱的全球政治经济环境而忧心忡忡。
en: PRINCETON – The approach of the hundredth anniversary of the outbreak of World War I in 1914 has jolted politicians and commentators worried by the fragility of current global political and economic arrangements.

zh: 事实上，卢森堡首相让－克洛德·容克最近提出欧洲日趋严重的南北分化让这块大陆倒退了整整一个世纪之多。
en: Indeed, Luxembourg’s prime minister, Jean-Claude Juncker, recently argued that Europe’s growing north-south polarization has set the continent back by a century.

zh: 1914年大战的教训不仅是民族仇恨的危险性。
en: The lessons of 1914 are about more than simply the dangers of national animosities.

zh: 一战的起因中包括金融全球化在何种情况下会等同于国家军备竞赛，进而对国际秩序构成威胁的有趣先例。
en: The origins of the Great War include a fascinating precedent concerning how financial globalization can become the equivalent of a national arms race, thereby increasing the vulnerability of the international order.

zh: 1907年，一场源自美国的大规模金融危机开始影响其他国家，并显露出国际金融体系的脆弱特征。
en: In 1907, a major financial crisis emanating from the United States affected the rest of the world and demonstrated the fragility of the entire international financial system.

zh: 对当前金融危机所采取的对策也具备类似的特征。
en: The response to the current financial crisis is replaying a similar dynamic.

zh: 沃尔特·白芝浩1873年的经典著作《朗伯德街》将伦敦形容为“全球有史以来经济力量和经济脆弱性最完美的结合。
en: Walter Bagehot’s 1873 classic Lombard Street described the City of London as “the greatest combination of economic power and economic delicacy that the world has ever seen.”

zh: ”根据小说家、工党议员兼1910年诺贝尔和平奖获得者诺曼·安吉尔的著名解释，复杂全球经济的相互依赖彻底消除了战争的可能。
en: In one influential interpretation, popularized by the novelist, Labour Party MP, and future Nobel Peace Prize laureate Norman Angell in 1910, the interdependency of the increasingly complex global economy made war impossible.

zh: 但反向结论同样站得住脚：鉴于全球经济脆弱性，巧妙地操纵控制能协助经济霸主取得军事成功。
en: But the opposite conclusion was equally plausible: Given the extent of fragility, a clever twist to the control levers might facilitate a military victory by the economic hegemon.

zh: 1907年股灾后，当时的霸主英国开始反思如何利用金融影响提升其整体战略优势。
en: The aftermath of the 1907 crash drove the hegemonic power of the time – Great Britain – to reflect on how it could use its financial clout to enhance its overall strategic capacity.

zh: 这是尼古拉斯·兰伯特最近一部研究一战及英国经济规划的重要著作《规划大决战》的结论内容。
en: That is the conclusion of an important recent book, Nicholas Lambert’s study of British economic planning and the First World War, entitled Planning Armageddon.

zh: 兰伯特展示了在一场宏伟的战略赌局中，英国如何把其军事 — — 尤其是海军优势与全球金融领导力相结合。
en: Lambert demonstrates how, in a grand strategic gamble, Britain began to marry its military – and especially naval – predominance and its global financial leadership.

zh: 1905年到1908年，英国海军部制定了对欧洲新兴强国德国发动金融经济战的大致计划轮廓。
en: Between 1905 and 1908, the British Admiralty developed the broad outlines of a plan for financial and economic warfare against Europe’s rising power, Germany.

zh: 经济战计划全面实施将破坏德国的金融体系，迫使其退出任何军事冲突。
en: Economic warfare, if implemented in full, would wreck Germany’s financial system and force it out of any military conflict.

zh: 当英国海军梦想家遭遇凯撒德国式的竞争对手，他们非常清楚如何利用对手的金融脆弱性增强自身的军事力量。
en: When Britain’s naval visionaries confronted a rival in the form of the Kaiser’s Germany, they understood how power could thrive on financial fragility.

zh: 1914年前，英国就对今天将谷歌、苹果或威瑞森等科技巨头与美国情报机构相联系的公私伙伴关系有所预测。
en: Pre-1914 Britain anticipated the private-public partnership that today links technology giants such as Google, Apple, or Verizon to US intelligence agencies.

zh: 伦敦银行为大部分世界贸易提供担保；劳埃德当之无愧地成为世界航运险的巨头。
en: London banks underwrote most of the world’s trade; Lloyds provided insurance for the world’s shipping.

zh: 上述金融网络提供的信息使英国政府能够发现敌对联盟战略上敏感的薄弱环节。
en: These financial networks provided the information that enabled the British government to discover the sensitive strategic vulnerabilities of the opposing alliance.

zh: 而对英国的对手，1907年的金融恐慌向他们展示了掌握金融力量是多么必要。
en: For Britain’s rivals, the financial panic of 1907 demonstrated the necessity of mobilizing financial power themselves.

zh: 如美国就意识到需要成立与英格兰银行相似的中央银行。
en: The US, for its part, recognized that it needed a central bank analogous to the Bank of England.

zh: 现实告诉美国金融家纽约需要建设自身的商业交易系统，像伦敦市场那样处理汇票并实现汇票的货币化（也叫“承兑业务 ” ） 。
en: American financiers were persuaded that New York needed to develop its own commercial trading system to handle bills of exchange in the same way as the London market and arrange their monetization (or “acceptance”).

zh: 开创美国承兑市场的核心人物是保罗·沃伯格，保罗是曾任德皇威廉二世私人顾问的那位伟大的汉堡银行家移民美国的亲弟弟。
en: The central figure in pushing for the development of an American acceptance market was Paul Warburg, the immigrant younger brother of a great Hamburg banker who was the personal adviser to Germany’s Kaiser Wilhelm II.

zh: 沃伯格兄弟（马克斯和保罗）在大西洋两岸共同努力推动德美金融体系的发展，打破英国在工业和金融领域的垄断地位。
en: The Warburg brothers, Max and Paul, were a transatlantic tandem, energetically pushing for German-American institutions that would offer an alternative to British industrial and financial monopoly.

zh: 他们深信英国的实力会随着德美两国实力的逐年增强而不断削弱。
en: They were convinced that Germany and the US were growing stronger year by year, while British power would erode.

zh: 1914年前世界金融市场的某些动态如今再度出现。
en: Some of the dynamics of the pre-1914 financial world are now reemerging.

zh: 在2008年那场金融危机的余波中，金融机构似乎既是大规模经济破坏的危险武器，又是国家权力应用的潜在工具。
en: In the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis, financial institutions appear both as dangerous weapons of mass economic destruction, but also as potential instruments for the application of national power.

zh: 在2008年的危机管理中，外国银行对美元资本的依赖构成一种主要弱点，需要美联储保证较大的换汇额度。
en: In managing the 2008 crisis, foreign banks’ dependence on US-dollar funding constituted a major weakness, and required the provision of large swap lines by the Federal Reserve.

zh: 解决这个问题需要对银行重新执行国有化，并停止大型金融机构的活动。
en: Addressing that flaw requires renationalization of banking, and breaking up the activities of large financial institutions.

zh: 在欧洲银行家和某些政府看来，美国当前修改对外国银行附属机构在美经营态度的做法凸显了上述趋势的势在必行。
en: For European bankers, and some governments, current efforts by the US to revise its approach to the operation of foreign bank subsidiaries within its territory highlight that imperative.

zh: 他们将美国此举视为一种新的金融保护主义，并威胁要予以报复。
en: They view the US move as a new sort of financial protectionism and are threatening retaliation.

zh: 地缘政治因素在其他国家也开始对银行经营起干扰作用。
en: Geopolitics is intruding into banking practice elsewhere as well.

zh: 俄罗斯银行正竭力在中东欧地区收购资产。
en: Russian banks are trying to acquire assets in Central and Eastern Europe.

zh: 亚洲贸易融资领域正不遗余力地限制欧洲银行的作用。
en: European banks are playing a much-reduced role in Asian trade finance.

zh: 中国银行被迫扩大其对全球商务活动的参与。
en: Chinese banks are being pushed to expand their role in global commerce.

zh: 很多国家已开始运用金融保护主义的方法扩大政治领域的杠杆作用。
en: Many countries have begun to look at financial protectionism as a way to increase their political leverage.

zh: 这种逻辑的下一步是思考如何让金融实力在外交冲突中转化为国家优势。
en: The next step in this logic is to think about how financial power can be directed to national advantage in the case of a diplomatic conflict.

zh: 制裁是对伊朗和朝鲜等无赖国家施压的常规程序，但却并不十分成功。
en: Sanctions are a routine (and not terribly successful) part of the pressure applied to rogue states like Iran and North Korea.

zh: 但向更深植根于全球经济的国家施压的效果却可能好得多。
en: But financial pressure can be much more powerfully applied to countries that are deeply embedded in the global economy.

zh: 1907年，随着一场几乎令全球陷入崩溃的划时代的金融危机，一些国家开始把金融视为能够而且应当转化为国家优势的代表原始力量的工具来加以运用。
en: In 1907, in the wake of an epochal financial crisis that almost brought a complete global collapse, several countries started to think of finance primarily as an instrument of raw power that could and should be turned to national advantage.

zh: 这种想法导致在1914年一战爆发。
en: That kind of thinking brought war in 1914.

zh: 一个世纪后的2007-2008年，世界经历了规模更大的金融震荡，并随后点燃了民族主义激情。
en: A century later, in 2007-2008, the world experienced an even greater financial shock, and nationalistic passions have flared up in its wake.

zh: 破坏性战略也许并非遥不可及。
en: Destructive strategies may not be far behind.

zh: 2020年萧条和金融危机的成因
en: The Makings of a 2020 Recession and Financial Crisis

zh: 发自纽约 — — 眼下已是纪念雷曼兄弟破产十周年之时，但关于此次金融危机的前因后果，以及人们是否已经吸收了足够教训以避免下一次危机的争论却仍未平息。
en: NEW YORK – As we mark the decennial of the collapse of Lehman Brothers, there are still ongoing debates about the causes and consequences of the financial crisis, and whether the lessons needed to prepare for the next one have been absorbed.

zh: 但展望未来，更事关重大的问题在于，引发下一次全球经济衰退和危机的因素究竟是什么，又会在何时引发呢？
en: But looking ahead, the more relevant question is what actually will trigger the next global recession and crisis, and when.

zh: 鉴于美国财政赤字庞大，中国正在推行宽松财政和信贷政策，欧洲仍处于复苏之路，当前的全球扩张势头可能会持续到明年。
en: The current global expansion will likely continue into next year, given that the US is running large fiscal deficits, China is pursuing loose fiscal and credit policies, and Europe remains on a recovery path.

zh: 等到2020年金融危机的爆发条件就会成熟，随后就是一场全球性经济衰退。
en: But by 2020, the conditions will be ripe for a financial crisis, followed by a global recession.

zh: 引发这场新危机的原因有十个，请让我一一道来：首先，当前推动美国年增长率高于其2％增长潜力的财政刺激政策是不可持续的。
en: There are 10 reasons for this. First, the fiscal-stimulus policies that are currently pushing the annual US growth rate above its 2% potential are unsustainable.

zh: 刺激措施将在2020年耗尽，随之而来的中度财政放缓会把经济增长率从3％拉至略低于2 ％ 。
en: By 2020, the stimulus will run out, and a modest fiscal drag will pull growth from 3% to slightly below 2%.

zh: 其次，由于经济刺激计划的实施时机有问题，美国经济现在已经过热，通胀正在超出目标。
en: Second, because the stimulus was poorly timed, the US economy is now overheating, and inflation is rising above target.

zh: 因此到2020年，美联储将继续将联邦基金利率从目前的2％提高到至少3.5 ％ ， 这可能推高短期/长期利率以及美元汇率。
en: The US Federal Reserve will thus continue to raise the federal funds rate from its current 2% to at least 3.5% by 2020, and that will likely push up short- and long-term interest rates as well as the US dollar.

zh: 与此同时，其他主要经济体的通货膨胀率也在上升，而油价上涨也在加剧通胀压力。
en: Meanwhile, inflation is also increasing in other key economies, and rising oil prices are contributing additional inflationary pressures.

zh: 这意味着其他主要央行将追随美联储实施货币政策正常化，这将减少全球流动性并对利率施加上行压力。
en: That means the other major central banks will follow the Fed toward monetary-policy normalization, which will reduce global liquidity and put upward pressure on interest rates.

zh: 第三，特朗普政府与中国、欧洲、墨西哥，加拿大和其他国家的贸易争端升级几乎是板上钉钉的事情，导致经济增长放缓和通胀上升。
en: Third, the Trump administration’s trade disputes with China, Europe, Mexico, Canada, and others will almost certainly escalate, leading to slower growth and higher inflation.

zh: 第四，其他美国政策将继续增加滞涨压力，促使美联储进一步加息。
en: Fourth, other US policies will continue to add stagflationary pressure, prompting the Fed to raise interest rates higher still.

zh: 政府正在限制内部/外部投资和技术转让，而这将破坏供应链。
en: The administration is restricting inward/outward investment and technology transfers, which will disrupt supply chains. It is restricting the immigrants who are needed to maintain growth as the US population ages.

zh: 政府限制了保持增长所需的移民流入，使得美国人口进一步老龄化，此外还阻碍了对绿色经济的投资，也缺乏基础设施政策去解决供给侧的瓶颈问题。
en: It is discouraging investments in the green economy. And it has no infrastructure policy to address supply-side bottlenecks.

zh: 第五，世界其他地区的增长可能会放缓 — — 而且越多国家对美国的保护主义政策发起报复，情况就越严峻。
en: Fifth, growth in the rest of the world will likely slow down – more so as other countries will see fit to retaliate against US protectionism.

zh: 中国必须放慢增长速度以应对产能过剩和过度杠杆化，否则就将触发硬着陆。
en: China must slow its growth to deal with overcapacity and excessive leverage; otherwise a hard landing will be triggered.

zh: 本已风雨飘摇的新兴市场将继续感受到美国保护主义和货币环境收紧的压力。
en: And already-fragile emerging markets will continue to feel the pinch from protectionism and tightening monetary conditions in the US.

zh: 第六，由于货币政策紧缩和贸易摩擦，欧洲也将出现增长放缓。
en: Sixth, Europe, too, will experience slower growth, owing to monetary-policy tightening and trade frictions.

zh: 此外，意大利等国家的民粹主义政策可能导致欧元区内产生无以为继的债务事态发展。
en: Moreover, populist policies in countries such as Italy may lead to an unsustainable debt dynamic within the eurozone.

zh: 政府与持有公共债务的银行之间尚未解开的“死循环”将放大这个风险分担机制有问题的不完全货币联盟的现有风险。
en: The still-unresolved “doom loop” between governments and banks holding public debt will amplify the existential problems of an incomplete monetary union with inadequate risk-sharing.

zh: 在这种情况下，下一轮全球经济衰退可能促使意大利和其他国家完全退出欧元区。
en: Under these conditions, another global downturn could prompt Italy and other countries to exit the eurozone altogether.

zh: 第七，美国和全球股市泡沫化。
en: Seventh, US and global equity markets are frothy.

zh: 眼下美国的市盈率已经比历史平均水平高出50 ％ ， 私募股权估值过高，低收益率和负期限溢价也使得政府债券变得过于昂贵。
en: Price-to-earnings ratios in the US are 50% above the historic average, private-equity valuations have become excessive, and government bonds are too expensive, given their low yields and negative term premia.

zh: 由于美国企业杠杆率达到历史高位，高收益信贷也变得日益昂贵。
en: And high-yield credit is also becoming increasingly expensive now that the US corporate-leverage rate has reached historic highs.

zh: 此外，许多新兴市场和一些发达经济体的杠杆率明显过高。
en: Moreover, the leverage in many emerging markets and some advanced economies is clearly excessive.

zh: 商业和住宅房地产在世界许多地方都太过昂贵了。
en: Commercial and residential real estate is far too expensive in many parts of the world.

zh: 随着全球风暴不断积聚成型，新兴市场股票，商品和固定收益持有物的价格修正将继续。
en: The emerging-market correction in equities, commodities, and fixed-income holdings will continue as global storm clouds gather.

zh: 随着具有前瞻性的投资者开始预测到2020年增长放缓，市场将在2019年之前对风险资产进行重新定价。
en: And as forward-looking investors start anticipating a growth slowdown in 2020, markets will reprice risky assets by 2019.

zh: 第八，一旦出现修正，流动性不足和紧急/降价抛售的风险会更大。
en: Eighth, once a correction occurs, the risk of illiquidity and fire sales/undershooting will become more severe.

zh: 经纪商-经营商的做市和囤货行为也会减少。
en: There are reduced market-making and warehousing activities by broker-dealers.

zh: 过度的高频/算法交易将增加“闪电式崩溃”的可能性。
en: Excessive high-frequency/algorithmic trading will raise the likelihood of “flash crashes.”

zh: 而固定收益工具则更加集中于开放式交易所交易和专用信贷基金。
en: And fixed-income instruments have become more concentrated in open-ended exchange-traded and dedicated credit funds.

zh: 在出现避险情绪的情况下，拥有大量美元计价负债的新兴市场和发达经济体金融部门将不无法最终求助于美联储。
en: In the case of a risk-off, emerging markets and advanced-economy financial sectors with massive dollar-denominated liabilities will no longer have access to the Fed as a lender of last resort.

zh: 随着通胀上升和政策正常化的推进，也无法指望中央银行能提供像前几年危机后那样的支持。
en: With inflation rising and policy normalization underway, the backstop that central banks provided during the post-crisis years can no longer be counted on.

zh: 第九，特朗普在最近增长率为4％时就已经在抨击美联储。
en: Ninth, Trump was already attacking the Fed when the growth rate was recently 4%.

zh: 那么试想如何在2020年大选之年增长率跌至不到1％且就业流失增加的情况下他会如何表现。
en: Just think about how he will behave in the 2020 election year, when growth likely will have fallen below 1% and job losses emerge.

zh: 尤其是如果民主党今年重夺众议院的话，特朗普就很可能忍不住要去人为制造外交政策危机来“转移注意力 ” 。
en: The temptation for Trump to “wag the dog” by manufacturing a foreign-policy crisis will be high, especially if the Democrats retake the House of Representatives this year.

zh: 由于特朗普与中国的贸易战已经开打，同时又不敢惹拥有核武器的朝鲜，他的最佳目标会是伊朗。
en: Since Trump has already started a trade war with China and wouldn’t dare attack nuclear-armed North Korea, his last best target would be Iran.

zh: 通过挑起与该国的军事对抗，他将引发一场与1973年，1979年和1990年的油价飙升大同小异的滞胀式地缘政治冲击。
en: By provoking a military confrontation with that country, he would trigger a stagflationary geopolitical shock not unlike the oil-price spikes of 1973, 1979, and 1990.

zh: 毋庸多言，这将使得即将到来的全球经济衰退更为严重。
en: Needless to say, that would make the oncoming global recession even more severe.

zh: 最后，上述特大风暴一旦席卷而来，应对它的政策工具将非常缺乏。
en: Finally, once the perfect storm outlined above occurs, the policy tools for addressing it will be sorely lacking.

zh: 财政刺激的空间已经受到大规模公共债务的限制。
en: The space for fiscal stimulus is already limited by massive public debt.

zh: 动用更多非常规货币政策的可能性将受到臃肿的资产负债表以及捉襟见肘的削减政策利率空间所限。
en: The possibility for more unconventional monetary policies will be limited by bloated balance sheets and the lack of headroom to cut policy rates.

zh: 在那些民粹主义运动高涨且政府近乎破产的国家，金融部门的救助行动将是无法容忍的。
en: And financial-sector bailouts will be intolerable in countries with resurgent populist movements and near-insolvent governments.

zh: 具体在美国来说，立法者限制了美联储向以美元计价负债向非银行和外国金融机构提供流动性的能力。
en: In the US specifically, lawmakers have constrained the ability of the Fed to provide liquidity to non-bank and foreign financial institutions with dollar-denominated liabilities.

zh: 在欧洲，民粹主义政党的崛起使得推动欧盟层面改革并创建必要机构来应对下一次金融危机和经济衰退的努力更加无以为继。
en: And in Europe, the rise of populist parties is making it harder to pursue EU-level reforms and create the institutions necessary to combat the next financial crisis and downturn.

zh: 2008年时各国政府手中还握有防止经济自由落体式下跌所需的政策工具，而必须直面下一次经济衰退的政策制定者却将受到束缚，而且总体债务水平还要高于上次危机期间。
en: Unlike in 2008, when governments had the policy tools needed to prevent a free fall, the policymakers who must confront the next downturn will have their hands tied while overall debt levels are higher than during the previous crisis.

zh: 当一切最终降临时，下一次危机和衰退可能会比上一次更加严重而持久。
en: When it comes, the next crisis and recession could be even more severe and prolonged than the last.

zh: 大型科技企业的危机处理手册
en: A Crisis Playbook for Big Tech

zh: 牛津 — — 预测是错误的：全球经济并没有在2008年金融危机后陷入崩溃。
en: OXFORD – The predictions were wrong: the global economy didn’t collapse after the 2008 financial crisis.

zh: 在纳税人出资的救助行动支持下，银行的业务日渐恢复，而多数机构的业务也逐步稳定下来。
en: Buoyed by taxpayer-financed bailouts, banks recovered and business at most institutions stabilized.

zh: 但如果说那个时代有一个延续至今的恶果，那就是彻底断送了民众对金融行业的信任。
en: But if there is one lingering casualty of that era, it is the erosion of public trust in the financial sector.

zh: 危机爆发十年后，普通市民仍然对华尔街缺乏最基本的信心。
en: Ten years after the crisis began, Main Street still has little faith in Wall Street.

zh: 今天类似的信任危机也困扰着科技行业。
en: A similar crisis of confidence plagues the technology industry today.

zh: 随着脸书和剑桥分析为企业利用乃至滥用个人数据寻找貌似合理的借口，民众对科技企业的信任正日趋接近崩溃。
en: As executives at Facebook and Cambridge Analytica rationalize their companies’ use and abuse of personal data, trust in technology firms is approaching a tipping point.

zh: 大型科技企业仍然可以挽救自己的声誉，但其中最强大的公司必须从根本上改变运营方式。
en: “Big Tech” can still salvage its reputation, but its most powerful companies will need to change fundamentally how they operate.

zh: 要想做到这一点，他们必须避免犯下十年前曾令金融行业几乎陷入困境的错误。
en: And to do that, they must avoid the mistakes that nearly crippled the financial sector a decade ago.

zh: 金融行业的五大关键教训应当指导今天科技行业的决策。
en: Five key lessons from the financial crisis should guide decision-making in the tech sector today.

zh: 首先，消费者的无知可能代价昂贵。
en: First, consumer illiteracy can be costly.

zh: 房地产泡沫破裂之前不久，许多投资者意识到他们对所购买的产品缺乏最基本的认识；甚至有人都不知道购买过任何产品。
en: Shortly before the housing bubble burst, many investors realized they had no understanding of the products they were buying; some didn’t even know they were buying anything.

zh: 金融新闻助长了这种无知的环境，因为他们只报导潜在的收益，而忽视风险的存在。
en: Financial journalism contributed to this atmosphere of ignorance by focusing only on the potential gains, and ignoring the risks.

zh: 人们参与技术也采用类似的方式。
en: People engage with technology in similar ways.

zh: 公司、政府和企业乐于将整体业务接入它们无法控制的平台。
en: Companies, governments, and businesses happily plug their entire operations into platforms they cannot control.

zh: 如果存在怀疑，也往往会遭到抑制，因为人们根本无法放弃技术所带来的便利。
en: Doubt, if it does arise, is usually subdued, because the technology is too convenient to abandon.

zh: 但就像危险的金融产品一样，控制新技术风险的唯一方法就是充分了解可能出现的问题。
en: But, just like perilous financial products, the only way to mitigate the risks of new technologies is to be fully educated about what could go wrong.

zh: 第二个教训是隐含成本具有累加效应。
en: The second lesson is that hidden costs add up.

zh: 金融危机爆发前，许多客户所购买的产品没有披露费用和财务附加成本，但这些却在后来演变为巨额负债。
en: Before the financial crisis, many customers were sold products with undisclosed fees and financial add-ons that became massive liabilities.

zh: 今天，更多投资者意识到高收益隐含着高风险，但在技术领域，隐含成本则继续套牢毫无戒心的客户。
en: Today, more investors recognize that higher returns imply higher risk, but in the technology business, hidden costs continue to entrap unsuspecting consumers.

zh: 其中某些成本是社会性的 — — 比如被广告商施压购买产品。
en: Some of these costs are social – like being pressured by advertisers to buy products.

zh: 还有些更加具体，像提供个人数据以换取相关服务。
en: And others are more tangible, like giving away personal data in exchange for access to a service.

zh: 第三，不公平的薪酬和激励机制会损害业务。
en: Third, inequitable pay and incentive structures are bad for business.

zh: 关于金融危机高峰时期 投资银行家攫取高额奖金的文章已经数不胜数。
en: Much has been written about the extraordinary bonuses paid to investment bankers during the height of the financial crisis.

zh: 但硅谷的首席执行官们也不是罗宾汉。
en: But the CEOs of Silicon Valley are no Robin Hoods, either.

zh: 科技企业家可能会告诉投资者他们想改变世界，但很多人同样沉醉于把企业出售给出价最高的竞标者时，他们自己会面对一个更加美好的世界。
en: Tech entrepreneurs might tell their investors they want to change the world, but many are intoxicated by the idea that the world will be better when they sell their business to the highest bidder.

zh: 第四，由男性主导的企业会承担更多不必要的风险。
en: Fourth, businesses that are male-dominated take more unnecessary risks.

zh: 记录金融危机的历史时，许多人认为性别多样性本可以减轻这种损害。
en: When the history of the financial crisis was being written, many argued that greater gender diversity would have mitigated the damage.

zh: 2010年，雷曼兄弟倒闭两年后，时任法国财政部长的克里斯蒂娜·拉加德曾打趣道如果这家企业当时由“雷曼姐妹”来管理，这次危机或许不会那么严重。
en: In 2010, two years after the collapse of Lehman Brothers, Christine Lagarde, then-France’s finance minister, quipped that the crisis would have been less painful if “Lehman Sisters” had been managing the store.

zh: 今天同样的逻辑也适用于科技行业。
en: The same logic applies to the tech sector today.

zh: 最后，正如我们十年前所学到的那样，全球经济已经深度互联；没有哪家银行太大不能倒闭或者不能挽救。
en: Finally, as we learned a decade ago, the global economy is deeply interconnected; no bank was too big to fail or to be rescued.

zh: 最大的科技企业也同样如此。
en: This is true for the largest technology companies as well.

zh: 亚马逊或谷歌的崩溃 — — 无论它们看似如何无懈可击 — — 都会造成毁灭性的连锁反应。
en: The collapse of Amazon or Google – however invulnerable they may seem – would have devastating ripple effects.

zh: 虽然许多人因为审查和知识获取方面的顾虑认为监管科技企业并不明智，但这些企业就像它们金融部门的同行一样，已经长了太大，不能再任凭它们自由发展。
en: While many argue that it would be unwise to regulate technology firms with a view to concerns over censorship and access to knowledge, these companies, like their financial-sector counterparts, have grown too big to be left to their own devices.

zh: 在金融危机爆发后的十年间，结构性改革已经协助稳定了银行和金融服务业。
en: In the decade since the financial crisis erupted, structural changes have helped stabilize the banking and financial-services industry.

zh: 规章制度提升了透明度，改善了消费者认知。
en: Regulations have increased transparency and improved consumer awareness.

zh: 但陈旧动态、权力结构及臃肿的薪酬标准却在很大程度上存活了下来。
en: But the old dynamics, power structures, and bloated pay scales have largely survived.

zh: 因此行业声誉依然支离破碎。
en: As a result, the sector’s reputation remains in tatters.

zh: 技术行业要想避免类似的命运，行业领袖必须提高消费者对其产品的认知 — — 教育民众认识到产品的潜在风险。
en: For the technology industry to avoid a similar fate, its leaders must increase consumers’ literacy about the products they offer – and the potential dangers they hold.

zh: 首席执行官必须支持监管、增加工作场所的多样性，并提升薪酬和激励机制的公平性。
en: CEOs must support regulation, increase workplace diversity, and make compensation and incentive structures more equitable.

zh: 最重要的是，技术行业领袖应当避免其他行业在危机期间所犯下的错误。
en: Above all, tech leaders should avoid the mistakes made by other industries navigating crisis.

zh: 而没有哪个行业比几乎摧毁全球经济的金融业提供了更加合适的实例研究样板。
en: And no industry offers a more relevant case study than the one that almost took down the global economy.

zh: 完成后危机时代的工作
en: Finishing the Post-Crisis Job

zh: 伦敦 — — 2017年8月9日是法国巴黎银行决定冻结22亿美元货币市场基金决策十周年纪念日。
en: LONDON – August 9, 2017, is the tenth anniversary of the decision by the French bank BNP Paribas to freeze some $2.2 billion worth of money-market funds.

zh: 我们这些当时活跃在金融市场上的人还清楚地记得那次事件标志着大萧条后最严重的全球金融危机启动。
en: Those of us who were active in financial markets at the time remember that event as the beginning of the worst global financial crisis since the Great Depression.

zh: 许多经济学家和金融观察家认为我们仍未能从那次危机及其背后势力所造成的后果中摆脱。
en: Many economists and financial observers argue that we are still living with the consequences of that crisis, and with the forces that incited it.

zh: 这在一定程度上的确是真的。
en: This is partly true.

zh: 许多发达经济体仍在实行量化宽松等非常规货币政策，并且生产率和（经过通胀调整后的）实际工资增长似乎大都陷入停滞当中。
en: Many developed economies still have in place unconventional monetary policies such as quantitative easing, and both productivity and real (inflation-adjusted) wage growth appear to be mostly stagnant.

zh: 但正确看待上述进展的确非常重要。
en: But it is important to put these developments in perspective.

zh: 许多人，包括2008年11月的英国女王，仍在不断询问 ： “ 为什么没有人能预见这次危机？
en: Many people, including the Queen of England in November 2008, still ask: “Why did no one see it coming?”

zh: ”事实上，许多金融观察家确曾警告美国的房屋价格上涨不可持续，尤其因为美国消费者国内个人储蓄的匮乏。
en: In fact, many financial observers did warn that housing prices in the United States were rising untenably, especially given the lack of domestic personal savings among US consumers.

zh: 作为高盛时任首席经济学家，我曾在几年时间里撰写了三份不同的报告，表明美国经常账户赤字是不可持续的。
en: As Chief Economist of Goldman Sachs at the time, I had written three different papers over a number of years showing that the US current-account deficit was unsustainable.

zh: 不幸的是，绝大多数人对这些研究成果视而不见，而且公司外汇销售人员可能厌烦了向客户提交大致相同的报告。
en: Unfortunately, these findings largely fell on deaf ears, and the firm’s foreign-exchange salespeople probably got bored passing on yet more of the same pieces to their clients.

zh: 2007年的某个时点，美国经常账户赤字据报占到国内生产总值的6-7 % （ 之后的全年数据下修到5%左右 ） 。
en: At one point in 2007, the US current-account deficit was reported to be 6-7% of GDP (it has since been revised down to around 5% for the full year).

zh: 上述数字高企反映了自20世纪90年代以来美国的贸易平衡稳步恶化。
en: This high figure reflected the fact that the US trade balance had been steadily deteriorating since the 1990s.

zh: 但由于没有显而易见的负面后果，自满情绪占据了主导地位，而美国继续花的比存的多。
en: In the absence of any obvious negative consequences, however, complacency had set in, and the US continued to spend more than it saved.

zh: 此外，整个20世纪90年代中国忙于向世界其他国家出口低附加值产品，而不仅限于美国消费者。
en: Meanwhile, China had spent the 1990s exporting low-value-added products to the rest of the world, not least to US consumers.

zh: 2007年，中国的经常账户盈余约为国内生产总值的10 % — —恰恰是与美国相反的镜像。
en: In 2007, its current-account surplus was around 10% of GDP – the mirror image of the US.

zh: 美国存款过低，而中国却存款过高。
en: Whereas the latter was saving too little, China was saving too much.

zh: 在某些观察家看来，这一巨大的国际收支失衡是危机爆发的源头。
en: For some observers, this huge international imbalance was the source of the crisis.

zh: 在崩溃之前的几年里，他们提出全球金融系统仅仅是在通过越来越聪明的方式回收盈余来完成自己的任务。
en: In the years leading up to the crash, they argued that the global financial system was simply doing its job, by finding increasingly clever ways to recycle the surpluses.

zh: 当然，我们现在知道这项任务完成的相当糟糕。
en: Of course, we now know that it performed that job rather poorly.

zh: 这十年间发生了很大变化。
en: Much has changed in the intervening decade.

zh: 2017年，中国的经常账户盈余占国内生产总值的1.5~2 % ， 而美国赤字则最有可能占国内生产总值的2 % — —或者可能高达3%左右。
en: In 2017, China will run a current-account surplus of 1.5-2% of GDP, and the US will most likely run a deficit of around 2% – but possibly as high as 3% – of GDP.

zh: 这是世界两大经济体最明显的进步。
en: This is a vast improvement for the world’s two largest economies.

zh: 但过去十年来其他国家的经常账户失衡仍然日渐加剧。
en: Still, other countries have built up ever-larger current-account imbalances over the past decade.

zh: 其中最主要的是德国，其外部盈余现在已经超过国内生产总值的8 % 。
en: Chief among them is Germany, whose external surplus now exceeds 8% of GDP.

zh: 德国的经常账户状况表明存在严重的收支失衡，如果决策不善有可能导致新一次危机爆发。
en: Germany’s current account suggests that there are deep imbalances that could lead to a new crisis if policymaking is not well coordinated.

zh: 欧洲最不需要又一次突然间的逆转，就像我们在希腊债务危机高潮期间所看到的那样。
